report.title: Roll Tide, Rest Tide: Alabama Takes the Bye Week and Gets Ready for November
report.byline: Mary-Kathryn 'MK' Strickland · Alabama Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Roll Tide, darling, and I mean that as a greeting. Mostly. I'm Mary-Kathryn Strickland, but everyone from the Quad to the press box calls me MK. I rode for the Tide equestrian team, I read blitz pickups the way some girls read Southern Living, and I can quote a legendary coaching maxim for every situation, perfectly, usually at dinner. My family has asked me to stop. I will not stop. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little belle-of-the-ball polish. When we win, you'll hear "Roll Tide" in seventeen different tones, each more satisfied than the last. When we lose, I'll say "We will not speak of it," and I will not speak of it.

The School in 60 Seconds
Alabama claims 18 national championships, 13 of them wire-service titles from the poll era. Paul "Bear" Bryant won six from 1958 to 1982, and Nick Saban won six more between 2007 and 2023. The Tide's Heisman winners are Mark Ingram II (2009), Derrick Henry (2015), DeVonta Smith (2020) and Bryce Young (2021). Alabama has 30 SEC championships, an NCAA-record 79 bowl appearances and 46 bowl wins, also a record, plus a record 16 straight 10-win seasons from 2008 through 2023. Bryant-Denny Stadium seats 101,821 and opened in 1929. Coach Bryant has a maxim for this, and I'll save it for dinner.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kalen DeBoer was hired Jan. 12, 2024, and his first two Tide teams went 9-4 and 11-4.

Players to Know
QB Keelon Russell: 148 of 221, 2,057 yards, 15 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Daniel Hill: 332 yards on 71 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR Lotzeir Brooks: 29 catches, 488 yards, 1 touchdown.
LB Yhonzae Pierre: 3.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Caleb Woodson: a team-high 63 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Alabama is 6-2 overall and 4-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 3rd in SEC.
The season so far: W 48-10 vs East Carolina Pirates (Sept. 5), W 45-17 at Kentucky Wildcats (Sept. 12), W 50-36 vs Florida State Seminoles (Sept. 19), W 49-18 vs South Carolina Gamecocks (Sept. 26), W 56-23 at Mississippi State Bulldogs (Oct. 3), L 17-20 vs Georgia Bulldogs (Oct. 10), L 10-26 at Tennessee Volunteers (Oct. 17), W 31-20 vs Texas A&M Aggies (Oct. 24).

This Week: Bye Week
No game for Alabama this week. We're off from Tuesday, Oct. 27, through Saturday, Oct. 31, so the rest of this report is about where we stand and what's next.
Last time out. We beat the Texas A&M Aggies 31-20 at home on Oct. 24. Keelon Russell went 19 of 30 for 311 yards, with 3 touchdowns and 1 interception. Daniel Hill ran 9 times for 36 yards. Rico Scott caught 6 balls for 156 yards.
Up next. We play the LSU Tigers on the road on Saturday, Nov. 7, 3:30 p.m. ET, at Tiger Stadium (LA) in Baton Rouge.
The open week is for rest, healing and a good week of practice. I'll be back with a full preview before the next kickoff.

report.title: Hogs Call on Halloween Night: Arkansas Hosts Missouri in a Border Battle
report.byline: Bubba Fayette-Dorsey · Arkansas Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Woooo, Pig, here comes the data! I'm Bubba Fayette-Dorsey, and I'm your Arkansas insider. I'm a grade-school science teacher from up in the Ozarks, and I call the Hogs before every stat, even the bad ones. On the podcast, my segment is called Hog Call: I call the Hogs, then I read the stat. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, built in 1938 with a listed capacity of 80,000. The playing surface is Frank Broyles Field, the band is the Best in Sight and Sound, and the fight song is "Arkansas Fight." The program claims a national title from 1964. The last five seasons went 9-4, 7-6, 4-8, 7-6 and 2-10, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about Calling the Hogs. It's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Ryan Silverfield became the 35th head coach in Arkansas history, and CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 30, 2025. He coached Memphis against Missouri in 2023, so he knows the folks coming to town this week.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 21.0 points per game and allowing 26.7.

Players to Know
QB KJ Jackson: 131 of 215, 1,444 yards, 7 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Braylen Russell: 205 yards on 58 carries, 2 touchdowns.
WR Chris Marshall: 43 catches, 633 yards, 2 touchdowns.
DL Quincy Rhodes Jr.: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Ja'Quavion Smith: a team-high 48 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Arkansas is 3-4 overall and 1-3 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 14th in SEC.
The season so far: W 31-14 vs North Alabama Lions (Sept. 5), L 10-43 at Utah Utes (Sept. 12), L 17-45 vs Georgia Bulldogs (Sept. 19), W 34-6 vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane (Sept. 26), L 7-34 at Texas A&M Aggies (Oct. 3), L 17-24 vs Tennessee Volunteers (Oct. 10), W 31-21 at Vanderbilt Commodores (Oct. 17).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
No. 23 Missouri (5-2, 2-2 SEC) at Arkansas (3-4, 1-3 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:45 p.m. ET (6:45 p.m. Central), Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium, Fayetteville, Ark., SEC Network.
Last time out. Both teams had the week off on Oct. 24.
Missouri's last game was a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. Simmons threw for 339 yards, and Donovan Olugbode caught nine passes for 127 yards. The Tigers got into the red zone three times and came away with three points.
Arkansas' last game was a 31-21 win at Vanderbilt on Oct. 17, its first SEC win in two years. Jackson went 21 of 31 for 251 yards and ran for a touchdown. Antonio Jordan, a Warren, Ark., native, had career highs with five catches for 74 yards.
Players to watch. Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons, an Ole Miss transfer, is 132 of 209 for 1,773 yards, 14 touchdowns and two interceptions. Running back Jamal Roberts leads the SEC in rushing with 867 yards and eight touchdowns on 167 carries. Wide receiver Cayden Lee has 47 catches for 678 yards and five touchdowns. On defense, Daeden Hopkins has seven sacks, and linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez has 76 tackles.
Arkansas quarterback KJ Jackson is 131 of 215 for 1,444 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Chris Marshall has 43 catches for 633 yards, second in the SEC in both. Braylen Russell leads the running backs with 205 yards. On defense, linebacker Ja'Quavion Smith has 48 tackles, and Quincy Rhodes Jr. has three sacks.
Availability. No official SEC availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Silverfield said Marshall, who hurt his leg at Vanderbilt, is expected to play. Arkansas center Caden Kitler, a team captain, is listed as the starter, though Kash Courtney started at Vanderbilt. Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said wide receiver Blair is back from a hamstring injury and will be fully available. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy has been sidelined since an offseason accident.
The coaches. Drinkwitz grew up in Alma, Ark., and has led Missouri since 2020. "I think the SEC is better when Arkansas is good," he said last fall.
Ryan Silverfield became the 35th head coach in Arkansas history the morning after last year's game. He coached Memphis against Missouri in 2023. "We know that they're going to be sound and well-coached," he said. He praised the Missouri wide zone running game and said it gets stronger in the fourth quarter.
Storylines. Simmons faced his old school, Ole Miss, two weeks ago, and he keeps it simple. "It's just another game for me," he said. Roberts has carried the load with Hardy out. For Arkansas, Jordan showed he can make plays when Marshall is out, and now the Hogs may have both.
Fun and true. The winner takes home the rivalry trophy. Missouri won the last four meetings, including 31-17 last year in Fayetteville. Arkansas last won in 2021, 34-17. Eight of the 16 games in the series were decided by one score. Only one first-year Arkansas coach has beaten Missouri: Glen Rose, 7-6 in St. Louis in 1944.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Delphine Arceneaux-Moss, Missouri's insider. Here's what I said:
"Woooo, Pig! Breaking news back at you, Delphine. It's our house tonight."
"Woooo, Pig! Seven sacks for Hopkins. Our quarterback should keep his eyes up."
"Woooo, Pig! And the Hogs would love to call that one."
And the last word from Delphine: "Breaking news: Silverfield would like to be the second."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Razorback Stadium opened in 1938 and seats 80,000. Fans will call the Hogs, the band is known as the Best in Sight and Sound, and the fight song is "Arkansas Fight." Arkansas claims a 1964 national title.
Missouri plays at Memorial Stadium in Columbia, with Faurot Field and Marching Mizzou. The fight song is "Every True Son, Fight Tiger," and the Tigers claim a 1960 national title. This is the first SEC night game Arkansas has hosted since Oct. 19, 2024.

report.title: War Eagle in the Grove: Auburn Brings Its Grit to Oxford on Halloween
report.byline: Lacey Bellamy · Auburn Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hey there, Auburn family! I'm Lacey Bellamy. I'm a proud former sorority president on the Plains, and I can recite every Iron Bowl down by heart. Ask me anything. I mean it. I'll even act them out, and in my reenactments, I always play the hero. Every single time. I'm sweet as sweet tea, and I'll have the sharpest take in the room, all wrapped in a nice Alabama drawl. When we win, I roll an imaginary oak in imaginary toilet paper and shriek "War Eagle!" When we lose, I sip my lemonade with great dignity and say "bless their hearts" about absolutely everybody. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a little Southern charm.

The School in 60 Seconds
Auburn has a national championship from 2010, the season Cam Newton led the Tigers. Home is Jordan-Hare Stadium, listed at 87,451. Bless its heart, there is no prettier place to spend a fall afternoon.

The Coach and the Scheme
Alex Golesh came to Auburn from South Florida. He was hired on Nov. 30, 2025.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 25.4 points per game and allowing 24.1.

Players to Know
QB Byrum Brown: 134 of 209, 1,365 yards, 8 touchdowns, 7 interceptions.
Byrum Brown on the ground: 471 yards on 124 carries, 6 touchdowns.
WR Keshaun Singleton: 36 catches, 431 yards, 2 touchdowns.
LB Elijah Melendez: 4 sacks, the team lead.
LB Elijah Melendez: a team-high 57 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Auburn is 4-3 overall and 2-3 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 11th in SEC.
The season so far: W 43-8 vs Southern Miss Golden Eagles (Sept. 12), L 39-44 vs Florida Gators (Sept. 19), W 21-15 vs Vanderbilt Commodores (Sept. 26), L 14-24 at Tennessee Volunteers (Oct. 3), W 27-24 at Georgia Bulldogs (Oct. 17), L 17-38 vs LSU Tigers (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Auburn (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at No. 12 Ole Miss (5-2, 3-2 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12:45 p.m. ET, Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, Oxford, Miss., SEC Network.
Last time out. Auburn lost 38-17 to LSU at home on Oct. 24. Brown was 15 of 24 for 160 yards and ran for a touchdown, and Singleton caught four balls for 64 yards. The week before, Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia 27-24 on a field goal as time expired.
Ole Miss lost 34-27 at Texas on Oct. 24. Chambliss threw two touchdowns, and Alexander caught eight balls for 87 yards.
Players to watch. Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown does a little bit of everything. He's 134 of 209 for 1,365 yards, eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, and he's also the leading rusher with 471 yards and six scores. Keshaun Singleton leads the receivers with 36 catches for 431 yards. Linebacker Elijah Melendez leads the defense in tackles with 57 and in sacks with four.
Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has thrown the most passes in every Rebel game. He's 167 of 262 for 1,926 yards, 16 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Running back Kewan Lacy has 388 yards and five touchdowns. Deuce Alexander leads the receivers with 43 catches for 610 yards and five scores. On defense, end Blake Purchase has 4.5 sacks and linebacker Keaton Thomas has 45 tackles.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Brown and Chambliss have each thrown the most passes in every game for their teams, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Alex Golesh came to Auburn from South Florida and was hired on Nov. 30, 2025. His Tigers run a balanced offense, and the defense has been the strength, with 16 sacks.
Pete Golding is in his first full season as Ole Miss head coach. His offense has scored on every red zone trip, first in FBS. Defensive tackle Will Echoles said, "Stopping the run has been an issue for us at times this year, but it's gotten better." He had reason to smile after the Rebels held Missouri to 39 rushing yards on 26 carries.
Storylines. Brown against the Ole Miss defense is the headline. If he can run and throw the way he did at Georgia, Auburn can hang around. Chambliss wants to bounce back after a 25 of 52 day at Texas, and Alexander is his go-to target. Melendez will try to crash the pocket, and both teams' big guys up front will decide who controls the clock.
Fun and true. Auburn won the 2010 national championship, the season Cam Newton led the Tigers, and Jordan-Hare Stadium is listed at 87,451. Ole Miss was founded in 1893 and won six SEC titles: 1947, 1954, 1955, 1960, 1962 and 1963. Last year the Rebels went 13-2. In this series, Auburn won 31-20 in 2021, and Ole Miss won 48-34 in 2022 and 28-21 in 2023.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Langston Fairbanks, Ole Miss's insider. Here's what I said:
"Bless your heart, Langston. I brought lemonade. You get one paragraph per glass."
"Byrum Brown leads us in throwing and running. In my reenactments, I play him. Obviously."
"I sipped my lemonade with great dignity after LSU. But that Georgia kick? I'm still shrieking 'War Eagle.'"
"Sugar, read it at halftime."
"I'm dressed as Aubie. Langston is dressed as a library."
"That's sweet, Langston. War Eagle, bless your heart."
And the last word from Langston: "Miss Bellamy, whatever happens, dinner is on me afterward. We'll say grace first."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Vaught-Hemingway Stadium opened in 1915 and is listed at 64,038 seats. Since 2023, the Rebels are 25-1 at home. Halloween in the Grove means tents, chandeliers and plenty of red-and-blue costumes. Auburn fans will bring their orange and blue, and Lacey will bring a pitcher.

report.title: Chomp in Atlanta: No. 17 Florida Takes On No. 3 Georgia on Halloween
report.byline: Dax Marchetti · Florida Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
That play had scales! I'm Dax Marchetti, and I'm your Florida insider. I'm a herpetology minor, and I compare every defense to a reptile species. Fair warning: I classify every opponent as a species, lovingly, and my reptile index is weirdly accurate. On the podcast, that segment is called Reptile Index. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Gainesville, built in 1930 with a listed capacity of 88,548. The playing surface is Steve Spurrier–Florida Field, the band is the Pride of the Sunshine, and the fight song is "The Orange and Blue." The program claims national titles from 1996, 2006 and 2008. The last five seasons went 6-7, 6-7, 5-7, 8-5 and 4-8, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about the Swamp. It's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jon Sumrall leads the Gators, and CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Nov. 30, 2025. It's his first season in Gainesville.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 39.6 points per game and allowing 28.3.

Players to Know
QB Aaron Philo: 105 of 149, 1,341 yards, 9 touchdowns, 3 interceptions.
RB Jadan Baugh: 763 yards on 135 carries, 13 touchdowns.
WR Dallas Wilson: 29 catches, 403 yards, 3 touchdowns.
LB Jayden Woods: 4.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Myles Graham: a team-high 48 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Florida is 5-2 overall and 3-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 4th in SEC. We're ranked No. 17 in ESPN's rankings this week.
The season so far: W 66-21 vs Florida Atlantic Owls (Sept. 5), W 52-3 vs Campbell Fighting Camels (Sept. 12), W 44-39 at Auburn Tigers (Sept. 19), W 52-28 vs Ole Miss Rebels (Sept. 26), L 17-45 at Missouri Tigers (Oct. 3), L 19-38 vs South Carolina Gamecocks (Oct. 10), W 27-24 at Texas Longhorns (Oct. 17).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
No. 17 Florida (5-2, 3-2 SEC) vs. No. 3 Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Atlanta, Ga. (neutral site), ABC.
Last time out. Both teams had an open date last week, so everybody is rested.
Florida's last game was a 27-24 win at Texas on Oct. 17. Jones went 22 of 35 for 155 yards and two touchdowns, and Baugh ran 25 times for 91 yards and a score.
Georgia's last game was a 27-24 loss to Auburn on Oct. 17. Stockton threw for 272 yards and two touchdowns, Phillips ran for 68 yards and a score, and Dandridge caught four balls for 88 yards.
Players to watch. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 117 of 158 for 1,570 yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. Dwight Phillips Jr. leads the rushers with 348 yards, and Craig Dandridge leads the receivers with 310 yards. Linebacker Raylen Wilson leads the defense with 44 tackles and four sacks, and defensive back KJ Bolden has an interception.
Florida running back Jadan Baugh is the engine, with 763 yards and 13 touchdowns on 135 carries. Aaron Philo leads the team in passing at 105 of 149 for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions, and Tramell Jones Jr. threw the most passes at Texas. Dallas Wilson leads the receivers with 29 catches for 403 yards. Linebacker Myles Graham leads the defense with 48 tackles, Jayden Woods has 4.5 sacks, and safety DJ Coleman has two interceptions.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Stockton has thrown the most passes for Georgia in every game. Philo did it for Florida in the first six games and Jones did it at Texas, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Kirby Smart leads Georgia, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 6, 2015. His teams went 14-1, 15-0, 13-1, 11-3 and 12-2 over the last five seasons, and Georgia claims national titles from 2021 and 2022. This year's Bulldogs score 43.0 points a game and allow 15.9.
Jon Sumrall is in his first season leading Florida, and CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 30, 2025. His Gators already have five wins after going 4-8 last season, and they score 39.6 points a game with a ground game that gains 194.3 yards a game.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Baugh and the Florida big guys up front against a Georgia defense that allows 15.9 points a game and has 22 sacks. On the other side, Stockton faces a Florida defense that also has 22 sacks. Georgia has won eight of the last 10 meetings, including 24-20 last year, so Florida has some history to change, and Georgia wants to bounce back from the Auburn loss.
Fun and true. Florida claims national titles from 1996, 2006 and 2008, its fight song is "The Orange and Blue," and its band is the Pride of the Sunshine. Georgia claims titles from 1942, 1980, 2021 and 2022, its band is the Georgia Redcoat Marching Band, and its fight song is "Hail to Georgia." Florida's last win in this series came in 2020, 44-28.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Thaddeus "Thad" Okafor-Brandt, Georgia's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thanks, Thad. I've been studying your defense all week. I'm classifying it as a snapping turtle."
"Very much so. Snapping turtles are patient, and they don't let go."
"Thirteen rushing touchdowns, Thad. Jadan Baugh is a crocodile in the red zone."
"Winning in Austin? That play had scales."
"Coach Sumrall is building a whole new swamp ecosystem. It's thriving."
"I'm dressing as an alligator. Obviously."
"Whatever happens, Thad, dinner's on me afterward. We'll say grace first."
And the last word from Thad: "Deal, Dax. I'll bring the music."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
This one is in Atlanta, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, so both fan bases will split the building. Expect orange and blue on one side and red and black on the other, plus plenty of Halloween costumes. Back home, Florida plays at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, the Swamp, listed at 88,548, and Georgia plays at Sanford Stadium, between the hedges, listed at 92,746.

report.title: Cowbells in Austin: Mississippi State Rings Its Way Into Texas on Halloween Night
report.byline: Wade Pettus · Mississippi State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Ring it if you mean it. (Ding.) Howdy, Bulldog people. I'm Wade Pettus, poultry-science graduate, and I chart Air Raid concepts on the back of feed-store receipts. I have a drawer full of them. It has never once been wrong about a third down. Every week I'll bring you the players, the matchup, the history and a little gentle Starkville deadpan. When we win, I ring the cowbell exactly once for every point we scored, no matter how long it takes. When we lose, the cowbell goes in a sock, out of respect. I believe football is best explained slowly, the way you'd explain a good hen house. I'm glad you're here.

The School in 60 Seconds
Mississippi State plays in the SEC and won the league championship in 1941, plus a division title in 1998. The Bulldogs have made 27 bowl appearances and produced 38 All-Americans, 171 All-SEC selections and 124 NFL players, 11 of them first-round draft choices. Our home, Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field, is the second-oldest stadium in FBS. CFBD dates it to 1914 and lists capacity at 61,337. I wrote that on a receipt, too.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jeff Lebby was hired Nov. 26, 2023, and this is his third season. He came from Oklahoma, where he was offensive coordinator for Brent Venables's first two seasons, 2022 and 2023. His first two years in Starkville went 7-18. This offseason he brought back Zach Arnett as defensive coordinator, Arnett's second stint in that job here.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 30.0 points per game and allowing 27.7.

Players to Know
QB Kamario Taylor: 104 of 159, 1,460 yards, 17 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Fluff Bothwell: 514 yards on 91 carries, 3 touchdowns.
WR Anthony Evans III: 53 catches, 647 yards, 5 touchdowns.
DL Jaray Bledsoe: 2.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Tyler Lockhart: a team-high 48 tackles.
A prayer for Kamario Taylor: the quarterback is out for the season, and we're praying for a full recovery.

The Conference Picture
Mississippi State is 4-3 overall and 2-3 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 11th in SEC.
The season so far: W 62-13 vs UL Monroe Warhawks (Sept. 5), W 38-13 at Minnesota Golden Gophers (Sept. 12), W 41-34 at South Carolina Gamecocks (Sept. 19), W 31-24 vs Missouri Tigers (Sept. 26), L 23-56 vs Alabama Crimson Tide (Oct. 3), L 0-31 at LSU Tigers (Oct. 17), L 15-23 vs Oklahoma Sooners (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Mississippi State (4-3, 2-3 SEC) at No. 11 Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 p.m. Central), DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin, Texas, ESPN.
Last time out. Mississippi State lost 23-15 to Oklahoma at home. Taylor started but left in the first half. Puckett went 17 of 24 for 158 yards and a touchdown, Bothwell ran for 111 yards, and Sanfrisco Magee had three catches for 65 yards and a touchdown.
Texas beat Ole Miss 34-27. Brown ran 23 times for 157 yards, and Wingo caught seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Manning threw for 212 yards.
Players to watch. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor was 104 of 159 for 1,460 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions, but he is out for the season. Parker Puckett takes over. Running back Fluff Bothwell has 514 yards and three touchdowns, and wide receiver Anthony Evans III leads the team with 53 catches for 647 yards. On defense, linebacker Tyler Lockhart has 48 tackles, and Jaray Bledsoe has 2.5 sacks.
Texas quarterback Arch Manning is 124 of 196 for 1,507 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Running back Raleek Brown has 422 yards and five touchdowns. Wide receiver Ryan Wingo has 33 catches for 456 yards and four touchdowns. On defense, Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks, and Jelani McDonald has 54 tackles.
Availability. No official SEC availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Mississippi State announced that Taylor will miss the rest of the season with a foot injury that needs surgery, and he is expected to make a full recovery. "Missing the rest of this season is hard to accept, but I know God has a plan," Taylor said. For Texas, Simmons hurt his ankle against Florida and missed the Ole Miss game.
The coaches. Jeff Lebby is in his third season at Mississippi State. "Nobody wants to be on that field more than Kamario," he said. "He's the ultimate teammate and competitor." Lebby is also weighing Puckett and AJ Swann at quarterback.
Steve Sarkisian is in his sixth season at Texas. He loved how his defense played without Simmons. "Nobody was just waiting for Colin to make a play," he said. "It was all 11 guys playing really well collectively together." He also said, "Believe me, we want Colin back as bad as anybody else."
Storylines. Taylor had huge games in wins over Minnesota, South Carolina and Missouri, and he says he is all in with his teammates. "Starkville is home," he said. Puckett now gets his chance. For Texas, McDonald played his best game of the year against Ole Miss, according to Sarkisian Brown carried the load with 23 carries and will try to do it again.
Fun and true. These teams have met the last two years. Texas won 35-13 in 2024 and 45-38 in 2025.
Mississippi State started this season 4-0, with wins over UL Monroe, at Minnesota, at South Carolina and over Missouri. After Saturday, the Bulldogs play three straight home games.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Caro Whitfield, Texas's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thank you, ma'am. I'll ring once for you. Politely. (ding.)"
"One hundred fifty-seven for Brown. My cowbell is processing it quietly."
"I wrote Puckett's first road start on a receipt. I'm keeping it."
And the last word from Caro: "Keep it, darling. Receipts are good business. Hook 'em."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium opened in 1924 and is listed at 100,119 seats. Texas began playing football in 1893 and claims national titles from 1963, 1969, 1970 and 2005.
Mississippi State plays at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field, the second-oldest stadium in FBS, dating to 1914, with room for 61,337. The Bulldogs won the SEC championship in 1941, and their fans bring the cowbells everywhere.

report.title: Tigers Cross the Border: Missouri Visits Arkansas on Halloween Night

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Show me the tape! I'm Delphine Arceneaux-Moss, and I'm your Missouri insider. I'm a J-school style beat reporter who breaks news and blitz tendencies. Fair warning: I "break news" on obvious things, live, with a fake news ticker sound. On the podcast, that segment is called Breaking News. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Memorial Stadium in Columbia, built in 1927 with a listed capacity of 71,168. The playing surface is Faurot Field, the band is Marching Mizzou, and the fight song is "Every True Son, Fight Tiger." The program claims a national title from 1960. The last five seasons went 6-7, 6-7, 11-2, 10-3 and 8-5, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about Homecoming, which the NCAA recognizes as starting at Missouri in 1911. Breaking news: it's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Eli Drinkwitz leads the Tigers, and CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Dec. 9, 2019. He grew up in Alma, Ark., so this week's trip is a homecoming of its own.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 31.1 points per game and allowing 19.6.

Players to Know

Arkansas' last game was a 31-21 win at Vanderbilt on Oct. 17, its first SEC win in two years. Jackson went 21 of 31 for 251 yards and ran for a touchdown. Antonio Jordan, a Warren, Ark., native, had career highs with five catches for 74 yards.

Arkansas center Caden Kitler, a team captain, is listed as the starter, though Kash Courtney started at Vanderbilt. Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said wide receiver Blair is back from a hamstring injury and will be fully available. Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy has been sidelined since an offseason accident.
The coaches. Drinkwitz grew up in Alma, Ark., and has led Missouri since 2020. "I think the SEC is better when Arkansas is good," he said last fall.
Ryan Silverfield became the 35th head coach in Arkansas history the morning after last year's game. He coached Memphis against Missouri in 2023. "We know that they're going to be sound and well-coached," he said. He praised the Missouri wide zone running game and said it gets stronger in the fourth quarter.
Storylines. Simmons faced his old school, Ole Miss, two weeks ago, and he keeps it simple. "It's just another game for me," he said. Roberts has carried the load with Hardy out. For Arkansas, Jordan showed he can make plays when Marshall is out, and now the Hogs may have both.

"Show me the tape! Breaking news, Bubba: it is Halloween, and there is a trophy on the field."
"Breaking news: the Hogs are feeling good."

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Boomer! (You say Sooner.) Louder, Norman, I can't hear you over the Schooner wheels. I'm Savannah Redbird-Lowe, former Oklahoma rodeo princess, and I read a defense the way I used to read a barrel pattern: clean turn, tight pocket, no tipped barrels. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the storylines and the history, told straight with a little Plains-state sass. When we win, you'll hear me holler "Boomer!" and wait for you. When we lose, I'll lift my chin and tell you we'll roll the Schooner again. Saddle up, y'all.

The School in 60 Seconds
Oklahoma football started in 1895. The program claims seven national championships (1950, 1955, 1956, 1974, 1975, 1985 and 2000), 50 conference titles and seven Heisman Trophy winners. The Sooners also hold the Division I record for consecutive wins, 47 straight, and Oklahoma is the only program where four different coaches have won more than 100 games. These days we're an SEC program. Home is Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman, listed at 86,112 seats in the CFBD venue file. Last season the Sooners went 10-3. The School in 60 Seconds

We claim four consensus national championships: 1963, 1969, 1970 and 2005, and the program has been led by three Hall of Fame coaches. report.title: Charts, Crabs and the Illini: Illinois Brings Its Big Oregon Win to College Park
report.byline: Margery Vandermolen · Illinois Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good afternoon, class! Oh, sorry. Old habits. Welcome, Illini Nation. I'm Margery Vandermolen, your Illinois insider, and I explain football the way your best-loved teacher explained long division: patiently, cheerfully and with a lot of charts. I'm a prairie-state numbers whiz. I've crunched the numbers on just about everything, and the numbers always say the same thing: orange. You'll get corn jokes from me. You'll get chart jokes. Sometimes you'll get a corn chart, which is both. And every Saturday morning I'll ask you the same question: "Orange you glad it's Saturday?" When something wonderful happens on the field, there's only one thing to say: "Oskee-wow-wow!" Each week I'll give you the players, the coaches and the matchup, explained clearly enough that Grandma and the grandkids can both follow along.

The School in 60 Seconds
Here's your history lesson, and yes, it will be on the test. Illinois is a founding member of the Big Ten and claims five national championships: 1914, 1919, 1923, 1927 and 1951. The 1923 title team opened Memorial Stadium and introduced the world to Harold "Red" Grange, the Galloping Ghost. On Oct. 18, 1924, at the stadium's dedication game, Grange scored four touchdowns against Michigan in the first 12 minutes. He ran for a fifth and threw for a sixth in a 39-14 win. ESPN once chose the legendary No. 77 as the greatest player in college football history. The stadium honors University of Illinois students who died in World War I. Illinois also claims 15 Big Ten titles. High fives all around.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bret Bielema was named the 26th head coach in Illinois history on Dec. 19, 2020. He's an Illinois native, and he said at the time, "Illinois and the Big Ten is home for me". One of his early wins was a nine-overtime victory at Penn State in 2021, the longest game in college football history.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 30.3 points per game and allowing 25.3.

Players to Know
QB Katin Houser: 122 of 184, 1,440 yards, 12 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Aidan Laughery: 514 yards on 75 carries, 2 touchdowns.
WR Collin Dixon: 54 catches, 678 yards, 10 touchdowns.
LB Ean Rhea: 2 sacks, the team lead.
DB Matthew Bailey: a team-high 49 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Illinois is 4-3 overall and 2-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 8th in Big Ten.
The season so far: W 42-23 vs UAB Blazers (Sept. 3), L 27-31 vs Duke Blue Devils (Sept. 12), W 48-10 vs Southern Illinois Salukis (Sept. 19), L 19-42 at Ohio State Buckeyes (Sept. 26), L 17-24 vs Purdue Boilermakers (Oct. 3), W 38-37 (OT) at Michigan State Spartans (Oct. 10), W 21-10 vs Oregon Ducks (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Illinois (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) at Maryland (2-5, 0-4 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, SECU Stadium, College Park, Md., FS1.
Last time out. Illinois beat Oregon 21-10 at home on Oct. 24. Laughery ran 13 times for 123 yards and a touchdown, and Dixon caught six passes for 65 yards and a score.
Maryland didn't play last week. Its last game was a 37-30 loss to Rutgers on Oct. 17, when Washington threw for 263 yards and two touchdowns and Durr caught six passes for 104 yards.
Players to watch. Illinois quarterback Katin Houser threw the most passes in the first six Illini games. He's 122 of 184 for 1,440 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. Michael Clayton II threw the most in the win over Oregon, going 11 of 18 with two touchdown throws. Wide receiver Collin Dixon is the go-to target, with 54 catches for 678 yards and 10 touchdowns. Aidan Laughery leads the rushers with 514 yards. On defense, defensive back Matthew Bailey has 49 tackles.
Maryland quarterback Malik Washington has thrown the most passes in all seven Terrapin games. He's 155 of 261 for 1,615 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. Chris Durr Jr. leads the receivers with 52 catches for 580 yards. DeJuan Williams leads the rushers with 281 yards and three scores. Linebacker Daniel Wingate has 44 tackles, and linebacker Zion Elee has 3.5 sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Houser threw the most passes for Illinois in six games, but Clayton did against Oregon, so watch the teams' pregame notes for who takes the first snap. Washington has thrown the most passes in every Maryland game.
The coaches. Bret Bielema was named the 26th head coach in Illinois history on Dec. 19, 2020. He's an Illinois native, and one of his early wins was a nine-overtime thriller at Penn State in 2021, the longest game in college football history. His team has already won 38-37 in overtime at Michigan State this year.
Maryland has new leadership this week. Mike Locksley stepped down as head coach last week, and co-defensive coordinator Aazaar Abdul-Rahim was named interim head coach. Abdul-Rahim is a Washington, D.C., native in his second stint with the Terps, and Saturday is his first game in charge. This year's Terps score 28.3 points a game, including a 62-0 win over Hampton and a 38-14 win at UConn.
Storylines. The matchup to circle is Dixon against a Maryland defense that allows 33.3 points a game. On the other side, Washington loves to throw it, and he went 30 of 44 for 359 yards and three touchdowns against Virginia Tech. Both teams run the ball well, too. Illinois gains 5.2 yards a carry and Maryland gains 4.5, so the big guys up front on both sides will be busy.
Fun and true. Illinois is a founding member of the Big Ten and claims five national championships, from 1914 to 1951. On Oct. 18, 1924, Harold "Red" Grange scored four touchdowns against Michigan in the first 12 minutes of the Memorial Stadium dedication game. These two teams have split their last four meetings, and Illinois won 24-6 last year. Back in 2018, Maryland won a wild one, 63-33.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Abigail "Abby" Chesapeake, Maryland's insider. Here's what I said:
"Good afternoon, class! Orange you glad it's Saturday?"
"Ten touchdown catches for Dixon. I made a chart, and the column went right off the top of the poster board."
"Oskee-wow-wow! I hugged three strangers and a mascot."
"Abby, after the game, I'm making you a chart of everything I learned today."
And the last word from Abby: "And I'm sprinkling Old Bay on it. Then we'll say grace and eat. Old Bay on that!"

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
SECU Stadium opened in 1950 and seats 51,802. The Mighty Sound of Maryland band will be on hand, and if you visit, ask somebody about Testudo, the diamondback terrapin who's at the heart of campus tradition. A Halloween noon kickoff should mean plenty of turtle shells in the stands.

report.title: Hoosier Hysteria, Football Edition: Indiana Hosts Minnesota and Floyd's Keepers in Bloomington
report.byline: Mallory Penhallow · Indiana Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well hello, Hoosier Nation, and welcome! I'm Mallory Penhallow, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and these days I run a 40-tab efficiency model on everything this football team does. I travel with the team, I live with the numbers, and yes, the clicker is rhinestone. My pageant answer to every question is the same: "It's the explosives, darling." Each week I give one opponent my honorary Miss Congeniality sash. It goes to whoever I roast the hardest, and I always do it with love. When we win, you get the full pageant wave. When we lose, it's "grace in defeat". and then I quietly open tab 41.

The School in 60 Seconds
Before Curt Cignetti showed up, Indiana had the most losses of any program in college football, 713 of them over 130-plus years. It had won three bowl games in its whole history, and the last one came in 1991. Then 2025 happened. The Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. The last team to win 16 games without a loss was Yale in 1894. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman, and he scored the deciding touchdown himself on a 12-yard run on fourth-and-4. Cignetti's quote still sounds like an acceptance speech to me: "We won the national championship at Indiana University. It can be done."

The Coach and the Scheme
Cignetti was hired on Nov. 30, 2023. Part of his rebuild came from bringing 13 transfers with him from his old school, James Madison.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 33.6 points per game and allowing 12.0.

Players to Know
QB Josh Hoover: 116 of 187, 1,741 yards, 18 touchdowns, 1 interception.
RB Turbo Richard: 711 yards on 106 carries, 6 touchdowns.
WR Charlie Becker: 42 catches, 726 yards, 8 touchdowns.
DL Tobi Osunsanmi: 9 sacks, the team lead.
LB Isaiah Jones: a team-high 61 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Indiana is 7-1 overall and 4-1 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 3rd in Big Ten. We're ranked No. 4 in ESPN's rankings this week.
The season so far: W 52-16 vs North Texas Mean Green (Sept. 5), W 55-0 vs Howard Bison (Sept. 12), W 38-0 vs Western Kentucky Hilltoppers (Sept. 19), W 29-23 vs Northwestern Wildcats (Sept. 25), W 47-15 at Rutgers Scarlet Knights (Oct. 3), W 20-17 at Nebraska Cornhuskers (Oct. 10), L 15-19 vs Ohio State Buckeyes (Oct. 17), W 13-6 (OT) at Michigan Wolverines (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Minnesota (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) at No. 4 Indiana (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, Ind., CBS.
Last time out. Minnesota beat Iowa 13-10 at home on Oct. 24, on Homecoming, and took back Floyd of Rosedale, the bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. Lindsey threw for 137 yards, and Tracy caught seven balls for 45 yards. The defense did the heavy lifting, holding Iowa to 10 points.
Indiana won 13-6 in overtime at Michigan on Oct. 24. Hoover went 8 of 18 for 81 yards, Richard ran 19 times for 68 yards, and the defense held Michigan to six points. It came one week after a 19-15 loss to Ohio State.
Players to watch. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 116 of 187 for 1,741 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. Turbo Richard leads the rushers with 711 yards and six scores, and Charlie Becker leads the receivers with 42 catches for 726 yards and eight touchdowns. On defense, Tobi Osunsanmi has nine sacks, and linebacker Isaiah Jones leads the team with 61 tackles.
Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 141 of 222 for 1,472 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. TJ Thomas leads the rushers with 325 yards, and Javon Tracy leads the receivers with 39 catches for 420 yards. Linebacker Maverick Baranowski leads the defense with 51 tackles, and TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hoover has thrown the most passes for Indiana in every game, and Lindsey has done the same for Minnesota, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Curt Cignetti was hired at Indiana on Nov. 30, 2023. In 2025, the Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. This year's team allows only 12.0 points a game.
P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017, after coaching Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and coached receivers for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His defense is the strength this year, stingy against the throw and good on third down.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Becker and Hoover against a Minnesota defense that allows only 159.7 passing yards a game. On the other side, the Gophers need their big guys up front to open running room against an Indiana defense that allows very little on the ground. Minnesota won the two recent meetings in this series, 38-31 in 2018 and 35-14 in 2021, so the Gophers have some happy memories. Indiana wants to stay near the top of the Big Ten race.
Fun and true. Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Gophers claim seven national championships. Indiana's 2025 team was the first to win 16 games without a loss since Yale in 1894, and quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Torvald "Tor" Engebretsen, Minnesota's insider. Here's what I said:
"Welcome to Bloomington, Tor! Hello, Hoosier Nation!"
"That's very sweet. I'll wear it over the sash."
"Nine sacks for Tobi Osunsanmi, Tor. It's the explosives, darling."
"Grace in defeat one week, grit on the road the next. Full pageant wave."
"Coach Cignetti said it best: 'It can be done.' I have it on a pillow."
"I'm dressing as Miss Congeniality. Wait, that's the sash. I'm giving it to you, Tor, with love."
"Deal, Tor. And keep the coat warm for me."
And the last word from Tor: "Whatever happens, Mallory, the cocoa's on me afterward. We'll say grace first."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
A Halloween afternoon in Bloomington means cream and crimson costumes in the stands at Memorial Stadium, and a CBS crowd watching at home. Minnesota fans just finished Homecoming week in Minneapolis, so their voices may still be a little hoarse. Back home, the Gophers play at Huntington Bank Stadium, listed at 50,850 seats.

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, neighbors. I'm Orrin Kalvelage, your Iowa insider. I grew up on a farm near Iowa City and haven't missed a home opener in my life. I own one black-and-gold sweater, and I wear it with pride every single week. My wife says it needs retiring. I say it's got plenty of Saturdays left in it.

Fair warning: Old Bay is my universal answer to every problem. On the podcast, my segment is called Old Bay Index, and I season each stat to taste. My rules are simple. report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Greetings, Wolverines, and welcome. I am Augustin Hartwell, but everybody calls me Gus. You'll know me by the maize sweater, the engineering-school pin and the coffee mug that says VICTORS. I travel with this team, and I label my data with fight-song lyrics. "Champions of the West" is a perfectly good column header, and I expect Dr. Ingrid Solvang, our Big Ten expert, to accept it. My motto is "Hail to the spreadsheet." When we win, I belt out "Hail to the Victors," off-key and proud. When we lose: "Victors. valiant. later." Then I head to the library.

The School in 60 Seconds
Michigan played its first game on May 30, 1879, and it has more wins than any other program in college football. The Wolverines claim 12 national championships, most recently in 2023. That 2023 team went 15-0, won the program's 45th Big Ten title, and beat Washington 34-13 for the national title. Three Wolverines have won the Heisman: Tom Harmon (1940), Desmond Howard (1991) and Charles Woodson (1997). Michigan Stadium has been home since 1927 and set the stadium's attendance record of 115,109 against Notre Dame on Sept. 7, 2013. Official sources list two different capacities, 107,601 and 109,901, so we note both.

The Coach and the Scheme
Kyle Whittingham was named Michigan's 22nd head coach on Dec. 26, 2025, with a five-year contract that runs through 2030. He spent 21 seasons as Utah's head coach, went 177-88 there, and had eight seasons with 10 or more wins. That makes him the 22nd head coach in a program history spanning 146 years, and he took over after Michigan fired Sherrone Moore. The standard he inherits is enormous: Michigan has more all-time wins than any program in college football, and the record crowd at Michigan Stadium is 115,109, set against Notre Dame on Sept. 7, 2013.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 20.3 points per game and allowing 15.7.

Players to Know

Running back Jordan Marshall leads the rushers with 319 yards and four touchdowns. JJ Buchanan is the top receiver with 33 catches for 539 yards and four scores. On defense, linebacker Troy Bowles has 55 tackles and end John Henry Daley has four sacks.
Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan leads the team at 74 of 127 for 1,066 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions. AJ Surace threw the most passes against Northwestern last week. Running back Antwan Raymond has 648 yards and six touchdowns, and receiver KJ Duff has been a highlight machine with 45 catches for 774 yards and nine touchdowns. Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Underwood threw the most passes in Michigan's first six games and Carr did against Indiana, while Lonergan and Surace have traded that role for Rutgers, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Kyle Whittingham was named Michigan's 22nd head coach on Dec. 26, 2025, after 21 seasons at Utah, where he went 177-88 with eight seasons of 10 or more wins. His Wolverines are built on defense, allowing 15.7 points a game.
Greg Schiano returned to Rutgers on Nov. 30, 2019, for his second stint. His team is the least penalized in FBS at 28.7 penalty yards a game.
Storylines. The big story is Raymond against a Michigan defense that allows only 2.8 yards a carry. Something has to give. On the other side, Buchanan and the Michigan offense want to get rolling after a long day against Indiana. Michigan's big guys up front will try to push around a Rutgers defense that gives up 5.8 yards a carry. And Duff will be looking for touchdown number 10.
Fun and true. The very first college football game was played in New Brunswick on Nov. 6, 1869, and Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4. Michigan played its first game on May 30, 1879, and has more wins than any program in college football. Three Wolverines have won the Heisman: Tom Harmon in 1940, Desmond Howard in 1991 and Charles Woodson in 1997.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Vinny Scolari, Rutgers's insider. Here's what I said:

"Victors. valiant. later. I spent Sunday in the library."

"I'm dressing as a spreadsheet. Very scary for opponents."

Fastball inside, change-up away, and then you get 'em. I travel and live with this team. I also maintain that Ann Arbor is just a suburb with a stadium. That's not a stat. That's a lifestyle.

Pat Fitzgerald is in his first season as head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 1, 2025. He was head coach at Northwestern from 2006 to 2023. report.title: Gophers on the Road: Floyd's Keepers Head to Bloomington to Face No. 4 Indiana
report.byline: Torvald "Tor" Engebretsen · Minnesota Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hello there. I'm Torvald Engebretsen, Tor to my friends, and I'm your Minnesota insider. I grew up in Minneapolis ice-fishing with my grandpa, and I know the history of every rivalry trophy this program plays for. Minnesota has more trophies than I have winter coats, and I have a lot of winter coats.

I'm dry, I'm earnest and I'm polite, but get me started on rivalry lore and I'm unstoppable. Here's my promise: every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you so. I celebrate our players as young people first, I respect every opponent, even the ones from south of the border, and I thank God for crisp autumn Saturdays. Cold enough for ya? Good.

The School in 60 Seconds
Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Golden Gophers claim seven national championships. Four of them, in 1936, 1940, 1941 and 1960, came from the major wire-service polls. Since 2009, home has been Huntington Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. CFBD lists 50,850 seats.

The last five seasons have been sturdy: 9-4, 9-4, 6-7, 8-5 and 8-5. Four winning seasons in five years. My grandpa would call that a good catch.

The Coach and the Scheme
P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017. CFBD lists his hire date as Jan. 6, 2017. He coached Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and spent time with the San Francisco 49ers. He was a receivers coach at Northern Illinois, Rutgers and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In 2019 he led the Gophers to one of their best seasons in half a century.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 26.6 points per game and allowing 20.1.

Players to Know
QB Drake Lindsey: 141 of 222, 1,472 yards, 9 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.
RB TJ Thomas: 325 yards on 57 carries, 1 touchdown.
WR Javon Tracy: 39 catches, 420 yards, 1 touchdown.
DL TJ Bush Jr.: 4 sacks, the team lead.
LB Maverick Baranowski: a team-high 51 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Minnesota is 5-2 overall and 3-1 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 4th in Big Ten.
The season so far: W 59-7 vs Eastern Illinois Panthers (Sept. 3), L 13-38 vs Mississippi State Bulldogs (Sept. 12), W 41-7 vs Akron Zips (Sept. 19), W 27-24 at Washington Huskies (Sept. 26), W 20-14 vs Michigan Wolverines (Oct. 3), L 13-41 at Purdue Boilermakers (Oct. 10), W 13-10 vs Iowa Hawkeyes (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Minnesota (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) at No. 4 Indiana (7-1, 4-1 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, Ind., CBS.
Last time out. Minnesota beat Iowa 13-10 at home on Oct. 24, on Homecoming, and took back Floyd of Rosedale, the bronze pig trophy introduced in 1935. Lindsey threw for 137 yards, and Tracy caught seven balls for 45 yards. The defense did the heavy lifting, holding Iowa to 10 points.
Indiana won 13-6 in overtime at Michigan on Oct. 24. Hoover went 8 of 18 for 81 yards, Richard ran 19 times for 68 yards, and the defense held Michigan to six points. It came one week after a 19-15 loss to Ohio State.
Players to watch. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 116 of 187 for 1,741 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. Turbo Richard leads the rushers with 711 yards and six scores, and Charlie Becker leads the receivers with 42 catches for 726 yards and eight touchdowns. On defense, Tobi Osunsanmi has nine sacks, and linebacker Isaiah Jones leads the team with 61 tackles.
Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 141 of 222 for 1,472 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. TJ Thomas leads the rushers with 325 yards, and Javon Tracy leads the receivers with 39 catches for 420 yards. Linebacker Maverick Baranowski leads the defense with 51 tackles, and TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hoover has thrown the most passes for Indiana in every game, and Lindsey has done the same for Minnesota, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Curt Cignetti was hired at Indiana on Nov. 30, 2023. In 2025, the Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship. This year's team allows only 12.0 points a game.
P.J. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017, after coaching Western Michigan from 2013 to 2016. He played receiver at Northern Illinois and coached receivers for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. His defense is the strength this year, stingy against the throw and good on third down.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Becker and Hoover against a Minnesota defense that allows only 159.7 passing yards a game. On the other side, the Gophers need their big guys up front to open running room against an Indiana defense that allows very little on the ground. Minnesota won the two recent meetings in this series, 38-31 in 2018 and 35-14 in 2021, so the Gophers have some happy memories. Indiana wants to stay near the top of the Big Ten race.
Fun and true. Minnesota started playing football in 1882 and has been in the Big Ten since the league began in 1896 as the Western Conference. The Gophers claim seven national championships. Indiana's 2025 team was the first to win 16 games without a loss since Yale in 1894, and quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Mallory Penhallow, Indiana's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thank you, Mallory. I brought cocoa, and a spare coat in case you get chilly."
"And I should mention we're bringing home a bronze pig. Well, it's already home. We won it Saturday."
"Maverick Baranowski has 51 tackles. In Minnesota, we call that a good catch."
"Floyd is back in Minneapolis. I may have hugged a pig. A bronze one. Respectfully."
"Coach Fleck rows the boat. We all row together."
"I'm dressing as Floyd of Rosedale. Bronze paint and everything."
"Whatever happens, Mallory, the cocoa's on me afterward. We'll say grace first."
And the last word from Mallory: "Deal, Tor. And keep the coat warm for me."

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Yo, Rutgers! How you doin'? Welcome! Vinny Scolari here, your Rutgers insider, born and raised off Exit 9 of the New Jersey Turnpike. I give directions by Turnpike exit for everything, and I mean everything. Where's the stadium? Exit 9. How am I feeling after a loss? Somewhere around Exit 7A. I grade every Big Ten trench battle like a boardwalk arm-wrestle: who pushed in, who flinched, who walked away with the stuffed animal. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I order a sub big enough for the whole studio. Six feet. Everybody eats. When we lose, I say "Fuhgeddaboudit". and then I can't. I really can't. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Jersey-style. "Exit 9 never lies."

The School in 60 Seconds
Here's something every college football fan should know. The very first college football game was played right in New Brunswick on Nov. 6, 1869, and Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4. That's right: the birthplace of the whole sport is off Exit 9. Home now is SHI Stadium in Piscataway, listed at 52,454. The man running the show is Greg Schiano, who came back to coach Rutgers again in December 2019. The Scarlet Knights play in the Big Ten, and every week is a heavyweight fight.

The Coach and the Scheme
Schiano's second stint began with his return on Nov. 30, 2019.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 28.7 points per game and allowing 33.3.

Players to Know
QB Dylan Lonergan: 74 of 127, 1,066 yards, 10 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.

"Six feet, Gus. Everybody eats."

"I'm dressing as a director's chair. Very supportive."
"Deal, darling. I'll bring dessert."
And the last word from Ridge: "Whatever happens, Kenzie, supper's on me. We'll say grace first."

It's Halloween at the Rose Bowl, listed at 88,565 seats, one week after UCLA's Homecoming. Back in Reno, Nevada fans just celebrated Homecoming Week and the football program's 130th birthday, since the team was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers.

report.title: Coming Soon to the Coliseum: USC Hosts Ohio State in a Halloween Classic
report.byline: Sterling Ashworth-Vance · USC Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
In a world... where one team plays every game like it's opening night... Good evening, I'm Sterling Ashworth-Vance, film buff, football historian and your guide to the Trojans. I treat every game like a premiere, because at USC, every game is one. The Coliseum is the grandest movie set in sports, and every fall our Trojans play the lead. When we win, the music swells and I say, "Roll credits." When we lose, I call it a second-act setback, because the best films always have one. Fight On!

The School in 60 Seconds
The Trojans were formed in 1888. The program has more than 860 wins and claims 11 national championships, seven of them from the AP and/or Coaches polls. We now play in the Big Ten, at the 77,500-seat Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park, right next to campus. CFBD dates the Coliseum to 1923. The last five seasons: 4-8, 11-3, 8-5, 7-6 in our first Big Ten year, and 9-4. A classic comeback arc.

The Coach and the Scheme
Lincoln Riley is in the director's chair, in his fifth season. CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2021.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 32.8 points per game and allowing 25.0.

Players to Know
QB Jayden Maiava: 183 of 274, 2,302 yards, 19 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB King Miller: 602 yards on 125 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR Kayden Dixon-Wyatt: 32 catches, 443 yards, 4 touchdowns.
S Kennedy Urlacher: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Deven Bryant: a team-high 44 tackles.

The Conference Picture
USC is 6-2 overall and 3-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 7th in Big Ten.
The season so far: W 42-26 vs San José State Spartans (Aug. 29), W 39-0 vs Fresno State Bulldogs (Sept. 4), W 49-30 vs Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (Sept. 12), W 42-35 at Rutgers Scarlet Knights (Sept. 19), L 27-41 vs Oregon Ducks (Sept. 26), W 25-21 vs Washington Huskies (Oct. 3), W 31-23 at Penn State Nittany Lions (Oct. 10), L 7-24 at Wisconsin Badgers (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
No. 2 Ohio State (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) at USC (6-2, 3-2 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Pacific), Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Los Angeles, NBC.
Last time out. Ohio State had a bye week. Its last game was a 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17, when Smith caught a touchdown and Jaylen McClain came up with a key strip sack.
USC lost 24-7 at Wisconsin. Maiava completed 31 throws for 258 yards and a touchdown to Taniela Tupou, but the Trojans could not get the run game going.
Players to watch. Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for 2,007 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions, but he is out with an elbow injury. Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair will make his first career start. Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has 52 catches for 984 yards and 12 touchdowns. Bo Jackson leads the ground game with 516 yards. On defense, safety Earl Little Jr. has 38 tackles, and Kenyatta Jackson Jr. has three sacks.
USC quarterback Jayden Maiava has completed 183 of 274 throws for 2,302 yards, 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back King Miller has 602 yards and four touchdowns, and wide receiver Kayden Dixon-Wyatt has 32 catches for 443 yards. Linebacker Deven Bryant has 44 tackles, and safety Kennedy Urlacher has three sacks.
Availability. No official availability report had been posted as of Tuesday, and Ohio State's first report is set for Wednesday night. Ryan Day said Sayin is out indefinitely but is in good spirits and should travel with the team. Day said the bye week came at a good time and he expects most of his injured defenders back. Austin Siereveld is expected to return from an illness, and Day said the Buckeyes should have "a full arsenal of guys up front." Running back Ja'Kobi Jackson remains out after foot surgery.
The coaches. Day is in his eighth season leading Ohio State. He has not said who will start at quarterback, and he said it's "definitely possible" both young players see the field. "We all need to rally around the young quarterback," he said. He also called Lincoln Riley "a tremendous mind and a really good coach."
Riley is in his fifth season at USC. His offense likes to throw it around, and this week he needs his big guys up front to open running lanes again.
Storylines. Whoever starts for Ohio State gets a huge first assignment: a sold-out Coliseum on a Saturday night. Center Carson Hinzman said the blockers need "to take a lot off their plate." McClain said, "It's pressure that you want."
For USC, Jaylen McClain called Maiava a "really good veteran quarterback." Tupou caught the only USC touchdown at Wisconsin.
Fun and true. USC leads the all-time series 13-10-1 and has won eight of the last 10 meetings. Seven meetings came on New Year's Day in the Rose Bowl. In the Rose Bowl after the 1979 season, Charles White scored on a 1-yard run with 1:32 left, and USC won 17-16. The 1973 Rose Bowl between these two drew 106,869 fans, still an NCAA bowl game record. USC has eight Heisman Trophy winners and Ohio State has seven.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Brecken "Buck" Holloway, Ohio State's insider. Here's what I said:
"In a world where two old powers meet on Halloween night..."
"Nine hundred eighty-four yards for Smith. That's a box office number."
"Get well soon, Julian. Everybody wants to see a healthy cast."
"And scene. Fight on."
And the last word from Buck: "Seven Heismans. I'll run a celebration route in the hallway."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
The Coliseum opened in 1923 and seats 77,500, right next to campus in Exposition Park. USC began playing football in 1888 and claims 11 national championships. Traveler and Tommy Trojan are campus icons.
Ohio State's home is Ohio Stadium, built in 1922 with room for 102,780. The Buckeyes claim national titles from 1942, 1954, 1957, 1961, 1968, 1970, 2002, 2014 and 2024. Brutus Buckeye leads the cheers.

report.title: Huskies Row to Lincoln: Washington Takes On Nebraska on Halloween Night
report.byline: Evangeline "Vangie" Tollefsrud · Washington Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Bow Down to Washington! I'm Evangeline "Vangie" Tollefsrud, and I'm your Washington insider. I'm a Seattle native, I row crew, and I boat to every home game. On the podcast, my segment is called Sailgate Report. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Husky Stadium in Seattle, built in 1920 with a listed capacity of 70,138. The playing surface is Alaska Airlines Field, the band is the University of Washington Husky Marching Band, and the fight song is "Bow Down to Washington." The program claims national titles from 1960 and 1991. The last five seasons went 4-8, 11-2, 14-1, 6-7 and 9-4, from 2021 through 2025. And if you visit, ask somebody about sailgating on Lake Washington. It's the tradition I'd show you first.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jedd Fisch leads the Huskies in his third season, and CollegeFootballData dates the hire to Jan. 14, 2024.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 27.9 points per game and allowing 22.7.

Players to Know
QB Demond Williams Jr.: 116 of 174, 1,396 yards, 8 touchdowns, 3 interceptions.
RB Brian Bonner Jr.: 296 yards on 64 carries, 1 touchdown.
WR Dezmen Roebuck: 48 catches, 484 yards, 3 touchdowns.

The Conference Picture

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Washington (4-3, 1-3 Big Ten) at Nebraska (5-2, 2-2 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 8:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. Central), Memorial Stadium, Lincoln, Neb., BTN.
Last time out. Both teams had an open date on Oct. 24.
Washington's last game was a 38-26 win at Purdue on Oct. 16, its first Big Ten win of the season. Brown went 21 of 27 for a career-high 302 yards and three touchdowns, and Trey Cooley ran eight times for 113 yards and a score.
Nebraska's last game was a 17-14 loss at Oregon on Oct. 17. Colandrea threw a touchdown and ran for another, and Gilmer caught six balls for 74 yards and a touchdown. A week before that, the Cornhuskers lost 20-17 to Indiana.
Players to watch. Washington's quarterback is a mystery for now. Demond Williams Jr. is 116 of 174 for 1,396 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions, but he has been out with a fractured rib since the Iowa game. Elijah Brown, a Stanford transfer, started at Purdue. Running back Brian Bonner Jr. has 296 yards, and wide receiver Dezmen Roebuck leads the team with 48 catches for 484 yards. On defense, safety Alex McLaughlin has 47 tackles and two interceptions, and linebacker Jacob Manu has 2.5 sacks.
Nebraska quarterback Anthony Colandrea is 137 of 219 for 1,570 yards, 14 touchdowns and four interceptions. Running back Jamal Rule has 391 yards and five touchdowns. Wide receiver Kwazi Gilmer has 38 catches for 492 yards and seven touchdowns. On defense, linebacker Owen Chambliss has 46 tackles, Jahsear Whittington has 3.5 sacks and Dwayne McDougle III has two interceptions.
Availability. No official Big Ten availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Washington coach Jedd Fisch said he won't name his starting quarterback until game time. Williams is back at practice but still has to prove the rib is ready. Sports Illustrated reports that Washington center Landen Hatchett has a season-ending neck injury. Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said running back Mekhi Nelson has been playing through an ankle injury and that the bye week was good for a banged-up running back room.
The coaches. Fisch is in his third season at Washington. He said Williams and Brown have split the first-team reps and have been great teammates. "Rising tides lift all ships," he said.
Rhule is in his fourth season at Nebraska. He said his team has to prepare for both quarterbacks. "We won't know until the first snap of the game," he said.
Storylines. Williams had started 21 straight games for Washington before missing the Purdue game. Brown came in during the Iowa game and has played well since. For Nebraska, Colandrea has been steady all year, and Rule leads a running game that has a lot of hands on deck.
Fun and true. These two have not met in the regular season in the last 10 years. Nebraska's two losses came by three points each, to Indiana and at Oregon. Washington's three losses came to Minnesota, USC and Iowa.
At home this year, Nebraska beat Ohio 49-21, Bowling Green 56-7, North Dakota 34-7 and Maryland 48-23.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Darla Rasmussen, Nebraska's insider. Here's what I said:
"Bow Down to Washington! I looked for a lake to sail in on, Darla. I found a lot of corn."
"Brown played like a captain on a calm morning."
"A Halloween night game in Lincoln. I'll trade my sailing jacket for a winter coat."
And the last word from Darla: "And I'll trade you a seat in a full house. Go Big Red."

Memorial Stadium opened in 1923 and seats 85,458. The Cornhusker Marching Band will be there, and the fight song is "Hail Varsity." Nebraska claims national titles from 1970, 1971, 1994, 1995 and 1997.

report.title: Polka Comes to Iowa City: No. 25 Wisconsin Visits Kinnick for a Halloween Noon Kickoff
report.byline: Lars "Brat" Ellefson · Wisconsin Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hand me the curds. (Polka accordion: oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, folks, I'm Lars Ellefson, but everybody calls me Brat. I was a fullback for the Badgers back in my day, and I still carry a cheese wedge to every game. Every single one. You'll notice I play a little polka before I share a stat. My doctor says it's good for my heart. When we win, I jump around, literally, and hand out cheese curds. When we lose, I eat a brat in thoughtful silence. Then I eat another one.

The School in 60 Seconds
(Oom-pah.) The Badgers have played in the Big Ten since it formed in 1896. Wisconsin is one of 26 programs to win 700 or more games. Home is Camp Randall Stadium, the fourth-oldest stadium in college football, opened in 1917 and listed at 80,321 seats. The last five seasons were 9-4, 7-6, 7-6, 5-7 and 4-8.

The Coach and the Scheme
Luke Fickell is the head coach, and CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 27, 2022. (Oom-pah.) His teams are built on defense, the way a good barn is built on a stone foundation. Spoken like a fullback.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 27.0 points per game and allowing 15.3.

Players to Know
QB Colton Joseph: 99 of 173, 1,256 yards, 11 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
Colton Joseph on the ground: 365 yards on 84 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR Tyrell Henry: 28 catches, 343 yards, 1 touchdown.
LB Sebastian Cheeks: 5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Cooper Catalano: a team-high 60 tackles.

The Conference Picture

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Last time out. Wisconsin beat USC 24-7 at Camp Randall on Oct. 24. Joseph went 12 of 14 with a touchdown throw, and Abu Sama III ran 17 times for 71 yards.
Iowa lost 13-10 at Minnesota on Oct. 24. Brown threw a touchdown throw to Reece Vander Zee, who caught four passes for 69 yards.
Players to watch. Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph has thrown the most passes in all seven Badger games, and he's also the team's leading rusher. He's 99 of 173 for 1,256 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions, with 365 rushing yards and four rushing scores. Tyrell Henry leads the receivers with 28 catches for 343 yards. On defense, linebacker Cooper Catalano has 60 tackles and linebacker Sebastian Cheeks has five sacks.
Iowa quarterback Hank Brown has 968 passing yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions, and he has thrown the most passes in six of Iowa's seven games. Jeremy Hecklinski did it in the 41-24 win at Washington. Running back Kamari Moulton leads the team with 541 rushing yards and four scores. Tony Diaz leads the receivers with 29 catches for 386 yards. Linebacker Cam Buffington has 62 tackles, and end Joseph Anderson has four sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Joseph has thrown the most passes in every Wisconsin game, and Brown did for Iowa last week, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Kirk Ferentz is in his 28th season at Iowa, the longest current tenure in FBS, and he's the Big Ten's all-time leader in wins. He's led the Hawkeyes since 1999, and before that he was head coach at Maine from 1990 to 1992. His defense allows 14.3 points a game this season.
Luke Fickell was hired at Wisconsin on Nov. 27, 2022. His Badgers allow 15.3 points a game, and they've already won 24-20 at Penn State and beaten Michigan State 31-3.
Storylines. The matchup to circle is the Iowa run game against the Wisconsin defense. The Hawkeyes gain 5.7 yards a carry, and the Badgers allow just 2.8. On the other side, Joseph and the Wisconsin big guys up front face an Iowa defense that allows only 2.4 yards a carry. Somebody's ground game is going to have a long afternoon.
Fun and true. Wisconsin has played in the Big Ten since the conference formed in 1896, and it's one of 26 programs with 700 or more wins. Iowa has been steady as a fence post, with records of 10-4, 8-5, 10-4, 8-5 and 9-4 over the last five seasons. This rivalry is as even as it gets lately. In the last ten regular-season meetings, each team has won five, and Iowa won 37-0 last season.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Orrin Kalvelage, Iowa's insider. Here's what I said:
"(Oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, Orrin! I brought curds for the whole tailgate. Squeaky fresh."
"(Oom-pah!) I jumped around so hard my cheese wedge fell off. Twice."
"Two coaches who love defense. This game might be decided by a punt. (Oom-pah.)"
"Orrin, whatever happens, come by the tailgate after. We'll say grace and have a brat."
And the last word from Orrin: "I'll be there, Lars. Go Hawks."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Kinnick Stadium seats 69,250, and a Halloween noon kickoff in Iowa City should bring out plenty of black-and-gold costumes. Iowa has won 13 conference championships, 11 in the Big Ten, and has been ranked No. 1 in the AP and Coaches polls 15 times. Wisconsin's home, Camp Randall Stadium, opened in 1917 and is the fourth-oldest stadium in college football.

report.title: Desert Wildcats in Lubbock: No. 22 Arizona Brings the Heat to No. 13 Texas Tech at Noon
report.byline: Inez Paloverde · Arizona Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi, hi, hi, Wildcat family, welcome! I'm Inez Paloverde, your Arizona insider, and I am a desert-sunrise optimist. I talk fast, I love hard, and I will defend this team to the last saguaro. I love the desert and I want you to love it too, so be warned: there will be cactus metaphors. A good defense is a lot like a cactus. It's beautiful from a distance, and you do not want to touch it. And when people complain about the Tucson heat, I just smile and say, "It's a dry hype." Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus all the sunshine I can carry. And I always end the same way: "Bear Down, friends."

The School in 60 Seconds
Let's start with those two words. "Bear Down" goes back to October 1926 and John "Button" Salmon, the student-body president and the Wildcats' quarterback. He was badly hurt in a car accident, and before he died he asked coach J.F. "Pop" McKale to tell the team to "bear down". It's been our rallying cry ever since. Home is Casino Del Sol Stadium in Tucson, listed at 50,782 seats. The program had a big 2025, going 9-4 and reaching the Holiday Bowl, where it lost to SMU 24-19.

The Coach and the Scheme
Brent Brennan was hired on Jan. 16, 2024. He went 4-8 his first season, then turned it around with nine wins in 2025.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 36.1 points per game and allowing 16.7.

Players to Know
QB Noah Fifita: 167 of 225, 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Kedrick Reescano: 303 yards on 80 carries, 5 touchdowns.
WR Isaiah Mizell: 27 catches, 493 yards, 5 touchdowns.
LB Chase Kennedy: 4 sacks, the team lead.
LB Taye Brown: a team-high 42 tackles.

The Conference Picture
