This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
No. 22 Arizona (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) at No. 13 Texas Tech (6-1, 3-1 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, Texas, ESPN.
Last time out. Arizona rolled past Iowa State 39-3 at home on Oct. 24. Fifita went 27 of 34 for 308 yards and two touchdowns, Mizell caught eight passes for 134 yards and a score, and Quincy Craig ran nine times for 51 yards and a touchdown. The Wildcat defense allowed just one field goal.
Texas Tech had its first loss of the season, 37-24 at Cincinnati on Oct. 24. Hammond went 24 of 37 for 227 yards, Williams ran 12 times for 81 yards, and Johnson caught seven passes for 81 yards.
Players to watch. Arizona quarterback Noah Fifita is 167 of 225 for 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Isaiah Mizell leads the Wildcats with 27 catches for 493 yards and five touchdowns. Kedrick Reescano leads the rushers with 303 yards and five scores. On defense, linebacker Chase Kennedy has four sacks and linebacker Taye Brown leads the team with 42 tackles.
Texas Tech quarterback Will Hammond is 139 of 205 for 1,561 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions. Running back J'Koby Williams is the workhorse, with 619 yards and five touchdowns on 86 carries. Wide receiver Kenny Johnson has 31 catches for 499 yards. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. leads the team with 6.5 sacks, and linebacker Austin Romaine leads with 53 tackles.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and the teams' box scores don't mark starters. Fifita has thrown the most passes for Arizona in all seven games, and Hammond has done the same for Texas Tech, so check the teams' pregame notes on Saturday morning.
The coaches. Joey McGuire was hired at Texas Tech on Nov. 8, 2021. Last season was the best in school history: the Red Raiders went 12-2, beat BYU 34-7 to win the Big 12 championship and made their first College Football Playoff. It was the program's first outright conference title since 1955. This year's team is built on the ground and on defense, and it allows 20.4 points a game.
Brent Brennan was hired at Arizona on Jan. 16, 2024. He went 4-8 in his first season, then turned it around with a 9-4 year in 2025 that ended in the Holiday Bowl. His 2026 Wildcats score 36.1 points a game and allow just 16.7.
Storylines. The matchup to circle is Fifita against a Texas Tech defense that has 6.5 sacks from Holmes alone. If the Red Raider big guys up front can get to Fifita, they can slow the Arizona passing game. On the other side, Williams and the Tech ground game face an Arizona defense that held Cincinnati to 7 points and Iowa State to 3. Whichever running game finds room first could decide the afternoon.
Fun and true. Arizona's rallying cry, "Bear Down," goes back to October 1926 and John "Button" Salmon, the student-body president and the Wildcats' quarterback. Before he died after a car accident, he asked coach J.F. "Pop" McKale to tell the team to "bear down," and it has been the school's motto ever since. These two have split their last two meetings: Arizona won 28-14 in 2019, and Texas Tech won 28-22 in 2024.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Bearcats, and welcome! I'm Lionel Abernathy, but everybody calls me Skyline, for reasons that will become obvious very quickly. I'm an engineering co-op kid, I chart everything, and I rank it all in Cincinnati chili ways. A three-way is respectable. A four-way is impressive. A five-way, with onions AND beans, is reserved for greatness. That goes for quarterbacks, defensive fronts and, yes, coaches' haircuts. When we win, I upgrade the team on air, three-way to five-way, no hesitation. When we lose, I downgrade to "plain spaghetti" and stare quietly into the distance. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a food tangent that somehow loops back into a very sharp stat. I travel with this team and I live with this team. That's a five-way take.

The School in 60 Seconds
Cincinnati has played football on the Nippert Stadium site since 1901, which makes it the second-oldest playing site in college football. That's history with extra cheese. In 2021 the Bearcats became the first team from outside the Power Five to make the College Football Playoff, where they played Alabama in the Cotton Bowl. Now we're in the Big 12. The Coach and the Scheme
Scott Satterfield became the 43rd head coach in program history on Dec. 5, 2022.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 35.4 points per game and allowing 26.4.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey, friends. I'm Moss Feldstein, your Colorado insider. I'm a physicist, a hacky-sack enthusiast and the guy running a quant model of the Buffs from a hammock under the Flatirons. I travel and live with this team, and I bring kombucha on every road trip. It's an acquired taste.

Here's my approach: chill vibes, sharp numbers. Every stat in this report is sourced, and when I compute one myself, I'll tell you. If I don't know something, I'll say the data's not in yet. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for mountain sunsets and the chance to keep fighting. Ralphie's running.

The School in 60 Seconds
Colorado has played at Folsom Field in Boulder since 1924. CFBD lists 50,183 seats. The Buffs won the 1990 national championship, shared with Georgia Tech. They have two Heisman winners: Rashaan Salaam in 1994 and Travis Hunter in 2024. The all-time record is 735-556-36 through 2025.

Colorado was a charter Big 12 member, left for the Pac-12 after 2010 and returned to the Big 12 in 2024. The last five seasons swing wildly: 4-8, 1-11, 4-8, a radical 9-4 in 2024 and 3-9 in 2025. High variance. Physicists love that. Fans, less so.

The Coach and the Scheme
Deion Sanders, "Coach Prime," leads the program. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 3, 2022. His résumé is unlike anyone's. He played 14 NFL seasons, won two Super Bowls and played nine Major League Baseball seasons. He's the only athlete to play in both a Super Bowl and a World Series. At Florida State he won the 1988 Jim Thorpe Award.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 20.1 points per game and allowing 30.1.

Players to Know

Last time out. Kansas State lost 28-17 at Arizona State on Oct. 24. Knuth was 26 of 41 for 194 yards and a touchdown, and Derrick Salley Jr. caught six balls for 63 yards.
Colorado lost 57-24 at Oklahoma State on Oct. 24. Wilson threw for 280 yards and two touchdowns, and Williams caught nine balls for 135 yards.

Jaron Tibbs leads the receivers with 34 catches for 325 yards and four touchdowns. On defense, end Wendell Gregory has 3.5 sacks and safety Logan Bartley has 45 tackles.
Colorado quarterback Isaac Wilson has thrown the most passes in each of the last four games. He's 77 of 128 for 979 yards, six touchdowns and seven interceptions. Julian Lewis threw the most in the first three games. JaQuail Smith leads the rushers with 298 yards, and Joseph Williams leads the receivers with 46 catches for 643 yards and five scores. Lamont Lester Jr. has five sacks, and linebacker Gideon Lampron leads the team with 65 tackles.

The coaches. Collin Klein was named Kansas State's 36th head coach on Dec. 4, 2025. He was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award as the Wildcats' quarterback, and he's the first K-State alum to lead the program since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77.
Deion Sanders, "Coach Prime," has led Colorado since his hire on Dec. 3, 2022. He played 14 NFL seasons, won two Super Bowls, played nine Major League Baseball seasons, and is the only athlete to play in both a Super Bowl and a World Series.
Storylines. The big matchup is the K-State ground game against a Colorado defense that allows 3.7 yards a carry. On the other side, Williams will be Wilson's top target, and Lester will try to chase down whoever plays quarterback for K-State.

"Dirt and data. My two best things after hacky sack."

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good evening, Cyclone Nation, and here's your Saturday forecast! I'm Twyla Hemmingsen, your Iowa State insider, coming to you live from the Ames weather center. Okay, it's my kitchen, but it has a very nice map on the wall. I'm high-energy, a little nerdy and joyful about it, and I talk about football the way the TV meteorologist talks about a cold front: pressure systems, wind shifts, and a big red blob moving across the screen. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, plus a full radar sweep of the opponent. Expect conditions to change quickly. When things are going our way, you'll hear "Forecast: loud, with gusts." When it's really rolling: "Cyclone warning in effect." Umbrellas optional, joy mandatory.

The School in 60 Seconds
Our home is Jack Trice Stadium in Ames, which holds 61,500. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete. The stadium got his name in 1997, and it is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man. Every Cyclone fan should know his story. On the field, Iowa State went 8-4 last season. Then came the biggest offseason storm in the country. Coach Matt Campbell left for Penn State and took three-year starting QB Rocco Becht with him. More than 50 Cyclones entered the transfer portal, including 16 starters. That's a full barometric reset.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jimmy Rogers was named Iowa State's 34th head coach on Dec. 5, 2025, coming from Washington State on a six-year contract. Before that he went 27-3 and won an FCS national title at South Dakota State, and he brought in more than 45 transfers to rebuild this roster.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 25.9 points per game and allowing 24.1.

Players to Know
QB Jaylen Raynor: 93 of 158, 1,107 yards, 7 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Aiden Flora: 716 yards on 102 carries, 6 touchdowns.
WR Omari Hayes: 19 catches, 237 yards, 1 touchdown.
DE Isaac Terrell: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Sullivan Schlimgen: a team-high 71 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Iowa State is 3-4 overall and 1-3 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 12th in Big 12.
The season so far: W 38-10 vs Southeast Missouri State Redhawks (Sept. 5), L 13-16 at Iowa Hawkeyes (Sept. 12), W 55-7 vs Bowling Green Falcons (Sept. 19), L 17-31 vs Utah Utes (Sept. 26), W 45-42 vs West Virginia Mountaineers (Oct. 3), L 10-24 at BYU Cougars (Oct. 9), L 3-39 at Arizona Wildcats (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Oklahoma State (5-2, 3-1 Big 12) at Iowa State (3-4, 1-3 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:00 p.m. ET (6:00 p.m. CT), Jack Trice Stadium, Ames, Iowa, FS1.
Last time out. Oklahoma State beat Colorado 57-24 at home. Mestemaker went 21 of 36 for 386 yards and four touchdowns. Justin Bowick caught five balls for 138 yards and a score, and Hawkins ran for 120 yards.
Iowa State lost 39-3 at No. 22 Arizona. Raynor fumbled late in the first half, and Jimmy Rogers gave backup Connor Moberly the second half to look for a spark. Flora was held to 36 yards.
Players to watch. Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker has completed 157 of 239 throws for 2,326 yards, with 20 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's thrown for 300 yards or more in six straight games. Wide receiver Wyatt Young has 36 catches for 639 yards and six scores. Running back Caleb Hawkins has 712 yards on 142 carries. Linebacker Ethan Wesloski leads the defense with 70 tackles and 3.5 sacks.
Iowa State running back Aiden Flora has 716 yards and six touchdowns on 102 carries. Quarterback Jaylen Raynor has thrown for 1,107 yards and seven touchdowns. Linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has 71 tackles, and defensive end Isaac Terrell has three sacks.
Availability. No official Big 12 availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Oklahoma State safety Mose Phillips hurt his shoulder against UCF and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Safety Quinton Hammonds was hurt recovering a fumble against Colorado and came back to the sideline in a sling. "Hopeful that we can get Q back," Eric Morris said.
The coaches. Jimmy Rogers settled the quarterback question early. "We're gonna go with Jaylen," he said, calling Raynor "the best leader on the team." Raynor will make his 43rd straight start, counting his time at Arkansas State. Rogers also said of Moberly, "his future's bright."
Eric Morris is in his first season in Stillwater. Mestemaker and Hawkins followed him from North Texas, and the Cowboys are No. 24 in the country after going 1-11 last season.
Iowa State defensive coordinator Jesse Bobbit was honest about the challenge. "He can make the throws," he said of Mestemaker. "You can see it on tape."
Storylines. Mestemaker ran 75 yards on one play in the 39-31 win over Oregon. That one run is half of his season rushing total.
Raynor is one of six team captains, elected by his teammates in the preseason. When he was benched, he spent the second half coaching up and cheering on Moberly.
Fun and true. This is Iowa State's fifth game against a ranked team in its first eight. The Cyclones are 3-1 at home this season, and their home wins include a 45-42 thriller over West Virginia.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Dusty Lockridge, Oklahoma State's insider. Here's what I said:
"Good evening, Cyclone Nation! Tonight's forecast: cold front from the south, wearing orange."
"Flora is the jet stream. Watch the radar."
"That's a captain. Sunshine in the forecast for that young man."
"Barometer's falling, Dusty. That's Cyclone weather."
And the last word from Dusty: "I'll bring the stopwatch, Twyla. You bring the forecast."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Jack Trice Stadium holds 61,500. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete, and it got his name in 1997. It is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man. Every visitor should know his story.
Oklahoma State has played football since 1901. The Cowboys claim the 1945 national championship, and Barry Sanders won the Heisman Trophy in 1988.

The last five seasons: 2-10 in 2021, then 6-7, a joyful 9-4 in 2023, and 5-7 twice. That 9-4 season is a memory I cherish.

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Wildcat family. I'm Hattie Brandvold. I have an agronomy degree, a purple denim jacket, a wheat-sheaf brooch and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it. Every drive gets named after a crop. A three-and-out is a dry sorghum patch. A long, patient march is winter wheat. And a touchdown? That's a bumper harvest, and you will hear me holler it. When we win, I do the Wabash Cannonball in my chair, tidy and joyful. When we lose, I whisper my most treasured words, "You can't rush a harvest," and I plant a tiny basil seed right there on set. Sweet as prairie pie, until I hand you the one fact that ends the argument.

The School in 60 Seconds
Kansas State football is the story of the biggest turnaround in the sport. When Bill Snyder took over in 1989, the program was in the middle of a 27-game winless streak. He turned it into a national contender that went to 11 straight bowl games and had six 11-win seasons in a seven-year stretch. Snyder won two Big 12 championships, one in 2003 with Darren Sproles and one in 2012. He went into the College Football Hall of Fame while still coaching, in December 2015. The Wildcats play at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan, and the rivalry with Kansas is the Sunflower Showdown, played for the Governor's Cup. Now that's a crop that keeps coming back every spring.

The Coach and the Scheme
Collin Klein was named the 36th head coach in school history on Dec. 4, 2025. You may remember him as the quarterback: he was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award that year, when K-State won the Big 12. He is the first K-State alum to be head coach since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77. Before this job he coached nine years in Manhattan, including two as offensive coordinator (2022-23) that went 19-8 with a Big 12 title, then ran the offense at Texas A&M.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 32.9 points per game and allowing 21.1.

Avery Johnson on the ground: 462 yards on 51 carries, 3 touchdowns.

DE Wendell Gregory: 3.5 sacks, the team lead.

The Conference Picture

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Last time out. Kansas State lost 28-17 at Arizona State on Oct. 24. Knuth was 26 of 41 for 194 yards and a touchdown, and Derrick Salley Jr. caught six balls for 63 yards.

Colorado quarterback Isaac Wilson has thrown the most passes in each of the last four games. He's 77 of 128 for 979 yards, six touchdowns and seven interceptions. Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Johnson threw the most passes in K-State's first six games and Knuth did last week, while Wilson has done it in Colorado's last four, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Collin Klein was named Kansas State's 36th head coach on Dec. 4, 2025. He was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award as the Wildcats' quarterback, and he's the first K-State alum to lead the program since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77.
Deion Sanders, "Coach Prime," has led Colorado since his hire on Dec. 3, 2022. He played 14 NFL seasons, won two Super Bowls, played nine Major League Baseball seasons, and is the only athlete to play in both a Super Bowl and a World Series.
Storylines. The big matchup is the K-State ground game against a Colorado defense that allows 3.7 yards a carry. K-State's big guys up front have allowed only three sacks, so Johnson and company should have time. On the other side, Williams will be Wilson's top target, and Lester will try to chase down whoever plays quarterback for K-State.
Fun and true. Kansas State has won the Sunflower Showdown against Kansas 18 straight times. These teams have met each of the last two years: K-State won 31-28 in 2024 and 24-14 in 2025.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Moss Feldstein, Colorado's insider. Here's what I said:
"Bless you, Moss, but I brought sweet tea and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it."

"Dry sorghum patch. You can't rush a harvest. I planted a basil seed on Sunday."
"Coach Klein grew up in our program. Homegrown crop."
"I'm dressing as a wheat sheaf. Very on brand."
"Moss, whatever happens, supper's on me. We'll say grace first."
And the last word from Moss: "Grateful for that, Hattie, and for a mountain sunset afterward. Ralphie's running."

report.title: Cowboys in Cyclone Country: No. 24 Oklahoma State Rides Into Ames on Halloween Night
report.byline: Dusty Lockridge · Oklahoma State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Cowboy fans. I'm Dusty Lockridge, your Oklahoma State insider. I'm an ag-econ grad, I wear orange from my hat to my boots, and I travel and live with this team. I explain offense with rodeo timing. A quick slant is a two-second ride. A long touchdown drive is the full eight seconds, with a good score from the judges.

Here's my word as a cowboy. Every number I give you has a source. When I do math myself, I'll tell you. If I don't know something, I'll say so. No bull, so to speak. I celebrate our players as young men first, I respect every opponent, and I thank the good Lord for fall Saturdays in Stillwater. Ride 'em, Pokes.

The School in 60 Seconds
Oklahoma State football started in 1901 and plays at Boone Pickens Stadium in Stillwater. CFBD lists 55,509 seats. The Cowboys claim the 1945 national championship, awarded by the AFCA, plus eleven conference titles. They've played in 34 bowl games and gone 22-12, including five New Year's Six wins. Running back Barry Sanders won the Heisman in 1988. The program counts 66 All-Americans.

The last five seasons have been a bucking bronco: 12-2, 7-6, 10-4, then 3-9 and 1-11.

The Coach and the Scheme
Eric Morris is our first-year head coach. Wikipedia says he was introduced on Dec. 8, 2025, while CFBD lists his hire date as Nov. 25, 2025. I'll flag that small difference. Before Stillwater he was head coach at Incarnate Word and North Texas, and offensive coordinator at Washington State.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 40.0 points per game and allowing 23.7.

Players to Know
QB Drew Mestemaker: 157 of 239, 2,326 yards, 20 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.
RB Caleb Hawkins: 712 yards on 142 carries, 2 touchdowns.
WR Wyatt Young: 36 catches, 639 yards, 6 touchdowns.
LB Ethan Wesloski: 3.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Ethan Wesloski: a team-high 70 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Oklahoma State is 5-2 overall and 3-1 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 2nd in Big 12. We're ranked No. 24 in ESPN's rankings this week.
The season so far: L 10-24 at Tulsa Golden Hurricane (Sept. 5), W 39-31 vs Oregon Ducks (Sept. 12), W 59-0 vs Murray State Racers (Sept. 19), W 41-24 at West Virginia Mountaineers (Sept. 26), W 42-28 vs UCF Knights (Oct. 10), L 32-35 at Houston Cougars (Oct. 17), W 57-24 vs Colorado Buffaloes (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Oklahoma State (5-2, 3-1 Big 12) at Iowa State (3-4, 1-3 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:00 p.m. ET (6:00 p.m. CT), Jack Trice Stadium, Ames, Iowa, FS1.
Last time out. Oklahoma State beat Colorado 57-24 at home. Mestemaker went 21 of 36 for 386 yards and four touchdowns. Justin Bowick caught five balls for 138 yards and a score, and Hawkins ran for 120 yards.
Iowa State lost 39-3 at No. 22 Arizona. Raynor fumbled late in the first half, and Jimmy Rogers gave backup Connor Moberly the second half to look for a spark. Flora was held to 36 yards.
Players to watch. Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker has completed 157 of 239 throws for 2,326 yards, with 20 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's thrown for 300 yards or more in six straight games. Wide receiver Wyatt Young has 36 catches for 639 yards and six scores. Running back Caleb Hawkins has 712 yards on 142 carries. Linebacker Ethan Wesloski leads the defense with 70 tackles and 3.5 sacks.
Iowa State running back Aiden Flora has 716 yards and six touchdowns on 102 carries. Quarterback Jaylen Raynor has thrown for 1,107 yards and seven touchdowns. Linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has 71 tackles, and defensive end Isaac Terrell has three sacks.
Availability. No official Big 12 availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Oklahoma State safety Mose Phillips hurt his shoulder against UCF and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Safety Quinton Hammonds was hurt recovering a fumble against Colorado and came back to the sideline in a sling. "Hopeful that we can get Q back," Eric Morris said.
The coaches. Jimmy Rogers settled the quarterback question early. "We're gonna go with Jaylen," he said, calling Raynor "the best leader on the team." Raynor will make his 43rd straight start, counting his time at Arkansas State. Rogers also said of Moberly, "his future's bright."
Eric Morris is in his first season in Stillwater. Mestemaker and Hawkins followed him from North Texas, and the Cowboys are No. 24 in the country after going 1-11 last season.
Iowa State defensive coordinator Jesse Bobbit was honest about the challenge. "He can make the throws," he said of Mestemaker. "You can see it on tape."
Storylines. Mestemaker ran 75 yards on one play in the 39-31 win over Oregon. That one run is half of his season rushing total.
Raynor is one of six team captains, elected by his teammates in the preseason. When he was benched, he spent the second half coaching up and cheering on Moberly.
Fun and true. This is Iowa State's fifth game against a ranked team in its first eight. The Cyclones are 3-1 at home this season, and their home wins include a 45-42 thriller over West Virginia.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Twyla Hemmingsen, Iowa State's insider. Here's what I said:
"Orange from my hat to my boots, Twyla. We're riding into Ames for the full eight seconds."
"Tough night in the desert. Those Cyclones will come home hungry."
"Prayers for Mose and Q. Good young men, both of them."
"I'll bring the stopwatch, Twyla. You bring the forecast."
And the last word from Twyla: "Barometer's falling, Dusty. That's Cyclone weather."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Jack Trice Stadium holds 61,500. It's named for Jack Trice, Iowa State's first Black athlete, and it got his name in 1997. It is still the only major college football stadium named for a Black man. Every visitor should know his story.
Oklahoma State has played football since 1901. The Cowboys claim the 1945 national championship, and Barry Sanders won the Heisman Trophy in 1988.

report.title: Frogs Ready for the Cattle Drive: TCU Hosts Kansas and Its Hoops Math on Halloween
report.byline: Ryder Galloway · TCU Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy, Frog fans, and welcome! I'm Ryder Galloway, your TCU insider. I'm a Stockyards cowboy who became a finance guy, so I wear boots with a quarter-zip and I explain defenses as cattle drives. You've got your point riders, your flank riders and your drag riders, and when everyone holds their spot, nobody gets loose. I travel with this team and I live with this team. Fair warning: if something goes wrong, anything at all, I will probably blame Dallas. Flat tire? Dallas. Missed field goal? Dallas. When we win, it's "Yeehaw!" and my hat goes flying. When we lose, I mutter about Dallas some more. And the best sound in football is me hollering "Yeehaw, that's a turnover!" Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, Fort Worth style.

The School in 60 Seconds
TCU has a national title on the wall. The 1938 Horned Frogs went 11-0, beat Carnegie Tech 15-7 in the Sugar Bowl and won the national championship. Quarterback Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy that year. The 2010 team went 13-0 and won the Rose Bowl, and in 2022 Sonny Dykes led TCU all the way to the College Football Playoff national championship game. Home is Amon G. Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, listed at 46,000. Not one bit of that history happened in Dallas. And the rivalry with Baylor has a name now, the Revivalry, and we just won it in Waco. Ten more minutes on that and I'd be throwing my hat again.

The Coach and the Scheme
Sonny Dykes was hired on Nov. 29, 2021, and in his first season he took the Frogs to the national title game.

TCU lost 24-20 to West Virginia at home on Oct. 24. Craig completed 33 of 47 for 372 yards and a touchdown, and Kari Ashley caught six balls for 118 yards. The week before, the Frogs won 17-6 at Baylor.

Lance Leipold has led Kansas since 2021. Before that he won six Division III national championships at Wisconsin-Whitewater and reached 100 wins faster than any coach in NCAA history, in his 106th game. His 2023 team went 9-4. Fun and true. TCU's 1938 team went 11-0, beat Carnegie Tech 15-7 in the Sugar Bowl and won the national title, and quarterback Davey O'Brien won the Heisman Trophy. "Howdy, Fitz, and welcome to Fort Worth! Not Dallas. Never Dallas."
"This is a football game, partner."
"Hayward gets after a quarterback like a flank rider after a stray. Yeehaw."
"Four points. I'm blaming Dallas. I don't know how yet, but I'll figure it out."
"Coach Dykes took us to the title game in year one. Not one bit of that happened in Dallas."
"I'm dressing as a cattle drive. All of it. The point riders, the flank riders, the drag riders."
"Whatever happens, Fitz, the barbecue's on me. We'll say grace first."

THE FANATIC EDITION

Howdy. Bodie Ratliff. Texas Tech insider. I ride bareback at the rodeo, and in tumbleweed season I chart Air Raid concepts on the back of feed-store receipts. I travel with the team. When we win, I say "Guns up," real quiet, and then I grin longer than anybody's comfortable with. When we lose, I stare into the wind with my hat in my hand. The School in 60 Seconds
Last season was the best in school history. Texas Tech went 12-2, crushed BYU 34-7 to win the Big 12 championship and made its first College Football Playoff. That was the program's first outright conference title since 1955. The run ended with a 23-0 loss to Oregon in the Orange Bowl. Home is Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, listed at 60,454. report.title: Space Game at the Bounce House: UCF Welcomes Baylor to Orlando for Friday Night Liftoff
report.byline: Knox Brevard-Stiles · UCF Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Charge On, Knights! I'm Knox Brevard-Stiles, your UCF insider. I grew up in Orlando, I'm a theme-park ride engineer, and I swear the stands really move. I measure crowd noise with a ride-safety gauge, and I wear a knight's helmet after big wins. Please keep your hands and feet inside the stadium at all times.

My Ride Check: every cheer gets measured, every claim gets checked. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll say so. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for Florida sunshine and fall football.

The School in 60 Seconds
UCF first fielded a varsity team in 1979 as an NCAA Division III program and reached Division I-A, now the FBS, in 1996. That made UCF the first program in NCAA history to play in all four divisions of college football. As a Division I-AA program, the Knights made the 1990 and 1993 playoffs. Today they play in the Big 12.

Home is the Acrisure Bounce House on UCF's main campus east of Orlando. Wikipedia lists 45,906 seats and CFBD lists 44,206. CFBD says it opened in 2007. The first game there was a 35-32 loss to No. 6 Texas on Sept. 15, 2007, and UCF led 24-23 early in the fourth quarter. Ride Check: the stands held up just fine that day.

The last five seasons: 9-4, 9-5, 6-7, 4-8 and 5-7.

The Coach and the Scheme
Scott Frost is back for a second run in Orlando. He coached UCF in 2016 and 2017, and his 2017 team went 13-0. Then he coached Nebraska from 2018 to 2022. CFBD lists his return as Dec. 7, 2024. As a player, he led Nebraska to the 1997 national championship. He has coached Heisman winner Marcus Mariota and Heisman candidate McKenzie Milton.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 32.7 points per game and allowing 23.0.

Players to Know
QB Keyone Jenkins: 108 of 159, 1,099 yards, 11 touchdowns, 3 interceptions.
RB Duke Watson: 577 yards on 85 carries, 3 touchdowns.
WR Josh Derry: 34 catches, 358 yards, 3 touchdowns.
Defender Isaiah Nixon: 2.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Tackett Curtis: a team-high 42 tackles.

The Conference Picture
UCF is 4-3 overall and 2-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 7th in Big 12.
The season so far: W 73-6 vs Bethune-Cookman Wildcats (Sept. 3), L 7-12 at Pittsburgh Panthers (Sept. 12), W 44-30 vs Georgia State Panthers (Sept. 19), W 21-13 vs TCU Horned Frogs (Sept. 26), L 17-27 at Houston Cougars (Oct. 3), L 28-42 at Oklahoma State Cowboys (Oct. 10), W 39-31 (OT) vs BYU Cougars (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) at UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12). Friday, Oct. 30, 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 p.m. Central), Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, ESPN.
Last time out. UCF beat No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime at home. Jenkins went 25 of 41 for 293 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another score, and found Derry on the first play of overtime. Tyren Hornes caught six passes for 137 yards.
Baylor lost 25-24 at Kansas. A 45-yard field goal try with 22 seconds left was blocked, the third Baylor field goal try the Jayhawks blocked that day. Freeman caught nine passes for 123 yards.
Players to watch. UCF quarterback Keyone Jenkins is 108 of 159 for 1,099 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions, and he has run for four more scores. Running back Duke Watson has 577 yards on 85 carries, and wide receiver Josh Derry leads the team with 34 catches for 358 yards. Linebacker Tackett Curtis has 42 tackles, and Isaiah Nixon has 2.5 sacks.
Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway is 113 of 217 for 1,352 yards, nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman has 58 catches for 678 yards and ranks third in the nation in receptions per game. Linebacker Travion Barnes has 51 tackles, and defensive end Garrick Ponder has four sacks.
Availability. The Big 12 has not posted an availability report for this game. UCF coach Scott Frost said Jenkins will start again. Alonza Barnett III, who hurt his hamstring in Week 2, is making progress, and Frost said, "I think he probably could play," though he was not sure Barnett was fully healthy yet. No injury news has surfaced for Baylor's starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Baylor parted ways with seventh-year coach Dave Aranda after the Kansas game. Athletic director Doug McNamee called Aranda "a genuine and honorable person" who "deeply cares for his players." Joe Klanderman, the first-year defensive coordinator, is the interim head coach for the rest of the season. He won four national titles at North Dakota State and led the defense at Kansas State before coming to Waco.
Scott Frost is in his second year of his second stint at UCF. He led the Knights in 2016 and 2017, and his 2017 team went 13-0.
Storylines. Jenkins has been the steady hand while Barnett heals. After the BYU win, Jenkins said, "It's still his team. Still his starting job." That is a great teammate talking.
Baylor's defense ranks third in the nation in sacks and fifth in tackles for loss per game. Watson and the big guys up front for UCF will need a strong night.
Fun and true. Baylor leads the series 2-1. UCF won the first meeting, 52-42 in the 2013 Fiesta Bowl. In 2023 in Orlando, Baylor came back from 35-7 down in the third quarter to win 36-35, the biggest comeback in Bears history, and in 2025 Baylor won 30-3 in Waco. After this one, Baylor goes home for Homecoming against Iowa State on Nov. 7.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Maggie Whitlock, Baylor's insider. Here's what I said:
"Ride check, Maggie! Lap bar down, arms inside, and welcome to the annual Space Game."
"Thirty-nine to thirty-one over the No. 2 team in the country. My hands are still up in the air."
"Jenkins giving his teammate the credit? That's a first-class ride, Maggie. Pure class."
"A 28-point comeback in our house? That one still makes my stomach drop like the big hill."
And the last word from Maggie: "Then buckle up, Knox. We like a late build."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Friday is UCF's annual Space Game, one of the fun themed nights on the schedule. Mike Monaco, Jordan Rodgers and Dana Boyle have the call on ESPN.

report.title: Slalom Gates and Skyline Chili: No. 6 Utah Heads to Cincinnati on Halloween
report.byline: Aspen Mortensen · Utah Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Send it, no fear, Ute fans! I'm Aspen Mortensen, your Utah insider. I used to race skis, and now I chart Utah's defensive speed like slalom gates. Who cut inside, who cleared the gate, who missed it. I'll be making avalanche puns. Consider yourself warned.

Here's my promise. Every number has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you plainly. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for the Wasatch, my family and fall football.

The School in 60 Seconds
Utah football began in 1892 and has played at the current site of Rice-Eccles Stadium since 1927. The Utes have won 27 conference championships in five conferences, and they have two BCS bowl wins: the 2005 Fiesta Bowl, 35-7 over Pittsburgh under Urban Meyer, and the 2009 Sugar Bowl under Kyle Whittingham. CFBD lists Rice-Eccles at 51,444 seats.

The last five seasons: 10-4, 10-4, 8-5, 5-7 and 11-2.

The Coach and the Scheme
Morgan Scalley is in his first season as head coach. He took over in December 2025. He played defensive back for Utah from 2001 to 2004, was on Whittingham's staff from 2007 and spent 10 seasons as defensive coordinator.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 37.4 points per game and allowing 14.6.

Players to Know
QB Devon Dampier: 136 of 198, 1,616 yards, 15 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.
RB Wayshawn Parker: 644 yards on 102 carries, 8 touchdowns.
WR Braden Pegan: 34 catches, 459 yards, 6 touchdowns.
DT Karson Kaufusi: 2 sacks, the team lead.
LB Trey Reynolds: a team-high 44 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Utah is 7-0 overall and 4-0 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 1st in Big 12. We're ranked No. 6 in ESPN's rankings this week.
The season so far: W 66-14 vs Idaho Vandals (Sept. 3), W 43-10 vs Arkansas Razorbacks (Sept. 12), W 33-0 vs Utah State Aggies (Sept. 19), W 31-17 at Iowa State Cyclones (Sept. 26), W 41-24 vs Kansas Jayhawks (Oct. 10), W 27-24 at Colorado Buffaloes (Oct. 17), W 21-13 vs Houston Cougars (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
No. 6 Utah (7-0, 4-0 Big 12) at Cincinnati (5-2, 2-2 Big 12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:45 p.m. ET, Nippert Stadium, Cincinnati, ESPN.
Last time out. Utah beat Houston 21-13 at home on Oct. 24, the Utes' first win ever over the Cougars. Dampier threw for 204 yards and ran for 150 more with two touchdowns.
Cincinnati beat No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24 on Homecoming in front of a sold-out Nippert crowd. French threw four touchdowns, and Tabb ran 16 times for 173 yards and a score. It was only the third top-10 win in Nippert Stadium history.
Players to watch. Utah quarterback Devon Dampier has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 136 of 198 for 1,616 yards, 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he ran for 150 yards and two scores last week. Wayshawn Parker leads the rushers with 644 yards and eight touchdowns, and Braden Pegan leads the receivers with 34 catches for 459 yards and six scores. Linebacker Trey Reynolds leads the defense with 44 tackles, and Karson Kaufusi has two sacks.
Cincinnati quarterback JC French IV has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 127 of 183 for 1,510 yards, 13 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Cole Tabb leads the rushers with 621 yards and nine scores on just 65 carries, and JV Gibson leads the receivers with 29 catches for 385 yards. Linebacker Jonathan Thompson leads the defense with 60 tackles, and Patrick Bauer has three and a half sacks.
Availability. The official Big 12 availability report hasn't been posted yet. Utah coach Morgan Scalley said starting offensive lineman Kelvin Obot, who was hurt at Colorado and missed the Houston game, has no timetable and is getting a second opinion. Cincinnati coach Scott Satterfield said the team is close to getting starting nose tackle Josh Hough back after he missed last week, and starting center Taran Tyo, who left last week's game, likely won't have an answer until late in the week. Check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Morgan Scalley is in his first season as Utah's head coach after taking over in December 2025. He played defensive back for the Utes from 2001 to 2004, joined the staff in 2007 and spent 10 seasons as defensive coordinator. After the Colorado win he said, "It's not always pretty, but we did enough."
Scott Satterfield became Cincinnati's 43rd head coach on Dec. 5, 2022. His offense runs the ball well and almost never gives it away.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Tabb and the Cincinnati big guys up front against a Utah defense that allows only 14.6 points a game. On the other side, Dampier and Parker face a Bearcats defense that just slowed down Texas Tech. These teams met for the first time last season, on Nov. 1 in Salt Lake City, where College GameDay was in town, and Utah won 45-14.
Fun and true. Utah football began in 1892 and has played on the current site of Rice-Eccles Stadium since 1927. The Utes have won two BCS bowls, the 2005 Fiesta Bowl and the 2009 Sugar Bowl. Cincinnati became the first team from outside the Power Five to make the College Football Playoff in the 2021 season, when the Bearcats played Alabama in the Cotton Bowl.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy, Cincinnati's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thanks, Skyline. I'll warn you now, there will be avalanche puns."
"Our defense eats gates for breakfast. Send it, no fear."
"Dampier runs like he's on a fresh powder day. Nobody catches him."
"Five losses to Houston, then finally a win. Every ski run has a bottom, and we made it to the lodge."
"Coach Scalley has been a Ute for a long time. He knows every gate on this course."
"I'm dressing as an avalanche. Big, fast and loud."
"Deal, Skyline. I'll bring the fry sauce."
And the last word from Skyline: "Whatever happens, Aspen, chili's on me. We'll say grace first."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
For the first time in program history, Cincinnati is hosting ranked opponents in back-to-back weeks, and it all happens on Halloween. Football has been played on the Nippert site since 1901, which Cincinnati calls the second-oldest playing site in college football.

report.title: Take Me Home, Country Bye Week: The Mountaineers Rest Up in the Hills
report.byline: Jolene Buckhannon · West Virginia Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Mornin', Mountaineers. Welcome. I'm Jolene Buckhannon. I used to captain the rifle team, so I count possessions the way I used to count rounds: every one matters and you don't waste any. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm calm, flat, deadpan as a holler on a Sunday morning. until I'm not. I also keep a running pepperoni-roll tally of every fumble the other team coughs up. One roll per fumble, and I eat the tally afterward. When we win, I sing one verse of "Country Roads," drop the mic, then lift it right back up, because mics cost money. When we lose, I count to ten out loud, real slow, like I'm reloading. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, straight shooting. "Load up, I don't miss."

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is Milan Puskar Stadium in Morgantown, listed at 60,000, and when that place sings "Country Roads," you feel it in your boots. The man in charge is a familiar one. Rich Rodriguez was named the 36th head coach in school history in December 2024, returning to the program he once led. His teams have always run the football, and this one sure does.

The Coach and the Scheme
Rodriguez was hired on Dec. 11, 2024.

Players to Know

report.title: Court Is in Session at Wallace Wade: Boston College Brings Its Gavel to Durham
report.byline: Siobhan Dunleavy · Boston College Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
All rise, Eagles fans. I'm Siobhan Dunleavy, your Boston College insider, grad student and former debate champion. I argue every play like it's a moot-court case, and I always appoint myself the judge, which my co-hosts find wicked unfair. When we win, I bang my toy gavel and announce, "Objection overruled, we WON." When we lose, I file an appeal with the Court of Iced Coffee. The court has never ruled in my favor, and I keep filing anyway. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, argued on the merits. "Objection: sustained."

The School in 60 Seconds
Boston College plays at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill, listed at 44,500.

The Coach and the Scheme
Bill O'Brien was named Boston College's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024. His résumé is a long exhibit list. At Penn State in 2012 and 2013 he went 15-9 and won the Bear Bryant and Maxwell Club coach of the year awards in 2012. With the Houston Texans he went 52-48 and won four AFC South titles.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 24.4 points per game and allowing 23.6.

Players to Know
QB Mason McKenzie: 107 of 185, 1,363 yards, 8 touchdowns, 7 interceptions.
Mason McKenzie on the ground: 614 yards on 119 carries, 5 touchdowns.
WR Javarius Green: 26 catches, 286 yards, 1 touchdown.
DE Demetrius Ballard: 4.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Anthony Palano: a team-high 61 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Boston College is 4-3 overall and 2-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 6th in ACC.
The season so far: L 15-34 at Cincinnati Bearcats (Sept. 5), W 28-21 vs Rutgers Scarlet Knights (Sept. 11), W 22-16 vs Maine Black Bears (Sept. 19), L 14-21 vs Virginia Tech Hokies (Sept. 26), L 16-25 at SMU Mustangs (Oct. 3), W 27-21 vs Pittsburgh Panthers (Oct. 17), W 49-27 at Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Boston College (4-3, 2-2 ACC) at Duke (5-2, 2-2 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Wallace Wade Stadium, Durham, N.C., CW.
Last time out. Boston College won 49-27 at Georgia Tech on Oct. 24. McKenzie ran 16 times for 170 yards and two touchdowns and threw for 101 yards and another score.
Duke won 19-16 at Virginia on Oct. 23. Eget went 14 of 25 for 211 yards, Sheppard ran for a touchdown, and Burton caught four passes for 59 yards.
Players to watch. Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie has thrown the most passes in all seven Eagle games, and he's also the team's leading rusher. He's 107 of 185 for 1,363 yards, eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, and he has 614 rushing yards and five rushing scores. Javarius Green leads the receivers with 26 catches for 286 yards. On defense, linebacker Anthony Palano has 61 tackles and end Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks.
Duke quarterback Walker Eget has thrown the most passes in all seven Blue Devil games. He's 122 of 197 for 1,440 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Running back Nate Sheppard is the workhorse, with 875 yards and nine touchdowns on 153 carries. Jonah Burton leads the receivers with 21 catches for 298 yards. Linebacker Nick Morris Jr. has 44 tackles, and end Kevin O'Connor has four sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. McKenzie and Eget have each thrown the most passes in every game for their teams this season, so check the teams' pregame notes before kickoff.
The coaches. Bill O'Brien was named Boston College's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024. He went 15-9 at Penn State in 2012 and 2013, won four AFC South titles with the Houston Texans, and coached Heisman winner Bryce Young as Alabama's offensive coordinator.
Manny Diaz was hired at Duke on Dec. 7, 2023. He was head coach at Miami from 2019 to 2021 and defensive coordinator at Penn State in 2022 and 2023. His Duke defense allows 16 points a game this season, and it held Tulane to three points and Stanford to seven.
Storylines. The case to watch is McKenzie against a Duke defense that allows 3.3 yards a carry. If the Duke big guys up front keep him from breaking loose the way he did in Atlanta, the Eagles will have to throw. On the other side, Sheppard gains plenty of yards behind a Duke run game that averages 5.3 yards a carry, and BC allows 4.0. Whoever controls the ground game probably controls the afternoon.
Fun and true. Duke's football rebirth under David Cutcliffe from 2008 to 2021 included the school's first Coastal Division title in 2013. Since then, the Blue Devils have stacked four straight winning seasons: 9-4, 8-5, 9-4 and 9-5. Boston College plays its home games at Alumni Stadium in Chestnut Hill. These two have split their last two meetings: BC won 26-6 in 2020, and Duke won 38-31 in 2022.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, Duke's insider. Here's what I said:
"All rise! The Honorable Siobhan Dunleavy presiding. Also prosecuting. Also on the jury."
"Objection overruled, we WON! I banged the gavel so hard it needs a cast."
"Two coaches with Penn State on the résumé. I move that they share a pregame handshake."
"I'm coming as a Supreme Court justice. Again."
"The court accepts. Objection: sustained."
And the last word from Harrison: "Siobhan, whatever the verdict, lunch is on me after the game. Grace first, then barbecue."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Wallace Wade Stadium opened in 1929 and seats 40,004. Duke has won 18 conference championships, eight in the ACC and ten in the Southern Conference, and the program counts 53 All-Americans. A Halloween noon kickoff means expect a few Blue Devil costumes in the stands, which is the easiest costume in Durham.

report.title: Golden Bears Go East: Cal Brings a Sign to Raleigh for a Halloween Noon Kickoff
report.byline: Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch · California Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Greetings, comrades of the Blue and Gold! I'm Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, your Cal insider. I'm writing a philosophy dissertation on the ethics of the fourth-down decision, and I have opinions. When I see a bad play-call, I don't just complain. I make a picket sign. I have a closet full of them: "THIRD-AND-LONG IS A SOCIAL CONSTRUCT." "RUN IT ON SECOND DOWN, PLEASE (RESPECTFULLY)." When we win, I raise a fist and shout "Power to the play-call!" When we lose, I organize a peaceful, fully permitted protest against the punter. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, argued with conviction.

The School in 60 Seconds
Every Cal fan knows the greatest play in college football history, and we just call it The Play. In the 1982 Big Game against Stanford, the Bears returned the final kickoff through five laterals, and Kevin Moen scored as the Stanford band wandered onto the field. Cal won 25-20. Our home is California Memorial Stadium in Berkeley, listed at 62,467, with the hills right behind it. Cal now plays in the ACC. A cross-country revolution, if you will.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tosh Lupoi was named the 35th head coach in program history on Dec. 4, 2025, replacing Justin Wilcox.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 23.4 points per game and allowing 31.6.

Players to Know
QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele: 149 of 219, 1,555 yards, 10 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Adam Mohammed: 336 yards on 73 carries, 3 touchdowns.
WR Chase Hendricks: 54 catches, 498 yards, 3 touchdowns.
LB JD McKinley: 3 sacks, the team lead.
DB Isaiah Crosby: a team-high 46 tackles.

report.title: Fire Up the Grill: The Wolfpack Hosts Cal for a Halloween Noon Cookout in Raleigh

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey there, Pack! I'm Rutherford Pegram, but everybody calls me Ruff, and I'm your NC State insider. I'm a Wake County native and an engineer, and I grill at the same Carter-Finley lot every home game. I explain schemes with grill thermometers. A defense running at 225 degrees? That's low and slow. An offense at 450? That's a sear.

Here's my promise. I'm loud, I'm warm and I'm gloriously dramatic, but I don't cook the numbers. Every stat here has a source. If I don't know something, I'll tell you the thermometer's still reading. I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God for good friends, good food and good football. I howl once per segment, no more, no less. Wolfpack, howl!

The School in 60 Seconds
NC State plays in the ACC and was a founding member in 1953, after years in the Southern Conference. The Wolfpack has won seven conference championships and played in 34 bowl games, winning 17. Since 1966, home has been Carter-Finley Stadium, the largest college football stadium in North Carolina. CFBD lists it at 58,000 seats. In 2010 the school brought back a live mascot, a Tamaskan dog named Tuffy. Good boy.

The last five seasons have been steady heat: 9-3, 8-5, 9-4, 6-7 and 8-5. Four winning seasons in five years. The grill stays lit in Raleigh.

The Coach and the Scheme
Dave Doeren led NC State starting in 2013. CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 1, 2012. Before Raleigh he was head coach at Northern Illinois in 2011 and 2012. The school relieved Doeren of his duties after the loss at Stanford, and running backs coach and special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel will serve as interim head coach for the rest of the season. He has promised a team that will be "hard, tough and together." We thank Coach Doeren for every Saturday he gave this program.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 32.3 points per game and allowing 28.1.

On defense, defensive back Isaiah Crosby has 46 tackles and linebacker JD McKinley has three sacks.
NC State quarterback CJ Bailey is 143 of 219 for 1,763 yards, 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, and he has thrown the most passes in every Wolfpack game this season. Saturday is his first game in charge, and he has promised a team that will be "hard, tough and together." report.text:

It goes from "yinz," meaning a beautiful, textbook form tackle, all the way down to "yikes," meaning somebody whiffed. I blow a homemade whistle for every grade. The producers love it. Okay, they tolerate it. I travel with this team and I live with this team. When we win, I holler "Yinz SEE that?!" so loud the board op flinches. The School in 60 Seconds

Then in 2021 under Pat Narduzzi, Pitt won its first ACC championship, beating Wake Forest 45-21 in the title game. Home is Acrisure Stadium, listed at 68,400, right there on the North Shore. Dat's history, n'at.

Pat Narduzzi was hired on Dec. 16, 2014. Defense is his thing.

report.title: Cardinal Versus Cardinals: Stanford Brings Its Birds and Brains to Louisville on Halloween

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey, team! I'm Ignatius Yamamoto-Ross, Iggy for short, your Stanford insider. I've founded three apps that failed and built one Cardinal model that works. I travel and live with this team, and I describe football in startup jargon. A two-minute drill is a sprint. A punt is a pivot. A blowout loss is a learning opportunity, and we've had a few.

Here's my mission statement. I disrupt hype, not facts. Every number in this report has a source. If I don't know something, I'll mark it "pending data." I celebrate our players as people first, I respect every opponent, and I'm grateful to God for a night under the lights. Let's ship it.

The School in 60 Seconds
Stanford has fielded teams nearly every year since 1892. The school dropped football in favor of rugby from 1906 to 1917. Fun branding history: the teams were the "Cardinal," then mostly the "Cardinals," then the "Indians" from 1930 to 1972, then "Cardinals" again, and finally "Cardinal" since the 1982 season. A student vote in 1975 to become the "Robber Barons" wasn't approved. Best rejected rebrand ever.

Stanford now plays in the ACC after many years in the Pac-12. Home is Stanford Stadium, which CFBD lists as built in 2006 with 50,424 seats. The last five seasons were rough: four straight 3-9 years from 2021 to 2024, then 4-8 in 2025. This is a rebuild, and we're in the early funding rounds.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tavita Pritchard is the new head coach, hired for the 2026 season. CFBD records his hire date as Nov. 28, 2025. He's a Stanford alum and former quarterback. He played on the 2007 team that upset USC, widely considered one of the biggest upsets in college football history. He started coaching as a Stanford graduate assistant in 2010 and became offensive coordinator in 2018. From 2023 to 2025 he coached quarterbacks for the Washington Commanders. Founder returns to the company. Love that story.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 19.9 points per game and allowing 35.5.

report.title: Black Knights March to the Bluff City: Army Visits Memphis on Halloween Night
report.byline: Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke · Army Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Attention on deck. I'm Captain Thaddeus Rourke, retired, your Army insider. I spent my career as a logistics officer, so I read every option play like a supply-chain plan: right item, right place, right time.

Standing orders for this column. Every fact is sourced, like a properly filed report. If I don't know something, I'll log it as "status unknown" and move on. I celebrate these cadets as young leaders first, I respect every opponent, and I thank God daily for the men and women who serve. Discipline is a love letter to your teammates. Copy that, and beat Navy.

The School in 60 Seconds
Army football represents the United States Military Academy and plays at Michie Stadium in West Point, New York. Wikipedia lists capacity at 36,000 and CFBD at 38,000, so I'm flagging that as conflicting. The Black Knights play in the American Conference.

The honors roll is long. Army claims five national championships, including AP titles in 1944 and 1945. The academy has three Heisman winners: Doc Blanchard (1945), Glenn Davis (1946) and Pete Dawkins (1958). It counts 24 players and four coaches in the College Football Hall of Fame and 37 consensus All-Americans.

The last five seasons: 9-4, 6-6, 6-6, a magnificent 12-2 in 2024 and 7-6 in 2025. Mission accomplished more often than not.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jeff Monken has commanded since 2014, and CFBD records his hire date as Dec. 24, 2013. He was head coach at Georgia Southern from 2010 to 2013. Before that he worked under Paul Johnson as running backs coach and special teams coordinator at Georgia Southern, Navy and Georgia Tech. Yes, Navy. We've forgiven him.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 35.3 points per game and allowing 22.1.

Players to Know
QB Cale Hellums: 39 of 69, 422 yards, 3 touchdowns, 1 interception.
Cale Hellums on the ground: 840 yards on 159 carries, 16 touchdowns.
OL Brady Anderson: 10 catches, 163 yards.
LB Victor Afolabi: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Elijah Walton: a team-high 52 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Army is 5-2 overall and 4-1 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 2nd in American.
The season so far: W 59-3 vs Bryant Bulldogs (Sept. 5), L 24-28 vs South Florida Bulls (Sept. 12), W 21-17 at Temple Owls (Sept. 25), L 29-31 at Louisiana Tech Bulldogs (Oct. 3), W 20-17 vs Tulane Green Wave (Oct. 10), W 56-24 vs Florida Atlantic Owls (Oct. 17), W 38-35 at Tulsa Golden Hurricane (Oct. 23).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Army (5-2, 4-1 American) at Memphis (6-2, 3-1 American). Saturday, Oct. 31, 8:00 p.m. ET (7:00 p.m. Central), Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis, Tenn., ESPNU.
Last time out. Army won 38-35 at Tulsa on Friday night, Oct. 23, for its third win in a row. The Black Knights trailed 35-28 in the fourth quarter. Hellums tied it with a 1-yard run with 1:50 left, and Dawson Jones kicked a 50-yard field goal as time ran out. Jones also made one from 51, and the school says he's the first Army kicker to make two field goals of 50 or more in one game. Hellums ran for 121 yards and three touchdowns, and Godspower Nwawuihe ran 12 times for 135 yards, including a 66-yard touchdown.
Memphis beat East Carolina 41-34 in overtime on Thursday, Oct. 22. Stokes threw for 320 yards and accounted for all five touchdowns, three throwing and two running. Jemyri Davis caught seven balls for 91 yards and two scores. The win made Memphis bowl-eligible for the 13th straight season.
Players to watch. Army quarterback Cale Hellums is the engine of the option. He has 159 carries for 840 yards and 16 rushing touchdowns, and he has completed 39 of 69 throws for 422 yards and three touchdowns. Brady Anderson leads the team with 10 catches for 163 yards. On defense, linebacker Elijah Walton has 52 tackles and linebacker Victor Afolabi has three sacks.
Memphis quarterback Marcus Stokes is 150 of 224 for 2,161 yards, 21 touchdowns and six interceptions. Running back Jaylin Carter has 128 carries for 833 yards and eight touchdowns. Tight end Hunter Tipton leads the receivers with 30 catches for 409 yards and five touchdowns. On defense, Elijah Kinsler has 5.5 sacks and linebacker Mike Montgomery has 58 tackles.
Availability. No official availability report had been posted for this game as of Tuesday. Early injury pages show no reported injuries for either team. Watch for the official report closer to kickoff.
The coaches. Jeff Monken has led Army since 2014, and he coached Georgia Southern before that. After the Tulsa win, he said the Black Knights still need to improve, especially after a rough third quarter. Meet Your Insider

The School in 60 Seconds
East Carolina played its first season in 1932. The Pirates have won seven conference championships and eleven bowl games, and they've produced 20 All-Americans. Four players have their jerseys retired. Except for the 1999 Miami game, the Pirates have played every home game at Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium since 1963. CFBD lists the stadium's capacity at 50,000 on natural grass. Today ECU plays in the American Conference at the FBS level.

The last five seasons have had real swells and troughs: 7-5 in 2021, 8-5 in 2022, a rough 2-10 in 2023, then 8-5 in 2024 and 9-4 in 2025. That 9-4 finish last year is the best of the stretch.

The Coach and the Scheme
Blake Harrell is the captain on this deck. Wikipedia lists him as head coach since the 2024 season, and CFBD records his hire date as Nov. 27, 2024. My public sources don't detail his earlier coaching stops, so I won't guess at them.

The beachy talk is real, but so is the analysis underneath it, I promise. When we win, it's "a perfect swell day" and a slow-motion hair flip. When we lose, I sigh "flat water" and post a sunset anyway, because it's still Boca. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, sun and stats. "Surf's up on tempo, babe."

The School in 60 Seconds
Florida Atlantic football is young, and it was built by a legend. Howard Schnellenberger founded the program from scratch and served as its first head coach. I love a program that's still writing its story.

report.title: Anchors Aweigh in Foxborough: Navy and No. 5 Notre Dame Renew a Classic at Gillette Stadium
report.byline: Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather · Navy Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Good afternoon, and welcome aboard. I'm Commander Annabel Merriweather, retired, your Navy insider. I spent my career as a surface warfare officer, and I read an option play the way I read a nautical chart: depth, current and where the rocks are hiding. I speak in nautical terms, and I cannot be stopped. When we win, I say, "Anchors aweigh!" and ring a ship's bell. When we lose, I say, "Steady as she goes," and plot a new course. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with crisp navigation.

The School in 60 Seconds
Navy plays at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium in Annapolis, listed at 34,000. Last season the Midshipmen went 11-2, won the Liberty Bowl 35-13 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll. They also won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy for the second straight season, beating Air Force 34-31 and Army 17-16. The win over Army came on a fourth-and-goal touchdown throw. Anchors aweigh. Navy has now beaten Army in back-to-back seasons, and in Annapolis that's the voyage everyone remembers.

The Coach and the Scheme
Brian Newberry was hired on Dec. 19, 2022. The scheme is the option, and it's the fleet's pride.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 29.7 points per game and allowing 29.1.

Players to Know
QB Jackson Gutierrez: 32 of 64, 692 yards, 7 touchdowns, 1 interception.
Jackson Gutierrez on the ground: 869 yards on 150 carries, 12 touchdowns.
TE Jordan Collins: 6 catches, 212 yards, 3 touchdowns.
LB MarcAnthony Parker: 4 sacks, the team lead.
LB Coleman Cauley: a team-high 58 tackles.

The Conference Picture

The season so far: W 42-15 vs Towson Tigers (Sept. 5), L 30-38 at Florida Atlantic Owls (Sept. 12), L 20-24 at UAB Blazers (Sept. 25), L 9-14 at Air Force Falcons (Oct. 3), W 34-26 vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane (Oct. 10), L 34-38 at UTSA Roadrunners (Oct. 17), L 39-49 vs North Texas Mean Green (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
No. 5 Notre Dame (6-1, independent) at Navy (2-5, 1-4 American). Saturday, Oct. 31, 12 p.m. ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough, Mass. (neutral site), ABC.
Last time out. Notre Dame had the week off. Its last game was a 28-24 loss at BYU on Oct. 17, when Carr threw for 261 yards, Nolan James Jr. ran for a touchdown, and Jaden Greathouse caught eight balls for 125 yards.
Navy lost 49-39 to North Texas on Oct. 24. Gutierrez ran 26 times for 228 yards and three touchdowns, and he threw a touchdown, too.
Players to watch. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr has thrown the most passes in all seven Irish games. He's 129 of 193 for 1,639 yards, 16 touchdowns and just one interception. Jordan Faison leads the receivers with 34 catches for 451 yards and four scores, and Jonaz Walton leads the rushers with 426 yards. On defense, linebacker Drayk Bowen has 38 tackles and defensive lineman Boubacar Traore has 3.5 sacks.
Navy quarterback Jackson Gutierrez is the engine of the option. He has 869 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns on 150 carries, and he's thrown for 692 yards and seven touchdowns on just 64 attempts. Tight end Jordan Collins has turned six catches into 212 yards and three scores. On defense, linebacker Coleman Cauley has 58 tackles and linebacker MarcAnthony Parker has four sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Carr has thrown the most passes in every Notre Dame game, and Gutierrez has done it in every Navy game since the opener, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Marcus Freeman was hired at Notre Dame on Dec. 3, 2021. His teams went 9-4, 10-3, 14-2 and 10-2 over the last four seasons, and this year's Irish score 41.1 points a game while allowing 13.4. They've forced 16 turnovers and lost just two.
Brian Newberry was hired at Navy on Dec. 19, 2022. Last season his Midshipmen went 11-2, won the Liberty Bowl 35-13 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll. They also won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy for the second straight season, beating Air Force 34-31 and Army 17-16.
Storylines. This game is a chess match between the Navy option and a Notre Dame defense that allows only 2.4 yards a carry. Navy gains 5.7 yards a carry, so something has to give. The Irish big guys up front will try to keep Gutierrez from turning the corner. On the other side, Carr has been nearly perfect with the ball, and Navy's defense allows 29.1 points a game.
Fun and true. Notre Dame claims 11 national championships, from 1924 through 1988. The Irish have won eight of the last nine regular-season meetings in this series, including 49-10 last year. Navy's lone win in that stretch was a thriller, 28-27 in 2016. And the Band of the Fighting Irish and the Navy midshipmen in the stands make this one of the most respectful scenes in the sport.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Declan Moriarty-Chen, Notre Dame's insider. Here's what I said:
"You would posit correctly, young man. Welcome aboard. Mind the ship's bell. It's loud."
"Six catches, 212 yards. Jordan Collins is a submarine. You never see him until he surfaces in the end zone."
"Steady as she goes. Two hundred twenty-eight yards is still a fine day at sea."
"I'm coming as a lighthouse. Practical and festive."
"The honor is mine, young man. Anchors aweigh."
And the last word from Declan: "Commander, whatever happens, I'd be honored to say grace with you after the game."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
This one's played away from both campuses, at Gillette Stadium outside Boston, and a Halloween noon kickoff in New England should bring plenty of sailors and leprechauns to the stands. Back in Annapolis, Navy usually plays at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, which seats 34,000. Notre Dame Stadium, built in 1930, seats 80,795, and visitors never miss "Touchdown Jesus."

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Mean Green, baby! I'm Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, your North Texas insider, coming at you from Denton, a town with more music going on per square block than just about anywhere in Texas. I'm a sports nerd and an indie-rock nerd, and I hear football the way I hear a record. Every offense has a tempo. Some are steady four-on-the-floor. Ours? The School in 60 Seconds
North Texas plays at DATCU Stadium in Denton, listed at 30,850. Eric Morris left for Oklahoma State, and Neal Brown took over. Mean Green, baby.

The Coach and the Scheme
Neal Brown was named the 21st head coach in North Texas history on Dec. 2, 2025. He had 10 seasons as an FBS head coach at Troy and West Virginia and went 72-51. At Troy he won the 2017 Sun Belt title and was the conference's Coach of the Year, and his 2016-18 teams went 31-8. His 2023 West Virginia team went 9-4. He's 5-1 in bowl games.

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Owl family! I'm Odalys Chen-Moreau, your Rice insider. I'm finishing a bioengineering PhD, and I model football like a clinical trial: control group, treatment group and a very long methods section. You should also know I'm basically a stats cop with a badge. If someone makes a sweeping claim off two games, I will walk over, flash the badge and say, "N equals too small." When we win, I shout "Statistically significant!" and do a dance worthy of any halftime show. When we lose, I say "N is too small to panic"... and then I panic quietly in the lab. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, peer-reviewed.

The School in 60 Seconds
Rice Stadium is one of the most historic venues in American sports. On Sept. 12, 1962, President John F. Kennedy stood there and gave his speech recommitting the country to landing on the moon. On Jan. 13, 1974, the stadium hosted Super Bowl VIII, when Miami beat Minnesota 24-7. It's listed at 47,000 seats. Rice is a small private school playing big-time football in the American Athletic Conference, and that's a story worth telling every single week. Our hypothesis is that grit travels well.

The Coach and the Scheme
Scott Abell was named head coach on Nov. 26, 2024, after seven seasons at Davidson.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 21.0 points per game and allowing 31.8.

Players to Know

This Week: Bye Week
No game for Rice this week. We're off from Tuesday, Oct. 27, through Saturday, Oct. 31, so the rest of this report is about where we stand and what's next.
Last time out. We lost to the Florida Atlantic Owls 51-49 on the road on Oct. 24. Gael Ochoa went 2 of 5 for 80 yards, with 1 touchdown. He also ran 12 times for 259 yards, with 4 touchdowns. Braylen Walker caught 1 balls for 71 yards, with 1 touchdown.
Up next. We play the North Texas Mean Green on the road on Saturday, Nov. 7, 4:00 p.m. ET, at DATCU Stadium in Denton.
The open week is for rest, healing and a good week of practice. I'll be back with a full preview before the next kickoff.

report.title: Green Wave in the Queen City: Tulane Rolls Into Charlotte for Friday Night Football

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Roll Wave! Hey now, I'm Antoine Ducros-Labat, but all Uptown calls me Twan. I've lived within earshot of a brass band my whole life, and I believe every football game is a brass-band parade: you dance your way through it, no matter what. I travel with the Green Wave and I live with the Green Wave, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little music and a lot of food. You'll hear me say a big play "deserved a beignet." I mean that literally. I keep a bag of them in the booth. Uptown on game day, there's a brass band on every corner and a Green Wave flag on every porch. When we win, the parade rolls all night. When we lose, we still dance home. Roll Wave, and save me a beignet.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Green Wave represent Tulane University and compete in the American Conference. Home is Yulman Stadium on campus in Uptown New Orleans, opened in 2014 and listed at 30,000 seats. And the music lately has been sweet: after 2-10 in 2021, Tulane went 12-2, 11-3, 9-5 and 11-3. That's four straight years of brass band, y'all.

Last time out. Charlotte had the week off after beating Temple 38-31 on Oct. 17 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. Rutledge ran for a career-high 123 yards, Derrick Eley caught six passes for 96 yards, and Aiden Bui, kicking for the first time in his career, hit a 47-yard field goal in the final two minutes.

"Darlin', I brought beignets for the whole section. Roll Wave!"
"Sixty-four tackles from Agu. That man shows up to every parade."
"Coach Hall wants a clean game. No fumbles, no fuss, just a good parade."

"Then we'll both bring the brass band, darlin'. Roll Wave!"

report.title: Aloha, Bye Week: Hawai'i Takes a Breather in the Islands
report.byline: Kainoa Akana-Baird · Hawai'i Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Aloha, Rainbow Warriors fans! I'm Kainoa Akana-Baird, your Hawai'i insider. When I'm not on the show, I teach big-wave surfing on O'ahu. And when I'm on the show, I do time-zone math, because when your team flies farther than anybody in college football, somebody has to keep the clocks straight. When we win, I say "Shoots!" and throw a shaka. When we lose, I shrug: "Island time. We'll catch the next wave." Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with aloha. "Island time, but on schedule."

The School in 60 Seconds
Home for us is the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, listed at 15,194. Last season was a big wave. Hawai'i went 9-4, opened the season by beating Stanford, and won the Hawai'i Bowl over Cal after coming back from 21 points down, tying the biggest comeback in program history. It was our first bowl bid since 2021.

The Coach and the Scheme
Timmy Chang was named Hawai'i's 25th head coach on Jan. 22, 2022. Before that, he was a Hawai'i legend. As our quarterback from 2000 to 2004, he set the NCAA career records for passing yards (17,072) and total offense, and he won a program-record 29 games as a starter. He was also a two-time Hawai'i Bowl Most Outstanding Player and a finalist for the Johnny Unitas Award as a senior. Before all that he was a record-setting quarterback at Honolulu's Saint Louis School. Local boy. He coached at Nevada, Jackson State, Emory & Henry and SMU before coming home. In 2025 he was the AFCA Region 5 Coach of the Year.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 20.8 points per game and allowing 24.5.

Players to Know
QB Micah Alejado: 202 of 337, 2,186 yards, 9 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.
RB DeVon Rice: 385 yards on 82 carries, 6 touchdowns.
WR Kainoa Carvalho: 35 catches, 399 yards.
LB Wynden Ho'ohuli: 2 sacks, the team lead.
LB Jamih Otis: a team-high 54 tackles.

The Conference Picture

The season so far: L 27-37 at Stanford Cardinal (Aug. 29), L 6-21 vs UNLV Rebels (Sept. 5), W 29-19 vs New Mexico State Aggies (Sept. 12), L 10-27 at Wyoming Cowboys (Sept. 26), L 16-20 vs San José State Spartans (Oct. 3), L 12-30 at Arizona State Sun Devils (Oct. 10), L 10-21 vs New Mexico Lobos (Oct. 17), W 56-21 at Northern Illinois Huskies (Oct. 24).

This Week: Bye Week
No game for Hawai'i this week. We're off from Tuesday, Oct. 27, through Saturday, Oct. 31, so the rest of this report is about where we stand and what's next.
Last time out. We beat the Northern Illinois Huskies 56-21 on the road on Oct. 24. Micah Alejado went 22 of 32 for 323 yards, with 3 touchdowns and 1 interception. DeVon Rice ran 12 times for 71 yards, with 3 touchdowns. Audric Harris caught 2 balls for 90 yards.
Up next. We play the UTEP Miners on the road on Saturday, Nov. 7, 9:30 p.m. ET, at Sun Bowl in El Paso.
The open week is for rest, healing and a good week of practice. I'll be back with a full preview before the next kickoff.

report.title: Send It to the Rose Bowl: Nevada Visits No. 7 UCLA on Halloween
report.byline: Ridge Corbell · Nevada Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Send it! What's up, Wolf Pack, I'm Ridge Corbell. I ski patrol at Tahoe in the winter, I scout football on a snowboard (figuratively, mostly), and I've discovered that snowboard slang explains advanced football stats better than anything on a whiteboard. Third-down conversion rate? That's just how often you land the jump. When we win, you'll hear "Sick!" and I'll mime a backflip. When we lose, I'll shrug and call it a powder day that went sideways, and then I'll dig into the film. Strap in.

The School in 60 Seconds
Nevada football was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers. We play at Mackay Stadium on the north end of campus. The "new" Mackay opened Oct. 1, 1966, seats 27,000, and its field sits 4,610 feet above sea level. Coach Chris Ault, running back Frank Hawkins and coach Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame, and fullback Marion Motley is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. We compete in the Mountain West. Recent years have been a climb: 8-5 in 2021, then 2-10, 2-10, 3-10 and 3-9.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jeff Choate was hired Dec. 4, 2023.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 26.3 points per game and allowing 22.0.

Players to Know
QB Carter Jones: 53 of 89, 654 yards, 3 touchdowns, 2 interceptions.
RB, the team rushing leader: 582 yards on 111 carries, 5 touchdowns.
WR Gary Givens III: 19 catches, 305 yards, 1 touchdown.
Defender Dylan LaBarbera: 4 sacks, the team lead.

The Conference Picture
Nevada is 3-4 overall and 2-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 6th in Mountain West.
