This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Nevada (3-4, 2-2 Mountain West) at No. 7 UCLA (7-0, 5-0 Big Ten). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4:15 p.m. ET, Rose Bowl, Pasadena, Calif., BTN.
Last time out. UCLA beat Michigan State 28-10 on Homecoming at the Rose Bowl, where the Bruins honored their 1966 Rose Bowl team. Anthony Woods ran 14 times for 112 yards and a touchdown, and Brian Rowe Jr. caught three balls for 74 yards and a score.
Nevada beat San José State 28-13 on Homecoming at Mackay Stadium. Duncan threw two touchdowns, and Marshaun Brown caught five balls for 52 yards and a score.
Players to watch. UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach has thrown the most passes in the last two games. He went 22 of 33 for 264 yards in his first start against Wisconsin and 18 of 31 for 198 yards and a touchdown against Michigan State. Wayne Knight leads the rushers with 627 yards and 12 touchdowns, and Semaj Morgan leads the receivers with 31 catches for 383 yards. Linebacker Sammy Omosigho has five and a half sacks, and Jalen Woods leads the defense with 59 tackles.
Nevada's Luke Duncan threw the most passes last week, going 18 of 29 for 178 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers. Carter Jones leads the team with 654 passing yards. Nevada's top running back has 582 yards and five touchdowns, and Gary Givens III leads the receivers with 19 catches for 305 yards. Linebacker EJ Smith leads the defense with 76 tackles, and Dylan LaBarbera has four sacks.
Availability. The official availability reports haven't been posted yet. UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is out for the season after a knee injury in the Oregon game. For Nevada, starting quarterback Carter Jones (arm) and AJ Bianco (ankle) both missed last week, and coach Jeff Choate said it was too early to say who will start. Check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Bob Chesney is in his first season at UCLA, with a hire date of Dec. 6, 2025. He's a Dickinson College graduate who was head coach at Salve Regina, Assumption, Holy Cross and James Madison, and at Holy Cross he won five straight Patriot League titles. He's the first UCLA coach to begin his tenure 6-0, and the Bruins have kept on winning.
Jeff Choate was hired at Nevada on Dec. 4, 2023. This week he said his goal is to keep the game close: "Let's just drag this thing into deep water and find out who's gonna swim in the fourth quarter."
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Nevada's run game against a UCLA defense that allows 15.3 points a game. Duncan, if he plays, has a story all his own: he spent his first three college seasons at UCLA. On the other side, Knight and UCLA's big guys up front face a Nevada defense that has had trouble stopping the run. This is just the 10th time Nevada has played a top-10 team since moving up to the top level of college football.
Fun and true. UCLA has been ranked in the AP top 10 at least once in every decade since the poll began in the 1930s, and the Bruins won the 1954 Coaches' Poll national title under Red Sanders. Nevada's Mackay Stadium field sits 4,610 feet above sea level, and Chris Ault, Frank Hawkins and Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Kenzie Rhee, UCLA's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thanks, Kenzie. Those mountains have no snow on them, but I'll allow it."
"And the mountain team sends it. Strap in."
"EJ Smith has 76 tackles. That dude never stops carving."
"Sick! I mimed a backflip. Nobody got hurt."
"Coach Choate wants deep water. I'm a snow guy, but I'm in."
"I'm dressing as a snowboard. Pasadena needs a little winter."
"Whatever happens, Kenzie, supper's on me. We'll say grace first."
And the last word from Kenzie: "Deal, darling. I'll bring dessert."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
It's Halloween at the Rose Bowl, listed at 88,565 seats, one week after UCLA's Homecoming. Back in Reno, Nevada fans just celebrated Homecoming Week and the football program's 130th birthday, since the team was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers.

report.title: Balloons Over San José: New Mexico Floats Into the Bay Area on Halloween
report.byline: Paloma Begaye-Ortiz · New Mexico Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Red or green? Both. ¡Hola, Albuquerque! I'm Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, and when I'm not at a Lobos game, I'm floating a hot-air balloon over the Rio Grande at sunrise. Every October I fly in the Balloon Fiesta, and every Saturday I read Lobo football like wind currents: where it's drifting, where it's rising, and when it's about to soar. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with some green-chile spice and a balloon metaphor for every drive. That offense floated like a balloon at dawn, up and up. When we win, I yell, "Red or green? BOTH!" and pump my fist. When we lose, I sigh, "Too much heat today."

The School in 60 Seconds
The New Mexico Lobos compete in the Mountain West. Our colors are cherry and silver. Home is University Stadium in Albuquerque, opened in 1960 and listed at 39,224 seats. The last five years started low: 3-9, 2-10, 4-8, then 5-7 and a big 9-4 in 2025. That's a balloon catching a thermal, y'all. Up and up.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jason Eck is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 16, 2024.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 37.0 points per game and allowing 11.3.

Players to Know
QB Toa Fa'avae: 49 of 87, 790 yards, 5 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Scottre Humphrey: 453 yards on 95 carries, 9 touchdowns.
TE Cade Keith: 20 catches, 265 yards, 2 touchdowns.
DE Brett Karhu: 5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Mercury Swaim: a team-high 43 tackles.

The Conference Picture

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) at San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4 p.m. ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose, Calif., MW+.
Last time out. New Mexico beat North Dakota State 21-16 on Homecoming in Albuquerque on Oct. 24, during a Pack Week that honored the Route 66 centennial. Kiefer Sibley ran 13 times for 91 yards and a touchdown, and Keith caught five balls.
San José State lost 28-13 at Nevada on Oct. 24. Viliami Teu ran for a touchdown, and Dominique McKenzie caught two balls for 60 yards.
Players to watch. New Mexico quarterback Toa Fa'avae has thrown the most passes in the last six games. He's 49 of 87 for 790 yards, five touchdowns and four interceptions. Scottre Humphrey leads the rushers with 453 yards and nine scores, and tight end Cade Keith leads the receivers with 20 catches for 265 yards. Brett Karhu has five sacks, and linebacker Mercury Swaim leads the defense with 43 tackles.
San José State's Luke Weaver threw the most passes in each of the first six games and leads the team with 1,620 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jabari Bates leads the rushers with 586 yards, and freshman Carson Clark leads the receivers with 47 catches for 551 yards and five scores. Jayland McGlothen has six sacks, and linebacker Dylan Lee leads the team with 71 tackles.
Availability. No official Mountain West availability report has been posted for this game yet. San José State's quarterback spot is the big question. Freshman Daniel Rolovich started the last two games, but he was hurt in the first quarter at Nevada, and Weaver came back in the fourth quarter to lead a late scoring drive. Who starts Saturday hasn't been announced, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Jason Eck leads New Mexico, with a hire date of Dec. 16, 2024. His defense allows 11.3 points a game and had taken the ball away 21 times through six games. The Lobos' only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma.
Ken Niumatalolo was hired at San José State on Jan. 21, 2024. Before the UTEP game he went with Rolovich because, as he put it, the staff "just felt like we needed a spark." He also said of the freshman, "He's got a big arm. He's big and strong and can run. He's not afraid."
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Humphrey and the New Mexico big guys up front against a Spartans defense that allows 22.5 points a game. On the other side, whoever plays quarterback for San José State has to find Clark against a Lobos defense that loves taking the ball away. San José State has won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season, and the Spartans are looking for an eighth straight home win over the Lobos.
Fun and true. San José State first played a regular season in 1898, and the Spartans count Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil among their alumni. New Mexico's University Stadium opened in 1960, and last season the Lobos went 9-4.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, San José State's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thanks, Tessa. I brought green chile. Red, too. Both!"
"You can, but the answer is always both."
"Humphrey runs like a balloon catching a thermal. Up and up."
"Too much heat for a while, then we soared. Red or green? BOTH!"
"Coach Eck builds a defense the way I pack a balloon basket. Nothing loose."
"I'm dressing as a hot-air balloon. Cherry and silver, of course."
"Deal, Tessa. I'll bring the green chile."
And the last word from Tessa: "Whatever happens, Paloma, supper's on me. We'll say grace first."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Oh for cute, they think they can run on us. Well, hi there, I'm Ingeborg Halvorsen, Inga to pretty much all of Fargo. I'm an agricultural economist by trade, and I've tracked every Bison championship since I was a girl with a notebook in the Fargodome stands. These days I keep a little model on my laptop about how a team moves from the FCS to the FBS, and so far, the Bison are making it look easy. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, nice as can be, until it's time not to be. When we win, I say, "Oh, for cute, we won!" When we lose, I say, "Oh, yah, that's a tough one," and I bring hotdish. Truth be told, I bring hotdish either way. Tater tot, of course.

The School in 60 Seconds
The Bison represent North Dakota State and now play in the FBS as members of the Mountain West. Home is the Fargodome, 18,700 seats, opened in 1992. And the trophy case, oh my. The Bison have won 18 national championships, none in their current division, and 39 conference championships. That includes 10 FCS national titles between 2011 and 2024. The last five seasons in the Missouri Valley went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1. Yah, we're used to winning around here.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tim Polasek is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 17, 2023. This team plays Bison football: run it, defend it, don't give it away.

For UTEP, Raymond Moore III has thrown the most passes the last two games and leads the team in rushing with 414 yards. Storylines. The matchup to watch is North Dakota State's defense against Moore, who can hurt you with his legs. The Bison's big guys up front have been tough to run on all season. On the other side, Hayes wants a clean day after five interceptions in the two losses, and UTEP's defense will try to force him into more mistakes. This is the first meeting between these schools in our records from 2016 through 2025.
Fun and true. North Dakota State has won 18 national championships, including 10 FCS titles between 2011 and 2024, and 39 conference championships. The Bison went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1 in their last five Missouri Valley seasons. UTEP's fight song is "El Paso Fight."
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Inga Halvorsen, North Dakota State's insider. Here's what I said:
"Thanks, Inga. I brought green chile from El Paso. It's Halloween, so I figured I'd bring the scariest thing I own."
"Then let's make it Hatch-hot hotdish. Neighbors share."
"Raymond Moore III runs like a five-alarm chile. Effort grade: Hatch-hot."
"A week off to rest the legs and sharpen the effort. We'll be fresh."
"Coach Walden is building it brick by brick, like my dad on a Sun Bowl job site."
"I'm dressing as Paydirt Pete. Pickaxe and all."
"Deal, Inga. Share the chile, and the hotdish."
And the last word from Inga: "Whatever happens, Neto, supper's on me. We'll say grace first."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Halloween in Fargo means bundling up, and the Fargodome, opened in 1992 and listed at 18,700 seats, keeps everybody warm and loud inside. UTEP fans call the Sun Bowl home, built in 1963 and listed at 51,500, with the Sound of the Southwest band and mascot Paydirt Pete.

report.title: Mountaineer Moonshine on Halloween Night: App State Rolls Down to Statesboro for a Rivalry Rumble
report.byline: Zeb Coldiron · App State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, howdy. Come on up the mountain. I'm Zebulon Coldiron, but you can call me Zeb, and I'm your App State insider. I'm a fourth-generation Watauga County kid, and I learned to whittle and read a defense on the same front porch. My granddaddy could spot a blitz before the snap and carve a perfect duck in the same afternoon. I'm still working on the duck.

I don't hurry, and I don't holler (much). I treat every week like a hike: steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. That means real numbers, plain talk, and a fair word for every visitor. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll go find out. Some programs get a stadium. We got a mountain with a stadium on it. Come up for the game, stay for the leaves, and bring your grandma a jacket.

The School in 60 Seconds
Appalachian State is in Boone, North Carolina, and has played FBS football in the Sun Belt since 2014. Before that, the Mountaineers were an FCS power from 1978 to 2013. They won three straight national championships from 2005 to 2007, the first FCS team to do it since the playoffs began in 1978. The program has won about 661 games and 22 conference championships. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do so.

Home is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team went unbeaten and unscored upon in the regular season, outscoring opponents 206-0. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,000. The last five seasons: 10-4, 6-6, 9-5, 5-6 and 5-8.

The Coach and the Scheme
Dowell Loggains is in his second season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024. He came to Boone from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator. Before that, he was an NFL offensive coordinator for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets. He played quarterback at Arkansas.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 30.1 points per game and allowing 23.1.

Players to Know
QB Malachi Singleton: 139 of 209, 1,700 yards, 9 touchdowns, 2 interceptions.
RB Jaquari Lewis: 420 yards on 83 carries, 8 touchdowns.
WR Sam Pickett III: 32 catches, 474 yards, 4 touchdowns.
DL Caleb Sandstrom: 5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Colton Phares: a team-high 51 tackles.

The Conference Picture
App State is 5-2 overall and 2-1 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 2nd in Sun Belt East.
The season so far: W 55-3 vs Maine Black Bears (Sept. 5), W 27-24 at East Carolina Pirates (Sept. 12), W 26-21 vs Charlotte 49ers (Sept. 19), L 31-41 at NC State Wolfpack (Sept. 26), L 3-10 vs Old Dominion Monarchs (Oct. 10), W 35-32 at Coastal Carolina Chanticleers (Oct. 16), W 34-31 (OT) vs James Madison Dukes (Oct. 22).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
App State (5-2, 2-1 Sun Belt) at Georgia Southern (3-4, 2-1 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 6:30 p.m. ET, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro, Georgia, ESPN+.
Last time out. App State beat James Madison 34-31 in overtime. Singleton went 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns, and Nate Branch caught six balls for 73 yards.
Georgia Southern had a bye. In its last game, on Oct. 15, the Eagles won 23-15 at Old Dominion. Turner Helton came in for Johnson and went 23 of 30 for 206 yards and a touchdown. Bynum had three tackles for loss, two sacks and a forced fumble, and he was named Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week.
Players to watch. App State quarterback Malachi Singleton has completed 139 of 209 throws for 1,700 yards, with nine touchdowns and just two interceptions. Running back Jaquari Lewis has 420 yards and eight touchdowns, and wide receiver Sam Pickett III has 32 catches for 474 yards. Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks, and linebacker Colton Phares leads with 51 tackles.
Georgia Southern quarterback Max Johnson has thrown for 1,601 yards, with 11 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Wide receiver Alex Taylor has 24 catches for 342 yards. Linebacker Anthony Bynum has four sacks, and linebacker Brandon Tyson has 38 tackles.
Availability. No official Sun Belt availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Johnson hurt his throwing shoulder at Old Dominion and is listed as questionable. "It's really progressed pretty fast, to be honest with you," Clay Helton said. "He walked out there and spun it." For App State, Singleton played through an ankle issue against James Madison.
The coaches. Clay Helton, who led USC to a Rose Bowl title, is 4-1 against App State. His son, Turner, is the backup quarterback who won the Old Dominion game. Georgia Southern has had 16 days to rest and get healthy.
Dowell Loggains is in his second season in Boone. He came from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator, and before that he called plays in the NFL for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets.
Storylines. Here's a fun one. Johnson's father, Brad, and App State backup Henry Hasselbeck's father, Matt, both played in the NFL, and they played in two games against each other, in 2004 and 2006.
Georgia Southern lineman Colin Alexander said a win over App State would make the team "really, really confident" about reaching the conference championship.
Fun and true. This is the 42nd meeting. App State leads the series 21-19-1, but Georgia Southern leads 13-6 in Statesboro. The teams have played every year since 1993, and these two programs are tied for second in the East Division.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Royce Ogeechee, Georgia Southern's insider. Here's what I said:
"Come on down off the mountain, Royce. I brought a jacket for your grandma."
"Two interceptions each. Those are careful young men."
"Praying both quarterbacks are healthy. A rivalry deserves its best."
"Three straight titles, Royce. That's a mountain worth the climb."
"Steady climbing, honest footing, Royce. Then a view at the top."
And the last word from Royce: "Hail Southern, Zeb. The creek is calling."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Allen E. Paulson Stadium opened in 1984 and holds 25,000. Ask anybody about Beautiful Eagle Creek, and the Southern Pride Marching Band will be in full voice.
App State won three straight FCS national championships from 2005 to 2007. Home in Boone is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team outscored its opponents 206-0 in the regular season. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do it.

Georgia Southern had a bye. In its last game, on Oct. 15, the Eagles won 23-15 at Old Dominion. Turner Helton came in for Johnson and went 23 of 30 for 206 yards and a touchdown. Bynum had three tackles for loss, two sacks and a forced fumble, and he was named Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week.
Players to watch. App State quarterback Malachi Singleton has completed 139 of 209 throws for 1,700 yards, with nine touchdowns and just two interceptions. Running back Jaquari Lewis has 420 yards and eight touchdowns, and wide receiver Sam Pickett III has 32 catches for 474 yards. Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks, and linebacker Colton Phares leads with 51 tackles.
Georgia Southern quarterback Max Johnson has thrown for 1,601 yards, with 11 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Wide receiver Alex Taylor has 24 catches for 342 yards. Linebacker Anthony Bynum has four sacks, and linebacker Brandon Tyson has 38 tackles.
Availability. No official Sun Belt availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Johnson hurt his throwing shoulder at Old Dominion and is listed as questionable. "It's really progressed pretty fast, to be honest with you," Clay Helton said. "He walked out there and spun it." For App State, Singleton played through an ankle issue against James Madison.
The coaches. Clay Helton, who led USC to a Rose Bowl title, is 4-1 against App State. His son, Turner, is the backup quarterback who won the Old Dominion game. Georgia Southern has had 16 days to rest and get healthy.
Dowell Loggains is in his second season in Boone. He came from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator, and before that he called plays in the NFL for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets.
Storylines. Here's a fun one. Johnson's father, Brad, and App State backup Henry Hasselbeck's father, Matt, both played in the NFL, and they played in two games against each other, in 2004 and 2006.
Georgia Southern lineman Colin Alexander said a win over App State would make the team "really, really confident" about reaching the conference championship.
Fun and true. This is the 42nd meeting. App State leads the series 21-19-1, but Georgia Southern leads 13-6 in Statesboro. The teams have played every year since 1993, and these two programs are tied for second in the East Division.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Zeb Coldiron, App State's insider. Here's what I said:
"Hail Southern, Zeb! She says thank you, and she says the Eagles are 4-0 on Halloween."
"That's a farm-strong day's work from Anthony."
"That's the goal, Zeb. A conference title game."
"Hail Southern, Zeb. The creek is calling."
And the last word from Zeb: "Steady climbing, honest footing, Royce. Then a view at the top."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Allen E. Paulson Stadium opened in 1984 and holds 25,000. Ask anybody about Beautiful Eagle Creek, and the Southern Pride Marching Band will be in full voice.
App State won three straight FCS national championships from 2005 to 2007. Home in Boone is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team outscored its opponents 206-0 in the regular season. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do it.

report.title: Big City Panthers: Georgia State Welcomes the Teal Tide to Atlanta
report.byline: Malik Overstreet · Georgia State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Next stop, third-and-long. What's up, Atlanta, I'm Malik Overstreet. I went to policy school, I know every MARTA stop by heart, and I know every Georgia State third-down tendency the same way. I travel with the Panthers and I live with the Panthers, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, at Atlanta speed. My system for sizing up opponents is simple: traffic. A defense that can't move is the Connector at rush hour. A defense that flies around is I-285 at 3 a.m. on a Sunday. We're the big-city kids in a conference full of small towns, and I love every road trip into the country. When we win, I dance like I just found a parking spot downtown. When we lose, I blame the traffic on 75/85. Let's ride.

The School in 60 Seconds
Georgia State football is young. The Panthers were founded in 2010 and play at the FBS level in the Sun Belt. Home is Center Parc Stadium, about ten minutes from our downtown campus, listed at 25,000 seats. The last five seasons: a strong 8-5 in 2021, then 4-8, 7-6, 3-9 and a tough 1-11 in 2025.

The Coach and the Scheme
Dell McGee is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Feb. 23, 2024.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 35.9 points per game and allowing 26.0.

Players to Know
QB Cameran Brown: 110 of 166, 1,356 yards, 14 touchdowns, 5 interceptions.
RB Lanear McCrary Jr.: 399 yards on 82 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR Rodshaun Dorsey: 24 catches, 418 yards, 8 touchdowns.
LB Xavier Esqillion: 7 sacks, the team lead.
LB Jaydon Hood: a team-high 45 tackles.

The Conference Picture

The season so far: W 59-10 vs North Carolina A&T Aggies (Sept. 4), W 31-17 at Kennesaw State Owls (Sept. 12), L 30-44 at UCF Knights (Sept. 19), W 35-14 vs Northern Illinois Huskies (Sept. 26), W 42-10 vs Old Dominion Monarchs (Oct. 3), L 22-49 at James Madison Dukes (Oct. 17), L 32-38 at Arkansas State Red Wolves (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Coastal Carolina (2-5, 1-2 Sun Belt) at Georgia State (4-3, 1-2 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 2 p.m. ET, Center Parc Stadium, Atlanta, ESPN+.
Last time out. Coastal had an open date last week. Its last game was a 35-32 loss to App State on Oct. 16, when Bailey threw for 298 yards and three touchdowns, Lee-Knicely ran 18 times for 90 yards, and Robby Washington caught five balls for 118 yards and a score.
Georgia State lost 38-32 at Arkansas State on Oct. 24. Pereira threw two touchdowns, Qwantavius Wiggins ran eight times for 99 yards and a score, and Dorsey caught three balls for 85 yards and a touchdown.
Players to watch. Coastal quarterback Deuce Bailey has thrown the most passes in every game. He's 109 of 204 for 1,638 yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. Dominic Lee-Knicely leads the rushers with 452 yards and three scores, and Colton Hinton leads the receivers with 297 yards and four touchdowns on 13 catches. On defense, linebacker Marcellius Pulliam has 67 tackles and end Ibrahim Diawara has five sacks.
Georgia State quarterback Cameran Brown threw the most passes in each of the first six games. He's 110 of 166 for 1,356 yards, 14 touchdowns and five interceptions, and he threw six touchdowns against Old Dominion. Ayden Pereira threw the most passes last week. Lanear McCrary Jr. leads the rushers with 399 yards and four touchdowns, and Rodshaun Dorsey leads the receivers with 24 catches for 418 yards and eight scores. Linebacker Xavier Esqillion has seven sacks, and Jaydon Hood has 45 tackles.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Bailey has thrown the most passes in every Coastal game, while Brown did for Georgia State in its first six games and Pereira did last week, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Ryan Beard leads Coastal Carolina, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2025. His defense has 15 sacks, 37 tackles for loss and 14 takeaways.
Dell McGee leads Georgia State, and CFBD dates his hire to Feb. 23, 2024. His offense holds the ball 32:34 a game and runs for 206 yards a game.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is the Georgia State ground game against a Coastal defense that allows 4.8 yards a carry. Coastal's big guys up front will need to slow McCrary and Wiggins. On the other side, Bailey and his receivers want to keep throwing deep, while Esqillion hunts for sack number eight. Georgia State is 3-0 at home this season, so Coastal will have to bring its best.
Fun and true. Georgia State football was founded in 2010. Coastal plays at Brooks Stadium in Conway, built in 2003, and its teal turf is the tradition Goldie would show you first. These two have met in every season since 2017, and Coastal has won five of those nine games, including a 51-0 win in 2020 and a 40-27 win in 2025. Georgia State won 42-40 in 2021 and 30-17 in 2023.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Goldie Seabrook, Coastal Carolina's insider. Here's what I said:
"Goldie! Welcome to the big city. How was the drive?"
"That's the Connector at rush hour. Welcome to my world."
"I blamed the traffic on 75/85. Then I moved on."
"Coach McGee's offense moves like the HOV lane. Smooth and fast."
"I'm dressing as a MARTA train. I'll arrive on time."
"Deal, Goldie. Let's ride."
And the last word from Goldie: "Malik, win or lose, the shrimp are on me after the game. We'll say grace first."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Center Parc Stadium sits about ten minutes from Georgia State's downtown campus and is listed at 25,000 seats. A Halloween afternoon in Atlanta should bring plenty of blue-and-white costumes, and Coastal fans will bring their teal.

report.title: Dukes of Harrisonburg: The Title Game Rematch Comes Home on a Thursday Night
report.byline: Lila Shenandoah · James Madison Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Purple reign, y'all! I'm Lila Shenandoah, your James Madison insider. I'm a former JMU cheer captain who somehow became the program's living encyclopedia. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I turn every stat into a cheer. Yes, even penalties. "Give me a FLAG! Give me a FIVE! Give me. a moment to collect myself!"

Here's what you get from me. Glam, volume, and receipts. I'm excited, I'm all-in, and every number I chant has a source behind it. Every opponent gets a respectful pom-pom wave, and I don't invent anything, ever. If I don't know, I'll say, "Hold that chant, I'm checking." The Shenandoah Valley shows up loud and proud for the Dukes. Give me a J, give me an M, give me a third-down stop.

The School in 60 Seconds
JMU first fielded a football team in 1972, and the Dukes play on campus at Bridgeforth Stadium in Harrisonburg, Virginia. CFBD lists it as built in 1975 with a capacity of 24,877. JMU won FCS national championships in 2004 and 2016 and finished as national runner-up in 2017 and 2019. The Dukes accepted an invitation to the FBS in 2021 and joined the Sun Belt. Famous Dukes include Charles Haley, who won five Super Bowl rings and is in both the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame.

The last five seasons are pure cheer material: 12-2, 8-3, 11-2, 9-4 and 12-2. Give me a W! Give me lots of them!

The Coach and the Scheme
Billy Napier is in his first season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 6, 2025. He was head coach at Louisiana from 2018 to 2021, going 40-12 with three straight seasons of 10 or more wins, and then at Florida from 2022 to 2025. Before becoming a head coach, he was offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Arizona State in 2017.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 41.4 points per game and allowing 18.2.

Players to Know
QB Camden Coleman: 131 of 212, 1,567 yards, 14 touchdowns, 2 interceptions.
RB George Pettaway: 824 yards on 124 carries, 8 touchdowns.
WR Corey Scott: 24 catches, 371 yards, 4 touchdowns.
LB JT Hooten: 3 sacks, the team lead.
LB Nakian Jackson: a team-high 59 tackles.

The Conference Picture
James Madison is 7-1 overall and 4-1 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 1st in Sun Belt East.
The season so far: W 20-13 vs Liberty Flames (Sept. 5), W 87-3 vs Wagner Seahawks (Sept. 12), W 26-13 at San Diego State Aztecs (Sept. 19), W 46-20 at Old Dominion Monarchs (Sept. 26), W 45-17 vs Marshall Thundering Herd (Oct. 3), W 27-24 at Georgia Southern Eagles (Oct. 10), W 49-22 vs Georgia State Panthers (Oct. 17), L 31-34 (OT) at App State Mountaineers (Oct. 22).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Troy (3-4, 1-2 Sun Belt) at James Madison (7-1, 4-1 Sun Belt). Thursday, Oct. 29, 7:30 p.m. ET, Bridgeforth Stadium, Harrisonburg, Va., ESPN2.
Last time out. James Madison lost 34-31 in overtime at App State on Oct. 22, its first loss of the season. Coleman went 22 of 39 for 232 yards and a touchdown, and Braeden Wisloski caught two passes for 84 yards and a score.
Troy lost 21-14 to UL Monroe at home on Oct. 24. The Trojans led 14-3 with less than three minutes to play before the Warhawks rallied in the final minutes. Jordan Lovett ran 17 times for 70 yards.
Players to watch. James Madison quarterback Camden Coleman is 131 of 212 for 1,567 yards, 14 touchdowns and just two interceptions. Wide receiver Corey Scott leads the Dukes with 24 catches for 371 yards and four scores. On defense, linebacker Nakian Jackson has 59 tackles and linebacker JT Hooten has three sacks.
For Troy, quarterback Goose Crowder is 102 of 183 for 1,162 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back Gavin Griffin has 398 rushing yards, and wide receiver TK Keyes has 13 catches for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Defensive back Donnie Smith has six sacks, and linebacker Keno Jones leads the team with 52 tackles.
Availability. The Sun Belt has not posted an availability report for this game. James Madison running back George Pettaway, the team's leading rusher with 824 yards and eight touchdowns, is out with a lower-body injury, according to the Daily News-Record. Nick Herman and Seth Cromwell are the next backs up. Troy quarterback Goose Crowder has been dealing with a shoulder injury, and coach Gerad Parker had not settled on a quarterback plan early in the week, according to AL.com. Tucker Kilcrease played after Crowder came out against UL Monroe. Watch the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Billy Napier is in his first season at James Madison. He went 40-12 at Louisiana from 2018 to 2021 and then coached Florida from 2022 to 2025. His Dukes score 41.4 points a game and allow 18.2.
Gerad Parker is in his third season at Troy. He was hired on Dec. 18, 2023. His team has a short week and a long trip after a tough Saturday.
Storylines. The Troy quarterback room is the big question. Whoever plays will face a James Madison defense that allows just 18.2 points a game. On the other side, the Dukes have to replace Pettaway's carries, and Smith will be hunting Coleman all night.
Coleman has been careful with the football. Two interceptions in 212 attempts is a fine way to keep a team in every game.
Fun and true. This is the fifth all-time meeting, and James Madison leads 3-1, including 2-0 at home. The teams met twice in the FCS playoffs, in 1994 and 1999. James Madison won the 2025 Sun Belt Championship Game 31-14 over Troy and went on to the College Football Playoff. In 2023, the Dukes won 16-14.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Marlo Pickens, Troy's insider. Here's what I said:
"Purple reign, y'all! Give me a T, give me an R, give me a warm welcome for our guests!"
"Give me a deep breath! Both teams want to turn the page."
"Give me a T, give me an O! Turnover margin, y'all!"
"Give me a P, give me an E, give me a costume contest!"
"Give me a handshake, Marlo. See you Thursday."
And the last word from Marlo: "Sixteen to fourteen in 2023. We were right there, Lila. That's not peanuts."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Bridgeforth Stadium seats 24,877, and the Dukes have won 11 straight games there. It is a Thursday night in the Shenandoah Valley two days before Halloween, so the night already feels like a party.

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Laissez les bons stats rouler! Bonjour, mes amis, I'm Amélie Fontenot, but everybody from Lafayette to Breaux Bridge calls me Mimi. By weekday I'm an accountant. A touchdown? Magnifique. A turnover? Ça c'est bon (if it's ours). Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little accordion in the background. When we win, I two-step around the desk. When we lose, I say "Laissez les bons temps... later," and eat my boudin solemnly. Allons!

The School in 60 Seconds
The Ragin' Cajuns represent the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, and you may remember the old names, Southwestern Louisiana and USL. We play in the Sun Belt. Home since 1971 has been Cajun Field in Lafayette, listed at 41,426 seats. Our recent history has some magnifique years: 13-1 in 2021 and 10-4 in 2024, with 6-7 seasons in between and 6-7 again in 2025. And the gameday? Cher, the food alone is worth the drive. I've never met a tailgate that didn't have a pot of something on it.

The Coach and the Scheme
Michael Desormeaux was hired Dec. 5, 2021.

report.title: Peaches, Parades and Bulldogs: Louisiana Tech Marches Into Mobile on Halloween
report.byline: Booker "Champ" Tullos · Louisiana Tech Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, that's just peachy. Howdy, Bulldog fans, I'm Booker Tullos, but folks around Ruston call me Champ. I grew up on a peach farm off the highway, played fullback for Tech, and to this day nothing in football makes me happier than a fourth-and-inches plunge into the end zone. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines in an easygoing north-Louisiana drawl, with peach puns baked right in like a cobbler. When we win, I holler "Peachy!" and do a fullback dive across the studio (the carpet has suffered). When we lose, I sigh "bruised peach," and then I go back and watch every snap. Sit a spell. And remember what my granddaddy said about peaches and football: the good ones take a whole season to ripen.

The School in 60 Seconds
Louisiana Tech first played in 1901 and has an all-time record of 654-508-37. The Bulldogs have won three Division II national championships and 25 conference titles, and played in 30 postseason games, 15 of them major college bowls. Since 1968, home has been Joe Aillet Stadium in Ruston, listed at 28,019 seats. After 13 seasons in Conference USA, Tech joined the Sun Belt on July 1, 2026, so this is our first fall in a new orchard. The recent climb: 3-9 three years running from 2021 to 2023, 5-8 in 2024 and 8-5 in 2025. That's a tree that's starting to bear fruit.

The Coach and the Scheme
Sonny Cumbie is the head coach, hired Nov. 30, 2021.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 32.3 points per game and allowing 21.0.

Players to Know
QB Blake Baker: 96 of 133, 1,160 yards, 10 touchdowns, 1 interception.
RB Andrew Burnette: 349 yards on 85 carries, 1 touchdown.
WR Jalen Mickens: 40 catches, 586 yards, 3 touchdowns.
LB Alonzo Jackson Jr.: 6.5 sacks, the team lead.
LB Alonzo Jackson Jr.: a team-high 48 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Louisiana Tech is 5-2 overall and 3-0 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 1st in Sun Belt West.
The season so far: W 80-6 vs Northwestern State Demons (Sept. 5), L 14-45 at LSU Tigers (Sept. 12), L 19-36 at Baylor Bears (Sept. 19), W 31-29 vs Army Black Knights (Oct. 3), W 32-31 vs Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns (Oct. 10), W 24-0 at UL Monroe Warhawks (Oct. 17), W 26-0 vs Old Dominion Monarchs (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Louisiana Tech (5-2, 3-0 Sun Belt) at South Alabama (4-3, 2-1 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3 p.m. ET, Hancock Whitney Stadium, Mobile, Ala., ESPN+.
Last time out. Louisiana Tech shut out Old Dominion 26-0 at home on Oct. 24. Baker went 28 of 34 for 303 yards and a touchdown, Burnette ran 20 times for 63 yards, and Eli Finley caught 10 balls for 128 yards and a score.
South Alabama lost 20-13 at Marshall on Tuesday, Oct. 20, so the Jaguars have had some extra days to get ready. Hollins threw for 148 yards, Phillips ran 16 times for 70 yards, and Jenkins caught four balls for 75 yards.
Players to watch. Louisiana Tech quarterback Blake Baker is 96 of 133 for 1,160 yards, 10 touchdowns and one interception. Trey Kukuk threw the most passes against Baylor and Army, but Baker has handled that role the last three games. Andrew Burnette leads the rushers with 349 yards, and Jalen Mickens leads the receivers with 40 catches for 586 yards and three scores. Linebacker Alonzo Jackson Jr. leads the defense with 48 tackles and 6.5 sacks.
South Alabama runs the ball first. Keenan Phillips has 514 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 96 carries. Jared Hollins plays quarterback and is 68 of 125 for 1,003 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions, after Bishop Davenport threw the most passes in the first two games. Brendan Jenkins leads the receivers with 25 catches for 430 yards and three scores. Safety Cole Blaylock leads the team with 46 tackles, and linebacker William Felton IV has two sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Baker has thrown the most passes for Louisiana Tech in five of seven games, and Hollins has done it for South Alabama in each of the last five, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Sonny Cumbie is Louisiana Tech's head coach, hired Nov. 30, 2021. His defense takes the ball away, with 13 takeaways and a plus-5 turnover margin, and his team has won tight ones, 31-29 over Army and 32-31 over Louisiana.
Major Applewhite has led South Alabama since 2024. He was head coach at Houston in 2017 and 2018, and as a player he quarterbacked Texas from 1998 to 2001. His Jaguars run the ball much more than they throw it and score 35.1 points a game.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Phillips and the South Alabama ground game against a Tech defense that has not allowed a point in two weeks. The Jaguars' big guys up front will need to open lanes. On the other side, Baker has been sharp, and Mickens and Finley give him places to throw. Tech is trying to stay unbeaten in league play in its first Sun Belt season.
Fun and true. Louisiana Tech first played football in 1901 and has won three Division II national championships and 25 conference titles. After 13 seasons in Conference USA, Tech joined the Sun Belt on July 1, 2026. South Alabama started its program in 2009, joined the FBS in 2012 and went 10-3 in 2022. These two have met before: Tech won 34-16 in 2017 and 30-26 in 2018, and South Alabama won 38-14 in 2022.

THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Greetings, Zips fans, and welcome! I'm Hollister Grubbs, but everybody calls me Zip. I'm a polymer-science grad from the Rubber City, and I measure football the only scientific way: in tire tread depth. Deep, grippy tread means a team that holds the road on third down. Bald tires mean a team sliding all over the place. I travel with this team and I live with this team, usually with a clipboard of formulas. When we win, I bounce like a superball: BOING! When we lose, I say, "Some tread wear today," and start scribbling equations to figure out why. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, vulcanized for durability. "That's some sticky tread."

The School in 60 Seconds
Akron plays at InfoCision Stadium, listed at 30,000, in a city that put the world on rubber tires. Our big rivalry is the Wagon Wheel game against Kent State. The trophy dates to 1946, and Kent State won the first nine games for it. Kent State won the 2025 meeting 42-35. Before that, we won the 2023 and 2024 meetings, 31-27 and 38-17.

He was NFL Rookie of the Year in 1996, made four Pro Bowls, and is in the College Football Hall of Fame. He even appeared on Broadway in "Chicago." That's a hat trick and then some. He's also one of only two NFL running backs, with Jim Brown, to rush for 10,000 yards without ever missing a start. Per the school, only Walter Payton started more consecutive regular-season games than his 130. Iron man. Goalie-approved.

Linebacker Justyce Betts has 58 tackles, and end Scoop Gardner Jr. has four sacks.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Kastantin and Lowry have each thrown the most passes in every game for their teams, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Lance Taylor was hired at Western Michigan on Dec. 8, 2022, and in December 2025 he signed an extension through the 2030 season. Last year he was MAC Coach of the Year, and the Broncos won the 2025 MAC championship, only the fourth conference title in school history.
Eddie George was named Bowling Green's 21st head coach on March 9, 2025. He won the 1995 Heisman Trophy at Ohio State, when he ran for 1,927 yards and 24 touchdowns. He was NFL Rookie of the Year in 1996, made four Pro Bowls, and is in the College Football Hall of Fame. He even performed on Broadway in "Chicago."
Storylines. The matchup to circle is Buckley against a Bowling Green run defense that allows 5.6 yards a carry. On the other side, Bradley will try to crash the pocket against a Western Michigan team that has given up only nine sacks. Lowry was named MAC Offensive Player of the Year last season, and he'll want to bounce back after a 12 of 29 day at Toledo. The Bronco big guys up front will be key in both directions.
Fun and true. Western Michigan won the Cannon Trophy in 2023 and 2025, and the 2025 team's seven conference wins tied for the second-most in school history. Bowling Green has won the last two meetings with the Broncos, 34-10 in 2023 and 31-13 in 2024. Before that, Western Michigan won 49-10 in 2019.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Corwin Dahlquist, Western Michigan's insider. Here's what I said:
"Corwin, I'm a goalie. I'll take whatever stops pucks. And syrup. Lots of syrup."
"Eight sacks for Myles Bradley. That's a hat trick, plus a hat trick, plus two more. In goalie terms, that's a brick wall."
"Two minutes in the penalty box for me. I've served my time."
"And he's ours. Goalie-approved."
"Corwin, win or lose, breakfast is on me after the game. We'll say grace first."
And the last word from Corwin: "Deal, Darcy. Full stack, extra syrup, and a prayer of thanks."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Waldo Stadium seats 30,200, and last season the Broncos averaged 20,000 fans a game at home for the first time since 2016. A Halloween noon kickoff in Kalamazoo means crisp fall air and plenty of brown-and-gold costumes. Bowling Green's home is Doyt L. Perry Stadium, which seats 24,000.

report.title: Flashes Out West: Kent State Makes Its First Trip to Hornet Stadium for Fireworks Friday
report.byline: Ozzie Brannigan · Kent State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hello, Golden Flashes fans. Welcome. I'm Ozzie Brannigan, your Kent State insider. I graduated from a campus with a famous fashion school, so I rate two things every week: uniforms and fourth-down decisions. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I'm a pessimist, and the annoying part is how often I'm right. When we lose, I say, "I expected this," and I mean it. When we win, there's a stunned silence, and then I say, "I expected this," which is not true at all. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, with realistic expectations. Very realistic. "I expected this. I always expect this."

The School in 60 Seconds
Kent State plays at Dix Stadium, listed at 25,319. Our rivalry with Akron is the Wagon Wheel game, a trophy that dates to 1946. Here is a rare happy fact: Kent State won the first nine Wagon Wheel games. And another one: we beat Akron 42-35 last season. We also won in 2020, 2021 and 2022, including a 69-35 game in 2020. Akron won in 2023 and 2024.

The Coach and the Scheme
Mark Carney is Kent State's 24th head coach. He was interim coach starting in April 2025, and the school removed the interim tag on Oct. 30, 2025.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 14.9 points per game and allowing 30.5.

Players to Know
QB Dru DeShields: 124 of 218, 1,439 yards, 8 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.
RB Brandon White: 235 yards on 68 carries.
WR Wayne Harris: 40 catches, 552 yards, 4 touchdowns.
LB Hayden Dawahare: 4 sacks, the team lead.
LB Hayden Dawahare: a team-high 43 tackles.

The Conference Picture
Kent State is 3-5 overall and 2-2 in league play. ESPN's standings have us 7th in MAC.
The season so far: L 0-57 at South Carolina Gamecocks (Sept. 5), W 36-15 vs Wofford Terriers (Sept. 12), L 3-59 at Ohio State Buckeyes (Sept. 19), W 26-13 vs Ball State Cardinals (Sept. 26), L 10-13 vs Ohio Bobcats (Oct. 3), L 7-38 at Western Michigan Broncos (Oct. 10), L 2-29 at South Florida Bulls (Oct. 17), W 35-20 vs Akron Zips (Oct. 24).

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Kent State (3-5, 2-2 MAC) at Sacramento State (1-7, 0-5 MAC). Friday, Oct. 30, 10:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. Pacific), Hornet Stadium, Sacramento, Calif., ESPN2.
Last time out. Kent State beat Akron 35-20 at home to keep the Wagon Wheel. After a 7-7 halftime tie, DeShields threw four touchdown passes and ran for another, and Harris caught nine passes for 156 yards and three scores.
Sacramento State lost 34-17 at Ball State, but the Hornets led twice in the first half. Sharman threw two touchdown passes, Jace Wilson caught a 55-yard score, and Silvera picked off two passes and made 11 tackles.
Players to watch. Kent State quarterback Dru DeShields is 124 of 218 for 1,439 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions, and he has run for a team-high four scores. Wide receiver Wayne Harris has 40 catches for 552 yards and four touchdowns, and running back Brandon White leads the rushers with 235 yards. Linebacker Hayden Dawahare leads the defense with 43 tackles and four sacks.
Sacramento State quarterback Jackson Sharman is 123 of 218 for 1,257 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. Wide receiver Matt Coleman has 39 catches for 492 yards and five scores, fourth in the MAC in receiving yards. Running back Isaiah Ene has 303 yards. Safety Boogsie Silvera leads the team with 61 tackles.
Availability. The MAC has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Sacramento State has used seven different starting groups on offense this year, and Silvera is the only Hornets defender to start all eight games.
The coaches. Mark Carney is in his second season as Kent State's head coach and is 8-12. Kent State removed his interim tag on Oct. 30, 2025, so Friday is one year to the day. His assistant head coach and defensive coordinator, Cherokee Valeria, coached Sacramento State's defensive backs from 2019 to 2024 and was part of three Big Sky championships.
Alonzo Carter is a first-time head coach. Sacramento State hired him on Dec. 15, 2025, and he's leading the Hornets through their first FBS season.
Storylines. Silvera is a fifth-year player whose path ran through Charleston Southern, McNeese and USF. He has three games this season with double-digit tackles.
The Hornets have football families, too. Coleman's father, Herman, played quarterback at Southern, and Onterrio Smith Jr., who has 33 catches for 350 yards, is the son of former Tennessee and Oregon running back Onterrio Smith, who played for the Minnesota Vikings.
The Sacramento State special teams group calls itself the Wefense. Kicker Grant Meadors hit a career-long 47-yarder at Ball State, and punter Hamish Adams of Melbourne, Australia, averaged 45.3 yards on six punts.
Fun and true. This is the first meeting between the schools. Sacramento State went 7-5 in 2025, its last FCS season, and has played four Friday night games since 2000. Adams is the program's third straight punter from Australia, and all three came through ProKick Australia.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Mateo Villaseñor, Sacramento State's insider. Here's what I said:
"I expected fireworks. I always expect fireworks. I just don't expect them to be for us."
"Four touchdown passes. I'm happy. I'm also nervous that I'm happy."
"Healthcare Appreciation Night is perfect. I'll need a nurse by the fourth quarter."
"Fine. Great punting. I expected that too."
And the last word from Mateo: "Three Aussie punters in a row. That's a family recipe."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Friday is Healthcare Appreciation and AANHPI Heritage Night at Hornet Stadium, and the postgame fireworks are back. Ted Emrich and former Texas running back Fozzy Whitaker will call the game on ESPN2.

report.title: Fireworks Friday at Hornet Stadium: Sacramento State Hosts Kent State
report.byline: Mateo Villaseñor · Sacramento State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
¡Hola, Hornets! I'm Mateo Villaseñor, your Sacramento State insider. I'm a farm-to-fork chef in the capital city, and before that I played linebacker for the Hornets, so I explain defenses the only way I know: like recipes. A good defense is a good sauce. Balance, heat and nobody leaving early. I narrate every play like a cooking competition. When we win, it's "Plate it up, chef!" and a chef's kiss. When we lose, I say, "Back to the kitchen," and sharpen a knife. On paper. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, served fresh.

The School in 60 Seconds
Sacramento State joined the MAC as a football-only member on July 1, 2026, for a five-year term, moving up from FCS to FBS. Last year, in our final Big Sky season, we went 7-5 and 5-3 in the league. This is a brand-new menu. The Hornets took the spot left by Northern Illinois, which moved to the Mountain West. The rest of our sports play in the Big West. Home is Hornet Stadium in Sacramento, listed at 21,195. New dish, new kitchen, same hungry Hornets.

The Coach and the Scheme
Alonzo Carter was hired on Dec. 15, 2025, after Brennan Marion left for Colorado. Carter is a first-time head coach who spent eight seasons on Brent Brennan's staffs at San Jose State and Arizona, and he's a Northern California native who started out as a high school coach in the state.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 15.2 points per game and allowing 32.9.

Players to Know
QB Jackson Sharman: 123 of 218, 1,257 yards, 8 touchdowns, 6 interceptions.

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides
Kent State (3-5, 2-2 MAC) at Sacramento State (1-7, 0-5 MAC). Friday, Oct. 30, 10:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. Pacific), Hornet Stadium, Sacramento, Calif., ESPN2.
Last time out. Kent State beat Akron 35-20 at home to keep the Wagon Wheel. After a 7-7 halftime tie, DeShields threw four touchdown passes and ran for another, and Harris caught nine passes for 156 yards and three scores.
Sacramento State lost 34-17 at Ball State, but the Hornets led twice in the first half. Sharman threw two touchdown passes, Jace Wilson caught a 55-yard score, and Silvera picked off two passes and made 11 tackles.
Players to watch. Kent State quarterback Dru DeShields is 124 of 218 for 1,439 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions, and he has run for a team-high four scores. Wide receiver Wayne Harris has 40 catches for 552 yards and four touchdowns, and running back Brandon White leads the rushers with 235 yards. Linebacker Hayden Dawahare leads the defense with 43 tackles and four sacks.
Sacramento State quarterback Jackson Sharman is 123 of 218 for 1,257 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. Wide receiver Matt Coleman has 39 catches for 492 yards and five scores, fourth in the MAC in receiving yards. Running back Isaiah Ene has 303 yards. Safety Boogsie Silvera leads the team with 61 tackles.
Availability. The MAC has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Sacramento State has used seven different starting groups on offense this year, and Silvera is the only Hornets defender to start all eight games.
The coaches. Mark Carney is in his second season as Kent State's head coach and is 8-12. Kent State removed his interim tag on Oct. 30, 2025, so Friday is one year to the day. His assistant head coach and defensive coordinator, Cherokee Valeria, coached Sacramento State's defensive backs from 2019 to 2024 and was part of three Big Sky championships.
Alonzo Carter is a first-time head coach. Sacramento State hired him on Dec. 15, 2025, and he's leading the Hornets through their first FBS season.
Storylines. Silvera is a fifth-year player whose path ran through Charleston Southern, McNeese and USF. He has three games this season with double-digit tackles.
The Hornets have football families, too. Coleman's father, Herman, played quarterback at Southern, and Onterrio Smith Jr., who has 33 catches for 350 yards, is the son of former Tennessee and Oregon running back Onterrio Smith, who played for the Minnesota Vikings.
The Sacramento State special teams group calls itself the Wefense. Kicker Grant Meadors hit a career-long 47-yarder at Ball State, and punter Hamish Adams of Melbourne, Australia, averaged 45.3 yards on six punts.
Fun and true. This is the first meeting between the schools. Sacramento State went 7-5 in 2025, its last FCS season, and has played four Friday night games since 2000. Adams is the program's third straight punter from Australia, and all three came through ProKick Australia.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Ozzie Brannigan, Kent State's insider. Here's what I said:
"Welcome to Sacramento, Ozzie! Farm-to-fork capital, Friday night lights and postgame fireworks."
"Look at that, Ozzie. Our quarterbacks have the same attempts, the same touchdowns and the same interceptions. That's a matched pair of plates."
"Coach Valeria coming home? We'll save him a seat at the table. A small one."
"Three Aussie punters in a row. That's a family recipe."
And the last word from Ozzie: "Fine. Great punting. I expected that too."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Friday is Healthcare Appreciation and AANHPI Heritage Night at Hornet Stadium, and the postgame fireworks are back. Ted Emrich and former Texas running back Fozzy Whitaker will call the game on ESPN2.

report.title: Pancakes in Kalamazoo: The Defending MAC Champs Host Bowling Green
report.byline: Corwin Dahlquist · Western Michigan Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hi there, Bronco fans! I'm Corwin Dahlquist, your Western Michigan insider. I studied paper engineering here in Kalamazoo, a town with deep paper-mill roots, so yes, I can tell you the tensile strength of a playbook page. I'm an earnest Michigan nerd, and I size up every opponent the way you'd size up a Kalamazoo diner breakfast. A short stack is light work. A full stack means you'll need a nap afterward. When we win, I declare a full stack and do a big syrup-pour gesture. When we lose, I mourn "short stack today" and eat dry toast on air, because I believe in accountability. Every week you'll get the players, the coaches and the matchup, served hot.

The School in 60 Seconds
Last season was a full stack with whipped cream on top. Western Michigan won the 2025 MAC championship, only the fourth conference title in school history. Lance Taylor was named MAC Coach of the Year. Quarterback Broc Lowry was MAC Offensive Player of the Year, and defensive end Nadame Tucker was Defensive Player of the Year and won the Vern Smith Leadership Award as the league's top player. The 2025 team won seven conference games, tied for the second-most in school history behind the 8-0 run in 2016. The Broncos also won the Cannon Trophy in 2023 and 2025, and Michigan MAC Trophies in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and they finished the season in the Myrtle Beach Bowl against Kennesaw State. Home is Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo, listed at 30,200.

The Coach and the Scheme
Lance Taylor was hired on Dec. 8, 2022, and in December 2025 he signed an extension through the 2030 season.

Through 8 games this season, we're scoring 26.6 points per game and allowing 20.4.

Players to Know

Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Kastantin and Lowry have each thrown the most passes in every game for their teams, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Lance Taylor was hired at Western Michigan on Dec. 8, 2022, and in December 2025 he signed an extension through the 2030 season. Last year he was MAC Coach of the Year, and the Broncos won the 2025 MAC championship, only the fourth conference title in school history.
Eddie George was named Bowling Green's 21st head coach on March 9, 2025. He won the 1995 Heisman Trophy at Ohio State, when he ran for 1,927 yards and 24 touchdowns. He was NFL Rookie of the Year in 1996, made four Pro Bowls, and is in the College Football Hall of Fame. He even performed on Broadway in "Chicago."
Storylines. The matchup to circle is Buckley against a Bowling Green run defense that allows 5.6 yards a carry. On the other side, Bradley will try to crash the pocket against a Western Michigan team that has given up only nine sacks. Fun and true. Western Michigan won the Cannon Trophy in 2023 and 2025, and the 2025 team's seven conference wins tied for the second-most in school history. "Welcome to Kalamazoo, Darcy! I saved you a booth. Short stack or full stack?"
"Short stack today. Dry toast on air, as promised. Accountability matters."
"A Heisman winner on Broadway. That's a full stack with whipped cream."
"I'm dressing up as a pancake. A full stack, naturally."
"Deal, Darcy. Full stack, extra syrup, and a prayer of thanks."

report.title: Cafecito to Go: FIU Brings Miami Flavor to Lynchburg on Halloween
report.byline: Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate · Florida International Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
¡Hola, Panther people! I'm Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, and I grew up in Sweetwater, five minutes from campus, at a kitchen table where my abuela taught me football with cafecito and dominoes. The dominoes were the players. The sugar packets were the defense. To this day I can't watch a fourth-down stop without craving a colada.

Here's what I am: the loudest, warmest, most bilingual hype machine FIU has ever had, and I will never, ever let anybody sleep on this program. Here's what I'm not: a person who makes things up. Every week I'll bring you the real numbers, the real schedule, and an honest, kind look at whoever we're playing. If I don't know something, I'll say "no sé" and go find out. Miami has a lot of teams, but only one is right down the street from my abuela's house. ¡Vamos, Panthers!

The School in 60 Seconds
FIU plays in Conference USA at the FBS level, and home is Pitbull Stadium in Miami. The stadium opened in 1995, and CFBD lists its capacity at 20,000, which matches Wikipedia's figure. The program's trophy case includes a share of the 2010 Sun Belt championship and three bowl appearances.

Look at the last five seasons and you'll see why last year mattered so much to my family: 1-11 in 2021, then three straight 4-8 years, then 7-6 in 2025 and the first bowl trip since 2019. The Panthers also play Florida Atlantic every year in the Shula Bowl.

The Coach and the Scheme
Willie Simmons is in Year Two. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024. Before FIU, he was head coach at Florida A&M from 2018 to 2023, winning a black college national championship and a SWAC title in 2023, and at Prairie View A&M from 2015 to 2017. He played quarterback at Clemson and The Citadel.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 20.1 points per game and allowing 16.3.

Players to Know
QB JJ Kohl: 131 of 227, 1,637 yards, 10 touchdowns, 8 interceptions.
RB Devonte Lyons: 383 yards on 84 carries, 1 touchdown.

DL DeeJay Holmes Jr.: 5 sacks, the team lead.

FIU (3-4, 1-2 Conference USA) at Liberty (6-1, 3-0 Conference USA). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Williams Stadium, Lynchburg, Va., CBSSN.
Last time out. Liberty won 34-6 at Kennesaw State on Thursday, Oct. 22. Purdie threw for 176 yards and a touchdown, and Davis ran for a score. Kennesaw State had won the last three meetings, so this one meant plenty.
FIU lost 26-23 to Middle Tennessee at home on Tuesday, Oct. 20, a "Paws at the Pit" night. Kohl threw three touchdowns, Lyons ran 19 times for 115 yards, and Kyle McNeal caught a scoring ball. The week before, the Panthers lost 27-24 at Jacksonville State.
Players to watch. Liberty quarterback Deshawn Purdie has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 80 of 133 for 1,226 yards and nine touchdowns, and he hasn't thrown an interception all season. Kam Davis leads the rushers with 583 yards and five scores, and Makai Jackson leads the receivers with 23 catches for 540 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Derrell Farrar leads the defense with 39 tackles, and Brenton Williams has three sacks.
FIU quarterback JJ Kohl has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 131 of 227 for 1,637 yards, 10 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Devonte Lyons leads the rushers with 383 yards, and Maguire Anderson leads the receivers with 36 catches for 568 yards. DeeJay Holmes Jr. has five sacks, and DeAndre Boykins leads the team with 37 tackles.
Availability. No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Purdie has thrown the most passes for Liberty every week, and Kohl has done the same for FIU, so check the teams' pregame notes.
The coaches. Jamey Chadwell has led Liberty since the 2023 season, after head coaching stops at North Greenville, Delta State, Charleston Southern and Coastal Carolina. His first Liberty team went 13-1. This year's Flames run the ball and play defense, allowing 14.0 points a game.
Willie Simmons is in his second year at FIU. In his first season, the Panthers went 7-6 and made their first bowl trip since 2019. Before that, he won a black college national championship and a SWAC title at Florida A&M in 2023. He played quarterback at Clemson and The Citadel.
Storylines. The matchup to watch is Davis and Liberty's big guys up front against an FIU defense that allows only 16.3 points a game. On the other side, Kohl needs to find Anderson against a Liberty defense that has been stingy all season. These teams have met four times since 2020. Fun and true. Liberty moved from FCS to FBS and became a full member in 2019. In 2020 the Flames entered the AP poll for the first time, at No. 25, and they joined Conference USA in 2023. FIU shared the 2010 Sun Belt championship and plays Florida Atlantic every year in the Shula Bowl.

"Gracias, Gideon. I brought cafecito and my abuela's dominoes."
"The dominoes are the players, the sugar packets are the defense. It's the scariest playbook in Miami."
"DeeJay Holmes Jr. gets to the quarterback like my abuela gets to the last pastelito. Fast."
"Two three-point losses in a row. My abuela needed two coladas. Then she said, 'Mija, next week.'"
"Coach Simmons wins everywhere he goes. ¡Vamos!"
"I'm dressing as a domino. Double six. The best one."
"Deal, Gideon. I'll bring the cafecito."
And the last word from Gideon: "Whatever happens, Lourdes, supper's on me. We'll say grace first."

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Low and slow wins the fourth quarter! I'm Burl Ashcraft-Neeley, and I'm your Jacksonville State insider. I'm a Calhoun County barbecue pitmaster who has never lived more than ten miles from campus. On the podcast, my segment is called Smokehouse Talk. My rules are simple. I keep it clean and kind, I celebrate players as people, I respect every opponent, and I never invent a stat, a quote or a fact. If I can't source it, you won't hear it from me.

The School in 60 Seconds
Home is AmFirst Stadium in Jacksonville, Ala., built in 1947 with a listed capacity of 24,000. The band is the Marching Southerners. This is the longest Conference USA road trip of the season for Jacksonville State, a long way from AmFirst Stadium and the Marching Southerners. Out in Las Cruces, the Organ Mountains will be watching over Aggie Memorial Stadium.

report.title: Owls After Dark: Kennesaw State Takes Its Hoot to Floyd on a Wednesday Night

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Hey, Owl Nation! I'm Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, your Kennesaw State insider. I'm a Marietta native with a computer science degree, and I've cheered this program since its very first season. I was there for version 1.0. I still have the T-shirt. It no longer fits. That's growth.

Here's my operating system. I'm a builder. I love that some programs have a hundred years of history while Kennesaw State gets to write ours right now, live, in front of us. I'm keeping the notes. Every number I share is sourced and debugged. Every opponent gets respect. When I don't know something, I'll log it as "unknown" instead of guessing. Bugs happen. We patch them, and we ship again. Let's go, Owls.

The School in 60 Seconds
Kennesaw State football began play in 2015 as an FCS member of the Big South Conference. In 2022 the Owls moved to the ASUN's new FCS football league, and after that season they began the transition to FBS ahead of joining Conference USA in 2024. That's an entire program history in about a decade. Speedrun.

Home is Fifth Third Stadium, just outside the Kennesaw city limits. The game feed lists it as Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, and CFBD lists it as built in 2010 with a capacity of 11,040. The last five seasons: 11-2, 5-6, 3-6, 2-10, and then a big jump to 10-4 in 2025. Last year the Owls finished the regular season 9-3 and 7-1 in Conference USA.

The Coach and the Scheme
Jerry Mack is the head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 1, 2024, so this is his second season. He was head coach at North Carolina Central from 2014 to 2017, going 31-15, and was later offensive coordinator and associate head coach at Rice. Jerry Mack is in his second season at Kennesaw State. He went 31-15 as head coach at North Carolina Central and later worked at Rice. His Owls are the defending Conference USA champions, and three of their six losses this year came by three points or fewer.

report.title: Blue Raiders at Floyd: Middle Tennessee Hosts Kennesaw State on Wednesday Night
report.byline: Opal Stonebriar · Middle Tennessee Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Well, hey there, sugar. Come in, sit down, and have a biscuit. I'm Opal Stonebriar, your Middle Tennessee insider. Folks call me the front-row grandma of Murfreesboro. I'm 34. It's a spiritual title.

Here's how this works. I will feed you, I will love on these boys like they're my own, and if you say something about my team that isn't true, I will correct you sweetly and with a citation. I don't make up numbers, I don't make up injuries, and when I don't know something I'll say, "Honey, I don't know yet." Murfreesboro is a city that grew up fast, and so did our program. Come sit with us, and you'll leave a Blue Raider. I promise.

The School in 60 Seconds
Middle Tennessee plays FBS football in Conference USA, out of Murfreesboro, Tennessee. The Blue Raiders have played in 14 bowl games and seven I-AA playoffs. Home is Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, which opened in 1933. The sources disagree on its size. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,788, and Wikipedia lists 27,303. I'm noting both until I check the media guide.

The last five seasons have been a climb and then a dip: 7-6 in 2021, 8-5 in 2022, 4-8 in 2023, and 3-9 in both 2024 and 2025.

The Coach and the Scheme

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 23.3 points per game and allowing 27.6.

Players to Know
QB Roman Gagliano: 126 of 215, 1,404 yards, 12 touchdowns, 2 interceptions.
RB Antonio Martin: 480 yards on 94 carries, 1 touchdown.
WR Cam'ron Lacy: 41 catches, 437 yards, 4 touchdowns.

Kennesaw State lost 34-6 to Liberty on Oct. 22. Collins went 15 of 26 for 124 yards, and Munroe caught three passes for 53 yards. Linebacker Baron Hopson made a season-high 12 tackles. Late in the fourth quarter, coach Jerry Mack gave Landon Varnes some snaps at quarterback.

Jerry Mack is in his second season at Kennesaw State. He went 31-15 as head coach at North Carolina Central and later worked at Rice. His Owls are the defending Conference USA champions, and three of their six losses this year came by three points or fewer.

report.title: Bears in Springfield: Missouri State Hosts Sam Houston on a Tuesday Night
report.byline: Clementine Bilyeu · Missouri State Insider · Week 9
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
Howdy from the Ozarks! I'm Clementine Bilyeu, your Missouri State insider. I'm a Springfield native and a float-trip guide, and I've been maroon since the day I was born. Mama swears my first word was "Bears." It was probably "boat," but I've chosen my story and I'm sticking with it.

I take a practical view of football, the same way I take a river. Read the current, respect the rocks, and keep everybody in the canoe. Missouri State is on a brand-new ride as an FBS program, and I'm thrilled to be your guide. I'll give you real numbers, honest takes, and kind words for every opponent. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll paddle off and find out. Springfield is the heart of the Ozarks, and our Bears are taking the whole region along. Pack a snack. It's going to be a fun float.

The School in 60 Seconds
Missouri State University is in Springfield, Missouri, and its first football team took the field in 1909. Until 2005, the school was known as Southwest Missouri State. The Bears were a founding member of the Gateway Football Conference in 1985, which later became the Missouri Valley Football Conference.

Home is Plaster Sports Complex, which CFBD lists with a capacity of 17,337 and a 1941 construction year. The last five seasons: 8-4, 5-6, 4-7, 8-4 and 7-6.

The Coach and the Scheme
Casey Woods is in his first season as head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 19, 2025. He was previously offensive coordinator at SMU and played wide receiver at Tennessee.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 24.4 points per game and allowing 34.9.

Players to Know
QB Henry Belin IV: 73 of 108, 887 yards, 6 touchdowns, 4 interceptions.
RB Ramone Green Jr.: 246 yards on 57 carries, 2 touchdowns.
WR Isaiah Myers: 38 catches, 796 yards, 7 touchdowns.
DE Josh Lukusa: 1.5 sacks, the team lead.

The Conference Picture

This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Last time out. Missouri State lost 61-38 at Delaware on Oct. 20, but Myers had a night to remember: 11 catches for 242 yards and two touchdowns. Belin went 26 of 35 for 337 yards and two scores, and Connor Lair ran 15 times for 85 yards and two touchdowns.
Sam Houston lost 30-24 to New Mexico State on Oct. 21 in Huntsville. Locke went 18 of 31 for 235 yards and a touchdown, Burns caught four passes for 117 yards and a score, and MJ Dowdy ran one in.
Players to watch. Missouri State wide receiver Isaiah Myers is the headliner: 38 catches for 796 yards and seven touchdowns. Henry Belin IV has thrown the most passes for the Bears in each of the last two games and is 73 of 108 for 887 yards, six touchdowns and four interceptions. Ramone Green Jr. leads the rushers with 246 yards and two scores. Linebacker Jared Lloyd leads the team with 80 tackles, and defensive end Josh Lukusa has 1.5 sacks.
Sam Houston quarterback Landyn Locke is 147 of 236 for 1,653 yards, 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Wide receiver Tim Burns Jr. has 15 catches for 329 yards and three scores, more than 20 yards a catch. Alton McCaskill leads the rushers with 220 yards. Linebacker Dean Ford leads the Bearkats with 44 tackles, and linebacker Elijah Groves has 2.5 sacks.
Availability. Conference USA has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either team, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Box scores don't mark starters, but Belin threw the most passes for Missouri State in each of its last two games, and Locke has done it in every Sam Houston game this season.
The coaches. Casey Woods is in his first season at Missouri State after serving as SMU's offensive coordinator. His Bears beat Kennesaw State 24-21 on Oct. 14 for their first FBS win under him, and the offense has scored 38 or more twice this season.
Phil Longo is in his second season at Sam Houston. He was named the program's 16th head coach in December 2024, and he's an air raid coach who previously ran offenses at Wisconsin, North Carolina and Ole Miss. Locke has thrown for at least 300 yards three times this year.
Storylines. The matchup to circle is Myers against a Sam Houston defense that allows 25.3 points a game. On the other side, Locke and Burns face a Missouri State defense that allows 34.9 points a game. Both teams struggle to run it: Sam Houston gains 2.9 yards a carry and Missouri State 3.9, so the big guys up front on both sides have plenty to prove.
Fun and true. Missouri State first fielded a football team in 1909 and was known as Southwest Missouri State until 2005. Sam Houston's close calls this year include a 24-21 loss at Troy in the opener and a 23-17 loss to Tulsa, and its lone win was a 59-0 shutout of Nicholls. Both teams also share a common opponent: Western Kentucky beat Missouri State 34-13 and Sam Houston 16-3.
From the preview booth. I shared the mic this week with Lemuel "Lem" Coxwell, Sam Houston's insider. Here's what I said:
"Howdy from the Ozarks! Lem, you're on my river tonight. Life jackets are by the door."
"Eighty tackles. Jared Lloyd shows up to every float on time and carries everybody's cooler."
"Two hundred forty-two yards. I had to check the river gauge twice."
"When the river's low, you paddle harder. Isaiah's our paddle."
"Pack a snack, Lem. It's going to be a fun float."
And the last word from Lem: "Ma'am, I brought a whole history book. Let's write a new page."

Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)
Tuesday brings a fresh matchup to Springfield: these two have no regular-season meetings from 2016 through 2025. Missouri State became a full FBS member in 2026, and this is its first FBS season.

report.title: Chile Heat in Las Cruces: New Mexico State Hosts Jax State on Wednesday Night

report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

Meet Your Insider
¡Buenas noches, Aggies! I'm Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, your New Mexico State insider. I'm a Las Cruces native, a chile farmer's daughter and an ag-science grad. That means I can tell you the soil pH of the practice field and how much Scoville heat a fourth-down stop packs. (A lot. A fourth-down stop is Christmas-style, red and green.)

Everything gets a chile grade from me. A routine first down? Mild. A 40-yard run? Hatch hot. But I don't heat up the facts. Every number I give you is real and sourced. Every opponent gets respect. If I don't know something, I'll say so, and then I'll go find out. In the Mesilla Valley, fall smells like roasting chile and fresh-cut grass. Our Aggies play with that same heat, and the Organ Mountains watch every snap.

The School in 60 Seconds
New Mexico State plays FBS football in Conference USA. The road here was winding. The Aggies were independent in 2013, a football-only Sun Belt member from 2014 to 2017, and independent again from 2018. They announced in November 2021 that they would join Conference USA in all sports starting in 2023. Home is Aggie Memorial Stadium in Las Cruces, which CFBD lists as built in 1978 with a capacity of 28,853.

The recent highs are real, though. The Aggies went 10-5 in 2023. The last five seasons: 2-10, 7-6, 10-5, 3-9 and 4-8.

The Coach and the Scheme
Tony Sanchez is the head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 23, 2023. He's an NMSU alum and a former Aggie wide receiver. He was head coach at UNLV from 2014 to 2019, and before that at Bishop Gorman High School in Las Vegas.

Through 7 games this season, we're scoring 24.6 points per game and allowing 25.4.

Players to Know

RB James Jones: 777 yards on 119 carries, 4 touchdowns.
WR TK King: 23 catches, 307 yards, 3 touchdowns.
DE Gabe Peterson: 5.5 sacks, the team lead.

The Conference Picture
