display.story_text:
Kent State flies across the country for a 7:30 p.m. Pacific kickoff, and Ozzie Brannigan has already decided the jet lag will be a problem. Mateo Villaseñor is in Sacramento with a fresh recipe and a defense that finally showed some flavor at Ball State.

Kent State (3-5) at Sacramento State (1-7), Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2 at Hornet Stadium in Sacramento. It's a MAC game and the first meeting between these schools. DraftKings has Kent State Golden Flashes −10 with a total of 46.5. My card: Sacramento State Hornets +10, Over 46.5, and a final of Kent State Golden Flashes 27, Sacramento State Hornets 22.

Ozzie speaks for Kent State. "Dru DeShields threw four touchdown passes and ran for another against Akron. We won 35-20. I expected to lose. Now I expect the plane to be late. Wayne Harris caught nine balls for 156 yards and three scores, and I'm suspicious of that too."

Mateo speaks for Sacramento State. "Plate it up, Ozzie. We led Ball State twice in the first half. Boogsie Silvera picked off two passes, and our special teams are a five-course meal. Matt Coleman has 39 catches for 492 yards."

Here is the part that matters. Before Akron, Kent State scored 0, 3, 10, 7 and 2 points in its five losses. The Flashes run for 3.0 yards a carry. A team that scores 14.9 points a game has no business laying 10 on the road.

Why Sacramento State? Because 10 points is a lot of cushion for a home team with a punter who flips the field and a kicker who just hit from 47. Kent State's defensive coordinator, Cherokee Valeria, coached Sacramento State's defensive backs for six seasons, so this is no mystery to either side. My final has Kent State by five, well inside the 10.

The worry is the Hornets' offense. Sacramento State has not run for a touchdown in six games and is minus-9 in turnover margin. It lost 48-7 to Ohio and 49-3 at Fresno State. If DeShields carries the Akron game into this one, the Flashes pull away.

Why the Over/Under? These offenses are poor, but these defenses are worse. Kent State allows 30.5 points a game and Sacramento State allows 32.9. Kent State's last game finished 35-20 and Sacramento State's finished 34-17. The total has ticked up a point, and Follow The Money likes that move. My 27-22 adds up to 49, two and a half over the over/under 46.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up has Kent State 25-24, takes Sacramento State and likes it, and goes Over. The Formula has Kent State 28-19, also on the Hornets, and the Over. Follow The Money stays off the side and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

Next Man Up: "Twenty-five to twenty-four. One point. Bring the fireworks."

The Formula: "Nine points. Still inside the 10."

Follow The Money: "The total moved up. Somebody stayed up late for this one."

Bottom of the card: two struggling teams on a Friday night, and the home team gets 10 points. Ozzie expects the worst. Mateo just wants the plate to look good.

Kent State Golden Flashes 27, Sacramento State Hornets 22. Sacramento State Hornets cover the 10. Over 46.5.

Fireworks Friday in Sacramento: Kent State Makes Its First Trip to Hornet Stadium

Kent State (3-5, 2-2 MAC) at Sacramento State (1-7, 0-5 MAC). Friday, Oct. 30, 10:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. Pacific), Hornet Stadium, Sacramento, Calif., ESPN2.

Your hosts are Ozzie Brannigan, a Kent State pessimist who grades uniforms and fourth-down decisions, and Mateo Villaseñor, a Sacramento State fan and farm-to-fork chef who explains defense like a recipe.

Mateo: Welcome to Sacramento, Ozzie! Farm-to-fork capital, Friday night lights and postgame fireworks.

Ozzie: I expected fireworks. I always expect fireworks. I just don't expect them to be for us.

Players to watch

Kent State quarterback Dru DeShields is 124 of 218 for 1,439 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions, and he has run for a team-high four scores. Wide receiver Wayne Harris has 40 catches for 552 yards and four touchdowns, and running back Brandon White leads the rushers with 235 yards. Linebacker Hayden Dawahare leads the defense with 43 tackles and four sacks.

Sacramento State quarterback Jackson Sharman is 123 of 218 for 1,257 yards, eight touchdowns and six interceptions. Wide receiver Matt Coleman has 39 catches for 492 yards and five scores, fourth in the MAC in receiving yards. Running back Isaiah Ene has 303 yards. Safety Boogsie Silvera leads the team with 61 tackles.

Mateo: Look at that, Ozzie. Our quarterbacks have the same attempts, the same touchdowns and the same interceptions. That's a matched pair of plates.

What happened last week

Kent State beat Akron 35-20 at home to keep the Wagon Wheel. After a 7-7 halftime tie, DeShields threw four touchdown passes and ran for another, and Harris caught nine passes for 156 yards and three scores.

Sacramento State lost 34-17 at Ball State, but the Hornets led twice in the first half. Sharman threw two touchdown passes, Jace Wilson caught a 55-yard score, and Silvera picked off two passes and made 11 tackles.

Ozzie: Four touchdown passes. I'm happy. I'm also nervous that I'm happy.

Injuries and availability

The MAC has not posted an availability report for this game, and no injury news has surfaced for either starting quarterback, so watch the teams' pregame notes. Sacramento State has used seven different starting groups on offense this year, and Silvera is the only Hornets defender to start all eight games.

What the coaches are up to

Mark Carney is in his second season as Kent State's head coach and is 8-12. Kent State removed his interim tag on Oct. 30, 2025, so Friday is one year to the day. His assistant head coach and defensive coordinator, Cherokee Valeria, coached Sacramento State's defensive backs from 2019 to 2024 and was part of three Big Sky championships.

Alonzo Carter is a first-time head coach. Sacramento State hired him on Dec. 15, 2025, and he's leading the Hornets through their first FBS season.

Mateo: Coach Valeria coming home? We'll save him a seat at the table. A small one.

Player storylines

Silvera is a fifth-year player whose path ran through Charleston Southern, McNeese and USF. He has three games this season with double-digit tackles.

The Hornets have football families, too. Coleman's father, Herman, played quarterback at Southern, and Onterrio Smith Jr., who has 33 catches for 350 yards, is the son of former Tennessee and Oregon running back Onterrio Smith, who played for the Minnesota Vikings.

The Sacramento State special teams group calls itself the Wefense. Kicker Grant Meadors hit a career-long 47-yarder at Ball State, and punter Hamish Adams of Melbourne, Australia, punted six times for 45.3 yards a kick.

What's happening on campus

Friday is Healthcare Appreciation and AANHPI Heritage Night at Hornet Stadium, and the postgame fireworks are back. Ted Emrich and former Texas running back Fozzy Whitaker will call the game on ESPN2.

Ozzie: Healthcare Appreciation Night is perfect. I'll need a nurse by the fourth quarter.

Anything else fun and true

This is the first meeting between the schools. Sacramento State went 7-5 in 2025, its last FCS season, and has played four Friday night games since 2000. Adams is the program's third straight punter from Australia, and all three came through ProKick Australia.

Mateo: Three Aussie punters in a row. That's a family recipe.

Ozzie: Fine. Great punting. I expected that too.

My call: Kent State Golden Flashes 27, Sacramento State Hornets 22.

display.fanatic_story:
Arizona vs Texas Tech: Haunted Hollow Parade Meets Bear Down

Arizona Wildcats vs Texas Tech Red Raiders kicks off Week 9's Halloween noon ET window at Galaxy Stadium, one hour after Lubbock's first-ever community Halloween parade, Haunted Hollow on Broadway, rolls through downtown. Tech fan Bodie Ratliff, a bareback rider who talks in single words, has to choose between the floats and his seat, while Arizona fan Inez Paloverde says Noah Fifita and No. 22 Arizona came to No. 13 Texas Tech to spoil the costume party.

Inez: Happy Halloween, Bodie! Your town finally got a parade, and you're going to miss it for football. I respect that.

Bodie: Priorities.

The parade is a genuine first for Lubbock. It steps off at 11 a.m. ET near Avenue A and East Broadway with floats, music and candy, and it ends at Mae Simmons Park. Kickoff is noon ET, so anybody who wants both had better wear running shoes under the costume.

Inez: I'll take a parade float home in my carry-on. Tucson's own big night is the All Souls Procession on Nov. 8, when the whole Westside walks from Barrio Hollywood to the Mercado District and burns the urn at the finale. I wrote a note for your Red Raiders to go in it. It says "Bear Down."

Bodie: Rude.

Both teams come in at 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big 12, and they took opposite roads last Saturday. Arizona crushed Iowa State 39-3 at home. Fifita went 27 of 34 for 308 yards and two touchdowns, Isaiah Mizell caught eight balls for 134 yards and a score, and Quincy Craig ran for a touchdown. The Wildcat defense allowed one field goal.

Texas Tech suffered its first loss, 37-24 at Cincinnati. Will Hammond went 24 of 37 for 227 yards, J'Koby Williams ran 12 times for 81 yards, and Kenny Johnson caught seven balls for 81 yards.

Bodie: Lesson.

Inez: That's almost a whole sentence. I'm so proud of you.

Fifita's season has been steady: 167 of 225 for 2,064 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. Mizell has 27 catches for 493 yards and five scores, and Kedrick Reescano leads the rushers with 303 yards and five touchdowns. Chase Kennedy has four sacks, and Taye Brown leads the team with 42 tackles.

Tech wins on the ground and on defense. Williams has 619 yards and five touchdowns on 86 carries, and Johnson has 31 catches for 499 yards. Hammond is 139 of 205 for 1,561 yards with six touchdowns and six interceptions. A.J. Holmes Jr. leads the defense with 6.5 sacks, and Austin Romaine leads it with 53 tackles. The Red Raiders allow 20.4 points a game, and they held Colorado to 7.

Inez: Our defense is a cactus, Bodie. Pretty from a distance, and you don't want to touch it. We allow 16.7 points a game.

Bodie: Spines.

The Big 12's initial availability report, posted at 10 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists four Arizona players out, one doubtful and seven questionable, and one Texas Tech player out, six questionable and four probable. Neither Fifita nor Hammond is on it. Fifita has thrown the most passes for Arizona in all seven games, and Hammond has done the same for Tech.

The coaching stories are big ones. Joey McGuire, hired on Nov. 8, 2021, is coming off the best season in Texas Tech history: 12-2, a 34-7 win over BYU for the Big 12 championship, the first outright conference title since 1955 and the first College Football Playoff trip. Brent Brennan arrived at Arizona on Jan. 16, 2024, went 4-8, then 9-4 with a Holiday Bowl trip in 2025. His 2026 Wildcats score 36.1 points a game.

Inez: Coach Brennan planted a seedling and grew a whole desert garden.

Bodie: Watered.

Arizona's rallying cry has a history worth telling on a day for remembering. In October 1926, student-body president and quarterback John "Button" Salmon was dying after a car accident and asked coach J.F. "Pop" McKale to tell the team to "bear down." It has been the school's motto ever since. Lubbock's Día de los Muertos gathering at Resthaven runs the same Saturday, with mariachis, pan dulce and a community ofrenda.

These two have split their last two meetings. Arizona won 28-14 in 2019, and Texas Tech won 28-22 in 2024.

Inez: Bear Down, Lubbock. Enjoy the parade, and save me some candy.

Bodie: Guns up.

Inez: Two words! It's a Halloween miracle.

My call: Texas Tech Red Raiders 29, Arizona Wildcats 25.

Cal vs NC State: Amato's Red Shoes and a Homecoming Reset

California Golden Bears vs NC State Wolfpack is a Week 9 Halloween noon ET Homecoming at Carter-Finley Stadium, and the Wolfpack will wear a red shoe sticker with Chuck Amato's initials on the back of their helmets, one week after the school relieved Dave Doeren of his duties. Ruff Pegram, an NC State grill man from Wake County, says interim coach Todd Goebbel and CJ Bailey owe the old coach a win, and Cal fan Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch, a Berkeley philosophy Ph.D. student with a sign for every occasion, says Tosh Lupoi's Bears came east to crash the reunion.

Ruff: Grill's at 450, Quentin. Homecoming, Halloween and a new man on the headset. Big day for the Pack.

Quentin: Respectfully, comrade, my sign today says "ALL COACHES ARE INTERIM."

It has been a heavy two weeks in Raleigh. Amato died on Oct. 19 at 80 at his Raleigh home. He played at N.C. State in the 1960s, then went 49-37 as its head coach from 2000 to 2006, with a school-record 11 wins in 2002, and he recruited Philip Rivers. Five days later, after a 31-28 loss at Stanford, athletic director Boo Corrigan announced Doeren's dismissal, and Goebbel, the running backs coach and special teams coordinator, took over for the rest of the season. Goebbel, a former quarterback at Kent State and Northern Iowa, has never been a head coach.

On Monday, Goebbel announced the helmet tribute. "This Saturday, we will honor the memory of former head coach Chuck Amato by wearing a red shoe sticker with the initials on the back of our helmet. As we all know, the fashion statement was real," he said. He also set his standard: "A foundation and a culture have been set, and the one thing we will stick to is hard, tough and together."

Ruff: Duke's Manny Diaz said it best. "I don't know anybody who loved N.C. State more than Chuck Amato did." I'm grilling in red today, top to bottom.

Quentin: I'll lower my sign for that one, Ruff. Respect for the man.

Then the sign goes back up. Cal lost 59-20 at SMU on Oct. 24, the week after a 41-7 home loss to Wake Forest. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele went 27 of 37 for 265 yards and a touchdown at SMU, and Chase Hendricks caught seven balls for 83 yards and a score. Sagapolutele is 149 of 219 for 1,555 yards, 10 touchdowns and five interceptions, after Jackson Brousseau threw the most passes in three straight October games. Hendricks leads the Bears with 54 catches for 498 yards, and Adam Mohammed has 336 rushing yards.

Quentin: I have filed a formal grievance with the scoreboard. It has not responded.

At Stanford, Bailey went 17 of 30 for 256 yards and two touchdowns and also led the team in rushing with 59 yards. Deandre Desinor caught three balls for 79 yards and a touchdown. Bailey is 143 of 219 for 1,763 yards with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, Keenan Jackson has six touchdown catches, the most on either roster, and Jayden Scott has 358 rushing yards. On defense, Popo Aguirre leads the team with 60 tackles and Elijah Satchell has four sacks.

Ruff: Sixty tackles. Popo flips the burgers, scrubs the grill and still helps you load the cooler.

The ACC's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists Jayden Scott among 12 NC State players out. Cal lists four players out and 10 questionable, Adam Mohammed among them. Neither Bailey nor Sagapolutele is on it, and Bailey has thrown the most passes for NC State in all seven games.

The numbers point at NC State's offense. The Wolfpack score 32.3 points a game, including a 73-0 win over Richmond and a 31-28 win over Louisville, and Cal allows 31.6. The Bears gain just 3.1 yards a carry.

Lupoi, named Cal's 35th head coach on Dec. 4, 2025, after Justin Wilcox, has ACC wins over Syracuse and Virginia Tech, both by one score.

Quentin: Coach Lupoi is building something, comrade. Respectfully, but firmly.

Ruff: Build it in Berkeley.

Cal still has the most famous ending in the sport. In the 1982 Big Game, the Bears ran the final kickoff back through five laterals, and Kevin Moen scored as the Stanford band wandered onto the field. Cal won 25-20. The last time these two met, in 2024, NC State won 24-23.

Quentin: Five laterals, Ruff. That's democracy in action.

Ruff: Then here's a fair election. Downtown, Boxcar is running a costume party from noon to 1 a.m. ET, with a puppy contest at 4 p.m. ET. Win or lose, I'm bringing you, and you're wearing red.

Quentin: Only if my sign gets a costume too.

My call: NC State Wolfpack 36, California Golden Bears 24.

display.fanatic_story:
SMU vs Syracuse: Otto Hits the Helmets for a Halloween Noon ET

SMU Mustangs vs Syracuse Orange is a Week 9 Halloween noon ET game at the JMA Wireless Dome, and for the first time ever, Syracuse will wear helmets featuring Otto, its Hall of Fame mascot, while kids in costumes parade the same Quad Walk route the team takes into the building. Nico Calabrese, a Salt City lifer, says Umari Hatcher and Fran Brown's Orange will treat the No. 19 Mustangs to a trick, and Tatum Delacroix-Price, a Highland Park boutique owner who grades game-day outfits, says Kevin Jennings and Rhett Lashlee's SMU are the only treat that matters.

Nico: Tatum! Otto on the helmets! Fifty years of me in an orange wig, and the team finally dressed up too.

Tatum: Nico, darling, a citrus fruit on a football helmet. I need a minute. I give it a B-plus for courage.

Syracuse Athletics announced the plan this week. The team walks into the Dome at 9:40 a.m. ET, and right behind it, young fans in costumes get the same walk and the same cheers. There's trick-or-treating on the Quad, and from 10:30 to 11:30 a.m. ET, participating suites inside the Dome hand out candy in a promotion called "Suite-4-Treats." Families can get four hot dogs, four sodas and two popcorns for $30.

Tatum: Suites handing out candy? Sugar, in Dallas the suites hand out valet tickets.

Nico: And nobody in Dallas has ever walked anywhere.

Then the costumes come off and the Mustangs show up with the best offense on the field. SMU is 6-1 and second in the ACC, and it beat California 59-20 on Oct. 24. Jennings went 16 of 23 for 223 yards and three touchdowns that day, and Kendrick Raphael ran 22 times for 104 yards and two scores. Jennings has thrown the most passes in all seven SMU games and is 156 of 215 for 2,062 yards, 19 touchdowns and five interceptions. He threw for 430 yards in the opener at Florida State and went 33 of 39 for 439 against Missouri State. Raphael has 641 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Yamir Knight leads the receivers with 38 catches for 443 yards.

Tatum: Two thousand yards in seven games. That's not a quarterback, Nico. That's a whole season of television.

Syracuse brings the drama. The Orange won 31-30 in overtime at North Carolina on Oct. 24. Steve Angeli went 20 of 34 for 256 yards and two touchdowns, Ahmad Miller carried 30 times for 125 yards and a score, and Hatcher caught four passes for 103 yards and a touchdown. Hatcher has 54 catches for 887 yards and eight touchdowns this season, and Angeli leads the team with 987 passing yards.

Nico: Overtime at UConn, 42-41. Overtime at Carolina, 31-30. This team doesn't do anything until it's dark out. Perfect for Halloween.

There's a costume question at quarterback too. Angeli, Amari Odom and Malachi Nelson have each thrown the most passes for Syracuse in at least one game, and Angeli did it last week. The ACC's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists Odom and Nelson out and Angeli questionable. SMU lists 10 players out and one questionable, and Kevin Jennings is not on it.

On defense, SMU's Marques White has 5.5 sacks and Alexander Kilgore leads the Mustangs with 39 tackles. They held Boston College to 16 points and Virginia to 13. For Syracuse, Chris D'Appolonia has a team-high 51 tackles and Tunmise Adeleye has four sacks.

The ground game may be a grind. SMU gains 4.4 yards a carry and Syracuse allows 4.2, while the Orange gain 3.8 and SMU allows 3.8. Syracuse scores 31.6 points a game, so this Dome won't be quiet.

Lashlee, hired at SMU on Nov. 29, 2021, took the Mustangs to the 2024 ACC championship game, where they lost 34-31 to Clemson on a field goal at the end. This year SMU has won all five home games in University Park. Brown, hired on Nov. 28, 2023, went 10-3 in his first year and 3-9 last season. SMU won last year's meeting 31-18.

Tatum: We've got a Heisman, Nico. Doak Walker, 1948. And the Pony Express with Eric Dickerson and Craig James.

Nico: We've got Otto. On a helmet. Beat that.

The Dome opened in 1980, seats 49,057 and goes by "The Loud House." Nobody has to worry about lake-effect snow on the costumes.

Nico: After the game, you're coming to my mom's for Sunday dinner. We say grace, then we share the salt potatoes.

Tatum: I'll bring the sweet tea and grade your mother's apron. Pony up or sit down.

My call: SMU Mustangs 32, Syracuse Orange 26.

Boston College vs Duke: BooFest Saturday and a Halloween Trial

Boston College Eagles vs Duke Blue Devils is a Week 9 Halloween noon ET kickoff at Wallace Wade Stadium, on the same Saturday Durham's Museum of Life and Science runs BooFest, with a costume catwalk and pumpkins popped in Gateway Park. Siobhan Dunleavy, a BC grad student and former debate champion, says Mason McKenzie and Bill O'Brien's Eagles are coming off a 399-yard rushing day, and Harrison Wexley-Moore IV, a Duke pre-everything overachiever, says Manny Diaz's defense and Nate Sheppard will rule the afternoon.

Siobhan: All rise! The Honorable Siobhan Dunleavy presiding. Also prosecuting. Also on the jury.

Harrison: Objection, your honor. That's a conflict of interest. I wrote a paper on it. Footnotes available upon request.

Durham has a full Halloween calendar. BooFest runs from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. ET, which means half the families in the stands will have candy in their pockets before kickoff. That afternoon, the Great British Bike Off fills Durham Central Park with vintage British motorcycles, horror movies and a bonfire. Then everybody gets an extra hour of sleep, because the clocks go back at 2 a.m. ET Sunday.

Harrison: An extra hour. I'll use it to grade the game film.

Siobhan: You'll need it, counselor. Exhibit A is Georgia Tech.

Exhibit A is hard to argue. Boston College won 49-27 in Atlanta on Oct. 24 and ran for 399 yards, its most since it ran for 496 at Syracuse in 2019. McKenzie carried 16 times for a career-high 170 yards and two touchdowns and threw for 101 yards and another score. Bo MacCormack III added a career-high 155 yards and three touchdowns. Charlie Comella intercepted two passes, taking the second one 47 yards for a touchdown, and the Eagles have 10 interceptions, the most in the ACC. Their 49 points were the most O'Brien's BC has scored against a Power Four opponent.

Siobhan: Exhibit B. McKenzie has 614 rushing yards, the most of any ACC quarterback.

McKenzie has thrown the most passes in all seven BC games. He's 107 of 185 for 1,363 yards, eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, with five rushing scores. Javarius Green leads the receivers with 26 catches for 286 yards. On defense, Anthony Palano has 61 tackles and Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks.

Duke won 19-16 at Virginia on Oct. 23. Walker Eget went 14 of 25 for 211 yards, Sheppard ran for a touchdown, and Jonah Burton caught four passes for 59 yards.

Harrison: A three-point win on the road. I accept that grade with gratitude.

Eget has thrown the most passes in all seven Duke games and is 122 of 197 for 1,440 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Sheppard has 875 yards and nine touchdowns on 153 carries. Burton leads the receivers with 21 catches for 298 yards. On defense, Nick Morris Jr. has 44 tackles and Kevin O'Connor has four sacks.

Harrison: Eight hundred seventy-five yards. Sheppard's carries deserve their own peer-reviewed journal.

The defense is Duke's closing argument. Diaz's Blue Devils allow 16 points a game and 3.3 yards a carry. They held Tulane to three and Stanford to seven. Diaz was hired on Dec. 7, 2023, after coaching Miami and running Penn State's defense. O'Brien, named BC's 37th head coach on Feb. 9, 2024, also coached at Penn State, then won four AFC South titles with the Houston Texans.

Siobhan: Two Penn State men on one field. I move that they share a pregame handshake.

Harrison: Seconded. Motion carries.

The ACC's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists six Boston College players out and one questionable, and 11 Duke players out, four questionable and one probable. Mason McKenzie and Nate Sheppard are not on it.

The ground game probably settles it. Duke runs for 5.3 yards a carry and BC allows 4.0, while BC runs for 4.7 and Duke allows 3.3. If McKenzie breaks loose again, the Eagles can play their game. If Duke keeps him bottled up, BC has to throw.

Wallace Wade opened in 1929 and seats 40,004. Duke has won 18 conference titles, eight in the ACC and ten in the Southern Conference. The last two meetings were split: BC won 26-6 in 2020, and Duke won 38-31 in 2022.

Siobhan: I'm coming as a Supreme Court justice. Again.

Harrison: I'm coming as a Blue Devil. It's the easiest costume in Durham.

Siobhan: After the verdict, I'm taking the bonfire at Central Park.

Harrison: Lunch first, counselor. Grace, then barbecue, then motorcycles.

My call: Duke Blue Devils 29, Boston College Eagles 18.

It's the hundredth meeting, a Halloween Homecoming at Kinnick Stadium with the Heartland Trophy at stake, and Iowa has won the last four in the series.

The Iowa side begins with what Wisconsin can't do through the air. Colton Joseph went 6 of 16 for 66 yards in the 17-7 loss at UCLA and 12 of 14 for 58 yards against USC. He is a runner first, and Iowa's run defense allows 2.4 yards a carry. On the road this year the Badgers lost 41-13 to Notre Dame and 17-7 at UCLA, with a 24-20 win at Penn State in between. Iowa gains 5.7 yards a carry at home. My final has Iowa by five.

Brat Ellefson, the old Badgers fullback, has his accordion going in the Kinnick lot. "Oom-pah! We just beat USC 24-7. Sebastian Cheeks has five sacks, Cooper Catalano has 60 tackles, and we allow 15.3 points a game. Have some curds."

Orrin Kalvelage answers from inside the same sweater, black for the Black Out. "Neighbor, we allow 14.3. Kamari Moulton has 541 rushing yards, and Cam Buffington has 62 tackles. We won 41-24 at Washington, and that trophy has lived here since 2022."

The danger is the Iowa passing game. Hank Brown threw two interceptions in the 13-10 loss at Minnesota, and the Hawkeyes managed just 10 points. Wisconsin's run defense allows 2.8 yards a carry. The Big Ten's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists Kamari Moulton out. If Iowa can't run, a field goal decides it, and three and a half is a lot in a field-goal game.

display.fanatic_story:
Wisconsin vs Iowa: Halloween Homecoming and the 100th Meeting

Wisconsin Badgers vs Iowa Hawkeyes is a Week 9 Halloween Homecoming Black Out at Kinnick Stadium, the 100th meeting between the two schools, with the Heartland Trophy at stake and Iowa hosting the Badgers for Homecoming for the first time since 1988. Lars "Brat" Ellefson, a former Badgers fullback who talks to a polka beat, says Colton Joseph and Luke Fickell's No. 25 Badgers will take the trophy back to Madison, and Orrin Kalvelage, a farm-country Hawkeye in the same sweater every week, says Kirk Ferentz's Hawkeyes aren't giving it up.

Brat: (Oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, Orrin! Hundredth meeting, and we lead it 49-48-2. I brought curds for the whole tailgate.

Orrin: Thank you kindly, Lars. We've won four straight and outscored you 118-26. I brought my sweater. It's black today, same as everybody's.

Iowa's game notes lay out the history. The series is 49-48-2 Wisconsin. The Heartland Trophy began in 2004, was designed and crafted by former Iowa player Frank Strub, and has stayed in Iowa City since 2022. The last time Iowa hosted Wisconsin for Homecoming, in 1988, the Hawkeyes won 31-6. Iowa has also sold out 32 straight games at Kinnick.

Halloween adds a few house rules. Iowa says costumes are welcome, but no prop weapons, and no costumes that could be mistaken for police or game officials.

Brat: No referee costumes? There goes my whole plan. I was gonna throw a flag on Orrin's sweater.

Orrin: That's why they made the rule, Lars.

Wisconsin arrives after a 24-7 win over USC at Camp Randall on Oct. 24. Joseph went 12 of 14 with a touchdown throw, and Abu Sama III ran 17 times for 71 yards. Joseph has thrown the most passes in all seven Badger games and leads the team in rushing. He's 99 of 173 for 1,256 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions, with 365 rushing yards and four rushing scores. Tyrell Henry leads the receivers with 28 catches for 343 yards. On defense, Cooper Catalano has 60 tackles and Sebastian Cheeks has five sacks.

Brat: (Oom-pah!) USC came to Madison and left with seven. I jumped so hard my cheese wedge fell off. Twice.

Iowa lost 13-10 at Minnesota on Oct. 24. Hank Brown threw a touchdown to Reece Vander Zee, who caught four balls for 69 yards. Iowa's notes say Brown and Jeremy Hecklinski split reps in that game, and Hecklinski led the 41-24 win at Washington. Brown has 968 passing yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions. Kamari Moulton leads the team with 541 rushing yards and four scores, and Tony Diaz has 29 catches for 386 yards. On defense, Cam Buffington has 62 tackles and Joseph Anderson has four sacks.

Orrin: Sixty-two tackles. Cam Buffington would help you fix a fence and then stay for supper.

The Big Ten's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists Kamari Moulton out, along with six other Hawkeyes, and three more Iowa players doubtful. Wisconsin lists one player out, two doubtful, two questionable and two probable.

These are two of the stingiest defenses in the Big Ten. Iowa allows 14.3 points a game and Wisconsin allows 15.3. Iowa gains 5.7 yards a carry against a Badger defense that allows 2.8, and Wisconsin's ground game runs into an Iowa defense that allows 2.4. Somebody's running backs are going to have a long afternoon.

Ferentz, in his 28th season, is the longest-tenured active head coach in college football and the winningest coach in Big Ten history. Fickell, hired on Nov. 27, 2022, has already won 24-20 at Penn State this year and beaten Michigan State 31-3.

Brat: Two coaches who love defense. This one might come down to a punt. (Oom-pah.)

Orrin: Lars, a good punt is a love letter to your defense. Our punter's from Hope Island, Australia. He writes long letters.

Wisconsin has played in the Big Ten since 1896, and Camp Randall, opened in 1917, is the fourth-oldest stadium in college football. Iowa won last year's meeting 37-0 and has won 12 of its last 16 Homecoming games.

Brat: Ninety-nine games and we still lead. That's a Wisconsin winter of patience, Orrin.

Orrin: Come by after the game, Lars. We'll say grace, have a brat, and you can visit the trophy. It likes it here.

My call: Iowa Hawkeyes 22, Wisconsin Badgers 17.

Illinois vs Maryland: Oktoberfest Hats and a Halloween Debut

Illinois Fighting Illini vs Maryland Terrapins is a Week 9 Oktoberfest-and-Halloween noon ET game at SECU Stadium, where the first 7,500 fans get Bavarian Alpine hats and interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim leads the Terps for the first time. Margery Vandermolen, a prairie-state numbers whiz with charts for everything, says Bret Bielema's Illini and Collin Dixon arrive fresh off beating Oregon, and Abby Chesapeake, a D.C.-suburb networker who puts Old Bay on everything, says Malik Washington and a hometown coach are about to change the mood in College Park.

Margery: Good afternoon, class! Orange you glad it's Saturday? I made a chart of every Alpine hat in the building. It's going to be a long chart.

Abby: Margery, sweetie, I'm wearing the hat, the costume and a bushel of crabs. Old Bay on that!

Maryland's promotional calendar has called this one "Oktoberfest in Terpsville" since August. "Prost!" the announcement said, before reminding everyone about Halloween: fans are encouraged to dress up, but full face masks are not permitted.

Abby: No masks. Fine by me. I want every Terp fan to see my face when we win.

The bigger change came on Oct. 21, when Maryland and Mike Locksley mutually agreed to part ways. Abdul-Rahim, a D.C. native who founded the football program at Friendship Collegiate Academy, took over. Before his first press conference on Oct. 27, he walked row to row in Tyser Tower and shook every hand. "I'm a D.C. native and proud of it, so it means a little bit more to me to be standing here as the interim head coach at the University of Maryland," he said. He also had a new way to count: "This is a five-game season for us, and as far as I'm concerned, we're 0-0 right now, and the kids are excited to show you guys a better brand of football."

Abby: Zero and oh, Margery. Write that on your chart.

Margery: I'll need a new color for it.

Illinois arrives at 4-3 after a 21-10 win over Oregon on Oct. 24. Aidan Laughery ran 13 times for 123 yards and a touchdown, and Dixon caught six balls for 65 yards and a score. Michael Clayton II threw the most passes in that game, 11 of 18 with two touchdown throws, after Katin Houser did it in the first six. Houser is 122 of 184 for 1,440 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. Dixon has 54 catches for 678 yards and 10 touchdowns, Laughery leads the rushers with 514 yards, and Matthew Bailey has 49 tackles.

Margery: Oskee-wow-wow! I hugged three strangers and a mascot.

Maryland had last week off. Its last game was a 37-30 loss to Rutgers on Oct. 17, when Washington threw for 263 yards and two touchdowns and Chris Durr Jr. caught six balls for 104 yards. Washington has thrown the most passes in all seven Maryland games and is 155 of 261 for 1,615 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. He went 30 of 44 for 359 yards and three touchdowns against Virginia Tech. Durr has 52 catches for 580 yards, and DeJuan Williams leads the rushers with 281 yards. On defense, Daniel Wingate has 44 tackles and Zion Elee has 3.5 sacks.

The Big Ten's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists Houser doubtful, one of two Illini doubtful, and eight more Illinois players out. Maryland lists five players out and six questionable, and Malik Washington is not on it.

Points shouldn't be scarce. Maryland scores 28.3 a game, including a 62-0 win over Hampton and a 38-14 win at UConn, but allows 33.3. Illinois scores 30.3 and allows 25.3, and it runs for 5.2 yards a carry. Maryland gains 4.5.

Bielema, an Illinois native, was named the school's 26th head coach on Dec. 19, 2020. One of his first big wins was the nine-overtime game at Penn State in 2021, and this year his team won 38-37 in overtime at Michigan State.

Margery: Nine overtimes. My chart needed an extension cord.

Illinois is a founding member of the Big Ten. On Oct. 18, 1924, Red Grange scored four touchdowns against Michigan in the first 12 minutes of the Memorial Stadium dedication game. Illinois won last year's meeting 24-6, and Maryland won a wild one in 2018, 63-33.

Abby: Sixty-three, Margery. Remember 2018. A Terp never forgets a score or a name.

SECU Stadium opened in 1950 and seats 51,802. Testudo has a halftime photo spot in the Family Section, and the Mighty Sound of Maryland will play under a sea of Alpine hats.

Abby: I'm going as a crab in lederhosen. Seasoned.

Margery: After the game, I'm making you a chart of everything I learned today.

Abby: And I'm sprinkling Old Bay on it. Then we'll say grace and eat.

My call: Illinois Fighting Illini 33, Maryland Terrapins 27.

display.story_text:
Notre Dame vs Navy prediction, pick against the spread and over/under: I'm on Navy Midshipmen +30.5 and Over 56.5 at DraftKings, with a final of Notre Dame Fighting Irish 43, Navy Midshipmen 15. The series reaches New England for the first time at noon ET Saturday, with Navy as the home team at Gillette Stadium and the Brigade marching onto the field before kickoff.

Thirty points is a lot to lay against an option team. Nobody has blown out Navy this season. Its losses came by eight at Florida Atlantic, four at UAB, five at Air Force, four at UTSA and ten to North Texas. Navy runs for 5.7 yards a carry, and long drives mean fewer possessions for CJ Carr. My final has Notre Dame by 28.

Declan Moriarty-Chen rides the early train down from South Station in his sweater vest. "Proposition one, Commander: Carr has 16 touchdown throws and one interception. Proposition two: we score 41.1 points a game and allow 13.4. Proposition three: we beat Stanford 58-7."

Notre Dame vs Navy: The Brigade Marches Into Foxborough

Notre Dame Fighting Irish vs Navy Midshipmen is a Week 9 Halloween noon ET game at Gillette Stadium, where the Brigade of Midshipmen marches onto the field at about 11:40 a.m. ET and the 99-game series is played in New England for the first time. Declan Moriarty-Chen, a sweater-vested Notre Dame grad student, says CJ Carr and No. 5 Notre Dame will make Foxborough feel like South Bend, and Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather, a former surface warfare officer, says Jackson Gutierrez and the option will take the clock and the crowd.

Declan: I would posit, Commander, that this is the most respectful rivalry in the sport.

Commander: You would posit correctly. Now mind the lighthouse. It's in our end zone today.

That's a real detail. Gillette Stadium has a lighthouse in its north end zone, and for one Saturday it belongs to the Navy home team. The stadium's event page says Navy is the designated home team and that this is Notre Dame's first game at Gillette. Navy has been here before, for the 2023 Army-Navy Game.

Commander: We know the harbor, young man. You're the tourist.

Declan: A tourist with 11 national championships, Commander.

The day begins early. Parking opens at 8 a.m. ET, and so does the official Fan Fest outside the stadium. The gates open at 10 a.m. ET. The MBTA is running a special event train from South Station at 9:50 a.m. ET, with stops at Back Bay and Dedham Corporate Center, that reaches Foxboro Station at 10:50 a.m. ET. Then, at about 11:40 a.m. ET, the Brigade marches on in formation.

Declan: I'll be on the 9:50 with a thermos and a rosary.

Commander: I'll be at the 50 for the march. Nobody talks during the march. Not even you.

Notre Dame is 6-1 and had the week off. Its last game was a 28-24 loss at BYU on Oct. 17, when Carr threw for 261 yards and Jaden Greathouse caught eight balls for 125 yards. Carr has led the Irish in throws in all seven games and is 129 of 193 for 1,639 yards, 16 touchdowns and one interception. Jordan Faison leads the receivers with 34 catches, and Jonaz Walton leads the rushers with 426 yards. On defense, Drayk Bowen has 38 tackles and Boubacar Traore has 3.5 sacks.

Declan: One interception in seven games. I've lost more library books.

Navy is 2-5 and lost 49-39 to North Texas on Oct. 24. Gutierrez ran 26 times for 228 yards and three touchdowns. He has 869 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns, and he's thrown for 692 yards and seven scores on just 64 attempts. Jordan Collins has turned six catches into 212 yards and three touchdowns. On defense, Coleman Cauley has 58 tackles and MarcAnthony Parker has four sacks.

Commander: Six catches, 212 yards. Collins is a submarine. You never see him until he surfaces.

The matchup is simple to state. Navy gains 5.7 yards a carry. Notre Dame allows 2.4. The Irish score 41.1 points a game and allow 13.4, and they've forced 16 turnovers while losing two. Navy allows 29.1 points a game.

Marcus Freeman was hired at Notre Dame on Dec. 3, 2021, and his teams went 9-4, 10-3, 14-2 and 10-2 over the last four seasons. Brian Newberry was hired at Navy on Dec. 19, 2022. Last season his Midshipmen went 11-2, won the Liberty Bowl 35-13 and won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy for the second straight year.

Declan: Eleven wins and a trophy named for your boss. I concede the point.

The history runs deep. The series began in 1927, and the teams met 93 years in a row through 2019, the longest continuous intersectional rivalry in college football. Notre Dame has won eight of the last nine regular-season meetings, including 49-10 last year. Navy's lone win in that stretch was 28-27 in 2016.

Commander: Twenty-eight to twenty-seven. I still have the program framed in my den.

Declan: I've seen it. It's next to a framed photo of the Naval Academy chapel.

It's Halloween, too, so expect leprechauns in the parking lots and at least one admiral in a pumpkin costume by the Tom Brady statue at Patriot Place.

Commander: I'm going as a lighthouse. Practical and festive.

Declan: Commander, whatever happens, I'd be honored to say grace with you after the game.

Commander: The honor is mine, young man. Anchors aweigh.

My call: Notre Dame Fighting Irish 43, Navy Midshipmen 15.

UAB vs South Florida: Black Out Halloween at Raymond James

UAB Blazers vs South Florida Bulls is a Week 9 Black Out Halloween noon ET game at Raymond James Stadium, where the Bulls wear black-on-black and the first 10,000 fans get Black Out rally towels. Reina Valdés-Kowalski, a Tampa Bulls roster maven, says Brian Hartline's Bulls and Michael Van Buren Jr. are ready for November, and Ozella Birchfield, a Birmingham steel-family granddaughter and community-theater actor, says Alex Mortensen's Blazers and Ryder Burton just pulled off the comeback of the year.

Reina: Ahoy, Ozella! Black towels, black jerseys, black sails. Welcome to Tampa.

Ozella: Darling, in Birmingham we invented black. It's called soot. Forged, not given!

USF's promotional calendar has listed Oct. 31 as Black Out/Halloween since August. The Bulls say it's the first game of a five-game stretch run, and Hartline isn't hiding the stakes. "We own our own destiny in our opinion," he said this week.

Reina: Destiny, Ozella. Also towels. Mostly towels.

UAB arrives with a story. On Oct. 15 against East Carolina, the Blazers trailed 17-9 with 1:02 left. They drove 93 yards for a touchdown, made the two-point conversion and then won in overtime on an 80-yard interception return for a touchdown. Final: 30-17.

Ozella: I gave a standing ovation so long the ushers asked me to sit. Then I stood again. Curtain call.

UAB is 4-3 and has been off since that night. Burton has led the Blazers in throws in all seven games. He's 91 of 167 for 1,184 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions, and he threw for 262 yards and two scores against the Pirates. Rod Robinson II leads the rushers with 436 yards, and CJ Smith leads the receivers with 19 catches for 350 yards. Muaaz Byard has a team-high 69 tackles, and Marlin Dean has five sacks.

South Florida is 5-2 and beat Kent State 29-2 on Homecoming, Oct. 17. Van Buren went 22 of 27 for 193 yards and a touchdown. He's 115 of 179 for 1,266 yards and six touchdowns and hasn't thrown an interception all season. D.J. Crowther has 518 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, and Bryson Rodgers leads the receivers with 30 catches for 334 yards. Ayden Jackson has 38 tackles, and Michael Williams II has four sacks.

Reina: No interceptions in seven games. Van Buren guards that ball like buried treasure.

Hartline spent the week off cutting things down. "Minimizing the call sheet will help with that," he said. "We want to make it simpler, not easier, but simpler will hopefully allow higher execution."

Ozella: Simpler, not easier. That's Shakespeare's note to every actor who ever overdid a death scene.

Both coaches are in their first year. Hartline was hired at South Florida on Dec. 3, 2025, and his Bulls allow 15.1 points a game. They held Florida International to nine and Bowling Green to six, and they won at Army 28-24. Mortensen was hired at UAB two days later, on Dec. 5, and his Blazers have beaten UL Monroe, Navy and East Carolina at home. UAB scores 23.3 points a game. South Florida scores 26.6.

Reina: Two rookies. One of them gets a towel thrown at him by 10,000 people.

The series is young and loud. UAB won 56-35 in 2023, and South Florida won 35-25 in 2024 and 48-18 last season.

Ozella: Fifty-six, Reina. Write that on your towel.

Raymond James Stadium opened in 1998 and seats 65,857. UAB fans will bring Blaze the dragon and the Marching Blazers from Protective Stadium, which opened in Birmingham in 2021.

Reina: I'm dressing up as a pirate. Which is what I wear every week.

Ozella: I'm coming as Lady Macbeth in a black towel. Out, damned spot!

Van Buren summed up the Bulls' week. "I feel like it's all adding up to us having a great November," he said.

Ozella: November begins Sunday, darling. Saturday is still October, and October is Birmingham's.

Reina: After the game, I'm taking you to dinner on the water. We'll say grace, and you can tell me theater stories.

Ozella: Deal, matey.

My call: South Florida Bulls 30, UAB Blazers 16.

Corwin: Welcome to Kalamazoo, Darcy! It's Family Weekend. I saved you a booth and a plush to stuff.

Western Michigan's Family Weekend runs Oct. 30 through Nov. 1, and Friday night includes Stuff-a-Plush, hat decorating with the Alumni Association and Halloween Escape Rooms and Glow Night on Sangren Mall. On Saturday, the free Family Fun Zone runs from 9 to 11:30 a.m. ET in Lot 3 at Oliver Road and Oliver Lane, and kids are encouraged to wear costumes to the game. There's a historical walking tour at The Oaklands at 9:30 a.m. ET, and Sunday ends with family brunch at Valley Dining Center.

Corwin: Brunch on Sunday. Pancakes. I'm emotionally prepared.

Darcy: You're always emotionally prepared for pancakes.

Bowling Green's own release calls it "a Halloween matchup inside Waldo Stadium," and it comes with history. This is the 59th meeting. The Falcons lead the series 35-20-3, they're 17-10-1 in Kalamazoo, and they've won the last three, including 34-10 on their last trip here in 2023.

Darcy: Seventeen wins in your building, Corwin. We know where the syrup is.

Michigan vs Rutgers: Halloween On the Banks in Piscataway

Michigan Wolverines vs Rutgers Scarlet Knights is a Week 9 "Halloween On the Banks" game at SHI Stadium, with trick-or-treating on the Rutgers Boardwalk from 8:30 a.m. ET and a haunted halftime show by the Marching Scarlet Knights. Gus Hartwell, a Michigan engineering-school stats savant in a maize sweater, says Kyle Whittingham's defense will keep KJ Duff quiet, and Vinny Scolari, an Exit 9 Jersey guy who gives directions by Turnpike exit, says Greg Schiano's Knights and Antwan Raymond are due on Halloween.

Vinny: Gus! Welcome to Exit 9! Grab a trick-or-treat bag. The food trucks are giving out free candy.

Gus: Vincent, I brought a laminated map, three backup routes and a workbook titled "Champions of the West."

Vinny: Fuhgeddaboudit. Follow the mechanical pumpkin.

That pumpkin is real. Rutgers says the Boardwalk will have a mechanical pumpkin, face painting, Halloween games, inflatables and a costume contest. BTN Tailgate goes live at Athletes Glen at 10 a.m. ET, and the band's halftime show is billed as haunted.

Rutgers likes this date. Its game notes say this is the sixth Halloween home game since 1964, and the Knights won four of the previous five. The famous one came in 1992, a Halloween Homecoming against Virginia Tech. Rutgers trailed 42-23 in the third quarter and 49-44 with 1:32 left, then went 78 yards, and Bryan Fortay found Chris Brantley in the end zone as time expired. Final: 50-49. It was Brantley's fourth receiving touchdown that day, a school record.

Vinny: Fifty to forty-nine, Gus. I was eight. I still have the ticket stub in my glove box at Exit 9.

Gus: I've added it to my workbook under "Things Vincent Mentions Weekly."

There's another number in those notes. Rutgers has played 29 Big Ten games since it last faced Michigan, and Schiano is 0-4 against the Wolverines.

Gus: Victors valiant, Vincent.

Vinny: Not on Halloween, pal.

Michigan is 4-3 and lost 13-6 in overtime to Indiana on Oct. 24. Tommy Carr went 20 of 32 for 167 yards, and JJ Buchanan caught six balls. Bryce Underwood led the Wolverines in throws in their first six games and is 72 of 124 for 924 yards, five touchdowns and six interceptions. Jordan Marshall leads the rushers with 319 yards, and Buchanan has 33 catches for 539 yards and four scores. Troy Bowles has 55 tackles, and John Henry Daley has four sacks.

Rutgers is 2-5 and lost 42-14 at Northwestern on Oct. 24, though Raymond ran 18 times for 150 yards and a touchdown. Dylan Lonergan is 74 of 127 for 1,066 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions, and AJ Surace has split the job with him. Raymond has 648 yards and six touchdowns. Duff has 45 catches for 774 yards and nine touchdowns. Chris Joines leads the tacklers with 34.

Vinny: Nine touchdowns for Duff. That's more than the exits between here and the shore. Almost.

The Big Ten's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan out and KJ Duff doubtful, and AJ Surace is not on it. Michigan lists six players out and six questionable, John Henry Daley among them, and Bryce Underwood is not on it.

The matchup is Raymond against a Michigan defense that allows 2.8 yards a carry and 15.7 points a game. On the other side, Michigan scores 20.3 points a game and gains 3.7 yards a carry against a Rutgers defense that allows 5.8. Rutgers ranks second nationally in fewest penalty yards a game, according to its notes.

Whittingham was named Michigan's 22nd head coach on Dec. 26, 2025, after 21 seasons at Utah. Schiano returned to Rutgers on Nov. 30, 2019, for his second stint.

Gus: Coach Whittingham would admire your discipline, Vincent.

Vinny: I'd yell "discipline" from the top of the Driscoll Bridge.

History is on everybody's side here. Rutgers beat Princeton 6-4 in New Brunswick on Nov. 6, 1869, in the first college football game, and the Knights have played 1,441 games, more than anyone. Michigan has more wins than any program, plus three Heisman winners: Tom Harmon, Desmond Howard and Charles Woodson.

Gus: I'm dressing as a workbook. Very scary for opponents.

Vinny: I'm dressing as the Turnpike. Very scary for everybody.

Gus: Win or lose, I'll split your six-foot sub. We'll say grace first.

Vinny: Six feet, Gus. Everybody eats.

My call: Michigan Wolverines 30, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 22.

Auburn vs Ole Miss: Powder Blue for Oxford's Halloween Return

Auburn Tigers vs Ole Miss Rebels is a Week 9 Halloween game at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, the first one played there since 1998, and Ole Miss has asked its crowd to wear powder blue. Langston Fairbanks, an Ole Miss fan in seersucker who reads Faulkner and Rebel film in the same sitting, says Trinidad Chambliss and Pete Golding's No. 12 Rebels will keep Oxford undefeated, and Lacey Bellamy, a former Auburn sorority president who reenacts every Iron Bowl, says Byrum Brown and Alex Golesh have one more upset in them.

Langston: Welcome to the Grove, Miss Bellamy. I've prepared a brief introduction. It runs three paragraphs.

Lacey: Bless your heart, Langston. I brought lemonade. You get one paragraph per glass.

Langston: Then I'll use my glass on 1998. Ole Miss notes say the last Halloween game in this stadium was against LSU, and the Rebels won 37-31 in overtime.

Lacey: Sugar, you're dressed as powder blue. I'm dressed as Aubie.

The Rebels have played on Oct. 31 sixteen times before this one and are 8-7-1, by the school's count. Two of those were against Auburn, both on the Plains. Auburn won 33-20 in 2009, and Ole Miss won 27-19 in 2015.

Lacey: We'll call that a tie, and Auburn leads the whole series 35-13 on the field.

Langston: Ole Miss won the last meeting, 28-21 in Auburn in 2023. The past is never dead, Miss Bellamy.

Lacey: Neither is Auburn, honey.

Auburn is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC, coming off a 38-17 home loss to LSU on Oct. 24. The week before, the Tigers won 27-24 at Georgia, their first win in Athens since 2005, according to Ole Miss's preview. Brown does a little bit of everything. He's 134 of 209 for 1,365 yards, eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, and he leads the team with 471 rushing yards and six scores. Keshaun Singleton has 36 catches for 431 yards. Elijah Melendez has 57 tackles and four sacks.

Lacey: In my reenactment of Athens, I play Brown and the kicker. Obviously.

Ole Miss is 5-2 and 3-2 in the league after a 34-27 loss at Texas. Chambliss is 167 of 262 for 1,926 yards, 16 touchdowns and seven interceptions, though he went 25 of 52 with three interceptions in Austin. Kewan Lacy has 388 yards and five touchdowns, and Deuce Alexander has 43 catches for 610 yards. Blake Purchase has 4.5 sacks, and Keaton Thomas has 45 tackles.

Langston: Our offense scores 36 points a game, Miss Bellamy. I've written a sonnet about it.

Lacey: Sugar, read it at halftime. I'll be getting more lemonade.

No official availability report is out for this game yet, so check the teams' pregame notes.

The real fight is at home in Oxford. Ole Miss has won 15 home games in a row, dating to a 26-14 win over Oklahoma on Oct. 26, 2024, and is 25-1 at Vaught-Hemingway since September 2023. Auburn allows 24.1 points a game and 3.7 yards a carry, and that defense will need every bit of it.

Golesh came to Auburn from South Florida, where he went 23-15 and won a bowl game in each of his three seasons. Golding is in his first full season running the Rebels. The Rebels held Missouri to 39 rushing yards in a 31-3 win.

Langston: Missouri left Oxford with three points and a chicken tender. We doubled the tender stands this year, you know.

Lacey: That's the kindest thing Ole Miss has ever done for a visitor.

Saturday is the 49th meeting between these two, by Ole Miss's count, and the 17th Halloween game in Rebel history.

Langston: Whatever happens, Miss Bellamy, dinner is on me. We'll say grace first.

Lacey: That's sweet, Langston. War Eagle, bless your heart.

My call: Ole Miss Rebels 33, Auburn Tigers 22.

display.fanatic_story:
Marshall vs Old Dominion: Monarch Masquerade, No Masks Allowed

Marshall Thundering Herd vs Old Dominion Monarchs is Week 9's Homecoming and "Monarch Masquerade" at S.B. Ballard Stadium, where ODU wants costumes and face paint but has banned masks. Winnie Pocklington, an Old Dominion fan who treats every first down like a knighthood, says Javen Gibson and the Monarch defense will crown a Homecoming winner, and Mercy Holderby, a Huntington nurse and the daughter of two Marshall grads, says Tony Gibson's Herd is going home 5-3.

Winnie: Hear ye, hear ye! The court welcomes the lady from Huntington to the Masquerade!

Mercy: Thank you, Winnie. Where's your mask?

Winnie: Confiscated, nurse. ODU says masks and toy weapons stay in the car. My scepter is in the trunk.

That part is true. Old Dominion's game preview invites fans to wear costumes and says face paint is welcome, but masks and replica weapons aren't allowed anywhere on campus, tailgates included. So it's a masquerade with painted faces.

Mercy: I'll be in green scrubs. Not a costume. I'm on call after this.

It's also Homecoming week in Norfolk, which ODU says runs Oct. 25 through Nov. 1. There's DaBaby and Friends at Chartway Arena, a Friday night boardwalk with fireworks at Whitehurst Beach, and a Spirit Walk before the game Saturday. At halftime, the 2026 Homecoming Royalty will be crowned.

Winnie: A coronation, Mercy. At halftime. I've been rehearsing my curtsy since August.

Marshall is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, and it's had extra rest after a 20-13 win over South Alabama on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Zion Turner went 21 of 33 for 181 yards, Khalil Wilkins ran eight times for 69 yards and Toby Payne caught seven balls. Carlos Del Rio-Wilson is 90 of 140 for 1,041 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions, and Turner has led the Herd in throws the last two games. Judah Price has 237 rushing yards. Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw has 25 catches for 335 yards and four scores, Caleb Clark-Glover has 51 tackles and Kelvon McBride has two sacks.

Mercy: Twenty to thirteen. I'll take a win with my whole heart, every single time.

Old Dominion is 2-6 and 1-4 after a 26-0 loss at Louisiana Tech. Jaxon Potter, a Washington State transfer, got his first big chance there and went 18 of 34 for 154 yards. Ja'Mez Drummer made a career-high 15 tackles, and Lucas Struck leads the team with 61. Quinn Henicle is 54 of 98 for 656 yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions, Devin Roche has 382 rushing yards and TJ Johnson has 17 catches for 265 yards. Javen Gibson has five sacks, and he made four tackles for loss in the 10-3 win at App State.

Winnie: Five sacks for Sir Javen. I've knighted him five times. He's running out of shoulders.

Mercy: Two Gibsons in one game, Winnie. Ours is the coach.

No official availability report is out for this game, so check both teams' notes for quarterbacks.

There are Norfolk fingerprints on the Marshall sideline, too. ODU's notes say Herd cornerbacks coach Chip West was on Old Dominion's first coaching staff, from 2007 to 2009, and Marshall strength coach Dwight Galt IV held the same job at ODU from 2019 to 2023.

Winnie: Traitors to the crown! Lovely men, I'm sure.

Then there's the history. ODU lists the series at 10-1 Marshall. The Monarchs' one win came 38-14 in 2016. Marshall won 42-35 in 2024 and 48-24 last season.

Mercy: Ten and one. I'm not bragging, Winnie. I'm charting.

Winnie: Chart this: Old Dominion's defense allows 26.8 points a game, and Marshall's allows 30.7. The court sees an opening.

Mercy: Our defense needs to show up for four quarters. I'll bring it coffee.

Winnie: Whatever happens, Mercy, dinner's on the court. We'll say grace first.

Mercy: The court is very kind. We Are, and God bless the Monarchs.

My call: Old Dominion Monarchs 25, Marshall Thundering Herd 20.

Kansas State vs Colorado: Buffs Halloween Bash at Folsom Field

Kansas State Wildcats vs Colorado Buffaloes is Week 9's Buffs Halloween Bash at Folsom Field, with kids trick-or-treating through Ralphie's Road before a 2 p.m. ET kickoff. Moss Feldstein, a Colorado physicist who runs the numbers from a hammock under the Flatirons, says Deion Sanders' Buffs and Joseph Williams are owed one, and Hattie Brandvold, a Kansas State agronomist who names every drive after a crop, says Collin Klein's Wildcats will win in Boulder again.

Moss: Welcome to Boulder, Hattie. Bring candy? CU is asking every tailgater on Benson Field and Franklin Field to hand some out.

Hattie: Bless you, Moss. I brought sweet tea, a field notebook with Flint Hills dirt on it and a bag of candy corn. It's a crop.

Moss: It is not a crop.

Hattie: It is in Manhattan.

CU's plan is a real one. Trick-or-treating runs from 11 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. ET around the stadium, and kids get clear candy bags so they can carry the haul inside. At noon ET, a costume parade leaves Chip's Kids Club on Duane Field, loops through Ralphie's Road and Franklin Field and heads back. Costumes are welcome for all ages, but masks and simulated weapons aren't allowed.

Moss: Before that, the student huddle is on the Duane Physics Lawn from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. ET. Physics Lawn, Hattie. They named it after me, basically.

Hattie: They did not.

Boulder also gets a Friday warmup, the Pearl Street Stampede at 9 p.m. ET, with the Golden Buffalo Marching Band and Chip.

Hattie: I'll be there in purple. Somebody has to show Pearl Street a real harvest.

K-State has won the last two meetings, 31-28 in Boulder in 2024 and 24-14 last season. Its athletics site says a third would be the Wildcats' longest run against CU since they won four in a row from 1997 to 2000.

Moss: High variance, Hattie. Physicists love that. Fans, less so.

Kansas State is 4-3 and 1-3 in the Big 12 after a 28-17 loss at Arizona State. Jacob Knuth went 26 of 41 for 194 yards there, and Derrick Salley Jr. caught six balls. Johnson led the throws in the first six games and is 118 of 187 for 1,301 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions, plus a team-high 462 rushing yards. Jaron Tibbs has 34 catches for 325 yards and four scores. Wendell Gregory has 3.5 sacks, and Logan Bartley has 45 tackles.

Hattie: Johnson running for 462 yards is winter wheat, Moss. Long, patient and golden.

Colorado is 2-5 and 0-4 in the league after a 57-24 loss at Oklahoma State, where Isaac Wilson threw for 280 yards and two touchdowns and Williams caught nine balls for 135. Wilson has led the Buffs in throws for four games and is 77 of 128 for 979 yards, six touchdowns and seven interceptions. Williams has 46 catches for 643 yards and five scores. JaQuail Smith has 298 rushing yards, Lamont Lester Jr. has five sacks and Gideon Lampron leads the team with 65 tackles.

Moss: Williams is my constant. Every equation needs one.

The Big 12's initial availability report, posted at 10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson out and Jacob Knuth doubtful. Colorado lists five players out and quarterback Julian Lewis doubtful, and Isaac Wilson is not on it.

The matchup is the K-State ground game against a Colorado defense that allows 3.7 yards a carry. K-State scores 32.9 points a game, and Colorado allows 30.1. Colorado, though, came within three of Utah, 27-24, two weeks ago.

Klein, a former K-State quarterback, was named head coach on Dec. 4, 2025. Sanders has run Colorado since Dec. 3, 2022.

Hattie: Coach Klein grew up in our program. Homegrown crop.

Moss: Coach Prime grew up everywhere. Free-range.

Moss: I'm dressing as a hammock. Very relaxing for everyone.

Hattie: I'm dressing as a wheat sheaf. Very on brand.

Hattie: Moss, whatever happens, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Moss: Grateful for that, Hattie, and for a mountain sunset afterward. Ralphie's running.

My call: Kansas State Wildcats 28, Colorado Buffaloes 23.

Coastal Carolina vs Georgia State: Boo & Brew Blackout in Atlanta

Coastal Carolina Chanticleers vs Georgia State Panthers is Week 9's Boo & Brew Halloween game at Center Parc Credit Union Stadium, where Georgia State wants a blackout crowd dressed in black and lets young Panthers in costume in for free. Goldie Seabrook, a Conway native from a shrimp-boat family who measures everything in tides, says Deuce Bailey and Ryan Beard's Chanticleers own this series, and Malik Overstreet, who knows every MARTA stop and every Panther third-down tendency, says Cameran Brown, Rodshaun Dorsey and Dell McGee's Panthers finally win it at home.

Malik: Goldie, wear black. Georgia State asked the whole stadium for a blackout.

Goldie: I brought teal, Malik. Teal is what the ocean wears at night.

Malik: The ocean is not on the guest list.

Georgia State has built a full afternoon around it. Panther Pregame comes with live music and a pumpkin-carving station, and once fans get inside, kids can trick-or-treat throughout the stadium. There are Halloween giveaways to take home, too.

Downtown will be crowded before the Panthers even kick off. Georgia and Florida bring their rivalry to Mercedes-Benz Stadium this year for the 2026 Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic, with a 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff, and Centennial Yards runs a Rise ATL party for both fan bases from 1 to 4 p.m. ET.

Malik: Two big games downtown on Halloween, Goldie. Take MARTA. Nobody is parking today.

Goldie: I've docked a shrimp boat in a crowded harbor, Malik. I'll find a spot.

The series is the part Goldie wants to talk about. These two have met every season since 2017, and Coastal has won five of the nine, including a 51-0 game in 2020 and a 40-27 win last season. Georgia State's game notes say Saturday is the 10th meeting and the fifth on the Panthers' home field, and the Panthers are still looking for their first home win against Coastal.

Goldie: Five of nine, Malik. The tide comes in on schedule.

Malik: The tide hasn't seen this Parc yet.

He has a point. Georgia State is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, and 3-0 at home after beating North Carolina A&T 59-10, Northern Illinois 35-14 and Old Dominion 42-10 on Homecoming. The Panthers have outscored those three visitors 136-34 and held every one of them to 14 or fewer, per the team's notes. Brown threw six touchdowns against Old Dominion, a program record, and Xavier Esqillion tied the school's single-game record with three sacks that day.

Malik: Six touchdowns, Goldie. That's a whole train car of them.

Brown is 110 of 166 for 1,356 yards, 14 touchdowns and five interceptions. Dorsey has 24 catches for 418 yards and eight scores, Lanear McCrary Jr. has run for 399 yards and four touchdowns, Esqillion has seven sacks and Jaydon Hood has 45 tackles. The Panthers have lost two straight on the road, though, 49-22 at James Madison and 38-32 at Arkansas State, where Ayden Pereira threw the most for Georgia State and had two touchdowns, and Qwantavius Wiggins ran eight times for 99 yards and a score.

Goldie: Low tide for you two weeks running, Malik. It happens to everybody.

Coastal is 2-5 and 1-2 in the league, and it had last week off. Its last game was a 35-32 loss to App State on Oct. 16, when Bailey threw for 298 yards and three touchdowns and Robby Washington caught five balls for 118 yards. Bailey is 109 of 204 for 1,638 yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. Dominic Lee-Knicely has run for 452 yards, and Colton Hinton has 13 catches for 297 yards and four scores. Marcellius Pulliam leads the defense with 67 tackles, and Ibrahim Diawara has five sacks.

The Chanticleers also don't get blown out. Five of their seven games were decided by eight points or fewer, including a 31-24 loss at West Virginia and a 27-21 win at Marshall.

Goldie: We keep it close, then we take it home. Ask anybody in Conway.

The Sun Belt's initial availability report, updated at 8:53 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists Georgia State quarterback Cameran Brown doubtful, with seven Panthers out. Coastal Carolina lists five players out and two questionable.

The matchup is the Georgia State ground game, which gains 5.4 yards a carry per the team's notes, against a Coastal defense that allows 4.8. The Chanticleers will need Pulliam and Diawara to slow McCrary and Wiggins.

Beard is in his first season at Coastal. CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2025. McGee was hired on Feb. 23, 2024, and with four wins already, he has matched what his Panthers won across 2024 and 2025 combined.

Malik: I'm dressing as a MARTA train. I'll arrive on time.

Goldie: I'm dressing as a shrimp boat. I'll arrive when the tide says so.

Malik: Goldie, win or lose, I'll ride you back to your car.

Goldie: Deal, Malik. The boiled shrimp are on me, and I brought enough for the blackout section.

My call: Georgia State Panthers 33, Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 25.

display.fanatic_story:
UConn vs Air Force: Space Force Day Black Out at Falcon Stadium

UConn Huskies vs Air Force Falcons is Week 9's Space Force Day Black Out at Falcon Stadium, a Halloween afternoon at the Academy with fireworks waiting for every Falcon score. Jo Ferrante, a Hartford-area former point guard who counts possessions, says Kalieb Osborne, Cyncir Bowers and Jason Candle's Huskies run it back from last November, and Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, a retired Air Force instructor pilot who gives everyone a call sign, says Evan Medders, Blake Fletcher and Troy Calhoun's Falcons get even.

Colonel: Welcome to the Academy, Ferrante. Your call sign is Fast Break. Wear black.

Jo: Colonel, it's Halloween. I was going to come as a point guard.

Colonel: You are a point guard.

Jo: Exactly. No costume needed.

Air Force has dressed the day up anyway. The home schedule lists it as Space Force Day and a Black Out, and the athletic department's game-day guide promises enhanced fireworks, pyrotechnics and stadium lighting when the Falcons take the field, when they score, before the fourth quarter and when they win. Falcon Alley opens three hours before kickoff, and somewhere on the grounds is the BobbleBird, a 6-foot-tall bobblehead of The Bird that moves to a new spot every home game.

Jo: A 6-foot bobblehead. That's taller than my whole backcourt.

Colonel: Find him, take a picture, and report back. That's an order, Fast Break.

The Halloween bit already has its punch. KRDO's Rob Namnoum, in a Halloween piece this week, wrote: "All we know is that this Saturday Air Force will dress up as football players."

Colonel: Football players. Ten-hut. Best costume on the field.

The Falcons are 5-2 and 3-2 in the Mountain West, and they run it the way they always have. Medders leads the team with 490 rushing yards and six touchdowns, Liam Szarka is 19 of 38 for 296 yards, and Simon Kibbee leads the receivers with eight catches for 135 yards. Fletcher has 72 tackles and Max Mustell has three sacks. Air Force runs for 343.0 yards a game, second in FBS, and holds the ball 36:22 a game.

The quarterback room has been busy. Szarka, Kemper Hodges, Medders and Howard Fisher IV have each led Air Force in throws in a game this season. Last week the Falcons lost 28-14 at Wyoming, with Medders running 21 times for 115 yards and Fisher throwing the most for Air Force.

Colonel: Rough landing in Laramie. We debriefed. Wheels up again Saturday.

Before that, the Falcons beat UNLV 41-31 at home, won 28-7 at Northern Illinois and beat Navy 14-9 in the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy chase.

UConn is 4-3 as an FBS independent and comes in off a 35-16 home win over UMass on Oct. 23. Osborne was 14 of 19 for 173 yards and two touchdowns, Bowers ran 15 times for 131 yards and a score, and JD Willoughby caught a touchdown.

Jo: Pack the Rent! That's how you close out a game, Colonel.

Osborne has led UConn in throws in every game. He's 112 of 182 for 1,594 yards, 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. Bowers has 564 yards and seven touchdowns, and Shamar Porter leads the receivers with 14 catches for 265 yards and three scores. Hayden Pegg has 47 tackles and K'Von Sherman has 3.5 sacks. The Huskies score 35.6 points a game.

Jo: Two interceptions all year. That's a point guard who never turns it over.

Colonel: Fast Break, two interceptions is what we call a clean preflight.

The Huskies have had a few close ones go the other way, 24-21 at Miami (Ohio) and 42-41 in overtime against Syracuse. They also beat Air Force 26-16 last November, the only meeting between these two in CollegeFootballData's records back to 2016.

Colonel: One meeting, Fast Break. That's a sample size of one.

Jo: One for one, Colonel. In basketball we call that a perfect night at the free-throw stripe.

The matchup is the Falcon option against a UConn defense that allows 3.3 yards a carry. Pegg and the Huskies up front have to stay home on every snap. On the other side, Bowers and Osborne meet an Air Force defense that allows 20.9 points a game. Possessions will be few, and Jo will be counting every one.

No official availability report is out for this game, so check the teams' pregame notes.

Candle is in his first season at UConn, hired on Dec. 6, 2025, after leading Toledo from 2016 to 2025. Calhoun has led Air Force since 2007, and CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 22, 2006.

Colonel: Twenty seasons in the cockpit. That's rare in this sport.

Jo: Respect, Colonel. Coach Candle is in year one and already has us scoring 35.6 a game.

Colonel: Fast Break, when the fireworks go off for us, you're allowed to clap.

Jo: Colonel, when Osborne finds Porter, you're allowed to say "nice dish."

Colonel: Deal. Dinner afterward, my treat, and you can bring the jersey.

My call: Air Force Falcons 29, UConn Huskies 27.

Bart: Ahoy, Teddy! New helmets, PeeDee marching right on the side. Hoist the colors.

Teddy: Nice lids, Bart. Does PeeDee march to Philly? We've got stairs for him.

Bart: PeeDee doesn't do stairs. PeeDee does parades.

He really does on Saturday. ECU's Halloween schedule has the Pirate Walk at 12:45 p.m. ET, with the team and the cheerleaders handing out candy along the route, and a costume parade following the team in. Kids can meet PeeDee at the Howard & Lyn Swain Promenade to join it. After the walk, ECU athletes hand out candy in front of TowneBank Tower, there's a kids costume contest at 2 in Charley's Kids Zone near Gate 4, and The Embers featuring Craig Woolard play the Tailgate Plaza before kickoff. Season-ticket holders can buy extra seats for $10.31, and student guest tickets are $10.31, too.

Teddy: Ten thirty-one for Ten thirty-one. Okay, Bart, that's clever. I'll give you that one.

Bart: First compliment from Philly all year. I'm framing it.

Then there's the football, and Bart has recent history on his side. ECU won the last three meetings, 49-46 in 2022, 56-34 in 2024 and 45-14 last season. In CollegeFootballData's meetings back to 2016, East Carolina leads 5-4, and Temple's biggest one was a 49-6 win in 2018.

Teddy: 2018, Bart. Write it on the tricorn.

Bart: There's no room. It's full of 2024.

East Carolina is 3-4 and 1-2 in the American. The Pirates have lost two straight in overtime, 30-17 at UAB and 41-34 at Memphis on Thursday, Oct. 22. Mitch Griffis threw for 199 yards at Memphis, Engleman ran 18 times for 92 yards and a touchdown, and Sides caught seven balls for 130 yards and a score. At home, ECU beat Rice 28-12 and North Carolina Central 42-9 and lost to App State 27-24.

Bart: Two overtimes on the road. We battled. The hull held, the sails didn't.

Emory Williams is 73 of 117 for 716 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions, and Griffis has led the Pirates in throws in four games. Engleman has 582 rushing yards and four touchdowns, Ray Ray Joseph Jr. has 31 catches, DJ Johnson Jr. has 51 tackles and Jasiyah Robinson has 2.5 sacks.

Temple is 2-5 and 1-2 in the league and had last week off. Its last game was a 38-31 loss to Charlotte on Oct. 17, when Sheppard threw for 236 yards and ran for two touchdowns and Peter Clarke caught five balls for 127 yards and a score.

Teddy: We rested. We trained. We drank raw eggs. Okay, not the eggs.

Sheppard has led Temple in throws in six of seven games and is 74 of 120 for 1,127 yards and eight touchdowns. Mason has 513 rushing yards and three scores, Colin Chase has 18 catches for 308 yards, and Curly Ordonez leads the defense with 63 tackles and two sacks. The Owls nearly won at Toledo, losing 49-48 in overtime, lost 21-17 to Army and beat South Florida 17-13 in Tampa.

Teddy: Curly Ordonez leads us in tackles and sacks, Bart. Running up the museum steps every snap.

Keeler leads Temple, and CollegeFootballData dates his hire to Dec. 1, 2024. His Owls run for 202.4 yards a game and give up only 37.3 penalty yards a game. Harrell is East Carolina's head coach, and CFBD records his hire date as Nov. 27, 2024. His defense allows 187.5 passing yards a game and has returned two interceptions for touchdowns.

The matchup is Mason and the Temple run game against an ECU defense that allows 3.3 yards a carry. On the other side, Engleman wants another big day and Sides is coming off his best night of the year.

Bart: I'm dressing as PeeDee, Teddy. Marching version.

Teddy: I'm dressing as Hooter the Owl. Nobody insult Hooter.

Bart: Teddy, nobody has insulted Hooter. Hooter is a fine owl.

Teddy: See, that's Pirate kind. After the game, the cheesesteaks are on me.

Bart: And the barbecue's on me. Eastern style, vinegar, no arguments.

My call: East Carolina Pirates 30, Temple Owls 23.
