Louisiana Tech vs South Alabama: Military Day, Halloween in Mobile

Louisiana Tech Bulldogs vs South Alabama Jaguars is Week 9's Military Appreciation Day, Honor Band and USA Day at Hancock Whitney Stadium, and on Halloween it's the first meeting between these two as Sun Belt rivals. Booker "Champ" Tullos, who grew up on a Ruston-area peach farm and thinks everything is peachy, says Blake Baker, Alonzo Jackson Jr. and Sonny Cumbie's Bulldogs stay perfect in league play, and Azalea Fairhope-Grice, a Mobile Mardi Gras float-builder with a whistle in her purse, says Keenan Phillips, Cole Blaylock and Major Applewhite's Jaguars go 4-0 at home.

Azalea: Well, hey, Champ! Welcome to Mobile. Pull up a lawn chair, honey.

Champ: Thank you kindly, Azalea. I brought peaches. A whole bushel.

Azalea: Darlin', this is a parade town. We throw beads, not fruit.

Saturday is crowded on the calendar, too. South Alabama has it down as Military Appreciation Day, Honor Band day and USA Day, all on Halloween, and it's the first time the Jaguars and Bulldogs meet as conference foes since Tech officially joined the league on July 1.

Champ: First conference game in Mobile. I wore my good overalls.

Azalea: Honey, those are your only overalls.

There's a home record at stake. South Alabama's game notes say the Jaguars are 3-0 at home for the first time since 2022 and the first time under Applewhite, and they're trying to open 4-0 at home for the first time since 2011. They beat Southeastern Louisiana 39-14, Ohio 41-36 and UL Monroe 52-35 at Hancock Whitney. Then they scored 56 at Arkansas State, which the notes call the program's most in a Sun Belt game. The blockers up front also made the Joe Moore Midseason Honor Roll on Oct. 14, the only Sun Belt group on the list.

Azalea: Fifty-six points, Champ. We had to build a second float to carry them all.

South Alabama is 4-3 and 2-1 in the league. Its last game was a 20-13 loss at Marshall on Tuesday, Oct. 20, so the Jaguars have had extra days to get ready. Jared Hollins threw for 148 yards, Phillips ran 16 times for 70 yards, and Brendan Jenkins caught four balls for 75 yards. Phillips has 514 rushing yards and five touchdowns, Hollins is 68 of 125 for 1,003 yards and seven touchdowns, Jenkins has 25 catches for 430 yards, Blaylock leads the team with 46 tackles, and William Felton IV has two sacks.

Azalea: We'll take the extra rest, darlin'. The float needed new sequins anyway.

Louisiana Tech is 5-2 and 3-0 in its first Sun Belt season, and the defense hasn't allowed a point in two games. The Bulldogs won 24-0 at UL Monroe and then shut out Old Dominion 26-0 at home on Oct. 24, when Baker went 28 of 34 for 303 yards and a touchdown and Eli Finley caught 10 balls for 128 yards and a score.

Champ: Two shutouts in a row, Azalea. Peach cobbler, served warm.

Baker is 96 of 133 for 1,160 yards, 10 touchdowns and one interception. Trey Kukuk led the Bulldogs in throws against Baylor and Army, but Baker has done it the last three games. Andrew Burnette has 349 rushing yards, Jalen Mickens has 40 catches for 586 yards and three scores, and Jackson has 48 tackles and 6.5 sacks. Tech has also won the tight ones, 31-29 over Army and 32-31 over Louisiana.

Champ: Alonzo Jackson Jr. is the juiciest peach in the orchard. Six and a half sacks!

Azalea: And Keenan Phillips is a float with a turbo engine.

The series is short. Tech won 34-16 in 2017 in Ruston and 30-26 in 2018, and South Alabama won the last one, 38-14 in Mobile in 2022. The Jaguars' notes say Caullin Lacy returned a punt 57 yards for a score that day and Yam Banks added a 24-yard interception return for another.

Champ: That was four years ago, Azalea. The peaches have grown since then.

Azalea: So has the float, honey.

Cumbie is in his fifth season at Louisiana Tech, and his defense has 13 takeaways and a plus-5 turnover margin. Applewhite has led South Alabama since 2024. He was head coach at Houston in 2017 and 2018, and as a player he quarterbacked Texas from 1998 to 2001. His Jaguars score 35.1 points a game.

The matchup is Phillips and the South Alabama ground game against a Tech defense that has gone two weeks without allowing a point. On the other side, Baker has been efficient, and Mickens and Finley give him places to throw.

No official availability report is out for this game, so check the teams' pregame notes.

Azalea: I'm dressing as a parade float. A walking one.

Champ: I'm dressing as a peach. I've been practicing my roll.

Azalea: Champ, honey, win or lose, you're riding on my float after the game.

Champ: Deal, Azalea. And the peaches are yours. Every last one.

My call: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs 33, South Alabama Jaguars 30.

Bianca Thornberry is pinning a red feather the size of a canoe paddle onto her hat outside L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium when Iggy Yamamoto-Ross walks up holding a laptop like a serving tray. "Bianca," Iggy says, "I'm here to pitch you on a Stanford upset." Bianca adjusts the brim. "Darling, I'm here to rate its hat-worthiness."

Stanford (4-4) at Louisville (4-3), Saturday at 3:15 p.m. ET on ACC Network at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium. It's an ACC game: Stanford is 2-3 in league play and Louisville is 3-2. DraftKings has Louisville Cardinals −22.5 with a total of 60.5. My card: Louisville Cardinals −22.5, Over 60.5, and a final of Louisville Cardinals 42, Stanford Cardinal 19.

Bianca speaks for Louisville, feather bouncing. "Hold your hats! Lincoln Kienholz has thrown for 1,844 yards. Lawayne McCoy has 513 receiving yards. Clev Lubin has five sacks. We beat Florida State 44-20 and Villanova 59-13. We score 38.7 a game, and we had a week off to rest. That's a three-hat afternoon."

Iggy speaks for Stanford, tapping his laptop. "Team, the product is iterating. Davis Warren threw four touchdowns against NC State. Micah Ford ran for 150 yards in that game and has eight rushing scores. We beat Louisville 38-35 the last time we met. Pivot accepted."

Why Louisville? Because this Stanford defense has been run over by good teams. The Cardinal lost 45-6 to Miami, 35-7 at Duke, 57-3 at Wake Forest and 58-7 at Notre Dame. Stanford allows 35.5 points a game. Louisville just had an open date, it runs the ball well, and In The Trenches likes the Louisville run game here. My final has Louisville winning by just more than the 22.5.

The risk is that Stanford is playing its best ball right now. It beat Elon 34-7 and then knocked off NC State 31-28. Warren hasn't thrown an interception in his last two games. And Louisville's offense has turned it over, with Kienholz throwing two interceptions at Syracuse.

Why the Over? Louisville games score. The Cardinals put up 41 on SMU and 44 on Florida State, and their loss to Ole Miss finished 41-38. Louisville scores 38.7 a game and allows 27.4, and Stanford allows 35.5. Warren has thrown for 303 and 396 yards in two of Stanford's wins. My 42-19 adds up to 61, over 60.5.

Now the room. Next Man Up has Louisville 43-18 and likes the Louisville side. The Formula has Louisville 41-20 and sides with Stanford, since its score lands just inside the 22.5. Both land on the Over. In The Trenches likes Louisville. Follow The Money likes Louisville too, but it likes the Under after the total ticked down.

Next Man Up started it: "Louisville rolls. Bianca, that's a three-hat day."

The Formula pushed back: "My score lands short of 22.5. I'll take Stanford."

Follow The Money answered: "Louisville, yes. Lots of points, no."

Bottom of the card: a rested Louisville team that scores in bunches, a Stanford defense that has given up big numbers to good teams, and a home crowd ready for a party. Iggy calls it a learning opportunity. Give me Louisville and the Over.

Cardinal Meets Cardinals: Stanford Visits Louisville on Halloween

Stanford (4-4, 2-3 ACC) at Louisville (4-3, 3-2 ACC). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:15 p.m. ET, L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium, Louisville, Ky., ACC Network.

Your hosts are Ignatius "Iggy" Yamamoto-Ross, the founder of three failed apps, and Bianca Thornberry, a Louisville derby-party hostess who rates every game's hat-worthiness.

Bianca: Welcome to Louisville, Iggy! Hold your hats.

Iggy: Thanks, Bianca. Quick question. Is it confusing that we're both Cardinals?

Bianca: Not at all, darling. We have an S on the end. And a much bigger hat budget.

Iggy: Noted. I'll put it in the deck.

Players to watch

Louisville quarterback Lincoln Kienholz has thrown the most passes in all seven games. He's 121 of 180 for 1,844 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Isaac Brown leads the rushers with 568 yards and four scores, and Lawayne McCoy leads the receivers with 513 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker T.J. Capers leads the defense with 53 tackles, Clev Lubin has five sacks, and defensive back Kaleb Beasley has five interceptions.

Stanford quarterback Davis Warren has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 163 of 271 for 1,933 yards, 11 touchdowns and two interceptions. Micah Ford leads the rushers with 679 yards and eight touchdowns, and Caden High leads the receivers with 30 catches for 440 yards. Safety Jay Green leads the team with 49 tackles.

Iggy: Micah Ford is pure product-market fit. Four touchdowns against Elon tied a Stanford single-game record.

Bianca: Kaleb Beasley has five interceptions, darling. That's a five-hat secondary.

What happened last week

Stanford beat NC State 31-28 at home on Friday, Oct. 23. Warren went 22 of 37 for 303 yards and four touchdowns, Ford ran 22 times for 150 yards, and High caught nine balls for 103 yards and a score. It was Stanford's second straight win, after a 34-7 victory over Elon.

Iggy: Two wins in a row. We're officially trending.

Louisville had an open date. Its last game was a 34-26 win at Syracuse on Oct. 17, when Kienholz threw for 310 yards and ran for two touchdowns, and McCoy caught five balls for 93 yards.

Bianca: Rest, film and a little extra time in the ice tub. I spent mine shopping for feathers.

Injuries and availability

display.fanatic_story:
Florida vs Georgia: The Rivalry Leaves Jacksonville for Atlanta

Florida Gators vs Georgia Bulldogs left Jacksonville for Week 9, and on Halloween the old neutral-site rivalry lands at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta while EverBank Stadium is rebuilt. Dax Marchetti, a Florida herpetology minor who classifies every opponent as a reptile species, says Jadan Baugh, Aaron Philo and Jon Sumrall's Gators win in the Bulldogs' home state, and Thaddeus "Thad" Okafor-Brandt, an indie-rock DJ turned defensive film savant, says Gunner Stockton, Raylen Wilson and Kirby Smart's Bulldogs keep their grip on the series.

Thad: Welcome to Atlanta, Dax! Track one, side A. Same classic record, new turntable.

Dax: Thanks, Thad. I've been studying your defense all week. I'm classifying it as a snapping turtle.

Thad: Is that a compliment?

Dax: Very much so. Snapping turtles are patient, and they don't let go.

Georgia's athletics site says this game has been played in Jacksonville since 1933 with only two exceptions. This year it's billed as the Invesco QQQ Atlanta Gridiron Classic, gates open at 2 p.m. ET and kickoff is at 3:30 p.m. ET. It goes to Tampa next fall and returns to Jacksonville in 2028, once the renovation is done. Scott Stricklin, Florida's athletic director when the deal was announced in 2024, said of Atlanta and Tampa, "Both cities are special to Gator fans and offer venues that will provide wonderful experiences for both fans and players."

Dax: Atlanta is in your home state, Thad. Our lizards are brave.

Thad: Brave lizards are still lizards, Dax.

The party still found a home. Sports Radio 680 The Fan is throwing a free Cocktail Party Tailgate at 123 Marietta Street from noon to 3 p.m. ET, with food, games and music, and Centennial Yards has a free Rise ATL game-day setup from 1 to 4 p.m. ET. The stadium points everybody to the SEC District MARTA stop.

Thad: A cocktail party with a train stop. That's a remix, and I like it.

Dax: I'm riding MARTA in a full alligator suit. Nobody sit near the tail.

Then there's the football. Georgia is 6-1 and 4-1 in the SEC. The Bulldogs had last week off after a 27-24 home loss to Auburn on Oct. 17, when Stockton threw for 272 yards and two touchdowns, Dwight Phillips Jr. ran for 68 yards and a score, and Craig Dandridge caught four balls for 88 yards. They won 20-17 at Alabama the week before.

Thad: Every great album has one track you skip. We're moving on.

Stockton has led Georgia in throws in all seven games and is 117 of 158 for 1,570 yards, 16 touchdowns and four interceptions. Phillips has 348 rushing yards, Dandridge has 310 receiving yards, and Wilson has 44 tackles and four sacks. The Bulldogs score 43.0 points a game and allow 15.9.

Florida is 5-2 and 3-2 in the league and also had last week off. Its last game was a 27-24 win at Texas on Oct. 17, when Tramell Jones Jr. went 22 of 35 for 155 yards and two touchdowns and Baugh ran 25 times for 91 yards and a score. Philo had led the Gators in throws in the first six games.

Dax: Winning in Austin? That play had scales.

Baugh has 763 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns on 135 carries. Philo is 105 of 149 for 1,341 yards and nine touchdowns, Dallas Wilson has 29 catches for 403 yards, Myles Graham has 48 tackles and Jayden Woods has 4.5 sacks. Florida scores 39.6 points a game and put up 66 on Florida Atlantic, 52 on Ole Miss and 44 at Auburn.

Dax: Thirteen rushing touchdowns, Thad. Jadan Baugh is a crocodile near the end zone.

Thad: Stockton completing that many throws is a perfect guitar solo, Dax.

Smart has led Georgia since 2016, and his teams went 14-1, 15-0, 13-1, 11-3 and 12-2 over the last five seasons, with national titles in 2021 and 2022. Sumrall is in his first season at Florida, and the Gators already have five wins after going 4-8 last year.

Thad: Coach Smart is the producer who never misses.

Dax: Coach Sumrall is building a whole new swamp ecosystem. It's thriving.

The series has been Georgia's lately. The Bulldogs have won eight of the last 10, including 34-20 in 2024 and 24-20 last year. Florida's last win was 44-28 in 2020.

Thad: Eight of 10, Dax. That's a greatest-hits album.

Dax: 2020 is on it too, Thad. Track seven. Crowd pleaser.

The matchup is Baugh and the Florida blockers against a Georgia defense with 22 sacks. On the other side, Stockton faces a Florida defense that also has 22 sacks.

The SEC's initial availability report, posted at 8:10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists Florida quarterbacks Tramell Jones Jr. and Aaron Philo questionable. Georgia lists three players out and three questionable, and Gunner Stockton is not on it.

Thad: I'm dressing as Uga. With a turntable.

Dax: Then I'll dress as Albert, and we'll ride MARTA home together.

Thad: Deal, Dax. Dinner's on me afterward, and I'll bring the music.

My call: Georgia Bulldogs 37, Florida Gators 28.

Arizona State vs BYU: All-Navy Cougars and an Endless Summer Soda

Arizona State Sun Devils vs BYU Cougars is a Week 9 Halloween afternoon at LaVell Edwards Stadium, and No. 8 BYU is wearing all navy, head to toe, against the team its own schedule video paired with a soda called "Endless Summer." Skylar Vanterpool, an Arizona State fan whose motto is "Hydrate and Dominate," says Reed Harris, Cardae Mack and Kenny Dillingham's Sun Devils spoil the costume, and Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi, a Provo trail guide whose dad jokes are so clean they sparkle, says Bear Bachmeier, Cade Uluave and Kalani Sitake's Cougars bounce back.

Bryce: Oh my heck, Skylar! Welcome to Provo. That's Y Mountain right there.

Skylar: It's beautiful, Bryce. Also, you're at altitude. Drink some water.

Bryce: The Sun Devil drank so much water in Provo. It heard the Cougars were a thirsty bunch.

Skylar: Hydrate, Bryce. And maybe workshop that one.

Back in January, BYU released its schedule as a set of Swig dirty sodas, calling it "a very on-brand schedule release," and KSL Sports called it a natural fit, since two Swig shops sit just outside the stadium's west side. Utah got "Drama Queen." The open week got "Water." Arizona State got "Endless Summer": Mountain Dew, pomegranate, grapefruit and fresh lime.

Skylar: Endless Summer. Bryce, that's not a soda. That's a lifestyle.

Bryce: It's a lot of Mountain Dew for a team that came to drink water.

Then on Monday, BYU showed its uniform for the game: navy helmet, navy jersey, navy pants, with white as the only other color. ColorWay Sports noted it's different from the navy jersey BYU wore against Iowa State on Oct. 9 with a white helmet and white pants, and that the last time BYU went navy from top to bottom was a 41-16 win over Southern Utah in 2023.

Bryce: All navy on Halloween. We're dressed as the night sky.

Skylar: You're dressed as a bruise, Bryce. A very handsome bruise.

BYU is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big 12, and it's coming off its first loss, 39-31 in overtime at UCF on Oct. 24. Bachmeier threw for 257 yards and two touchdowns, and Kyler Kasper caught six balls for 129 yards and a score. Before that, the Cougars beat Notre Dame 28-24, Iowa State 24-10 and TCU 17-10.

Bryce: Why did the Cougar lose in Orlando? Too many rides. We're home now.

Bachmeier has led BYU in throws in all seven games and is 116 of 184 for 1,514 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions. LJ Martin has 344 rushing yards, Legend Glasker has 28 catches for 498 yards, Uluave has 45 tackles and Tausili Akana has 3.5 sacks. The Cougars allow 18.6 points a game.

Arizona State is 4-3 and 2-2 in the league, and it beat Kansas State 28-17 at home on Oct. 24. Mack ran 26 times for 159 yards and four touchdowns, Mikey Keene threw for 160 yards, and Harris caught six balls for 147 yards.

Skylar: Four touchdowns, Bryce. Cardae Mack was the most hydrated man in Tempe.

Keene has led the Sun Devils in throws the last two games, after Cutter Boley did it in the first five. Boley is 105 of 173 for 1,360 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions. Harris has 47 catches for 800 yards and eight scores, Mack has 400 rushing yards and six touchdowns, Owen Long has 63 tackles and Julian Hugo has four sacks. The road has been rough: Arizona State lost 48-20 at Texas A&M and 53-25 at Texas Tech.

Skylar: Eight hundred yards, Bryce. Reed Harris is the whole summer.

Sitake played fullback for BYU under LaVell Edwards, and his teams went 11-2 and 12-2 the last two seasons. Dillingham took Arizona State to the 2024 Big 12 title, beating Iowa State 45-19 in the championship game.

Bryce: Coach Sitake was a fullback. He still runs downhill.

Skylar: Coach Dillingham coaches with so much energy, he probably runs on electrolytes.

These two have split their recent meetings. BYU won 27-17 in 2021, and Arizona State won 28-23 in 2024.

The matchup is Harris against a BYU defense that doesn't allow much. On the other side, the Cougars want Martin and the run game to keep Bachmeier ahead of the chains.

No official availability report is out for this game, so check the teams' pregame notes.

Bryce: I'm dressing as Cosmo the Cougar. Navy edition.

Skylar: I'm dressing as an Endless Summer. Sunhat, sunglasses, one large cup.

Bryce: Whatever happens, Skylar, the first round of dirty sodas is on me.

Skylar: Deal, Bryce. I'll bring the water.

My call: BYU Cougars 37, Arizona State Sun Devils 19.

display.fanatic_story:
Kansas vs TCU: A Halloween Blackout for the Haunting at the Carter

Kansas Jayhawks vs TCU Horned Frogs is the Week 9 Haunting at the Carter, a Halloween blackout in Fort Worth and the first time the Frogs have hosted a home game on Halloween since 2009. Fitz Calloway, a hoops-first Lawrence native who turns every football stat into basketball points, says Dylan Edwards, Isaiah Marshall and Lance Leipold's Jayhawks steal the night, and Ryder Galloway, a Stockyards cowboy turned finance guy who explains defenses as cattle drives, says Jaden Craig, Koron Hayward and Sonny Dykes's Frogs keep the herd together.

Ryder: Howdy, Fitz, and welcome to Fort Worth! Not Dallas. Never Dallas.

Fitz: Thanks, Ryder. I brought a basketball. Old habits.

Ryder: Leave it in the truck, partner. Tonight everybody wears black.

Fitz: Black? Ryder, I came in crimson and blue. I'm going to look like a highlighter at a funeral.

TCU's game notes put it plainly: the game "is a blackout and marks the first time the Frogs have hosted a home game on Halloween since 2009." It's also the first TCU home game this season with a 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff, and the first meeting in Fort Worth between these two since 2021.

Ryder: Seventeen years without a home Halloween, Fitz. We've been saving up.

Fitz: For seventeen years you've been saving costumes? That's a lot of cowboy hats.

The history runs purple. TCU leads the all-time series 27-9-4, including 12-2-2 in Fort Worth, and the notes say the Frogs "have won five straight and 11 of the last 12 against KU." The one Kansas win in recent memory came in 2018, 27-26. The last two in Fort Worth went 59-23 in 2020 and 31-28 in 2021.

Fitz: One point in 2018, Ryder. A free throw. I remember every free throw.

Both teams are 3-4 and 1-3 in the Big 12. Kansas is coming off a 25-24 win over Baylor, with Edwards running 30 times for 156 yards and Marshall throwing two touchdown throws. Nik McMillan caught a touchdown among his 66 yards.

Fitz: Thirty carries, Ryder. Dylan Edwards played the whole fourth quarter like it was overtime.

TCU lost 24-20 to West Virginia on Oct. 24, even though Craig went 33 of 47 for 372 yards. Kari Ashley caught six balls for 118 yards. Every TCU loss has been close: 15-10 to North Carolina, 21-13 at UCF, 17-10 to BYU and 24-20 to West Virginia.

Ryder: Four losses by a combined twenty-four points. That's not a stampede, Fitz. That's a few strays.

Craig, a Harvard transfer, is TCU's first new quarterback in charge in three seasons, and he has led the Frogs in throws in all seven games. He's 162 of 240 for 2,066 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jeremy Payne leads the rushers with 429 yards, Ed Small has 38 catches for 514 yards, Hayward has 4.5 sacks and Hudson Hooper has 41 tackles. The defense allows 13.9 points a game, and the notes say it has given up only 17 plays of 20 yards or more, the fewest in the Big 12.

Ryder: Seventeen big plays all year. That's a fence nobody gets through.

Marshall has led Kansas in throws in all seven games. He's 105 of 196 for 1,506 yards, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Edwards has 531 rushing yards and four touchdowns, McMillan has 25 catches for 466 yards and five scores, Trey Lathan has 48 tackles and Leroy Harris III has 3.5 sacks. Kansas scores 31.0 points a game.

Fitz: Thirty-one a game, Ryder. In my world that's a bad shooting night, but we'll take it.

Dykes is in his fifth season at TCU, and the notes say the 2022 National Coach of the Year won 36 games in his first four, the most by a Frogs coach since Francis Schmidt won 37 from 1929-32. Leipold has led Kansas since 2021.

Fitz: Coach Leipold wins everywhere he goes. That's a Hall of Fame jump shot.

Ryder: Coach Dykes has more wins here than anybody since the Hoover administration. Not one of them in Dallas.

The matchup is Edwards against a TCU front that has been very hard to run on. On the other side, Craig wants to push the ball down the field against a Kansas defense that allows 24.0 a game.

The Big 12's initial availability report, posted at 10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists six Kansas players out, with Isaiah Marshall probable, and seven TCU players out, with Jeremy Payne doubtful and Kari Ashley questionable.

Fitz: I'm dressing as a jayhawk. A real one. Beak and all.

Ryder: I'm dressing as a cowboy, Fitz.

Fitz: You're always dressed as a cowboy.

Ryder: Exactly. Saves a costume. Whatever happens, the brisket's on me.

Fitz: Deal, Ryder. Rock Chalk, and save me a burnt end.

My call: TCU Horned Frogs 25, Kansas Jayhawks 20.

Minnesota vs Indiana: Homecoming, Hoosierween and GameDay at the Fountain

Minnesota Golden Gophers vs Indiana Hoosiers is Week 9 Homecoming on Halloween in Bloomington, with ESPN's College GameDay at Showalter Fountain from 9 a.m. to noon ET and a Hoosierween carnival in Dunn Meadow the night before. Tor Engebretsen, a Minnesota ski-hill Gopher who owns enough coats to lend one out, says Drake Lindsey, Maverick Baranowski and P.J. Fleck's Gophers crash the party, and Mallory Penhallow, a former Miss Monroe County runner-up, says Josh Hoover, Charlie Becker and Curt Cignetti's Hoosiers keep the crown.

Mallory: Welcome to Bloomington, Tor! Hello, Hoosier Nation!

Tor: Thank you, Mallory. I brought cocoa, and a spare coat in case you get chilly.

Mallory: That's very sweet. I'll wear it over the sash.

Tor: And I should mention we're carrying a bronze pig around this week. We kept Floyd of Rosedale on Saturday.

IU Bloomington Today calls the game a matchup that "pits the defending Big Ten and national champion Indiana Hoosiers against the Minnesota Golden Gophers." Homecoming week wraps with a parade Friday at 5:30 p.m. ET, beginning at Kirkwood and Washington Street and heading east to the Sample Gates. After the parade, the Union Board hosts a student carnival in Dunn Meadow with the theme "Hoosierween," and costumes are encouraged.

Mallory: Hoosierween, Tor. I'm going as last year's trophy.

Tor: I'm going as a Minnesota winter. I just have to stand here.

Then Saturday, GameDay is live from Showalter Fountain with Rece Davis, Desmond Howard, Pat McAfee, Nick Saban and Kirk Herbstreit. Tailgate fields open at 9 a.m. ET, and the stadium gates open 90 minutes before the 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff on Merchants Bank Field. The university's advice for the day is to bring extra layers in case it gets cold.

Tor: Extra layers. Mallory, they wrote that advisory for me.

Mallory: They wrote it because of you, Tor. You're wearing four coats.

Indiana is 7-1 and 4-1 in the Big Ten. Its only loss was 19-15 to Ohio State on Oct. 17, and last week it won 13-6 in overtime at Michigan. Turbo Richard ran 19 times for 68 yards in that one.

Mallory: Thirteen to six in overtime, Tor. Ugly is still a win. My pageant coach said that about my baton routine.

Hoover has led Indiana in throws in all eight games. He's 116 of 187 for 1,741 yards, 18 touchdowns and one interception. Richard has 711 rushing yards and six scores, Becker has 42 catches for 726 yards and eight touchdowns, Tobi Osunsanmi has nine sacks and Isaiah Jones has 61 tackles. The Hoosiers allow 12.0 points a game and have shut out Howard and Western Kentucky.

Tor: Eighteen touchdowns and one interception. Mallory, does Hoover ever get cold?

Mallory: He's never been to Minnesota, Tor.

Minnesota is 5-2 and 3-1 in the league, and it beat Iowa 13-10 on Oct. 24 to keep Floyd. Before that, it beat Michigan 20-14 and won 27-24 at Washington. The losses were 38-13 to Mississippi State and 41-13 at Purdue.

Lindsey has led the Gophers in throws in all seven games and is 141 of 222 for 1,472 yards, nine touchdowns and six interceptions. TJ Thomas has 325 rushing yards, Javon Tracy has 39 catches for 420 yards, Baranowski has 51 tackles and TJ Bush Jr. has four sacks. Minnesota allows 20.1 points a game.

Tor: Thirteen to ten over Iowa. That's a classic. Nobody scores, everybody's happy.

Cignetti was hired at Indiana on Nov. 30, 2023, and in 2025 the Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 for their first national championship. Fleck has led Minnesota since 2017.

Tor: Coach Fleck rows the boat. We all row together.

Mallory: Coach Cignetti said it best: "It can be done." I have it on a pillow.

Minnesota won the last two meetings, 38-31 in 2018 and 35-14 in 2021.

Tor: Two in a row, Mallory. I'm just saying it out loud so the pig can hear.

The matchup is Becker and Hoover against a Minnesota defense that's stingy against the throw. On the other side, the Gophers need their big guys up front to open running room against a front led by Osunsanmi.

The Big Ten's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists seven Minnesota players out, quarterback Michael Merdinger among them, and Drake Lindsey is not on it. Indiana lists two players out, with Josh Hoover probable.

Mallory: Whatever happens, Tor, I'll save you a spot at the fountain.

Tor: Deal, Mallory. The cocoa's on me, and the coat is yours to keep.

My call: Indiana Hoosiers 34, Minnesota Golden Gophers 11.

Autzen is a Halloween blackout, Oregon is wearing white feathers on black helmets for the first time, and a former Ducks head coach is running the other side's offense.

The case for Oregon is the home crowd and a Northwestern team that has been close on the road. The Wildcats lost 29-23 at Indiana and beat Michigan State 24-21 away from home. Oregon has won three of its four games at Autzen and beat Northwestern 34-14 last season. My final has Oregon by 7, past the 3.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Northwestern vs Oregon: White Wings, Black Helmets and an Old Coach

Northwestern Wildcats vs Oregon Ducks is a Week 9 Halloween blackout at Autzen Stadium, where the Ducks will wear black helmets with white feathers for the first time, against a No. 20 Northwestern offense run by a former Ducks head coach. Ezra Lindqvist, a Northwestern data journalist who footnotes his own jokes, says Aidan Chiles, Griffin Wilde and David Braun's Wildcats keep rolling, and Nix Wyatt-Aldana, a Eugene sneaker-and-uniform designer who reviews jerseys and route trees with equal ferocity, says Dylan Raiola, Matayo Uiagalelei and Dan Lanning's Ducks bounce back.

Nix: Welcome to Autzen, Ezra! Before we begin, I have to review your outfit.

Ezra: I was afraid of that.

Nix: Purple quarter-zip, pumpkin pin for Halloween. Seven out of ten. The pin is carrying you.

Ezra: Footnote: the pin was my mother's idea, and she will be thrilled.

On Wednesday, Oregon showed its look for the game: black helmets with white feathers, black jerseys with gray numbers and white pants. The Oregonian's Aaron Fentress noted that "Oregon has worn black helmets with silver feathers over the past two seasons, but not with white feathers." The team's caption was three words: "Bold by design." Fans are asked to wear black, and On SI says this is the second of three blackout games at Autzen this season.

Nix: White wings on a black helmet, Ezra. Ten out of ten. I may need to sit down.

Ezra: Footnote: you are already sitting down.

Nix: I'm sitting down harder.

The other story is on Northwestern's sideline. Northwestern's offensive coordinator used to coach Oregon. On SI wrote that Lanning has warned about how well that Northwestern offense works, and The Oregonian's headline called it a matchup "against a former Ducks coach." Oregon also has a new play-caller this week in Jay Johnson.

Ezra: A former Ducks coach, back in Eugene, on Halloween. Footnote: this is the scariest thing that's happened here all year.

Nix: Old coaches are always welcome, Ezra. Their offenses aren't.

Northwestern is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big Ten. Its only loss was 29-23 at Indiana, and it beat Penn State 34-13 and Rutgers 42-14 last week. Against Rutgers, Chiles went 19 of 25 for 219 yards and three touchdowns, Caleb Komolafe ran 13 times for 150 yards, and Wilde caught nine balls for 133 yards.

Ezra: Forty-two points, Nix. I footnoted every one.

Chiles has led the Wildcats in throws in all seven games. He's 117 of 164 for 1,617 yards, 12 touchdowns and one interception. Komolafe has 551 rushing yards and five scores, Wilde has 39 catches for 615 yards, and Braydon Brus has 62 tackles and four sacks. Northwestern scores 34.7 points a game and allows 16.6.

Nix: One interception, Ezra? That's a clean silhouette. I hate it.

Oregon is 4-3 and 2-2 in the league, and it lost 21-10 at Illinois on Oct. 24. Raiola went 27 of 41 for 246 yards, Jordon Davison ran for 92 yards and a touchdown, and Dakorien Moore caught nine balls. The Ducks have lost three times, 39-31 at Oklahoma State, 17-15 to UCLA and 21-10 at Illinois. Raiola has led them in throws in three of the last four games.

Davison has 422 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, Dakorien Moore has 34 catches for 417 yards, Uiagalelei has six sacks and Koi Perich has 46 tackles. Oregon scores 33.1 a game and allows 20.7.

Nix: Six sacks for Matayo. He wears the uniform. The uniform doesn't wear him.

These two met last September in Evanston, and Oregon won 34-14 wearing a combination called "High voltage."

Ezra: Footnote: I have not recovered from High voltage.

Lanning was hired on Dec. 11, 2021. Braun became Northwestern's interim coach in 2023 and was named the permanent head coach that November.

Nix: Coach Lanning would tackle a bear for this team.

Ezra: Coach Braun would write the bear a thank-you note. Then tackle it.

The matchup is Komolafe and Northwestern's big guys up front against Uiagalelei and an Oregon front that needs a good day. On the other side, the Ducks want Davison running early so Raiola can play ahead of the chains.

No official availability report is out for this game, so check the teams' pregame notes.

Nix: I'm dressing as a white feather.

Ezra: I'm dressing as a footnote. Very small. Very important.

Nix: Whatever happens, Ezra, dinner's on me.

Ezra: Deal, Nix. Footnote: I'm holding you to it.

My call: Oregon Ducks 29, Northwestern Wildcats 22.

Colorado State vs Utah State prediction, pick against the spread and over/under: I'm on Utah State Aggies −6.5 and Under 63.5 at DraftKings, with a final of Utah State Aggies 34, Colorado State Rams 27. It's Halloween afternoon at Maverik Stadium in Logan, where Utah State has asked the whole crowd to wear black.

The Aggies have the defense, and the Rams haven't found a road game they can win. Utah State allows 23.0 points a game and ranks first in the Pac-12 in total defense. Colorado State allows 44.0 points a game and gave up 41 or more in five of its seven games. Away from Fort Collins, it lost 59-45 at UTSA and 66-27 at Texas State. Utah State won five straight in this series from 2018 through 2023 and has won five of the past six in Logan.

Hyrum Tolleson hands out cups of Aggie Ice Cream in the Maverik Stadium lot. "Asher Cunningham made 17 tackles and forced two fumbles against Washington State, and we came back from 16-3. Eli Wood has 37 catches and five touchdowns. Have a double scoop, neighbor."

Ansel Rimrock, still in trail shoes, takes a single. "Hauss Hejny just threw for 333 yards and ran for two scores against San Diego State, and Tre'Shawn Moore took an interception back for a touchdown. We put up 56, Hyrum."

My concern is the Utah State offense. The Aggies score 14.9 points a game, Grady Brosterhous has six interceptions, and they scored 17 or fewer in five games, including a 20-17 loss at Texas State last week. If Hejny's offense plays like it did against San Diego State, a touchdown margin won't hold.

The total is about Utah State's games. None of the Aggies' seven games reached 56 combined points, and five finished at 37 or fewer. Colorado State's games run high, including those 59-45 and 66-27 road losses, but Utah State hasn't scored more than 21 in any game this season. display.fanatic_story:
Colorado State vs Utah State: Wear Black on Halloween in Logan

Colorado State Rams vs Utah State Aggies is a Week 9 Halloween afternoon game at Maverik Stadium, where Utah State has asked everyone to wear black and Logan's downtown shops spend Friday handing out treats to kids in costume. Ansel Rimrock, a Fort Collins trail runner who measures every trip in foothill miles, says Jim Mora's Rams have Hauss Hejny back, and Hyrum Tolleson, a Cache Valley dairyman who has been up before the sun since he was 8, says Bronco Mendenhall's Aggies, Asher Cunningham and Eli Wood will make the Rams earn every yard.

Hyrum: Welcome to Logan, neighbor. Double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream?

Ansel: It's Halloween, Hyrum. And I ran here. Technically, I ran the last two miles.

Hyrum: Then you've earned the double. Black spoon, to match the dress code.

This is the 81st meeting of an old mountain rivalry. The series began in 1902 and has run through six conferences, from the Rocky Mountain Athletic Conference to the rebuilt Pac-12. Colorado State's game notes have the Rams ahead 40-38-2. Utah State won five straight from 2018 through 2023, and Colorado State won the last one, 42-37 in Fort Collins in 2024, after a 29-point fourth-quarter comeback.

Ansel: Twenty-nine points in one quarter, Hyrum. That's a sunrise summit.

Hyrum: I remember. I milked the cows in silence the next morning. The cows understood.

Colorado State is 3-4 and coming off a 56-49 win over San Diego State. Hejny, back at quarterback for the first time since Sept. 19 after a hamstring injury, threw for 333 yards and three touchdowns and ran for two more. The Pac-12 named him its offensive player of the week, and safety Tre'Shawn Moore was the defensive player of the week after returning an interception 38 yards for a touchdown.

Hejny was honest about the nerves. "Nerves are good," he said, in quotes reported by Nathan Wright of the Loveland Reporter-Herald. "I like when I have nerves because it means it matters to me and it's a big game and I'm excited to play."

Ansel: Nerves are just your legs telling you the climb is real.

For the season, Hejny is 71 of 104 for 952 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. Mel Brown has 454 rushing yards on just 52 carries, RJ Vick has 24 catches for 367 yards, and Oumar Diomande has 67 tackles. Durell Robinson ran for two scores against the Aztecs.

Utah State is 2-5 and lost 20-17 at Texas State last week. Grady Brosterhous is 99 of 178 for 1,120 yards, seven touchdowns and six interceptions. Javen Jacobs has 435 rushing yards, and Wood has 37 catches for 479 yards and five touchdowns. He's on the Biletnikoff Award watch list. Brevin Hamblin has 58 tackles, and Jordan Pendleton has 2.5 sacks.

Hyrum: Eli Wood catches everything and says thank you after. That's how his mother raised him.

The Aggies' defense is the reason this game can be close. Utah State allows 344.0 yards a game, first in the Pac-12. Cunningham was the Walter Camp national defensive player of the week after the 17-16 win over Washington State on Oct. 9, with 17 tackles and two forced fumbles. Both fumbles came in the second half and led to touchdowns as Utah State came back from 16-3 down at halftime.

Hyrum: Seventeen tackles. That's a full barn before breakfast.

Ansel: Our offense runs like the Horsetooth trail. Uphill, downhill, no stopping.

Colorado State has scored 38.6 points a game and allowed 44.0. Utah State has scored 14.9 and allowed 23.0. The Rams lost 59-45 at UTSA and 66-27 at Texas State, and they're still looking for a road win.

Hyrum: You're 0-2 away from home, Ansel. Bring a map.

Ansel: I've got a map. I've also got Hejny.

The Pac-12's advance availability report, updated at 10:02 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists three Colorado State players out and Mel Brown questionable, and Hejny is not on it. Utah State lists eight players out, four for the season, with Eli Wood questionable.

Mora was hired at Colorado State on Nov. 26, 2025. Mendenhall has led Utah State since his hire on Dec. 6, 2024. KSL's Brian Preece put it plainly in Logan this week: the Aggies have five games left and need four wins to reach a bowl.

Hyrum: Four of five. On a dairy, that's called a Tuesday.

Colorado State has played on Halloween before, and its notes say it beat Utah State both times the two met on Oct. 31.

Ansel: History is on the trail with me.

Hyrum: History didn't have to eat lunch in Cache Valley.

After the game, Logan throws a free Halloween Silent Disco at Laub Plaza from 9 p.m. to midnight ET.

Ansel: Headphones on, Hyrum. You can dance to whatever you want, and I won't have to hear it.

Hyrum: Polka. It's always polka. Come by the dairy in the morning, and I'll put you to work.

Ansel: Deal. Bring the spoons.

My call: Utah State Aggies 34, Colorado State Rams 27.

UTEP (1-6, 0-3 Mountain West) at North Dakota State (6-2, 3-2 Mountain West), Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on MW+ at the Fargodome in Fargo. Nathan Hayes has 12 touchdown throws, Jackson Williams has 503 receiving yards, Donovan Woolen has 55 tackles. We lost at New Mexico last week, and we bring hotdish either way."

Hotdish Meets Hatch Chile: UTEP Visits North Dakota State on Halloween

UTEP (1-6, 0-3 Mountain West) at North Dakota State (6-2, 3-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Fargodome, Fargo, N.D., MW+.

Your hosts are Neto Galindo, a UTEP fan and Sun Bowl ironworker's kid who grades effort by chile heat, and Inga Halvorsen, a North Dakota State fan and agricultural economist who has tracked every Bison title since she was a girl.

Inga: Oh, for cute, you made it to Fargo! Welcome, Neto.

Neto: Thanks, Inga. I brought green chile from El Paso. It's Halloween, so I figured I'd bring the scariest thing I own.

Inga: And I brought tater tot hotdish. I bring hotdish either way, hon.

Neto: Then let's make it Hatch-hot hotdish. Neighbors share.

Players to watch

North Dakota State quarterback Nathan Hayes has thrown the most passes in all eight games. He's 123 of 196 for 1,470 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions. Myles Mitchell leads the rushers with 393 yards, and Jackson Williams leads the receivers with 32 catches for 503 yards. Linebacker Donovan Woolen leads the defense with 55 tackles, and Kelton McCaslin has four sacks.

For UTEP, Raymond Moore III has thrown the most passes the last two games and leads the team in rushing with 414 yards. EJ Colson Jr. threw the most in the first five games and leads in passing with 628 yards and seven touchdowns. Kam Thomas leads the receivers with 270 yards, linebacker Isaiah Bogerty leads the defense with 42 tackles, and Sterling Miles has 3.5 sacks.

Inga: Against Nevada, Jackson Williams caught a missed field goal in the end zone and ran it back 100 yards. That young man deserves extra hotdish.

Neto: Raymond Moore III runs like a five-alarm chile. Effort grade: Hatch-hot.

What happened last week

North Dakota State lost 21-16 at New Mexico on Oct. 24, on Homecoming weekend in Albuquerque. Hayes threw for 198 yards and two touchdowns, and Williams caught four balls for 71 yards. It was the first meeting on record between the schools.

Inga: Oh, yah, that's a tough one. I made a second hotdish on the bus.

UTEP had an open week. The Miners last played on Oct. 17, losing 24-11 to San José State at the Sun Bowl. Moore threw for 195 yards, and Thomas caught four balls for 96 yards.

Neto: A week off to rest the legs and sharpen the effort. We'll be fresh.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Hayes has thrown the most passes for North Dakota State every week, and Moore has done it for UTEP the last two games, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Tim Polasek leads North Dakota State, with a hire date of Dec. 17, 2023. His team plays Bison football: run it, defend it, don't give it away. The Bison allow 12.5 points a game, they've taken the ball away 14 times, and they shut out Fordham 38-0 and Wyoming 28-0.

Scotty Walden leads UTEP, with a hire date of Dec. 4, 2023. His offense runs the ball on most plays, and his team's best day came Sept. 12, a 51-10 win over Texas Southern. The open week gave his staff extra time to prepare.

Inga: Coach Polasek is Fargo through and through. Practical, like a good snow shovel.

Neto: Coach Walden is building it brick by brick, like my dad on a Sun Bowl job site.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is North Dakota State's defense against Moore, who can hurt you with his legs. The Bison's big guys up front have been tough to run on all season. On the other side, Hayes wants a clean day after five interceptions in the two losses, and UTEP's defense will try to force him into more mistakes. This is the first meeting between these schools in our records from 2016 through 2025.

What's happening on campus

Halloween in Fargo means bundling up, and the Fargodome, opened in 1992 and listed at 18,700 seats, keeps everybody warm and loud inside. UTEP fans call the Sun Bowl home, built in 1963 and listed at 51,500, with the Sound of the Southwest band and mascot Paydirt Pete.

Neto: I'm dressing as Paydirt Pete. Pickaxe and all.

Inga: I'm dressing as a casserole dish. Very warm, very Fargo.

Anything else fun and true

North Dakota State has won 18 national championships, including 10 FCS titles between 2011 and 2024, and 39 conference championships. The Bison went 14-1, 12-3, 11-4, 14-2 and 12-1 in their last five Missouri Valley seasons. UTEP's fight song is "El Paso Fight."

Inga: Whatever happens, Neto, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Neto: Deal, Inga. Share the chile, and the hotdish.

My call: North Dakota State Bison 37, UTEP Miners 10.

display.fanatic_story:
FIU vs Liberty: Candy, a Parade and Homecoming on Halloween

Florida International Panthers vs Liberty Flames is a Week 9 Homecoming and Hall of Fame Weekend game in Lynchburg, and the Halloween morning parade rolls down University Boulevard tossing candy before the 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff at Williams Stadium. Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, an FIU fan from Sweetwater who learned football from her abuela over cafecito and dominoes, says JJ Kohl and Willie Simmons have Liberty's number, and Gideon Fairweather, a Lynchburg youth pastor who coaches middle-school football, says Jamey Chadwell, Kam Davis and Deshawn Purdie will keep the Flames perfect in Conference USA.

Gideon: Lourdes! You made the parade. Did you catch any candy?

Lourdes: Two Tootsie Rolls and a pencil. I'm saving the pencil for the scorebook.

Gideon: That's the spirit. Liberty's alumni tailgate has Family Candy Games at 1 p.m. ET. You can enter.

Lourdes: Gideon, I'm a grown woman. Of course I'm entering.

This series is short and loud. Liberty leads it 3-1, and the last two meetings both went to overtime, with the home team winning both. The Flames won 31-24 in Lynchburg in 2024. Last November in Miami, FIU won 34-27 for its first win over Liberty. The Flames tied that one with a field goal at the final horn, and the Panthers won it in overtime with an interception on fourth down after Maguire Anderson caught a touchdown.

Lourdes: My abuela watched that one with me. She hasn't stopped talking about it.

Gideon: I prayed for her. Then I went home and watched film with my seventh graders.

Liberty is 6-1, 3-0 in Conference USA and first in the conference. The Flames have won six in a row since a 20-13 loss at James Madison to open the season. They score 31.6 points a game, the most in the league, and allow 14.0, the fewest. Liberty's notes say the Flames haven't thrown an interception this year. Purdie is 80 of 133 for 1,226 yards and nine touchdowns, Davis has 583 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 83 carries, and Makai Jackson has 23 catches for 540 yards and five touchdowns. Derrell Farrar leads the defense with 39 tackles.

Gideon: Makai Jackson gets more than 23 yards a catch. My middle schoolers get about three, and they're thrilled.

FIU is 3-4 and 1-2 in the league, and it has lost two straight conference games by three points, 27-24 at Jacksonville State and 26-23 to Middle Tennessee at home. Kohl is 131 of 227 for 1,637 yards, 10 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Devonte Lyons had a career-high 115 rushing yards against Middle Tennessee and has 383 for the year. Anderson has 36 catches for 568 yards and four touchdowns, DeeJay Holmes Jr. has five sacks, and DeAndre Boykins leads with 37 tackles.

Lourdes: Three points, three points. My abuela says the dominoes owe us.

The defenses are why both fan bases are nervous. FIU allows 16.3 points a game, second in the league behind Liberty, and its athletic department says opponents have scored touchdowns on only five of 19 trips inside the Panthers' 20. Liberty has held five straight opponents under 20 points, and its notes say the Flames are 14-0 under Chadwell when they do that.

Gideon: Fourteen and oh. I put that on the whiteboard in the youth room.

Lourdes: Put this under it. FIU won the last one.

Chadwell is in his fourth season at Liberty, and his first Flames team went 13-1. Simmons is in his second season at FIU, after a first year in which the Panthers won their last four to reach a bowl. The Panthers are 0-3 on the road this season, and the FIU notes say this is the program's first Halloween game since 2015.

Lourdes: Coach Simmons turns seasons around. Ask anyone in the 305.

Gideon: Coach Chadwell turns Homecoming into a family reunion. His Flames have gone 3-0 on Homecoming.

Friday night, the Presbyterian Cemetery Ghost Walk leads lantern tours on Bailey Street, with popcorn and cider at the end. After the game, Homecoming's Blacklight Bowling at Montview runs until midnight ET.

Gideon: Ghost walk Friday, bowling Saturday. Lourdes, I'll even let you keep score with your pencil.

Lourdes: Deal. And I'll teach your seventh graders dominoes.

My call: Liberty Flames 27, Florida International Panthers 12.

Darnell Vidrine is resetting the optimism counter on his folding table outside Malone Stadium when Dee Broussard sweeps up in pearls and a black-and-gold sundress. "Good evening, good morning, good whatever-time-it-is," Darnell says. "Bless your heart, sugar," Dee answers, adjusting her pearls. "That counter's been reset a lot." Darnell taps it proudly. "Every week, Dee. It still works."

Southern Miss (2-5, 1-2 Sun Belt) at UL Monroe (1-6, 1-2 Sun Belt), Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at Malone Stadium in Monroe. DraftKings has Southern Miss Golden Eagles −3.5 with a total of 55.5. My card: Southern Miss Golden Eagles −3.5, Over 55.5, and a final of Southern Miss Golden Eagles 32, UL Monroe Warhawks 26.

Dee speaks for Southern Miss, smoothing her dress. "We beat Louisiana 35-31 last week, sugar. Jamarice Wilder ran for 154 yards in that one, Steven Robinson has eight rushing touchdowns, Mario Sanders has 569 receiving yards, and Mathis Haygood has 63 tackles. To the top."

Darnell speaks for UL Monroe, counter in hand. "I KNEW IT! We won 21-14 at Troy, and Aidan Armenta threw two touchdowns with no interceptions. He threw for 362 yards at South Alabama. Noah Flemmings has 65 tackles. And we beat Southern Miss 38-21 in 2024. Keep the faith, y'all."

Why Southern Miss? Because the Golden Eagles can run on this defense. UL Monroe allows 37.3 points a game and gave up 62 to Mississippi State, 45 to Florida Atlantic and 52 at South Alabama. Pearls and an Optimism Counter: Southern Miss Visits UL Monroe on Halloween

Southern Miss (2-5, 1-2 Sun Belt) at UL Monroe (1-6, 1-2 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 3:30 p.m. ET, Malone Stadium, Monroe, La., ESPN+.

Your hosts are Dee Broussard, a Southern Miss fan and former sorority president who calls everybody "sugar" and means it, and Darnell Vidrine, a UL Monroe fan and overnight Delta radio host who keeps an optimism counter running all season.

Darnell: Good evening, good morning, good whatever-time-it-is! Welcome to Monroe, Dee.

Dee: Thank you, sugar. Is that the famous optimism counter?

Darnell: Set to 100, like every week. But this week, Dee, I didn't have to reset it. We WON.

Dee: Well, bless it. Congratulations, Darnell. Truly.

Players to watch

Southern Miss quarterback Landry Lyddy has thrown the most passes in the last five games. He's 101 of 170 for 1,196 yards, seven touchdowns and four interceptions. Steven Robinson leads the rushers with 577 yards and eight scores, and Mario Sanders leads the receivers with 40 catches for 569 yards and five touchdowns. Linebacker Mathis Haygood leads the defense with 63 tackles, and Jameer Lewis has four sacks.

UL Monroe quarterback Aidan Armenta has thrown the most passes in the last four games. He's 96 of 153 for 1,121 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions. Austin Carlisle, who threw the most passes in the second and third games, leads the team in rushing with 237 yards, and Marcellus Jackson leads the receivers with 32 catches. Linebacker Noah Flemmings leads the defense with 65 tackles, and Kevontay Wells has three sacks.

Dee: Steven Robinson runs like he's late for a formal. Eight touchdowns, sugar.

Darnell: Noah Flemmings has 65 tackles. I can FEEL it every time he hits somebody.

What happened last week

UL Monroe won its first game of the season, 21-14 at Troy on Oct. 24, on Troy's Military Appreciation day. Armenta went 13 of 22 for 147 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions.

Darnell: I KNEW IT! I may have sniffled on the air. Okay, I definitely sniffled.

Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31 on Homecoming at "The Rock" on Oct. 24. Jamarice Wilder ran 13 times for 154 yards and a touchdown, and Sanders caught six balls for 77 yards.

Dee: Homecoming win at home. To the top, y'all! I pointed skyward so hard I lost an earring.

Injuries and availability

No official availability report has been posted for this game yet, and box scores don't mark starters. Lyddy has thrown the most passes for Southern Miss in five straight games, and Armenta has done it for UL Monroe in four straight, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Blake Anderson is in his first season at Southern Miss, with a hire date of Dec. 11, 2025. His team throws it well and just got a big day from the run game, too. The defense is the work in progress, but the Golden Eagles found a way against Louisiana.

Bryant Vincent leads UL Monroe, with a hire date of Dec. 5, 2023. Two of his team's early losses were one-score games, 26-20 at UAB and 38-35 to SE Louisiana, and last week his defense held Troy to 14 points.

Dee: Coach Anderson walked in and got to work. I respect a man with a plan.

Darnell: Coach Vincent keeps the faith. He's a counter-reset kind of coach.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is the Southern Miss run game against a UL Monroe defense that has had a hard time stopping the run. Robinson and Wilder will test the Warhawks' big guys up front. On the other side, Armenta wants another clean day after throwing for 362 yards at South Alabama earlier this season. Southern Miss won four of the six meetings since 2017, including 49-21 last season, but UL Monroe won 38-21 in 2024.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in Monroe, and Malone Stadium, opened in 1978 and listed at 27,617 seats, gets the home crowd back after last week's trip to Troy. Southern Miss fans just celebrated Homecoming at The Rock, which wears a new name this fall, Renasant Stadium. The nickname isn't going anywhere.

Dee: I'm dressing as a string of pearls. Elegant, timeless, a little bit sparkly.

Darnell: I'm dressing as a 2 a.m. radio show. Everybody's welcome to call in.

Anything else fun and true

UL Monroe football dates to 1931. The school's teams were the Northeast Louisiana Indians for a long stretch and became the Warhawks in 2006, and the program moved up to what is now FBS in 1994. Southern Miss went 7-6 last season, a lovely bounce back after a 1-11 year in 2024.

Darnell: Whatever happens, Dee, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Dee: Deal, sugar. I'll bring the sweet tea.

My call: Southern Miss Golden Eagles 32, UL Monroe Warhawks 26.

Utah vs Cincinnati: Wear Black, Bring a Costume, No Masks

Utah Utes vs Cincinnati Bearcats is a Week 9 Halloween game at Nippert Stadium, where the Bearcats have asked fans to wear black for Breast Cancer Awareness and invited kids to come in costume, as long as nobody wears a mask. Aspen Mortensen, a Utah fan and former ski racer who reads defenses like slalom gates, says Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker will keep the Utes perfect, and Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy, a UC engineering co-op student who ranks everything in chili ways, says Scott Satterfield, JC French IV and Cole Tabb are about to do it again.

Skyline: Aspen! You came in costume.

Aspen: I'm a ski racer, Skyline. This is my regular jacket.

Skyline: It's black. You're following the dress code. I'm proud of you.

Aspen: I'm following the snow. Black shows up better in an avalanche.

Last Saturday, Cincinnati beat No. 8 Texas Tech 37-24 on the university's 100th Homecoming. The athletic department called it the Bearcats' first home win over an AP top-10 team since a 30-11 win over Rutgers in 2006. Tabb ran for a career-high 173 yards on 16 carries, including a 58-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. French threw a career-best four touchdowns, and MJ Cannon forced a fumble and made a one-handed interception just before halftime.

Skyline: That's a five-way win, Aspen. Spaghetti, chili, cheese, onions and beans. The full plate.

Aspen: Enjoy it. We beat you 45-14 last year.

Skyline: We remember. Coach Satterfield remembers. That's why he asked for help.

Satterfield wanted the whole building in it this week. "I know it's Halloween, but dress up and come out yelling in this game," he said Monday.

Aspen: Yelling doesn't scare me. I've heard a glacier crack.

Utah is 7-0, 4-0 in the Big 12, and first in the conference. The Utes score 37.4 points a game and allow 14.6. Dampier is 136 of 198 for 1,616 yards, 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he ran for 150 yards and two touchdowns in last week's 21-13 win over Houston. Parker has 644 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, Braden Pegan has 34 catches for 459 yards and six touchdowns, and Trey Reynolds leads the defense with 44 tackles.

Satterfield saw that Houston game. "Their quarterback, he had a great game last week against Houston," he said.

Aspen: Dampier runs like a downhill racer. Straight down, no brakes.

Cincinnati is 5-2 and 2-2 in the league. French is 127 of 183 for 1,510 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. Tabb has 621 rushing yards and nine touchdowns on just 65 carries. JV Gibson has 29 catches for 385 yards, Patrick Bauer has 3.5 sacks, and Jonathan Thompson leads the defense with 60 tackles. The Bearcats score 35.4 points a game and allow 26.4.

Skyline: Tabb is a three-way. Fast, smart and somehow still underrated.

Aspen: Three-way is spaghetti, chili and cheese. Even I know that.

Skyline: You've been studying.

The Bearcats lost 34-7 at Arizona and 45-42 at West Virginia before beating Texas Tech. Utah has won two road games, 31-17 at Iowa State and 27-24 at Colorado.

Aspen: Close one in Boulder. I'll admit it. Tight gates.

The Big 12's initial availability report, posted at 10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists two Utah players out and one questionable, and two Cincinnati players out, one doubtful and two questionable.

Before kickoff, The Den student tailgate runs from noon ET on Sigma Sigma Commons with LaRosa's pizza, a costume contest for a pair of Bearcats basketball tickets and a field-goal kick contest for $50.

Skyline: I'm entering the kick contest. Engineering. It's all angles.

Aspen: I'm entering the costume contest. As a ski racer.

Skyline: That's not a costume.

Aspen: It is in Ohio.

Skyline: Whatever happens, Aspen, the chili's on me afterward. Four-way, onions.

Aspen: Deal. Hold the onions on the ride home.

My call: Utah Utes 33, Cincinnati Bearcats 25.

Virginia vs Wake Forest: Pumpkins, Parachutes and "Thriller"

Virginia Cavaliers vs Wake Forest Demon Deacons is a Week 9 Halloween game in Winston-Salem, where trick-or-treating runs inside Gate 5 before kickoff and the band plays "Thriller" at halftime. Prescott Ashby-Lowell, a fourth-generation Wahoo in a game-day bow tie who refuses to say "campus," says Tony Elliott, Beau Pribula and Jekail Middlebrook can slow it down, and Eloise Brightman-Rowe, a Wake Forest debate grad, says Jake Dickert, Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez will roll the Quad by dinner.

Eloise: Resolved, Prescott: Wake Forest is the best place in America to spend Halloween.

Prescott: I accept the premise with one amendment. The Grounds are a close second.

Eloise: You can't say "Grounds" here. It's a Deacon Halloween. There's a pumpkin patch at Gate 5.

Prescott: Then I shall select a pumpkin with good posture.

Wake Forest is 6-1, 4-1 in the ACC and second in the conference. The Demon Deacons have won four in a row and beat Stanford 57-3, NC State 38-14 and Cal 41-7 in their last three games before an off week. Lopez is 140 of 207 for 1,947 yards, 17 touchdowns and one interception. He threw for 267 yards and four touchdowns in the win at Cal. Hernandez missed that game but still has 49 catches for 720 yards, Ty Clark III leads the rushers with 328 yards, Langston Hardy has 5.5 sacks, and Vincent Firenze leads the defense with 49 tackles.

Dickert spent the off week worried about rust, and he said Monday that a team can't just show up after two weeks off and expect game speed.

Eloise: Rebuttal time, Prescott. One interception all season.

Prescott: I concede the interception. I do not concede the afternoon.

Eloise: Noted for the record. The judges are unmoved.

Prescott: The judges are wearing Wake Forest sweaters, Eloise.

Virginia is 4-4 and 2-3 in the league. Pribula is 119 of 183 for 1,369 yards, 13 touchdowns and two interceptions. Middlebrook has 513 rushing yards and ran for 117 and a touchdown against Duke last week, and Jacobie Henderson leads the Cavaliers with 40 tackles. Matthew Fobbs-White has four sacks.

The Duke game hurt. Will Bettridge's 30-yard field goal put Virginia up 16-13 with three minutes left, and Duke answered with a seven-play, 75-yard drive to win 19-16.

Prescott: Three minutes, Eloise. We were three minutes from a proper Saturday.

Eloise: I'll give you that one. Bow tie to bow tie.

Elliott didn't hide from it. "Guys have got to strain a little bit harder," he said.

Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz is sketching a game-week roadmap on a whiteboard outside CEFCU Stadium when Paloma Begaye-Ortiz walks up holding two foil-wrapped burritos. "Red or green?" Paloma asks. Tessa studies them like a product spec. "Can I A/B test both?" Paloma laughs. "Both, Tessa. Always both."

New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) visits San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West) Saturday at 4 p.m. ET on MW+ at CEFCU Stadium in San Jose. DraftKings has New Mexico Lobos −14.5 with a total of 42.5. My card: New Mexico Lobos −14.5, Over 42.5, and a final of New Mexico Lobos 31, San José State Spartans 15.

Paloma speaks for New Mexico. "We beat North Dakota State 21-16 last week, and Kiefer Sibley ran for 91 yards and a touchdown. Scottre Humphrey has nine rushing touchdowns, Brett Karhu has five sacks, and Mercury Swaim has 43 tackles. Our defense allows 11.3 points a game. Red or green? BOTH!"

Tessa speaks for San José State. "Rollback. We lost 28-13 at Nevada, and our quarterback spot is a work in progress. Daniel Rolovich got hurt early, and Luke Weaver came back late. Weaver has 11 touchdown throws. Carson Clark has 47 catches, Jayland McGlothen has six sacks and Dylan Lee has 71 tackles. And we've won the last four meetings."

Why New Mexico? Because the Lobos defend and run the ball. New Mexico allows 11.3 points a game, and its only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma. San José State scored 13 points at Nevada and 13 against Wyoming, and it's sorting out its quarterbacks. My final has the Lobos winning by 16.

The risk is the New Mexico passing game. Toa Fa'avae threw for 92 yards last week and 59 at Hawai'i, with interceptions in both, and the Lobos won those games 21-10 and 21-16. McGlothen can get after the quarterback, and the Spartans have won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season. If New Mexico can't throw, this stays close.

Why the Over? New Mexico can score in a hurry: 38 against Central Michigan, 70 against Mercyhurst, 42 at New Mexico State and 61 against UTEP. The last five meetings between these teams finished 48-41, 32-21, 38-21, 52-24 and 35-28. My 31-15 adds up to 46, over 42.5.

Now the room. The Formula has New Mexico 31-15, sides with New Mexico, and likes the Over. Next Man Up has New Mexico 30-15, sides with New Mexico, and likes the Over. Follow The Money sits out both, since the spread and the total haven't budged. The Formula opened: "New Mexico's defense wins this by more than two scores."

Next Man Up agreed: "And the Lobos score enough for the Over."

Follow The Money shrugged: "Nothing moved. I'm watching."

Bottom of the card: a New Mexico defense that takes the ball away, a San José State team sorting out its quarterbacks and a Halloween crowd in San Jose. Give me the Lobos and the Over.

Balloons and Product Launches: New Mexico Visits San José State on Halloween

New Mexico (6-1, 3-0 Mountain West) at San José State (4-4, 2-2 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 4 p.m. ET, CEFCU Stadium, San Jose, Calif., MW+.

Your hosts are Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, a New Mexico fan who flies a hot-air balloon in the Balloon Fiesta every October, and Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, a San José State fan and tech product lead who treats game week like a launch.

Tessa: Welcome to San Jose, Paloma! I've got the roadmap, the standup and the retro all scheduled.

Paloma: Thanks, Tessa. I brought green chile. Red, too. Both!

Tessa: Can I A/B test them?

Paloma: You can, but the answer is always both.

Players to watch

New Mexico quarterback Toa Fa'avae has thrown the most passes in the last six games. He's 49 of 87 for 790 yards, five touchdowns and four interceptions. Scottre Humphrey leads the rushers with 453 yards and nine scores, and tight end Cade Keith leads the receivers with 20 catches for 265 yards. Brett Karhu has five sacks, and linebacker Mercury Swaim leads the defense with 43 tackles.

San José State's Luke Weaver threw the most passes in each of the first six games and leads the team with 1,620 yards, 11 touchdowns and six interceptions. Jabari Bates leads the rushers with 586 yards, and freshman Carson Clark leads the receivers with 47 catches for 551 yards and five scores. Jayland McGlothen has six sacks, and linebacker Dylan Lee leads the team with 71 tackles.

Paloma: Humphrey runs like a balloon catching a thermal. Up and up.

Tessa: Carson Clark has 47 catches as a freshman. That's a feature I'd demo to anybody.

What happened last week

New Mexico beat North Dakota State 21-16 on Homecoming in Albuquerque on Oct. 24, during a Pack Week that honored the Route 66 centennial. Kiefer Sibley ran 13 times for 91 yards and a touchdown, and Keith caught five balls.

Paloma: Too much heat for a while, then we soared. Red or green? BOTH!

San José State lost 28-13 at Nevada on Oct. 24. Viliami Teu ran for a touchdown, and Dominique McKenzie caught two balls for 60 yards.

Tessa: Rollback. I opened a bug ticket on the bus ride home.

Injuries and availability

No official Mountain West availability report has been posted for this game yet. San José State's quarterback spot is the big question. Freshman Daniel Rolovich started the last two games, but he was hurt in the first quarter at Nevada, and Weaver came back in the fourth quarter to lead a late scoring drive. Who starts Saturday hasn't been announced, so check the teams' pregame notes.

What the coaches are up to

Jason Eck leads New Mexico, with a hire date of Dec. 16, 2024. His defense allows 11.3 points a game and had taken the ball away 21 times through six games. The Lobos' only loss was 14-6 at Oklahoma.

Ken Niumatalolo was hired at San José State on Jan. 21, 2024. Before the UTEP game he went with Rolovich because, as he put it, the staff "just felt like we needed a spark." He also said of the freshman, "He's got a big arm. He's big and strong and can run. He's not afraid."

Paloma: Coach Eck builds a defense the way I pack a balloon basket. Nothing loose.

Tessa: Coach Niumatalolo ships fixes fast. I respect that.

Player storylines

The matchup to watch is Humphrey and the New Mexico big guys up front against a Spartans defense that allows 22.5 points a game. On the other side, whoever plays quarterback for San José State has to find Clark against a Lobos defense that loves taking the ball away. San José State has won the last four meetings, including 35-28 last season, and the Spartans are looking for an eighth straight home win over the Lobos.

What's happening on campus

It's Halloween in San Jose, and San José State is hosting Trick or Treat with the Spartans and Youth Spirit Day. Families can trick-or-treat before kickoff, and local youth dance and cheer groups will perform on the field at halftime. CEFCU Stadium opened in 1933 as Spartan Stadium and is listed at 30,456 seats.

Paloma: I'm dressing as a hot-air balloon. Cherry and silver, of course.

Tessa: I'm dressing as a software update. Nobody knows when I'll arrive.

Anything else fun and true

San José State first played a regular season in 1898, and the Spartans count Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil among their alumni. New Mexico's University Stadium opened in 1960, and last season the Lobos went 9-4.

Tessa: Whatever happens, Paloma, supper's on me. We'll say grace first.

Paloma: Deal, Tessa. I'll bring the green chile.

My call: New Mexico Lobos 31, San José State Spartans 15.

South Carolina vs Oklahoma: Norman Moves Halloween to Friday

South Carolina Gamecocks vs Oklahoma Sooners is a Week 9 SEC game in Norman, where the city asked families to go trick-or-treating on Friday, Oct. 30, because the Sooners are home on Halloween for the first time since 2009. Beaumont "Beau" Cheraw, a Gamecock superfan who times everything to dramatic music, says LaNorris Sellers, Matt Fuller and Dylan Stewart will make it three in a row, and Savannah Redbird-Lowe, a former Oklahoma rodeo princess who reads defenses like barrel patterns, says John Mateer, Isaiah Sategna III and Brent Venables' defense will close the gate.

Beau: (hums a space-movie fanfare) Savannah. I've arrived.

Savannah: Boomer, sugar. You hummed that in the parking lot, too.

Beau: Every entrance deserves a score.

Savannah: Then you'll love this one. Norman moved Halloween for us.

The City of Norman recommended trick-or-treating from 7 to 9 p.m. ET Friday, citing game-day traffic and road closures. The last time the Sooners played at home on Halloween, against Kansas State in 2009, the city made the same call. Not everyone is going along. Norman resident Michael Gamboa told the OU Daily his neighborhood will go out on Saturday anyway. "They're always ready for the 31st, not the 30th, not the 29th," he said.

Beau: I respect Mr. Gamboa. That's a man with his own soundtrack.

South Carolina is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC after back-to-back wins over ranked teams, 38-19 at Florida and 27-24 over Tennessee. Against the Vols, Sellers ran for 96 yards and two touchdowns, Stewart forced a fumble in the final minute, and Malik Orsan hit a 48-yard field goal as time expired. Sellers is 133 of 219 for 1,548 yards, 13 touchdowns and five interceptions. Fuller has 513 rushing yards and five touchdowns, Mazeo Bennett Jr. has 31 catches for 324 yards, and Justin Okoronkwo leads the defense with 53 tackles.

Beau: Walk-off field goal, Savannah. I had the music cued. Fans on the field.

Savannah: Darling, I saw. Very cinematic.

Shane Beamer isn't letting his team live in that moment. "We can't let that be the highlight of the season," he said.

Oklahoma is 4-3 and 2-2 in the league after a 23-15 win at Mississippi State. Mateer went 22 of 29 for 283 yards and two touchdowns, and Sategna had eight catches for 164 yards. Mateer is 136 of 204 for 1,591 yards, 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions for the season, and Sategna has 41 catches for 578 yards. Owen Heinecke leads the defense with 53 tackles, and Adepoju Adebawore has four sacks. The Sooners allow 17.7 points a game, and they beat Texas 27-24 earlier this month.

Savannah: That's a tidy barrel pattern, Beau. Seventeen a game.

Venables has seen what Stewart did to Tennessee. "He can wreck a game if you let him," he said.

Beamer, for his part, sounded impressed by the Sooners' defense. "It's a blur when you watch them on tape," he said.

Beau: A blur. That's what my music does to people.

Oklahoma won last year's meeting 26-7.

Savannah: Twenty-six to seven, sugar. I'll hum something for you.

Beau: Please don't. You hum like a gate hinge.

The SEC's initial availability report, posted at 8:10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists five South Carolina players out and two doubtful, and eight Oklahoma players out, one doubtful and four questionable. LaNorris Sellers is not on it.

Beau: What's the plan after the game, Savannah? Candy?

Savannah: Saturday trick-or-treating, Gamboa style. You can carry the music.

Beau: I brought a speaker. It plays "Sandstorm" on loop.

Savannah: In Norman, we have the Pride of Oklahoma. They'll drown you out.

Beau: Let them try.

Savannah: Whatever happens, Beau, the first plate of fried okra is on me.

Beau: Deal. I'll provide the entrance music.

My call: Oklahoma Sooners 26, South Carolina Gamecocks 21.

Purdue vs Penn State: Halloween, All-U Day and a Velveeta Show

Purdue Boilermakers vs Penn State Nittany Lions is a Week 9 Halloween game at Beaver Stadium on All-U Day, with a band called Velveeta playing the Block Party at 10 a.m. ET and a volleyball White Out against Purdue in Rec Hall at 12:30 p.m. ET. Barnaby Wolcott-Reese, a West Lafayette mechanical engineer who built a scale Boilermaker Special in his garage, says Ryan Browne and Fame Ijeboi will keep rolling, and Luann Kessler, a former Penn State volleyball setter who loves Creamery ice cream, says Rocco Becht, Chase Sowell and Tony Rojas end the skid.

Luann: Barnaby, you're early. The Block Party doesn't open until 10 a.m. ET.

Barnaby: I drove my scale Special. It has a top speed of four miles an hour.

Luann: So you left Thursday.

Barnaby: Wednesday. Engineers allow for margin.

There's a lot happening in University Park on Saturday. Penn State women's volleyball hosts Purdue at Rec Hall for its White Out and Senior Day, and the first 1,000 fans who show a mobile football ticket at the doors get in free. The Blue Band marches to the stadium at 3 p.m. ET, and Penn State has played 20 previous games on Halloween. The Nittany Lions are 11-8-1 in them, dating to 1888, and last played on Halloween in 2020 against Ohio State.

Luann: Volleyball first, Barnaby. I'll teach you how to call a ball out.

Barnaby: I'll calculate whether it was actually out.

Luann: That's why nobody sits with you.

Penn State is 3-4 and 0-4 in the Big Ten after losses to Wisconsin, Northwestern, USC and Michigan, the last one 21-18 in Ann Arbor. Becht is 132 of 210 for 1,664 yards, 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Sowell had a career-high 11 catches for 151 yards at Michigan and has 34 catches for 510 yards on the year. Rojas has five sacks and two interceptions, and he has posted double-digit tackles in three games in a row.

Matt Campbell talked about adversity on Tuesday. "How do you not waver and flinch when adversity hits?" he asked.

He also stood by his locker room. "As I continue to say, we have the right people in the locker room," he said.

Luann: That's a coach, Barnaby. Steady hands. Like a good set.

Barnaby: Steady hands are my whole profession.

Purdue is 3-4 and 2-2 in the league, coming off a bye after a 38-26 loss to Washington on Oct. 16. Even in that game, the Boilermakers' defense forced five takeaways. Browne is 145 of 221 for 1,822 yards, 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Ijeboi has 568 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, Asaad Waseem has 38 catches for 588 yards, and Jojo Hayden leads the defense with 48 tackles. Purdue won 24-17 at Illinois and beat Minnesota 41-13 in October.

Barnaby: Five takeaways, Luann. Our defense was a vending machine.

Luann: And you still lost by 12.

Barnaby: The vending machine was out of change.

The series has been one-sided. Penn State leads it 17-3-1 and has won 11 straight against Purdue, dating to 2005. The last meeting was a 49-10 Penn State win in West Lafayette in 2024.

Barnaby: Eleven straight. I've run the numbers. Twelve is unlikely.

Luann: You said that about the cheese band, too.

The Big Ten's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists two Purdue players out and two questionable, and 11 Penn State players out, with Chase Sowell questionable. Rocco Becht is not on it.

Barnaby: I am going to see Velveeta, by the way. Ten a.m. ET. Front row.

Luann: You'll love them. They're smooth.

Barnaby: Everything at Penn State is smooth. The ice cream, the cheese band, the setter.

Luann: Flattery won't help you on Saturday. But I'll buy the Creamery cones after.

Barnaby: Deal. I'll drive us there in the Special.

Luann: We'll walk. We'd like to get there tonight.

My call: Penn State Nittany Lions 34, Purdue Boilermakers 23.
