Nevada vs UCLA: Snowboards, Storyboards and a Rose Bowl Debut

Nevada Wolf Pack vs UCLA Bruins is a Week 9 Halloween afternoon at the Rose Bowl, where Nevada makes its first trip to Pasadena and UCLA students get in free and get Halloween candy on Bruin Family Weekend. Ridge Corbell, a Tahoe ski patroller and snowboarder whose motto is "Send It," says Dominic Kelley, EJ Smith and Ky Woods can make it a game, and Kenzie Rhee, a Westwood film-school producer who storyboards every drive, says Wayne Knight and Sammy Omosigho keep No. 7 UCLA unbeaten.

Kenzie: I've storyboarded your whole afternoon, Ridge. Panel one: you see the San Gabriel Mountains and forget to watch the kickoff.

Ridge: Panel two: I ask why there's no snow on them.

Kenzie: Panel three: I explain Southern California.

This is only the second meeting between these teams. The first was the 2013 season opener at the Rose Bowl, and UCLA won 58-20. Nevada trailed just 17-13 at halftime before UCLA scored 20 points in the third quarter, with a blocked punt returned for a touchdown. The Bruins' quarterback that day was Brett Hundley, and he's on the Big Ten Network call Saturday as the analyst.

Ridge: So the guy who beat us is calling the game.

Kenzie: He'll be fair. Mostly.

UCLA is 7-0 and 5-0 in the Big Ten, its first such marks since 2005. Bob Chesney, who came over from James Madison, is the first coach in UCLA history to open his tenure 7-0. Knight has 627 rushing yards and 12 rushing touchdowns, and he has run for a score in all seven games. Anthony Woods has added 459 yards and six touchdowns. Omosigho has 5.5 sacks and leads the country with five forced fumbles. Last week, Ty Dieffenbach threw a 63-yard touchdown to Brian Rowe Jr. to open the second half of a 28-10 win over Michigan State.

Kenzie: That's the best shot of the year. Wide angle, the ball in the air, Rowe running under it.

Ridge: You'd frame a punt if it had nice light.

Nevada is 3-4 and 2-2 in the Mountain West after a 28-13 win over San José State. Jeff Choate's roster has 17 Northern Nevada products, and Reno's Marshaun Brown caught a touchdown and threw one in that game. Kelley has 582 rushing yards and five touchdowns. Smith has 76 tackles, fifth in the country. Ky Woods returned a kickoff 90 yards against San José State and was tackled eight yards short of the end zone.

Ridge: Eight yards from the end zone. That's the difference between a tidy run and eating snow.

Kenzie: I'd have cut away before the tackle. Better ending.

The Wolf Pack defense is the reason Ridge drove south. Nevada allows 153.9 passing yards a game, sixth in the country, and only Western Kentucky has thrown for 200 yards against it. UCLA runs for 233.0 yards a game, though, and allows 15.3 points.

Ridge: We stop the throws, you run it. Fine. We'll sit in the snow and wait.

Kenzie: There's no snow, Ridge.

Ridge: I brought my own. It's in the cooler.

Kenzie: That's ice for the drinks.

Kenzie: Halftime is a dance performance and the UCLA Marching Band. Please don't try to join either one.

Ridge: I make no promises. Send it.

Kenzie: I'm storyboarding security walking you back to your seat.

Ridge: Make it a good shot. Slow motion.

Kenzie: Deal. Whatever happens, Ridge, a costume from the gift shop is on me.

Ridge: I'm already wearing one. Ski patrol.

Kenzie: That's your work jacket.

My call: UCLA Bruins 34, Nevada Wolf Pack 14.

Zeb Coldiron whittles on a Watauga County porch and calls every drive a hike. Royce Ogeechee grew up in Bulloch County hearing his granddad tell stories about the old Eagles dynasty. On Halloween night in Statesboro, these old rivals meet for the forty-second time, and the East Division is on the table.

App State (5-2) at Georgia Southern (3-4), Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+ at Allen E. Paulson Stadium in Statesboro. It's a Sun Belt game. DraftKings has Georgia Southern Eagles −5.5 with a total of 56.5. Action Network opened Georgia Southern −3.5 with a total of 54.5. My card: Georgia Southern Eagles −5.5, Under 56.5, and a final of Georgia Southern Eagles 29, App State Mountaineers 23.

Royce speaks for Georgia Southern. "Hail Southern! Max Johnson hurt his throwing shoulder at Old Dominion, and he's questionable. Clay Helton says the rehab progressed pretty fast, and Johnson walked out there and spun it. Turner Helton went 23 of 30 in relief, and we won 23-15. Anthony Bynum was Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week. And we've had sixteen days to rest up."

Zeb speaks for App State. "Come on up the mountain. Malachi Singleton went 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns in our overtime win over James Madison. Jaquari Lewis has 8 rushing touchdowns, and Caleb Sandstrom has 5 sacks. But steady footing matters. We scored three points against Old Dominion."

Here is the part that matters. Both teams are 2-1 in the league, tied for second in the East. Georgia Southern gives up 23.0 points a game, and App State gives up 23.1. Neither run game has found much room.

Why Georgia Southern? Follow The Money likes the Eagles after a two-point move, from −3.5 to −5.5. Next Man Up has Georgia Southern 30-22. Clay Helton is four and one against App State, and the Eagles lead the series in Statesboro thirteen to six. They're also unbeaten on Halloween.

display.fanatic_story:
Halloween Rivalry Night: App State Visits Georgia Southern

App State (5-2, 2-1 Sun Belt) at Georgia Southern (3-4, 2-1 Sun Belt). Saturday, Oct. 31, 6:30 p.m. ET, Allen E. Paulson Stadium, Statesboro, Georgia, ESPN+.

Your hosts are Zeb Coldiron, a fourth-generation Watauga County whittler who treats every week like a hike, and Royce Ogeechee, a Bulloch County farm kid who grew up hearing about the Eagles' dynasty years from his granddad.

Zeb: Come on down off the mountain, Royce. I brought a jacket for your grandma.

Royce: Hail Southern, Zeb! She says thank you, and she says the Eagles are 4-0 on Halloween.

Players to watch

App State quarterback Malachi Singleton has completed 139 of 209 throws for 1,700 yards, with nine touchdowns and just two interceptions. Running back Jaquari Lewis has 420 yards and eight touchdowns, and wide receiver Sam Pickett III has 32 catches for 474 yards. Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks, and linebacker Colton Phares leads with 51 tackles.

Georgia Southern quarterback Max Johnson has thrown for 1,601 yards, with 11 touchdowns and only two interceptions. Wide receiver Alex Taylor has 24 catches for 342 yards. Linebacker Anthony Bynum has four sacks, and linebacker Brandon Tyson has 38 tackles.

Zeb: Two interceptions each. Those are careful young men.

What happened last week

App State beat James Madison 34-31 in overtime. Singleton went 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns, and Nate Branch caught six balls for 73 yards.

Georgia Southern had a bye. In its last game, on Oct. 15, the Eagles won 23-15 at Old Dominion. Turner Helton came in for Johnson and went 23 of 30 for 206 yards and a touchdown. Bynum had three tackles for loss, two sacks and a forced fumble, and he was named Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Week.

Royce: That's a farm-strong day's work from Anthony.

Injuries and availability

No official Sun Belt availability report had been posted as of Tuesday. Johnson hurt his throwing shoulder at Old Dominion and is listed as questionable. "It's really progressed pretty fast, to be honest with you," Clay Helton said. "He walked out there and spun it." For App State, Singleton played through an ankle issue against James Madison.

Zeb: Praying both quarterbacks are healthy. A rivalry deserves its best.

What the coaches are up to

Clay Helton, who led USC to a Rose Bowl title, is 4-1 against App State. His son, Turner, is the backup quarterback who won the Old Dominion game. Georgia Southern has had 16 days to rest and get healthy.

Dowell Loggains is in his second season in Boone. He came from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator, and before that he called plays in the NFL for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets.

Player storylines

Here's a fun one. Johnson's father, Brad, and App State backup Henry Hasselbeck's father, Matt, both played in the NFL, and they played in two games against each other, in 2004 and 2006.

Georgia Southern lineman Colin Alexander said a win over App State would make the team "really, really confident" about reaching the conference championship.

Royce: That's the goal, Zeb. A conference title game.

What's happening on campus

Allen E. Paulson Stadium opened in 1984 and holds 25,000. Ask anybody about Beautiful Eagle Creek, and the Southern Pride Marching Band will be in full voice.

App State won three straight FCS national championships from 2005 to 2007. Home in Boone is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team outscored its opponents 206-0 in the regular season. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do it.

Zeb: Three straight titles, Royce. That's a mountain worth the climb.

Anything else fun and true

This is the 42nd meeting. App State leads the series 21-19-1, but Georgia Southern leads 13-6 in Statesboro. The teams have played every year since 1993, and these two programs are tied for second in the East Division.

Zeb: Steady climbing, honest footing, Royce. Then a view at the top.

Royce: Hail Southern, Zeb. The creek is calling.

My call: Georgia Southern Eagles 29, App State Mountaineers 23.

Oklahoma State vs Iowa State: All Orange Meets All Black in Ames

Oklahoma State Cowboys vs Iowa State Cyclones is a Week 9 Halloween night at Jack Trice Stadium, where Iowa State wears all black and asks fans to "Pack The Jack, Wear Black" while No. 24 Oklahoma State comes in all orange. Dusty Lockridge, an Oklahoma State ag-econ grad who explains offense with rodeo timing, says Drew Mestemaker, Wyatt Young and Ethan Wesloski keep rolling, and Twyla Hemmingsen, an Iowa State fan who forecasts every Saturday from her kitchen weather center, says Aiden Flora, Sullivan Schlimgen and Kyle Konrardy send a front through.

Twyla: Forecast for Ames, Saturday night: 61,500 people dressed in black, with a chance of noise.

Dusty: And one section of orange. We'll look like a jack-o'-lantern.

Twyla: A jack-o'-lantern that's about to get carved.

Dusty: Easy, Twyla. It's a holiday.

This is the 60th meeting, and the 31st in Ames. Oklahoma State leads the series 34-22-3, but Iowa State has won the last two meetings at Jack Trice and won 20-13 in Stillwater in last season's finale, when the Cyclones ran for 233 yards to Oklahoma State's 27. Iowa State has beaten a ranked team at home in five of the last nine seasons, and Cyclone fans still talk about 2011, when Iowa State beat the No. 2 Cowboys 37-31 in double overtime in Ames.

Dusty: You had to bring up 2011.

Twyla: My kitchen weather center has a framed photo of it. Next to the barometer.

Oklahoma State is 5-2 and 3-1 in the Big 12 under first-year coach Eric Morris, who brought in 91 new players. The Cowboys have scored 30 or more in six games in a row and beat Colorado 57-24 last week, when Mestemaker threw for 386 yards and four touchdowns. He has 2,326 yards, 20 touchdowns and six interceptions this season, and he has thrown for 300 yards in six games in a row. Young has 36 catches for 639 yards, Justin Bowick has 34 for 607, Caleb Hawkins has 712 rushing yards, and Wesloski has 70 tackles.

Dusty: Rodeo timing, Twyla. Mestemaker gets the snap, counts two, and the ball's gone. Eight seconds is a long ride for a defense.

Twyla: Eight seconds is about how long your Cowboys lasted at Tulsa.

Dusty: That was the opener. We've won five of six since.

Iowa State is 3-4 and 1-3 in the league under Jimmy Rogers, and this is its third ranked opponent in a row. Last week was rough, a 39-3 loss at Arizona. Flora has 716 rushing yards and six touchdowns, and he's the only player in the country this season with a rushing touchdown, a throwing touchdown and a punt return touchdown. Schlimgen leads the Big 12 with 10.1 tackles a game and made 15 at Arizona. Konrardy has hit 20 field goals in a row from 45 yards and in, and his career best is 63.

Twyla: Sixty-three yards, Dusty. You could hang laundry on that kick.

Dusty: In Ames in October, it'd freeze in midair before it dried.

Twyla: That's why we use the dryer.

The Big 12's initial availability report, posted at 10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists one Oklahoma State player out and three questionable, and three Iowa State players out, with quarterback Connor Moberly questionable.

Twyla: Costumes are welcome, but masks aren't allowed. So no hiding when the second half goes sideways.

Dusty: I'm coming as a rodeo clown. Face paint only.

Twyla: Fitting. You'll be the one running from the bull.

Dusty: Whatever happens, Twyla, your hot cocoa is on me, and I'll leave that barometer alone.

Twyla: Then you're wearing black to Stillwater next year.

Dusty: Let's not get crazy. Charcoal, maybe.

My call: Oklahoma State Cowboys 30, Iowa State Cyclones 27.

Clemson vs Florida State: Drones, Dabo and a 130th Birthday

Clemson Tigers vs Florida State Seminoles is a Week 9 Halloween night at Doak Campbell Stadium, where Florida State debuts its first-ever drone show, and Clemson plays on the 130th anniversary of its first game, a 14-6 win over Furman on Oct. 31, 1896. Dixie-Lynn Pruitt, a former Tiger Band flag captain who owns 43 orange items, says Tait Reynolds, Gideon Davidson and Will Heldt bring the Tigers home happy, and Gianna Ravello, a Tallahassee lobbyist type who reads football news like legislation, says Ashton Daniels, Duce Robinson and Rylan Kennedy carry it on a voice vote.

Gianna: Dixie-Lynn, I've read the whole game day release. Three times. With a highlighter.

Dixie-Lynn: I've read none of it. I'm wearing all 43 orange items.

Gianna: All of them?

Dixie-Lynn: The socks count as two.

Florida State calls the day Operation Garnet Storm. Trunk or Treat opens on Langford Green at 3 p.m. ET, the game ball arrives by parachute with the USSOCOM Para-Commandos, and concession stands will have candy for fans in costume. Peter Warrick gets the National Football Foundation On-Campus Salute in the first quarter before his College Football Hall of Fame induction. At halftime, the Marching Chiefs lead into Garnet Hour, with the drone show and a synchronized light show.

"Operation Garnet Storm is a comprehensive campaign to provide our fans a one-of-a-kind experience in Doak Campbell Stadium," interim director of athletics Bruce Warwick said.

Gianna: Section one, subsection drone show. I've already filed my approval.

Dixie-Lynn: I'll be watching the drones for orange ones.

There's history on the Clemson side, too. Dabo Swinney is 116-30 in ACC regular-season play, and a win would give him 117 and tie Bobby Bowden's conference mark, on the field named for Bowden. Clemson has won its last four games in Tallahassee, including 29-13 in 2024, when Swinney passed Bowden for the most overall wins as an ACC head coach.

Gianna: Tie Bowden. At Bobby Bowden Field. That's bad manners, Dixie-Lynn.

Dixie-Lynn: That's a history lesson, sugar.

Clemson is 4-3 and 2-2 in the ACC, coming off a 20-16 home loss to Virginia Tech. Reynolds has completed 120 of 180 throws for 1,096 yards, and he ran for a touchdown against the Hokies. Davidson has 492 rushing yards and five touchdowns, Bryant Wesco Jr. has 34 catches for 378 yards, and Heldt has six sacks. Corey Myrick leads the Tigers with 53 tackles.

Dixie-Lynn: Heldt's going to visit your quarterback so often, he'll need a guest room.

Gianna: Noted for the record. Objection also noted.

Florida State is 3-4 and 1-3 in the league and had last week off after a 43-35 overtime loss at Miami. Daniels threw for 298 yards and four touchdowns in that game and has 1,618 yards, 12 touchdowns and eight interceptions on the year. Robinson caught five balls for 113 yards and two scores at Miami and has 407 receiving yards. Kennedy has six sacks, and Chris Jones has 46 tackles. Earlier this month, Florida State scored the final 38 points in a 38-7 win over Virginia.

Gianna: Thirty-eight unanswered. I'd like that entered into the minutes.

Dixie-Lynn: Enter this: you lost to SMU at home.

Gianna: Tabled.

The ACC's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists seven Clemson players out and one questionable, and nine Florida State players out, with quarterback Malachi Marshall probable.

Dixie-Lynn: I'm coming as a Tiger. I'm always coming as a Tiger.

Gianna: I'm coming as the drone show. I've got a light-up headband.

Dixie-Lynn: If the Seminoles win, I'll wear one garnet item. Small. Maybe a hair tie.

Gianna: If Clemson wins, I'll draft you a resolution honoring Furman, 1896.

Dixie-Lynn: Make it a joint resolution. Furman deserves it.

Cougars and Aztecs Meet Under the San Diego Lights

Washington State (1-7, 0-4 Pac-12) at San Diego State (3-5, 2-2 Pac-12). Saturday, Oct. 31, 7:00 p.m. ET, Snapdragon Stadium, San Diego, CBSSN.

Your hosts are Hank Palouse, a Washington State fan who drives a combine and keeps a shoebox of game tapes in the cab, and Kai Delgado-Sorensen, a San Diego State fan who surfs Ocean Beach most mornings.

Kai: Welcome to sunshine, Hank. You can leave the combine at home.

Hank: Brought the shoebox, though. Cougs never quit.

Players to watch

Washington State quarterback Owen Eshelman has started the last two games. Caden Pinnick, who started the first six, has thrown for 952 yards. Wide receiver Branden Ganashamoorthy leads the team with 30 catches for 401 yards and three touchdowns, and Kirby Vorhees has 275 rushing yards. On defense, linebacker Keith Brown has 60 tackles, and defensive tackle Jirah Leaupepetele has 2.5 sacks.

San Diego State quarterback Stone Saunders, a redshirt freshman and Kentucky transfer, gets his second straight start. Running back Javion Kinnard leads the team with 526 rushing yards. Wide receiver Jaylon Hawkins has 322 receiving yards and three touchdowns. Linebacker Sione Hala has 83 tackles, and linebacker Djibril Rahman has 3.5 sacks.

Kai: Hala's in on every play. That's a surfer who never gets out of the water.

What happened last week

Washington State lost 31-10 at home to Boise State. Eshelman completed 21 throws for 191 yards and ran the ball 23 times. Ganashamoorthy and Daniel Blood played all 76 snaps on offense.

San Diego State lost 56-49 at Colorado State in a wild one. The 105 combined points were the most in a game in San Diego State's Division I history. Saunders went 23 of 33 for 369 yards and two touchdowns in his first college start. Hawkins caught six balls for a career-high 164 yards and scored a touchdown for the fifth straight game. Lucky Sutton ran for 98 yards and two scores, and Kinnard added two more on just 10 carries.

Hank: One hundred sixty-four yards for Hawkins. That one's going in the shoebox, even if he's not ours.

Injuries and availability

The Pac-12's advance availability report, updated at 10:03 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists one Washington State player out for the season and two questionable, and six San Diego State players out, one doubtful and seven questionable. Coach Kirby Moore said wide receiver Darrius Clemons (ankle) and safety Jeremiah Bernard (shoulder) are day-to-day and set to return to practice this week. For San Diego State, Jayden Denegal remains day-to-day.

What the coaches are up to

Moore is in his first season at Washington State. He wants sharper practices this week. "We talk about deliberate practice," he said. "That really starts with bringing great energy, having verbal combat, doing your assignment, making sure you're not thinking out there, that you're just reacting."

Sean Lewis is in his third season at San Diego State. He named Saunders the starter on Monday. "Stone will start this week," Lewis said. "So, he'll get the bulk of the one reps as we go forward."

Kai: Clear call from the coach. Gnarly.

Player storylines

Saunders came into his first start with just 15 career throws. His 369 yards were the most ever by an Aztec quarterback making his first start on the road, going back to 1969. He also became the first Aztec to throw for 300 yards since Jalen Mayden in the 2022 Hawai'i Bowl.

Ganashamoorthy has played 503 snaps this season, the most of any wide receiver in the Pac-12. Washington State's only win so far came 48-7 over Duquesne, and the Cougars lost 17-16 at Utah State. They're looking for their first win over an FBS team.

Hank: One-point loss. I've watched it twice. Still hurts.

What's happening on campus

Snapdragon Stadium opened in 2022 and seats 35,000. San Diego State began playing football in 1921 and has won 21 conference championships.

Washington State is in Pullman, where the first Cougar team took the field in 1894. Home is Martin Stadium, which opened in 1972 on ground that dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field.

Anything else fun and true

The Aztecs went 9-4 last year and are trying to get to a bowl game for a second straight season. They have won two close home games this year, 31-29 over Texas State and 26-23 over Fresno State.

Hank: Ganashamoorthy, five hundred and three snaps. That young man has earned a nap.

Kai: Bring him to the beach after, Hank. Respect.

My call: San Diego State Aztecs 27, Washington State Cougars 25.

display.fanatic_story:
Mississippi State vs Texas: Cowbells, Kracker and a Halloween Night

Mississippi State Bulldogs vs Texas Longhorns is a Week 9 Halloween night at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, where Uncle Kracker plays the LBJ Lawn before kickoff and a sold-out crowd fills the stadium for a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff. Wade Pettus, a poultry-science grad who sketches Mississippi State plays on feed-store receipts, says Fluff Bothwell, Anthony Evans III and Parker Puckett can ring the cowbell in Austin, and Caro Whitfield, a former rodeo queen who prices every Longhorn like a blue-chip stock, says Arch Manning, Raleek Brown and Ryan Wingo will send the Bulldogs home quietly.

Caro: Welcome to Austin, darling. Hook 'em.

Wade: Thank you, ma'am. I'll ring once for you. Politely. (ding.)

Caro: Once is plenty. We have a concert going.

Longhorn City Limits runs a Halloween edition on the LBJ Lawn. The Tito's Tailgate and Bulleit Frontier Lounge open at 3 p.m. ET, Julianna Rankin takes the stage at 4 p.m. ET, and Uncle Kracker is scheduled for about 5:30 p.m. ET. Admission is free, and Pinkerton's BBQ is on site.

"Halloween night at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium is going to be something special," athletics director Chris Del Conte said.

Wade: I'll be singing "Drift Away" while the Bulldogs do the opposite.

Caro: Darling, that song spent 28 weeks at No. 1 on the adult contemporary chart. Your Bulldogs have not.

There's some old history here. Texas leads the all-time series 4-2, and the first meeting was in Austin in 1921, a 54-7 Texas win. Mississippi State's last win in the series came in Austin, too, 28-10 in 1992. Texas has won the last three meetings, 38-11 in Dallas on Jan. 1, 1999, 35-13 in Austin in 2024 and 45-38 in overtime in Mississippi last season. That one had 83 combined points, the most in the series.

Wade: Thirty-four years since we won here. I've been saving receipts that long.

Caro: You've been saving receipts since the first Bush administration, darling.

One fun note from the Mississippi State notes: the Bulldogs are one of four SEC programs that have used the same five men up front on offense in every game this season, and Texas is one of the other three. Nobody on either front has needed a name tag all year.

Wade: Same five boys, every week. Like a church choir with shoulder pads.

Caro: Our five sing better.

Mississippi State is 4-3 and 2-3 in the SEC, and it lost 23-15 to Oklahoma at home last week. Puckett went 17 of 24 for 158 yards and a touchdown, Bothwell ran 17 times for 111 yards, and Sanfrisco Magee caught three balls for 65 yards and a touchdown. Evans leads the team with 53 catches for 647 yards and five touchdowns, and Bothwell has 514 rushing yards. On defense, Tyler Lockhart has 48 tackles and Jaray Bledsoe has 2.5 sacks. The Bulldogs opened 4-0, with wins over UL Monroe, at Minnesota, at South Carolina and over Missouri. The notes also credit tight end Sam West with a touchdown throw to Camden Capehart on a trick play against Oklahoma.

Wade: A tight end throwing touchdowns. That's my kind of receipt.

Caro: That's a one-time dividend, sugar.

Texas is 5-2 and 2-2 in the league, and it beat Ole Miss 34-27 last week. Brown ran 23 times for 157 yards, Ryan Wingo caught seven balls for 111 yards and a touchdown, and Manning threw for 212 yards. Manning has 1,507 passing yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions on the season. Wingo has 33 catches for 456 yards and four touchdowns, Simmons has 10.5 sacks, and Jelani McDonald has 54 tackles. The Longhorns beat Ohio State 24-23 and won 20-17 at Tennessee, and they lost 27-24 to Oklahoma and Florida.

Caro: Ten and a half sacks. Darling, that is a premium asset.

Wade: My cowbell has a premium too. It's just louder.

Mississippi State said Tuesday that quarterback Kamario Taylor will miss the rest of the season with a foot injury that requires surgery, and the SEC's initial availability report, posted at 8:10 p.m. ET Wednesday, lists him out. It lists Colin Simmons questionable for Texas, and Arch Manning is not on it.

Wade: I'm coming as a cowbell. Big one. Painted maroon.

Caro: I'm coming as a rodeo queen, which is to say I'm coming as myself.

Wade: Whatever happens, Caro, dinner's on me, and you ring my cowbell on Speedway.

Caro: Then you learn the words to "The Eyes of Texas" and sing them nicely.

Wade: Deal. I'll write them on a receipt.

Caro: Keep the receipt, darling. Receipts are good business.

My call: Texas Longhorns 35, Mississippi State Bulldogs 19.

display.fanatic_story:
Georgia Tech vs Pitt: Hail to Heroes on Halloween Night

Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets vs Pittsburgh Panthers is a Week 9 Halloween night on the North Shore, where Acrisure Stadium hosts Hail to Heroes for military members, veterans and first responders, and theme-ticket fans get a knit camo beanie. Wendell Quist, a Georgia Tech aerospace engineer who charts the flight of every punt, says Alberto Mendoza, Justice Haynes and Jordan Allen can quiet the place, and Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci, a steel-town fan who grades every tackle from "yinz" to "yikes" with a homemade whistle, says Holden Geriner, Cataurus Hicks and Damon Ferguson Jr. will keep the Panthers home happy.

Yinz: How's it goin', n'at? Welcome to Pittsburgh, Wendell.

Wendell: Thank you, Yinz. I brought my calculator, a warm coat and a pumpkin with a slide rule carved in it.

Yinz: A slide rule. On Halloween. You're a scary man, Wendell.

Saturday is the Aldrich Foundation Hail to Heroes game, sponsored by GBU Life and the Aldrich Foundation, with on-field and in-game recognitions for those who serve. Pitt calls it "one of the most meaningful days on the home schedule each season." Kickoff is 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2, and 93.7 The Fan has the radio call.

Wendell: I'll take the beanie. It's going to be cold on the river.

Yinz: The beanie's camo, Wendell. You'll finally blend in with a crowd.

This is an old series. Pitt and Georgia Tech meet for the 19th time in a series that dates to 1918, and the Panthers lead it 12-6. Pitt is 5-2 against Georgia Tech in Pittsburgh and has won five of the last six meetings. Last season Pitt won 42-28 in Atlanta over a Georgia Tech team ranked No. 15 at the time. The Jackets won the 2022 meeting 26-21.

Wendell: I have the 2022 game laminated.

Yinz: I have the 2025 game tattooed. Kidding. It's a sticker.

Georgia Tech is 2-5 and 1-3 in the ACC. Mendoza is 153 of 215 for 1,714 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he threw for 335 yards at Virginia Tech two weeks ago. Haynes has 515 rushing yards and four touchdowns, and Allen leads the team with 42 catches for 517 yards. On defense, safety Tae Harris has 45 tackles, and Noah Carter has three sacks. The Jackets' best win this season was 28-25 over Duke. Last week they lost 49-27 at home to Boston College, which ran for 399 yards, though Dalen Penson had a career day with five catches for 88 yards and a touchdown.

Coach Brent Key took it on himself. "It's on coaching, so that's on me. I'll take full responsibility," he said.

Wendell: That's a coach who checks his own math.

Yinz: Respect, Wendell. That's a yinz answer.

Pitt is 5-3 and 2-3 in the league. The Panthers opened 5-0, with home wins over Miami (Ohio), UCF, Syracuse and Bucknell and a 35-33 win at Virginia Tech, and then lost to North Carolina, at Boston College and at Miami. Geriner went 18 of 32 for 268 yards and a touchdown in the 52-23 loss at Miami, and Hicks caught five balls for 149 yards and a score there. Hicks has 31 catches for 649 yards and five touchdowns on the season. Ferguson, a freshman, has 477 rushing yards and four touchdowns. Cruce Brookins leads the defense with 55 tackles, and Jaeden Moore has 4.5 sacks.

Pat Narduzzi has been sure about this group all fall. "We have a team that can win an ACC championship with Mason or without Mason," he said.

Yinz: Brookins with 55 tackles. That's a whole lotta yinz.

Wendell: My chart says Hicks has a very long flight path. I don't love that chart.

The ACC's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists 16 Georgia Tech players out, Noah Carter among them. Pitt lists nine players out, including quarterback Mason Heintschel, and Damon Ferguson Jr. questionable.

Wendell: I'm coming as a punt. A high one. With hang time.

Yinz: I'm coming as a Terrible Towel. Same as every year.

Wendell: Whatever happens, Yinz, dinner's on me, and you say "y'all" on the jumbotron.

Yinz: Then you say "n'at" at your next engineering meeting.

Wendell: Deal. I'll put it in the minutes.

My call: Pittsburgh Panthers 36, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 21.

display.fanatic_story:
Miami vs North Carolina: Neon Trees and No. 1 in Chapel Hill

Miami Hurricanes vs North Carolina Tar Heels is a Week 9 Halloween night at Kenan Stadium, where Neon Trees plays Chapel Thrill Game Day on Polk Place and Carolina hosts the nation's No. 1 team for the sixth time ever. Javi "The Breeze" Castillo, a former Miami defensive back who scouts in a white suit and sunglasses, says Darian Mensah, Malachi Toney and Javian Mallory keep the Canes rolling, and Ainsley Pemberton, a North Carolina fan, former debutante and kinesiology PhD, says Billy Edwards Jr., Jordan Shipp and Xavier Lewis can make it a long night for the visitors.

Javi: It's all about the U, baby! Number one in the sun, Canes get it done!

Ainsley: Welcome to Chapel Hill, darling. Do you need a sweater?

Javi: It's Halloween, Ainsley. I'm dressed as a guy who doesn't need a sweater.

Chapel Thrill opens three hours before kickoff in front of Wilson Library, and about two and a half hours before kickoff the Tar Heels take the Old Well Walk through Polk Place and around the Bell Tower to Kenan. Neon Trees broke out in 2010 with "Animal," which reached No. 1 on the Billboard Alternative charts. It's also Rams Club Day, and this is Carolina's 100th season in Kenan Stadium, which opened in 1927 and seats 50,500.

Ainsley: I'll be singing "Animal" on Polk Place, darling. With manners.

Javi: I'll be singing it too. About Toney.

The last No. 1 team to visit Kenan was Clemson in 2019. The recent history here belongs to Carolina, which has won the last five meetings with Miami, including three at Kenan. The 2023 game was a 41-31 Tar Heels win, and the 2021 game was 45-42. Carolina won 62-26 in 2020.

Javi: Five straight. Ainsley, I'm not here to talk about history. I'm here to make some.

Ainsley: Bless your heart, darling. History is very patient.

Miami is 7-0 and 5-0 in the ACC and has scored at least 33 points in every game, including 77 against Florida A&M. Mensah has completed 166 of 204 throws for 2,151 yards, 22 touchdowns and one interception. Toney has 66 catches for 952 yards and 11 touchdowns, Mallory has 444 yards and seven touchdowns on 59 carries, Marquise Lightfoot has five sacks and Mohamed Toure has 35 tackles. Last week the Canes beat Pittsburgh 52-23, with Mensah going 31 of 37 for 387 yards and four touchdowns and Toney catching 16 balls for 194 yards and three scores. They also won 41-13 at Clemson and 43-35 in overtime against Florida State.

Bill Belichick spent Monday praising the other team's receiver. "At his age, that's pretty impressive. I don't see any weak points in his game," he said of Toney.

Javi: When Coach Belichick says that, you frame it, hermano.

North Carolina is 4-3 and 2-2 in the league. Edwards has thrown for 1,531 yards, 11 touchdowns and five interceptions, Shipp has 41 catches for 543 yards and Benjamin Hall has 283 rushing yards. Lewis has seven sacks and Derek McDonald has 71 tackles. Carolina lost 31-30 in overtime to Syracuse last week, when Edwards opened with 11 straight completions and McDonald, facing his old school, made a career-high 16 tackles. The Tar Heels won at Pittsburgh, 21-17, and at Duke, 24-20.

Shipp knows what has to change. "We need to turn those field goals into touchdowns," he said.

Ainsley: Sixteen tackles against his old school, darling. That's good manners and good football.

Javi: Good manners. I'll put that on a T-shirt and sell it in Coral Gables.

The ACC's initial availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists six Miami players out, and five North Carolina players out and five questionable.

Javi: I'm coming as a sunbeam. Orange and green.

Ainsley: I'm coming as Carolina blue, darling. It's not a costume. It's a lifestyle.

Javi: Whatever happens, Ainsley, the cafecito is on me, and you say "It's all about the U."

Ainsley: Then you wear the sweater on Franklin Street.

Javi: Deal. But the sunglasses stay on.

My call: Miami Hurricanes 35, North Carolina Tar Heels 20.

It's Halloween night and Trojan Family Weekend at a sold-out Coliseum, the Buckeyes and Trojans meet for the first time as Big Ten opponents, and USC is seven and six all-time on Halloween.

Ohio State's defense is the reason. The Buckeyes allow 13.4 points a game and score 39.3, and their only loss was 24-23 at Texas. After the 1979 season, Charles White scored on a 1-yard run with 1:32 left, and USC won 17-16. The 1973 Rose Bowl between them drew 106,869 fans. This is the first meeting since 2017, and the first as Big Ten opponents. USC has eight Heisman Trophy winners and Ohio State has seven.

Buck: Seven Heismans. I'll run a celebration route in the hallway.

Sterling: Eight, Buck. Roll the credits slowly.

Ryan Day had kind words for the other sideline. He called Lincoln Riley a "tremendous mind and a really good coach."

Sterling: That's a quote for the poster, Buck.

Last week they lost 24-7 at Wisconsin, where Maiava completed 31 throws for 258 yards and found Taniela Tupou for the only touchdown.

Buck: Nine hundred eighty-four yards for Smith. That's a box office number, Sterling. Even you have to say it.

Sterling: Box office, yes. But the sequel is in our building.

Buck: I'm coming as Brutus Buckeye. Big head, big smile.

Sterling: I'm coming as a director. Beret, megaphone, folding chair with my name on it.

Buck: Whatever happens, Sterling, dinner's on me, and you narrate my hallway routes in the trailer voice.

Sterling: Then you run one lap around Tommy Trojan and say "Fight On."

Buck: Deal. I'll run it as a post route.

My call: Ohio State Buckeyes 34, USC Trojans 23.

Missouri vs Arkansas: Homecoming Hogs Host a Halloween Night Visit

Missouri Tigers vs Arkansas Razorbacks is a Week 9 Halloween night at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, the last stop of the University of Arkansas' 105th annual Homecoming Week, with kickoff at 7:45 p.m. ET on SEC Network. Delphine Arceneaux-Moss, a Missouri journalism-school style reporter who breaks obvious news with a fake ticker sound, says Jamal Roberts, Austin Simmons and Daeden Hopkins keep the trophy in Columbia, and Bubba Fayette-Dorsey, an Ozark grade-school science teacher who calls the Hogs before every stat, says KJ Jackson, Chris Marshall and Quincy Rhodes Jr. bring it home.

Delphine: Ding-ding-ding! Breaking news, Bubba: it is Halloween.

Bubba: Woooo, Pig! Breaking news back at you. It's our Homecoming.

Delphine: Ding-ding! Also breaking: water is wet.

Arkansas is throwing a party. The school calls Razorback Stadium "the biggest trick-or-treat location in the State of Arkansas" for this one. Fans of all ages can trick-or-treat from the tailgate lots to inside the stadium, the first 300 kids in costume get a free hot dog and drink, and a Halloween laser show takes over halftime. The Hog Walk is at 5:15 p.m. ET, gates open at 6:15 p.m. ET, and the Trick-or-Treat Trailgating Parade rolls from the Upper Ramble to Maple Street at 6:45 p.m. ET. Friday night, the stadium gets a red glow. It's the first time since 2015 that the Hogs have played in Fayetteville on Halloween.

Bubba: Free hot dogs for the first 300 kids. I'm going as a kid.

Delphine: Ding! Breaking news: you are a grown man, Bubba.

Bubba: Science says I'm young at heart. Woooo, Pig!

The history belongs mostly to Missouri. The Tigers lead the series 13-4, this is the 18th meeting and the sixth in Fayetteville, and it's the first night game between these teams in Arkansas. Missouri has won the last four, including 31-17 last year. Arkansas last won 34-17 on Nov. 26, 2021. The games keep getting tight, though: 28-24 in 2016, 48-45 in 2017, 50-48 in 2020, 29-27 in 2022 and 28-21 in 2024.

Missouri is 5-2 and 2-2 in the SEC. Roberts leads the SEC in rushing with 867 yards and eight touchdowns on 167 carries. Simmons, an Ole Miss transfer, has thrown for 1,773 yards, 14 touchdowns and two interceptions. Cayden Lee has 47 catches for 678 yards, Hopkins has seven sacks and Nicholas Rodriguez has 76 tackles. The Tigers beat Florida 45-17 and Texas A&M 27-6 at home, then lost 31-3 at Ole Miss on Oct. 17, when Simmons threw for 339 yards and Donovan Olugbode caught nine balls for 127. Simmons keeps it calm: "It's just another game for me."

Delphine: Ding-ding! Eight hundred sixty-seven yards. That's a headline, Bubba.

Arkansas is 3-4 and 1-3 in the league. Jackson, from Montgomery, Ala., has completed 131 of 215 throws for 1,444 yards and seven touchdowns, and he leads the team with three rushing touchdowns. Marshall has 43 catches for 633 yards, second in the SEC in both. Rhodes, a North Little Rock native, leads the defense with 5.5 tackles for loss and three sacks, and Ja'Quavion Smith has 48 tackles. The Hogs won 31-21 at Vanderbilt on Oct. 17, their first SEC win in two years, when Jackson ran for a touchdown and Warren native Antonio Jordan had career highs with five catches for 74 yards.

Bubba: Five catches for a Warren kid! My whole fourth-grade class made posters.

The coaches have Arkansas roots on both sides. Eli Drinkwitz grew up in Alma, Ark., and said last fall, "I think the SEC is better when Arkansas is good." Ryan Silverfield was hired the morning after last year's game and is looking for his first win over Missouri. "Having faced Missouri in the past, we know that they're going to be sound and well-coached," he said.

Delphine: Ding! Breaking news: Drinkwitz is being nice to you.

Bubba: He grew up in Alma. He knows how to call the Hogs.

The SEC's initial availability report, posted at 8:10 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists three Missouri players out and four Arkansas players out, with Chris Marshall questionable.

Delphine: I'm dressing as a news anchor. Same as every day, but with a cape.

Bubba: I'm going as a Razorback, snout and all, for the laser show.

Delphine: If Missouri wins, you read my ticker on air for a week.

Bubba: If Arkansas wins, you call the Hogs from the top row. Loud.

Delphine: Ding-ding! Deal.

My call: Missouri Tigers 27, Arkansas Razorbacks 21.

Vangie: Bow Down to Washington! I packed purple, Darla. I also packed a life jacket. Where's the lake?

Darla: There's a pond behind my uncle's barn. It's mostly ducks.

Nebraska athletic director Troy Dannen confirmed the look on his monthly radio show, and KETV reported it this way: "He also confirmed Memorial Stadium, on Saturday, will feature the skull and crossbones at midfield. Plus the black balloons will be out for the blackout game against Washington."

The day runs on a schedule. Nebraska's game page lists parking lots opening at noon ET, the Cornhusker Kickoff Tailgate at 4 p.m. ET, the Husker Legacy Walk at 5:30 p.m. ET, gates at 6:30 p.m. ET and kickoff at 8 p.m. ET on BTN.

Darla: Eight hours of tailgate, Vangie. On a farm we call that a short workday.

Vangie: In Seattle we call it a regatta with no water.

The history is older than either of them. Nebraska's notes say Saturday is "the 11th all-time meeting," and the Huskers lead the series 5-4-1, including 2-1-1 in Lincoln. The first one, per Washington's notes, was played in Lincoln on Oct. 17, 1925, and "The game ended in a 6-6 tie." In 1991 in Lincoln, the Huskies trailed 21-9 in the third quarter and won 36-21. In 1998, "Nebraska buried the Dawgs, 55-7." The last one was 2011, when "Nebraska rolled up 309 rushing yards in a 51-38 win." This is the first meeting as Big Ten opponents, and Nebraska goes to Seattle in 2027.

Vangie: Thirty-six to twenty-one, Darla. In your house. I'd like that one framed.

Darla: Frame 1997 too. We won at No. 2 Washington that year, and Nebraska's notes say it's still the last time the Huskers beat a top-10 team on the road.

Then there's the holiday itself. Nebraska's game notes say, "Nebraska owns a 17-2 record all-time on Halloween." The last Halloween game was 2015 at Purdue, and the last one at home was 1998 against Texas.

Darla: Seventeen and two on Halloween. We don't hand out candy, Vangie. We hand out losses.

Vangie: Cute. I'll take full-size candy instead.

Both teams come in off an open week. Washington is 4-3 and 1-3 in the Big Ten after a 38-26 win at Purdue, where Brown went 21 of 27 for 302 yards and three touchdowns, with three interceptions. Williams, who has 1,396 yards and eight touchdown throws this year, is working back from a fractured rib, and Fisch isn't saying who plays. "Obviously, there's a competitive advantage that we will not give up," he said. He also had kind words for both: "Rising tides lift all ships."

Vangie: Our guy Williams has passed 1,000 career rushing yards. Washington's notes say he's at 1,076, the third Husky quarterback to do it, after Jake Locker and Marques Tuiasosopo.

Darla: Those are big names. Tell him to save his legs for the Penn State game.

That's next for Washington, on Nov. 7 at Husky Stadium, and the notes say it will be the Nittany Lions' "first visit to Seattle in 105 years." The Huskies also have punter Hunter Green, who sits No. 1 in the Big Ten at 47.9 yards a kick. Sports Illustrated reported that center Landen Hatchett is out for the season with a neck injury, a real loss up front.

Vangie: Hunter Green kicks it farther than I can row in a minute. I've checked.

Nebraska is 5-2 and 2-2 in the league after two three-point losses, 20-17 to Indiana and 17-14 at Oregon. Colandrea has 1,570 yards and 14 touchdown throws, Kwazi Gilmer has 38 catches for 492 yards and seven scores, Jamal Rule has 391 rushing yards and Chambliss leads the team with 46 tackles. The Blackshirts allow 15.4 points a game, and Nebraska's release says Big Ten opponents "have converted just 8-of-49 third downs."

Darla: Eight of forty-nine, Vangie. That's my free-throw shooting at the county fair, and I'm a volleyball player.

Rhule knows what's coming. "They're a vertical passing offense," he said. "They push the ball down the field." He also put the losses on the staff: "I think we've got to do a better job as coaches."

On the Nebraska side, the Huskers have held all seven opponents to 23 points or fewer, which the release says Nebraska last did in 2001. Washington scores 27.9 a game, so something gives.

The Big Ten's availability report, posted at 8 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists Demond Williams Jr. questionable and Landen Hatchett out.

Vangie: Fine, Darla. I'll wear black. But I'm wearing my rowing jacket over it.

Darla: Deal. And I'll find you a lake by 2027. Go Big Red.

Vangie: Bow Down to Washington. See you at the Legacy Walk.

My call: Nebraska Cornhuskers 33, Washington Huskies 19.

Army vs Memphis: Homecoming, Hero Day and Halloween in the 901

Army Black Knights vs Memphis Tigers is the Week 9 Homecoming and Hero Day game on Halloween night at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, and Memphis promises fireworks around the bowl of a stadium it just spent $226.5 million to rebuild. Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke, a retired Army logistics officer who reads every option play like a supply chain, says Cale Hellums, Dawson Jones and Jeff Monken's Black Knights march out of Memphis happy, and Otis Delaney-Crum, a Memphis blues guitarist who sings bass in his gospel choir, says Marcus Stokes, Hunter Tipton and Charles Huff's Tigers keep the party going.

Otis: Well, hello there, Captain. Welcome to the 901. I tuned the guitar just for you.

Thaddeus: Attention on deck, Otis. I've got a mission brief, a pressed uniform and a costume for later.

Otis: What's the costume?

Thaddeus: A slightly more relaxed Army officer.

The whole week has been a party in Memphis. The university's homecoming page lists Friday's ROARFest Block Party and Pep Rally on the Alumni Mall, with "food trucks, giveaways, the Mighty Sound of the South, the Memphis Spirit Squads, a live DJ and dance party, appearances by the 2026 Homecoming Court, games, a kid zone and Tent-or-Treat fun for children." On Saturday, the Blue Crew tailgate opens at noon ET in the Student Tan Lot, the alumni tailgate opens at 5:30 p.m. ET on Tiger Lane, and the band alumni play during the game.

Otis: Tent-or-Treat, Captain. Kids go tent to tent for candy. It's the most organized thing in Memphis.

Thaddeus: Otis, that's a supply chain. I approve.

The stadium is new, too. Memphis says the renovation added a four-level West Tower, "360 degree sound, fireworks around the bowl of the stadium and one of the largest ribbon boards in all of college football," and capacity now sits at 45,632.

Otis: Fireworks every time we score. Bring earplugs, Captain.

Thaddeus: I've heard louder, Otis. But never in a stadium.

These two don't see much of each other. Memphis notes say this is "just the sixth time" they've met, and the first since Nov. 23, 2002, when DeAngelo Williams led Memphis to a 38-10 win at home. The release adds that only three current Tigers were alive for that one, and Anthony Richard Jr. was "just 8 months old."

Otis: Eight months old, Captain. He was a baby. Now he's a cornerback.

Thaddeus: Time marches, Otis. So do we.

Both teams come in hot. Army is 5-2 and 4-1 in the American after Jones booted a 50-yard field goal as time expired to win 38-35 at Tulsa. He also hit from 51 in the first quarter, and Army says he's the first Black Knights kicker to make two from 50 or longer in a game. Hellums ran 30 times for 121 yards and three touchdowns that night, and Godspower Nwawuihe added 135 yards on 12 carries, with a 66-yard score.

Thaddeus: Two from fifty, Otis. Our kicker resupplied the whole operation from long range.

Otis: That's a long note to hold, Captain. Even for a bass.

For the season, Hellums has 840 rushing yards and 16 rushing touchdowns on 159 carries. Army scores 35.3 points a game, and Elijah Walton leads with 52 tackles.

Memphis is 6-2 and 3-1 in the league, and the Tigers are fresh off a 41-34 overtime win over East Carolina. They trailed by two scores before Stokes won it with a scramble and Ellis Ellis Jr. sealed it with an interception. That win made Memphis bowl eligible for the 13th season in a row, which the school calls the longest such run by a non-Power 4 program. Stokes has 2,161 yards and 21 touchdown throws, Jaylin Carter has 833 rushing yards and eight scores, Tipton has 30 catches for 409 yards and Elijah Kinsler has 5.5 sacks. Memphis scores 36.1 a game.

Otis: Thirteen in a row, Captain. That's a long gig with no night off.

There's a coaching wrinkle, too. The Brigade Review notes that the last time Huff saw a triple-option team was 2021, when his Marshall team beat Navy 49-7. His defensive coordinator that day, Lance Guidry, is the same one Army sees on Saturday.

Thaddeus: Then Coach Guidry knows what's coming, Otis. Knowing and stopping are two different missions.

Otis: Captain, that's the most Army thing anybody's ever said to me.

The matchup is simple to say and hard to do: Army's option against a Memphis defense that has never seen it this year, and Stokes against an Army defense that allows 22.1 a game.

Otis: After the game I'm playing "Hound Dog" on Beale. Come sing with me, Captain.

Thaddeus: I'll hold the low notes, Otis. Copy that, and beat Navy.

Otis: Navy's not here, Captain.

Thaddeus: Navy's always here, Otis. Go Army.

My call: Memphis Tigers 31, Army Black Knights 28.

Texas State vs Boise State: Halloween Black-Out on the Blue Turf

Texas State Bobcats vs Boise State Broncos is a Week 9 Halloween night at Albertsons Stadium in Boise, the first The Blue After Dark game, with kickoff at 10 p.m. ET on CW and a Kellen Moore bronze statue unveiled on the blue turf at halftime. Yesenia Calderwood, a Texas State fan who floats the San Marcos River with a sun hat and a radio, says Brad Jackson, Torrance Burgess Jr. and Jacob Bonilla can steal one in the first meeting, and Thatcher Bluestem, a Boise State fan whose car, pancakes and opinions are all blue, says Maddux Madsen, Dylan Riley and Boen Phelps keep the Broncos rolling.

Thatcher: Paint it blue! Welcome to Boise, Yesenia. Tonight we wear black.

Yesenia: Eat 'em up, Cats! You told me everything here is blue.

Thatcher: Black on the outside. Blue on the inside. Like a good pancake.

Yesenia: That is not how pancakes work, Thatcher.

Boise State is going big for the holiday. Fans are asked to wear black, the first 3,000 students get a custom game day shirt, and the tailgate lots turn into a trunk-or-treat with candy for the kids. Parking opens at 2 p.m. ET and gates open at 8 p.m. ET. Costumes are welcome inside, but masks come off at security, and candy has to come in clear containers. At halftime, the Keith Stein Blue Thunder Marching Band and Spirit Squad perform with new lighting, and then the Kellen Moore statue is unveiled on the field. Athletic director Jeramiah Dickey put it this way: "It's about 6 games, 6 sellouts. Everything counts and everything matters."

Yesenia: Candy in clear bags. Back home we float the river with snacks in a cooler.

Thatcher: Bring the cooler. Just make it clear.

This is the first meeting between these schools, and both are new to the Pac-12 this season. Boise State is 6-1 and 3-0 in the league and has won six in a row, and the Broncos are bowl-eligible for the 29th straight season, second only to Georgia among active runs. Spencer Danielson won his 30th game at Boise State last week, the eighth Bronco head coach to get there. Texas State is 4-3 and 2-1 in the league, and G.J. Kinne's 27th win with the Bobcats tied him for second among their Division I head coaches. His teams are 17-7 at home.

Madsen has completed 124 of 189 throws for 1,445 yards and 14 touchdowns, with no interceptions through seven games. The school says he's the first Bronco to do that since the program joined the top level in 1996. He's 17-1 in league games he has led and fourth in school history with 631 career completions. Riley has 963 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 140 carries, freshman Rasean Jones has 29 catches for 437 yards, Phelps has 41 tackles and Jayden Virgin-Morgan has three sacks. At Washington State last week, Riley ran 13 times for 128 yards and two touchdowns in a 31-10 win, Boise State's first ever in Pullman.

Thatcher: Seven games, no interceptions. That's bluer than an October sky.

Nola Brandvik spent 30 seconds staring at a photo of a cornfield after the Hawai'i game, and she says it helped. Now she's flying to Las Vegas on Halloween, where Vegas Monroe-Kalani has already rated the opening act and promised a show.

Northern Illinois (0-7) at UNLV (4-3), Saturday at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. It's a Mountain West game. DraftKings has UNLV Rebels −23.5 with a total of 53.5. My card: Northern Illinois Huskies +23.5, Under 53.5, and a final of UNLV Rebels 35, Northern Illinois Huskies 15.

Nola speaks for Northern Illinois. "I'm calm. Very calm. We were tied with Hawai'i in the second quarter, and then the crop got hailed on. DeAree Rogers caught eight balls for 115 yards and two touchdowns. Telly Johnson Jr. has 502 rushing yards. The roots are still in the ground."

Vegas speaks for UNLV. "And that's the show, folks. Jackson Arnold has 10 touchdown passes and two interceptions, and he runs it too. We held Hawai'i to six and North Dakota State to seven. But I'll be honest, our last act was Air Force, and that one got a bad review, 41-31."

Here is the part that matters. UNLV scores 24.1 points a game. That is not a team built to win by four touchdowns. The Rebels' four wins were 21-6, 38-10, 39-31 and 13-7. To cover 23.5, UNLV has to do something it has done once all season.

Why Northern Illinois? Because the Huskies have stayed within this number in five of seven games. They lost 24-28 to Illinois State, 7-28 to Air Force and 23-41 at Wyoming. Action Network's opening number was UNLV −24.5, and it has come down a point. Both The Formula and Next Man Up like the Huskies. My final has UNLV by twenty.

The worry is the Northern Illinois defense. It allows 38.6 points a game, and Hawai'i scored 56 last week. Taron Dickens threw two interceptions. If UNLV gets the running game going with Jai'Den Thomas and Arnold, this could be the one blowout.

Why the Over/Under? UNLV plays low-scoring games. Its seven games ended 21-27, 21-6, 6-44, 38-10, 39-31, 13-7 and 31-41. Northern Illinois scores 15.1 points a game. UNLV runs the ball and uses the clock. Action Network's opening total was 52.5 and it has moved up to 53.5, but I want the Under. My 35-15 adds up to 50, three and a half under the over/under 53.5.

Now the room. The Formula has UNLV 35-16 and likes Northern Illinois and the Under. Next Man Up has UNLV 35-14 and likes Northern Illinois and the Under. Follow The Money likes Northern Illinois after the move and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Formula: "Same result. Take the points."

display.fanatic_story:
Halloween Night on the Strip: Northern Illinois Visits UNLV

Northern Illinois (0-7, 0-3 Mountain West) at UNLV (4-3, 2-1 Mountain West). Saturday, Oct. 31, 10:30 p.m. ET (7:30 p.m. Pacific), Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas, CBSSN.

Your hosts are Nola Brandvik, a Northern Illinois agricultural scientist from DeKalb who thinks about the Huskies like a corn crop, and Vegas Monroe-Kalani, a former headliner dancer who calls every UNLV game a show and rates the opening act.

Vegas: The show starts Saturday night. Welcome to Las Vegas, Nola.

Nola: Thank you. I'm calm. Very calm. I brought a sweater. It's October.

Players to watch

Northern Illinois quarterback Taron Dickens is 138 of 210 for 1,364 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Running back Telly Johnson Jr. has 95 carries for 502 yards and four touchdowns. Wide receiver DeAree Rogers leads the team with 57 catches for 537 yards and four touchdowns. On defense, Jack Murray has 49 tackles and Avery Jones has two sacks.

UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold is 108 of 182 for 1,386 yards, 10 touchdowns and two interceptions. The school says he leads the league with 16 total touchdowns, 10 throwing and six running. Running back Jai'Den Thomas has 112 carries for 543 yards and three touchdowns. Wide receiver Kayden McGee has 16 catches for 330 yards and four touchdowns. Safety Jake Pope leads the defense with 63 tackles, Tre Fulton has 3.5 sacks and Mumu Bin-Wahad has three interceptions.

What happened last week

Northern Illinois lost 56-21 at home to Hawai'i on Oct. 24. The game was tied at 14 in the second quarter before Hawai'i scored 35 points in a row. Rogers caught eight balls for 115 yards and two touchdowns, of 49 and 25 yards. Dickens threw for 171 yards, and Johnson ran for 63.

UNLV had an open date on Oct. 24, its second bye of the season. The Rebels' last game was a 41-31 loss at Air Force on Oct. 17. McGee caught five balls for 99 yards and two touchdowns that day, and Arnold ran for a score.

Nola: After the Hawai'i game I stared at my cornfield photo for 30 seconds. It helped.

Injuries and availability

The official Mountain West availability report hadn't been posted as of Tuesday and usually comes out on game day. Unofficial notes from mid-October list UNLV receiver DeAngelo Irvin Jr. as out. McGee was listed as questionable that week but played at Air Force. Dickens was listed as questionable before the Hawai'i game and played.

What the coaches are up to

Rob Harley was the Huskies' defensive coordinator until he was promoted to interim head coach when Thomas Hammock resigned on Feb. 18 to return to the NFL. After the Hawai'i game, Harley said, "We have to find a way, and it starts with me first, to find a way to increase the consistency with the base stuff that we do."

Dan Mullen is in his second season at UNLV after being hired on Dec. 12, 2024. The Rebels are 7-2 at home under Mullen. This week he talked about tackling and getting healthy after the break.

Player storylines

Rogers is on a roll for the Huskies. Arnold, an Auburn transfer, didn't throw his first interception of the season until the North Dakota State game on Oct. 10. That came after 142 straight throws without one.

What's happening on campus

UNLV is throwing a Halloween party at Allegiant Stadium. The Rebel Village Fan Zone in Lot C is free, and a band called The Lucky Devils plays before the game.

Halloween is also Nevada Day, the day Nevada became the 36th state in 1864. UNLV last played on Halloween in 2020, when it hosted Nevada in the first game ever played at Allegiant Stadium.

Northern Illinois is in its first season in the Mountain West as a football-only member, so this trip is all new.

Anything else fun and true

The Huskies have won all five meetings with UNLV, the latest 38-30 in 2015. UNLV is still looking for its first win in the series.

UNLV says it has already played in five different time zones this season and is the only school in the top level of college football scheduled to do that in 2026. The Rebels are 2-7 all-time on Halloween, and their last Halloween win was 35-31 over San Jose State in 1992.

Vegas: Saturday night, under the lights, on Halloween. That's my kind of opening act.

Nola: Knee-high by the Fourth of July. Or by Halloween. I'll take either.

My call: UNLV Rebels 35, Northern Illinois Huskies 15.

Oregon State vs Fresno State: Halloween Night Under the Valley Lights

Oregon State Beavers vs Fresno State Bulldogs is a Week 9 Halloween night at Valley Children's Stadium in Fresno, the first time these two meet as Pac-12 opponents, with kickoff at 11 p.m. ET on USA Sports. Juniper Ostrowski, an Oregon State forestry PhD who charts treetop weather and red-zone efficiency and corrects everyone's tree metaphors, says Braden Atkinson, Jesse Legree and Takari Hickle keep the Beavers on top of the league, and Rosalind "Roz" Ayala, a Fresno State fan and raisin-grower's daughter who calls herself the Valley Girl, says Jayden Mandal, Josiah Freeman and K'vion Thunderbird make it two in a row over Oregon State.

Roz: Not that Valley, babe! Welcome to Fresno on Halloween.

Juniper: Measure twice, kick once! I came as a Douglas fir.

Roz: Of course you did. The needles are on backward.

Juniper: Those are cones, Roz. That's a fir thing.

Fresno State is turning the Red and White Lot into a Trunk or Treat, with tailgaters signing up their picnic spaces for the kids. The Bulldogs have a good Halloween history, too: they're 7-4-1 on Oct. 31, including 5-0-1 at home, though they haven't played on Halloween since 2009. Oregon State is 4-9-1 on Halloween. Ryan Leaf has the call on TV, and former Bulldogs coach Pat Hill is on the radio with Paul Loeffler.

Juniper: Four and nine on Halloween. I'll hold my cones a little tighter.

These two go back to 1981. Fresno State leads the series 9-6 and is 6-1 at home against Oregon State, and the teams have traded wins in each of the last six meetings. In 2001, David Carr threw for 340 yards and four touchdowns as Fresno State beat No. 10 Oregon State 44-24. In 2003, Brett Visintainer kicked a career-long 47-yard field goal with 31 seconds left for a 16-14 win. In 2022, the Beavers scored as time expired to win 35-32. Last year, Fresno State won 36-27 in Corvallis, its first road win over the Beavers since 1991.

Roz: Trading wins every time. That means it's our turn to win again, right?

Juniper: That's not how forests work. Or calendars.

Oregon State is 5-2 and 3-0 in the league, first in the Pac-12, and has won five straight without trailing in any of them. Atkinson has completed 189 of 273 throws for 2,604 yards, 24 touchdowns and two interceptions, and he has gone 129 throws without an interception, with Matt Moore's school record at 182. Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns, AJ Newberry has 431 rushing yards, Aiden Sullivan has 53 tackles and Hickle has six sacks. In the 48-30 win over Washington State on Oct. 17, Atkinson threw for 347 yards and three touchdowns. JaMarcus Shephard is 5-2 in his first season.

Juniper: Legree is a giant sequoia. Tall, strong and impossible to miss.

Fresno State is 4-3 and 1-2 in the league. The Bulldogs allow 20.9 points a game, second in the conference, and they have thrown one interception in 201 team attempts. Mandal, in his first season as the No. 1 quarterback, has 1,393 yards, eight touchdowns and that one interception, plus two rushing scores and a 21-yard catch. Freeman has 32 catches for 445 yards, Rayshon Luke has 333 rushing yards and Thunderbird has 61 tackles. The Bulldogs have outscored opponents 45-8 in the third quarter. Matt Entz is 13-7 at Fresno State and won two FCS national titles at North Dakota State.

Roz: Forty-five to eight in the third quarter. That's when the raisins dry, babe.

Juniper: That is not how raisins work.

Three Oregon State staffers have worked at Fresno State: offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen, running backs coach Lee Marks and general manager Ron McKeefery. So some of the Beavers know their way around the building.

The Pac-12's advance availability report, updated at 10:04 p.m. ET Wednesday, Oct. 28, lists two Oregon State players out, one for the season, and three Fresno State players out and five questionable.

Roz: I'm going as a raisin. Small, sweet and wrinkly.

Juniper: I'm staying a Douglas fir. Nobody wants a raisin next to a tree.

Roz: Whatever happens, Juniper, dinner's on me, and you say "Not that Valley, babe" on your podcast.

Juniper: Then you learn three tree species.

Roz: Deal. I already know raisin.

My call: Oregon State Beavers 30, Fresno State Bulldogs 27.

Rosalind "Roz" Ayala, the raisin-grower's daughter who calls herself the Valley Girl, waves her off. "Not that Valley, babe. We're unbeaten at home on Halloween, and we won in your building last year."

My concern is Atkinson. He has thrown for 2,604 yards, and Jesse Legree has 46 catches for 1,040 yards and 14 touchdowns. Oregon State scores 42.7 a game and beat San Diego State 66-14 and Washington State 48-30. If Fresno State can't move the ball, five and a half is not a lot.

The total comes down to the Fresno State defense. The Bulldogs' seven games ended 39-0, 49-3, 26-10, 38-24, 26-6, 38-31 and 26-23, and only two of those went past 57.5. My 30-27 adds up to 57. DraftKings has Oregon State −5.5 and 57.5. The consensus spread opened at Oregon State −5.5 and hasn't moved. The consensus total opened at 58.5 and is 57.5 as of Oct 27, 2026, 4:44 PM ET.

The room is with me on the Under. The Formula has Oregon State 30-27 and is on Fresno State and the Under without backing either. Next Man Up has Oregon State 29-26, is on Fresno State without backing it and likes the Under. Follow The Money has no side pick and likes the Under, and it keeps no score of its own. In The Trenches has no pick. Letdown Watch has no score this week.

The Formula: "Three points. Halloween treat for the home team."

Next Man Up: "The Pac-12's advance report, updated at 10:04 p.m. ET Wednesday, doesn't list Atkinson, Mandal or Legree, so no quarterback change in my numbers."

A defense that's second in the league, a quarterback who doesn't throw it to the other team and a home crowd in costume. Give me the Bulldogs and the Under.

Oregon State Beavers 30, Fresno State Bulldogs 27. Fresno State Bulldogs cover the 5.5. Under 57.5.
